title: sessions should require positive conversational evidence, not be the default shape
description:
OPERATOR OBSERVATION (2026-07-31): 'maybe we shouldn't assume something is a session by default? why do we do that?'

MEASURED against the live index (23,296 sessions):
  sessions with ZERO messages: 5,255 (22.6% of the archive)
    claude-code-session  5,193   (31.7% of that origin)
    claude-ai-export        45
    codex-session           17

THE DEFECT: the ingest path's default disposition is 'this is a session'. Anything not positively recognised as something else still becomes one. Every classification gap therefore manifests as session inflation rather than as a loud unrecognised-record report.

FOUR SEPARATE INCIDENTS, ONE CAUSE:
  hook events ingested as standalone sessions   83,286 -> 18,391 after repair
  agent-<id>.meta.json sidecars                 4,945 phantoms, 21% of the index
  a toolu_* tool-use id and 7 wf_* ids          became sessions outright
  beads issue audit-logs (proposed)             924, averted only because the
                                                acquisition route shipped opt-in
Each was fixed by adding a SPECIFIC refusal (an OriginSpec artifact rule, a
write_hook_event path, a parse gate). None changed the default. So the next
unrecognised record type will do it again and the fix will again be a special
case.

PROPOSED INVARIANT: a session requires positive evidence of a conversation — at
minimum one message carrying authored content. A record failing that test is
REFUSED LOUDLY and routed to what it actually is (session_event, attachment,
assertion, ObservedRepositoryEffect). 'I do not recognise this' must never
produce a session.

This is the record-level sibling of aggz invariant 2 ('exactly one chokepoint
may write a session') and the record-level form of the fail-loud principle being
applied at field level elsewhere. Its structural value: it converts every FUTURE
classification gap from silent inflation into a visible refusal — which is
exactly what the new claude_parse_coverage event (PR #3419) was invented to
detect after the fact.

TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE ACTING, do not assume:
1. The hook-inflation postmortem DELIBERATELY RETAINED 832 genuinely-empty
   sessions (see polylogue-ne6k, which corrected an earlier plan to delete
   them). A naive 'refuse empty' rule would destroy a considered decision.
   5,193 is far more than 832, so the majority are unexplained.
2. Possible overlap with the 5,382 sessions carrying created_at_ms NULL
   (dataset finding C4) — similar magnitude, may be the same population. A
   dataset-hypotheses lane is measuring C4 concurrently; reconcile before
   designing.

AC: the default disposition for an unrecognised record is refusal with a
recorded reason, not session creation; empty-session count is explained
(intentional vs artifact) and the artifact class is eliminated at its source;
a regression test pins that an unrecognised record type does not create a
session.
notes: RECONCILIATION 2026-07-31: GENUINELY OPEN, confirmed live. sessions with message_count=0 in the live index = 5,257 (bead measured 5,255, consistent modulo ongoing ingest). This is a broader invariant than the specific phantom-session fixes already merged (PR #3403/#3428/#3426, tracked on polylogue-b508, currently in_progress not open) — 9ykn's own note explicitly distinguishes "each incident gets a specific refusal" from "the default disposition changes", and the latter is unimplemented: no positive-evidence-required gate exists at the general record-classification chokepoint. The 5,257 empty sessions include the 832 intentionally-retained genuinely-empty ones (per polylogue-ne6k) plus an unexplained majority — that reconciliation (which of the 5,257 are which) has also not been done. Real, unaddressed work on both the invariant and the explanation-of-existing-rows AC.
close_reason: Merged PR #3497 (18606faf9): session writes now require positive conversational evidence — unrecognised records are refused loudly with a recorded reason (regression-pinned); the 5,257 empty sessions fully reconciled read-only (4,945 agent-*.meta sidecars + 228+ envelope-only JSONL + 3 tool-results misdispatch + 2 .gemini misdetections + 47 claude-ai empties + 17 codex empties; 5,192/5,193 overlap C4's NULL created_at_ms population); ne6k's own correction established no genuinely-empty construct, so no carve-out. Artifact classes eliminated at ingest source; existing rows purge with the v46→v50 rebuild.

title: paths.archive_root() ignores polylogue.toml, splitting the archive root
description:
polylogue/paths/_roots.py:archive_root() resolves POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT from
the environment only and never consults polylogue.toml's [archive] root, even
though polylogue/config.py documents and implements a 5-layer resolution
(default, site TOML, user TOML, env, CLI) that DOES honour it.

Consequence: any process without POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT set in its own
environment (bare CLI invocations, hook writers, the browser-capture
receiver, ad hoc scripts) silently falls back to XDG_DATA_HOME/polylogue
instead of the operator's configured root (e.g. /realm/db/polylogue),
splitting archive state across two directories that nothing reconciles.

Measured live damage before the fix: 108,094 files (2.2 GB) accumulated
in ~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks/pending/ since 2026-07-14 while the
daemon (which does get POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT from its systemd unit) drained
/realm/db/polylogue/hooks/pending/ instead -- nothing processed the XDG-root
backlog. Browser-capture spool and inbox/ content were also split across
both roots at different times depending on which process's environment
happened to have the override set.

Fix: polylogue.config gained resolve_archive_root() (same layered precedence
as load_polylogue_config, extracted so paths._roots can reuse it via a lazy
function-local import without an import cycle -- config.py already imports
polylogue.paths for GEMINI_DRIVE_FOLDER). paths.archive_root() now checks
POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT first (fast path, no config import) and falls back to
resolve_archive_root() (site/user TOML, then XDG default) when unset.
Nothing is cached, preserving per-test POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT isolation.

Explicitly out of scope for this fix: migrating the ~176K files already
misplaced under the XDG root (hooks pending+acknowledged, browser-capture
spool, inbox) -- that is a separate data-migration lane.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #3414 (1e53bf89f): archive_root() falls back to config.resolve_archive_root() when POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT is unset, verified by test suites and devtools verify --quick.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Fixed via PR #3414 (branch feature/fix/archive-root-honours-config, commit e9e7a7245). paths.archive_root() now falls back to polylogue.config.resolve_archive_root() (site/user TOML archive.root) when POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT is unset, instead of silently defaulting to XDG_DATA_HOME/polylogue. Verified: devtools test on tests/unit/core/test_paths.py (new TestArchiveRootHonoursConfigFile suite, 25 passed), test_config_resolution_regression.py (9 passed), plus config/cli-paths/browser-capture-token/hook-spool suites (143 passed); devtools verify --quick green. Data migration of the ~176K files already misplaced under the XDG root (hooks pending+acknowledged, browser-capture spool, inbox) is explicitly out of scope -- needs a separate follow-up.

title: newer chatgpt exports are NOT supersets - April holds 33% more messages than July
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31, comparing chatgpt-data-2026-04-23 against chatgpt-data-2026-07-29 over the 2,094 conversations present in BOTH.

  April  109,657 messages total / 97,403 in the common set
  July    72,981 messages total / 44,834 in the common set
  EVERY ONE of the 2,094 common conversations lost messages. Not one gained.

Not deletion, not branch pruning (July's current_node path count is also far
below April's), and not head/tail truncation (survivors are spread across the
full 0-100% index range with identical date spans). OpenAI DROPPED WHOLE
CATEGORIES between export generations:

  content_type              April     July     delta
    code                    20,384        0  -20,384
    computer_output          8,192        0   -8,192
    execution_output         6,816        0   -6,816
    tether_browsing_display  1,399        0   -1,399
    tether_quote             1,178        0   -1,178
    system_error               177        0
    sonic_webpage               30        0
    citable_code_output          8        0
    text                    37,829   24,890  -12,939
    multimodal_text          1,457      694     -763
    user_editable_context      821        1     -820
    thoughts                17,374   17,506     +132  (retained)
    reasoning_recap          1,738    1,743       +5  (retained)

  role
    tool                    24,914        0  -24,914   <- the ENTIRE tool layer
    system                   5,099        0   -5,099
    assistant               54,513   32,839  -21,674
    user                    12,877   11,995     -882

The whole code-interpreter / tool-use / browsing layer is absent from the newer
export. This also explains why model-produced sandbox files carry no file id in
the July data (polylogue-dt5s): the tool messages that created them are gone.

CONSEQUENCES - these change import strategy, not just this one file:

1. A newer export can be a STRICT SUBSET of an older one. 'Latest wins' is
   wrong for this provider. Coalescing must be a per-message UNION keyed on
   message id, with each export treated as a partial observation.
2. The April 2026 and Oct 2025 exports are NOT superseded and must never be
   pruned as redundant. They are the only surviving record of 24,914 tool
   messages and 20,384 code blocks.
3. This is precisely the aggz/superset question the operator raised for
   aistudio, now confirmed with hard numbers on a second provider: neither
   revision is a superset, so any model that must pick ONE winner loses data.
   The content-only comparison relation (#3401) must classify this pair as
   'conflict', not 'contains' in either direction.
4. Absence detection should compare across export generations per message id,
   not per conversation - a conversation present in both looked fine at
   session granularity while silently losing 78% of its messages.

AC: importing all three chatgpt exports yields the UNION of their messages;
a conversation present in several exports carries every message any export
observed; and a regression test pins that the newer-export-is-subset case
does not delete previously-ingested messages.
notes:
VERIFIED THREE WAYS (2026-07-31) after the finding was challenged as implausible for a GDPR export.

1. THE EXPORT IS COMPLETE AS DELIVERED. Checked every file against the export's
   own export_manifest.json: 3,266 declared files, 3,266 present, ZERO missing,
   ZERO size mismatches, 18.091 GB declared vs 18.092 GB actual (delta is the
   manifest itself, which is not self-declared). So the loss is not download
   corruption, not truncation from the 5 stalled resumes, and not extraction
   error. It is what OpenAI shipped.

2. IT IS A FORMAT CHANGE, NOT RETENTION AGE-OUT. Conversations created as
   recently as 2026-07-27 - two days before the export was generated - also
   contain ZERO tool-role and ZERO system-role messages. Across the ENTIRE July
   export the only roles present are assistant (59,728) and user (13,253).
   A retention window would have spared recent conversations; it did not.

3. THE TOOL LAYER IS NOT HIDING IN chat.html EITHER. grep over the 221 MB
   chat.html: execution_output 0, computer_output 0, tether_quote 0. The
   rendered view carries no more than the JSON.

WHAT APRIL STILL HAS (answers 'are the sandbox files in April then?' - yes):
   April non-json members            9,958   (vs 3,228 .dat in July)
   distinct file ids in member names 9,887
   file ids referenced INSIDE tool messages 10,453
     of those WITH bytes present      9,225   (88.2%)
   asset_pointer + metadata.attachments refs  3,189 distinct, 1,104 with bytes (34.6%)

   So in April the file ids live in the TOOL messages, which is exactly why
   July - having deleted the tool layer - cannot resolve model-produced files.
   April is the only record of ~9,225 attachment blobs.

CONVERSATION-LEVEL COVERAGE IS ALSO NON-NESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS:
   in April but not July   309
   in July but not April   378   (some created as far back as 2023-02-14,
                                  i.e. April was ALSO missing old conversations)
   Neither export is a superset at conversation level either.

CONTEXT FROM THE WEB: incomplete ChatGPT exports are a documented user
complaint (community.openai.com/t/incomplete-data-export-with-conversations-json/1019950,
Nov 2024: a user's export dropped everything before 2024-10-28, 35MB -> 4MB, no
official response). The specific tool-layer removal is not publicly documented,
so treat provider export completeness as untrusted and verify per generation.
DECISIVE RESOLUTION RULE (2026-07-31). The union is not a heuristic merge - the two exports are in STRICT CONTAINMENT and there is no genuine disagreement anywhere in the corpus. Proven by field-walking all 44,171 messages present in both exports:

  field observations           748,209
    both set & AGREE           291,774
    both set & CONFLICT          2,479   (0.33%)
    only April                 453,956
    only July                        0   <- July contributes NOTHING April lacks

And the 2,479 'conflicts' are subsetting one level deeper, not disagreement.
They occur in exactly two fields - metadata.content_references (1,766) and
metadata.search_result_groups (713) - and inspecting them shows identical
record COUNTS (29,528 both sides) and identical type distributions (file 8,543,
grouped_webpages 7,363, webpage_extended 6,239, hidden 4,889, attribution
1,073, sources_footnote 951 - the same on both sides). What differs is the KEY
SET of each citation record:

  April keys: alt end_idx error fallback_items items matched_text prompt_text
              refs safe_urls start_idx status style type
  July  keys: alt fallback_items items prompt_text type

July dropped end_idx, start_idx, matched_text, refs, safe_urls, error, status,
style. Note start_idx/end_idx: July's citations LOST THEIR TEXT ANCHORS, which
is the conceptual core of a citation.

Also lost from message.metadata between generations (top-level keys present in
April, absent in July): can_save, message_type, timestamp_, request_id,
default_model_slug, CITATIONS (20,471 messages!), reasoning_status,
turn_exchange_id, finish_details, is_complete. New in July: NONE.
Envelope fields nulled in July: status (finished_successfully -> null, 42,000),
weight (1.0 -> null, 44,164), author.metadata removed - including
real_author='tool:web' on 237 messages.

message CONTENT is byte-identical on all 44,171 common messages. Zero content
conflicts.

THEREFORE the correct algorithm is deterministic and lossless, and needs no
conflict policy at all:

  for each message id, and each field PATH (including inside nested citation
  records), take the value from whichever acquisition has one; where several
  have one they are equal; record which acquisition supplied each field.

'Record the disagreement' is not needed for this provider pair because there IS
no disagreement - only presence vs absence. This is a much stronger position
than the earlier framing and should be the default model for every origin:
treat an acquisition as a partial observation, merge at field-path granularity,
and only escalate to a recorded conflict if two acquisitions ever assert
DIFFERENT non-null values for the same path - which happened zero times here.
VERDICT: LIVE (actively in_progress) — This is a fresh, ongoing investigation (created + started 2026-07-31) with extensive live-verified findings (chatgpt export union/subset semantics) still being landed; not stale, not closable. — evidence: bd show polylogue-geop --json (status=in_progress, started_at=2026-07-31T03:18:49Z, notes describe multi-step live verification concluding with a 'decisive resolution rule' still pending implementation of the AC's import/union behavior).
2026-07-31 verification pass (independent re-derivation, no code changes needed):

Confirmed the AC is already satisfied by PR #3413 (db6274ab6, merged
2026-07-31T07:48:52Z, "fix(storage): union messages/blocks across
acquisitions, not re-parses"), landed by a concurrent pass on this same
bead before this verification pass started. Traced the fix end to end:

1. write_parsed_session_to_archive (archive_tiers/write.py) now calls
   _union_with_existing_rows before its full-replace DELETE, gated on a
   raw_id discriminator: union fires only when incoming raw_id and the
   session's currently-stored raw_id are BOTH known and DIFFER (proven
   different acquisition -- the April/July case). Same raw_id, unknown
   provenance, or an explicit force_replace all fall back to plain
   replace, correctly preserving a same-acquisition re-parse's ability to
   retract a wrong prior parse.
2. Matched messages/blocks coalesce column-wise; a message/block entirely
   absent from the new acquisition is reinjected verbatim; blocks.tool_input
   gets a recursive field-path JSON union -- this is what restores the
   narrowed citation keys measured in this bead's field-walk.
3. test_reingest_with_poorer_export_unions_fields_instead_of_deleting_them
   pins exactly the AC's regression case: two different raw_ids, a dropped
   tool-role message and narrowed citation keys both restored.
4. Cross-checked against the LIVE archive (read-only): 100% of currently-
   materialized chatgpt-export sessions have an accepted raw_revision_heads
   row; spot-checked cohort chatgpt:68f099af-5860-8332-a55b-aa33a065e259
   (Oct 2025: 6 messages, April 2026: 10 messages) -- April's 10-message
   raw is applied, Oct's 6-message raw is superseded_prefix, and the
   materialized session correctly shows 10 messages. Union/containment
   resolution is live-correct today, not just in the test suite.

AC verdict: SATISFIED by #3413 for messages/blocks -- both AC clauses
about union/no-deletion hold, and the regression test the AC asked for
exists.

Explicitly OUT of this AC and correctly deferred to polylogue-u8x7 (filed
by #3413 itself, left open, unclaimed): session_events/session_model_usage
rollups and web_content_constructs/file_edits sidecar tables are NOT yet
unioned, so a reinjected message's usage/citation-sidecar rows can still
show zero/absent even though the message and its blocks are correctly
restored. Real, separate, smaller-blast-radius gap (cost/analytics
metadata, not conversation content) -- tracked there, not here.

I attempted a redundant top-level fix (a content-blind "refuse the whole
write" guard in the same file) before discovering #3413 already existed
in a rebase I'd pulled; reverted immediately after it broke
test_provider_usage_model_vanishing_on_reingest_leaves_no_stale_rollup
(same-acquisition retraction), confirming #3413's raw_id discriminator is
the correct design and a cruder identity-subset check is not.
close_reason: AC satisfied by #3413 (merged): field-path union of messages/blocks across different acquisitions, discriminated by raw_id, with the exact regression test the AC required. Verified independently against the live archive. Residual sidecar/usage-rollup union scope (not part of this AC) tracked separately in polylogue-u8x7.

title: Cull the repair surface: 10k lines of manual repair against 2.7k of convergence, with targets guarding schema-impossible states
description:
## Measured shape

    repair/maintenance surface   ~10,164 lines
      storage/repair.py            7,154   (123 top-level defs, 22 public entrypoints)
      maintenance/*.py             3,010
    daemon convergence             2,665 lines
      convergence.py                 637
      convergence_stages.py        2,028

A 3.8:1 ratio of manual repair machinery to the automatic convergence meant to
make it unnecessary. Convergence registers only FIVE stages: `fts`, `embed`,
`insights`, `claude_workflow`, `sinex_publication`. `repair.py` exposes eleven
repair targets.

This contradicts the project's own stated principle: *if Polylogue can maintain
a condition fully automatically it should, there is NO break-glass tier, and
once the automatic path maintains an invariant the redundant manual surface is
DELETED rather than demoted.*

## Per-target analysis (live archive, frozen 2026-07-30)

Note first: `REPAIR_HANDLERS[target]` is a name->function dispatch table, so
"no external references" means dynamically dispatched, NOT dead. Every target
below is reachable via `run_safe_repairs`/`run_archive_cleanup`.

### Structurally impossible — delete (strongest case)

| target | live violations | why it cannot occur |
| --- | -- | --- |
| `orphaned_messages` | **0** | `messages.session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(session_id) ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `orphaned_attachments` | **0** | `attachment_refs.session_id`/`message_id` both `NOT NULL ... ON DELETE CASCADE` |

`PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set in `storage/sqlite/connection_profile.py`, so
these are enforced, not decorative. The schema forbids the state; the repair
scans for it anyway. Zero violations is not luck.

Delete both repairs, both previews, their `SAFE_REPAIR_TARGETS`/`CLEANUP_TARGETS`
entries, and their debt-status rows.

### Spent one-shot migrations — delete once confirmed

| target | live violations | note |
| --- | -- | --- |
| `message_type_backfill` | **0** | A backfill for a column added later. Confirm the write path always sets it (NOT NULL would settle it), then the migration is spent. |

A backfill is inherently one-shot: once the historical rows are filled and the
writer populates the column, the repair guards nothing.

### Symptom-treating — the repair is the wrong fix

| target | live violations | note |
| --- | -- | --- |
| `session_timestamp_backfill` | **5,382, GROWING** | Was 1,117 after the hook de-inflation; now 5,382. A backfill whose backlog grows means the WRITE PATH is still producing the defect. |

This is the "fix the automatic path" case, and the most valuable finding here.
Do not keep running the backfill; find why sessions are still written with
`created_at_ms IS NULL` and stop that. The repair has been masking a live
writer bug, which is exactly what a break-glass tier does to you.

### Cause fixed elsewhere — expect near-no-op

| target | live violations | note |
| --- | -- | --- |
| `empty_sessions` | 5,255, of which **4,945** are `.meta` phantoms | PR #3403 fixes the cause (an ungated parse chokepoint in `revision_backfill.py`). After it lands, ~310 remain, and some of those are legitimately empty (sessions carrying only `session_events` after the v46 reclassification). Re-measure post-rebuild before deciding. |

### Genuinely load-bearing — keep

`raw_materialization`, `session_insights`, `orphaned_blobs`,
`superseded_raw_snapshots`, `stale_supersession_receipts`. These were exercised
for real this session (raw materialization and authority blockers had to be
unstuck manually). But note that needing them manually is itself evidence the
automatic path has gaps -- `session_insights` in particular overlaps the
`insights` convergence stage and should be examined for redundancy.

## Sequencing

The `archive.py` decomposition lane may relocate `repair.py`'s seam
(`architecture-hotspots.md` note-on-#3 leaves its `storage/` vs `maintenance/`
placement explicitly undecided). Do the deletions after that lands, or they
collide.

## Acceptance criteria

- `orphaned_messages` and `orphaned_attachments` repair+preview+registry entries
  deleted, with the FK/CASCADE constraint cited as the replacement guarantee.
- `message_type_backfill` deleted after confirming the writer always populates it.
- A separate bead opened for the `created_at_ms IS NULL` WRITER defect, with the
  1,117 -> 5,382 growth as evidence; the backfill target is not deleted until
  that is fixed.
- Line count of `storage/repair.py` reported before and after.
- No new registry or allowlist introduced by any of this.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-30: my per-target verdict on `empty_sessions` was wrong, and wrong in the dangerous direction.

I classified it as 'cause fixed elsewhere, expect near-no-op after #3403'. polylogue-ne6k, which already existed and which I failed to read before writing this analysis, records the opposite: **repair_empty_sessions would DELETE the 832 genuinely-empty sessions the hook-inflation postmortem deliberately chose to retain.**

So the target is not a soon-to-be-no-op. It is actively destructive against data an earlier postmortem made a considered decision to keep. Running it after #3403 lands would remove real archive content, not phantom rows.

Revised verdict for `empty_sessions`: do NOT delete the target as spent, and do NOT run it. It needs a decision about the 832 retained-empty sessions first (ne6k owns that), and any culling work must treat ne6k as a blocker rather than a footnote.

Method failure worth recording, because it is the same one twice in a day: I derived a verdict from live measurement plus code reading without first checking whether an existing bead already contained the answer. 587 open beads exist; `bd list` silently caps its output (returned 50 of 1,234 records), so a survey that trusts its default limit sees 4% of the backlog and reads as exhaustive. Query the exported .beads/issues.jsonl directly rather than the CLI default.

The rest of this bead's analysis is unaffected: the FK/CASCADE structural-impossibility case for orphaned_messages and orphaned_attachments stands on schema evidence, and the session_timestamp_backfill growth finding (1,117 -> 5,382) stands on measurement.
VERIFICATION (group3 sweep): LIVE. This bead's own most recent note (2026-07-29/30) revised its own initial verdict: empty_sessions repair target is NOT safe to cull (would delete the 832 genuinely-empty sessions ne6k deliberately retains) -- explicitly blocked on ne6k decision. orphaned_messages/orphaned_attachments FK-impossibility case and session_timestamp_backfill growth finding stand. This is an open decision-and-cull task, not stale; git log shows only a beads-note commit (32266aff7), no implementation commit.
EXECUTION RECIPE for the safe subset (iteration 6; small-model-grade): (1) delete repair_orphaned_messages + repair_orphaned_attachments functions, their REPAIR_HANDLERS/SAFE_REPAIR_TARGETS/PREVIEW_HANDLERS entries (repair.py:7202 region), their tests, and any CLI help text naming them — justification is schema evidence already in this bead (NOT NULL + ON DELETE CASCADE makes the states unrepresentable; live violation count 0). (2) DO NOT touch empty_sessions (ne6k: would delete 832 deliberately-retained sessions — blocked, needs that decision first). (3) session_insights target: deletable only with a convergence-parity proof (automagic ruling; convergence registers an insights stage — prove the daemon path covers what repair_session_insights does, record it, then delete). (4) POST-DRAIN REWRITE BOUNDARY (radical-replacement candidate from the dissection): after the lb39z/lkrc drain + 1fijp, the surviving repair surface is approximately: message_type_backfill (verify spent — it was a one-time shape fix), orphaned_blobs (belongs to blob_gc's domain — move or delete), superseded_raw_snapshots (belongs to raw_retention's domain — move), empty_sessions (ne6k decision). Target: repair.py under ~500 lines or gone entirely with survivors relocated to their owning modules. Falsification for (1): FK pragma check + insert-attempt test proving the states cannot exist.

2026-08-03 cross-check against the live raw-authority convergence work (lb39z), prompted by an operator concern that this whole area risks being "repair with an audit trail" instead of real invariants: examined lb39z's actual landed/planned items and the picture is mixed, not uniformly bad --

GOOD (matches invariants-by-construction): item 1 (PR #3574) fixed the classifier's own bug that was wholesale-quarantining byte-identical duplicates and shared-root forks ("any size tie or unique-chain failure quarantines everyone") -- this is a root-cause detection fix, not a repair actuator. Item 4 (PR #3588) added BOTH a constructor-level invariant (RawAuthorityFrontierItem.__post_init__ raises if an actuator/state pairing isn't executable) AND a static AST-based lint (devtools lab policy raw-authority-frontier-executability) that fails CI if a future pairing becomes unreachable -- structural prevention, not runtime cleanup. Item 5's proposed design (_maximal_evidence_fallback wiring) is explicitly guarded to be structurally incapable of ever retiring an accepted head "by construction, not by a runtime check that could be bypassed" -- also invariant-shaped.

MORE REPAIR-SHAPED BUT DEFENSIBLE AS ONE-TIME: items 2 and 3 (write-back / append-chain-backfill actuators) apply corrected classification retroactively to rows that were already wrongly quarantined BY THE NOW-FIXED bug -- this is a one-time backfill of historical damage from a bug that's since been root-caused, analogous to a data migration after a fixed logic error, not permanent repair machinery, PROVIDED it actually runs once against the live archive and then goes away.

THE ACTUAL RISK, which is exactly this bead's subject: whether these actuators (and the ~20 others in repair.py) get DELETED after their one-time live drain, or linger as permanent REPAIR_HANDLERS entries "just in case." Recommend this bead's AC explicitly require: for every raw-authority actuator lb39z/hjpx/yla8 land and run live, confirm it is removed from repair.py / the maintenance target catalog in the SAME PR that runs its final live application (or immediately after, once the drain is confirmed complete) -- not left registered as a standing manual surface. This is the concrete, checkable version of "prove drain-then-delete actually happens" rather than trusting the ratio measurement alone.
Promoted P0 2026-08-03: this bead already argues the exact direction the operator just mandated (10,164 lines repair/maintenance vs 2,665 lines daemon convergence, 3.8:1 ratio, citing project's own no-break-glass-tier doctrine). Now the vehicle for executing that mandate. Sequencing: polylogue-lkrc's one-time census+physical-sort pass must land FIRST (the fragmented raw-authority tables are still actively referenced per lr6dx's finding, not yet safe to delete) -- this bead's actual deletion work follows lkrc, not in parallel with it.
STALE-NOTE CORRECTION 2026-08-04: this bead's own prior note said 'polylogue-lkrc's one-time census+physical-sort pass must land FIRST' — lkrc's OWN most recent note (2026-08-03, operator pushback) retracted the physical-sort framing entirely ('dropped the physically sort blobs into labeled folders framing... categorize + prevent recurrence, not build a folder taxonomy'). Corrected sequencing: lkrc's actual current scope is (1) re-run the already-fixed classifiers (omsw artifact taxonomy, 1fijp admission arms) against the existing quarantined backlog once so most auto-resolve, (2) whatever doesn't cleanly resolve stays flagged/quarantined evidence with no folder invented, (3) rrxe4 (test-suite-as-integrity-checker) is the ONGOING check that the quarantine bucket doesn't regrow — explicitly NOT a standing repair mechanism. This bead's own goal (delete repair.py surface once its premise is gone) is fully compatible with that framing: lkrc's one-time reclassification pass still lands first (there is real existing damage to clear), but it is a throwaway operation/actuator run, not new permanent product code — nothing about it argues for building a unified RawAuthorityReconciler class as durable infrastructure. Operator directive (2026-08-04): the codebase should get simpler after blobstore-pristine, never gain a bigger unified repair abstraction as the vehicle for getting there.

title: 21% of index sessions are metadata sidecars materialized as conversations (agent-*.meta, toolu_*, wf_*)
description:
## What the data shows

Classifying every `claude-code-session` session_id in the live index by the shape
of its native_id:

     8,586  (52.6%)  parent:agent-*   real subagent transcripts
     4,945  (30.3%)  <agent>.meta     SIDECAR METADATA, not a conversation
     2,762  (16.9%)  uuid             real top-level sessions
         7            wf_*            workflow ids
         3            toolu_*         TOOL-USE ids
        16,312 total

Content of the suspicious classes:

    .meta    4,945 sessions   0 with messages   4,286 with events
    toolu_       3 sessions   0 with messages       0 with events
    wf_          7 sessions   0 with messages       0 with events

The `.meta` rows originate from
`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` --
a per-subagent metadata sidecar. 5,053 raws come from `*.meta.json` paths.

**The real subagent transcript is separately and correctly ingested.** Sampled
300 `.meta` sessions and looked for the corresponding `%:agent-<id>` session:
300 of 300 found. So these are not the only record of anything; they are
duplicate phantom rows standing beside the real session.

Net effect: 4,945 of 23,230 index sessions -- **21% of the archive's session
count** -- are metadata sidecars materialized as conversations.

## Why this matters beyond a wrong count

This is the same pathology as the hook-event inflation already fixed once
(83,286 -> 18,391 sessions, `write_hook_event`, PR #3265): a per-session sidecar
record ingested as a standalone session. A different sidecar type, the identical
bug class, and it survived that repair because the fix was specific to hook
events rather than to the category.

Consequences that are not merely cosmetic:

- Every per-session aggregate -- counts, cost rollups, activity timelines,
  "how many sessions did I have" -- is inflated by 21% for claude-code.
- 659 of them carry neither messages nor events, so they are pure empty rows.
- Search and read surfaces can return a `.meta` session that has no content to
  show.
- `toolu_*` sessions mean a TOOL-USE id was promoted to a session identity,
  which indicates identity derivation falling back to whatever id it found
  rather than failing loudly.

## Hypothesis for the mechanism (needs confirming before fixing)

Provider detection / payload lowering treats any JSON document under a
`subagents/` directory as a session-bearing payload, so a `.meta.json` sidecar
is lowered into a `LoweredPayloadSpec` and parsed. `provider_session_id` then
falls back to the filename stem (`agent-<id>.meta`), producing a well-formed but
meaningless identity. The `toolu_*` and `wf_*` cases look like the same fallback
picking up whichever id field is present in a fragment.

That should be verified in `sources/dispatch.py` and the Claude Code parser
before any fix -- the shape above is inference from the data, not yet traced in
code.

## Direction

Two candidate fixes, and the second is the one that matches
`polylogue-aggz`'s spirit:

1. Narrow: skip `*.meta.json` under `subagents/`, and attach its content to the
   subagent session it describes rather than to a session of its own.
2. Structural: a payload may only become a session when it yields a session
   identity the PROVIDER asserted. A filename-derived or fragment-derived
   fallback identity should be a parse refusal, not a session. That kills
   `.meta`, `toolu_*` and `wf_*` in one rule, and prevents the next sidecar
   format from doing this again -- which is exactly what the hook-event fix
   failed to do.

Prefer (2), with (1) only if (2) proves too broad. Under (2) this stops being a
category anyone has to remember.

## Acceptance criteria

- No session exists whose identity was derived from a filename stem or a
  non-session fragment id.
- The metadata carried by `*.meta.json` is still retained and attached to the
  subagent session it describes -- this must not become data loss.
- Sampled `.meta` ids resolve to their real `%:agent-<id>` session, which keeps
  its content.
- claude-code session count drops by roughly 4,945; verify against
  `.agent/scripts/corpus-fidelity-audit.py` that absences do NOT rise, i.e. that
  nothing real was removed.
- Anti-vacuity: state the production line mutated and the resulting failure.

Ref polylogue-aggz
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03): PREMISE HALF-STALE — the code fix is fully merged (PR #3403 / 299523de1, "refuse to synthesize session identity from unasserted ids", the structural option-2 the description prefers; source comment cites this bead). The phantom rows persist live only because no rebuild has run (verified 2026-07-31: 4,945 `%.meta` sessions still present). This bead is now purely a POST-REINDEX VERIFICATION item riding 818fy (correctly wired: blocked-by 818fy).

REMAINING WORK = verification after the rebuild, no new code:
1. Post-rebuild count check: `sqlite3 'file:/realm/db/polylogue/index.db?mode=ro' "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE session_id LIKE 'claude-code-session:%.meta'"` == 0; same for toolu_*/wf_* shapes.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
## Traced mechanism (not the original hypothesis)

The original hypothesis ("provider detection treats any JSON under
subagents/ as session-bearing, provider_session_id falls back to the
filename stem") was PARTLY wrong and PARTLY right, in a way that matters.

**Live daemon ingest path (sources/live/batch.py + pipeline/services/
ingest_worker.py) already refuses this correctly**, and has since well
before this session (classify_artifact_path's agent-*.meta.json branch
dates to 82fc0e4ff2, 2026-03-27; the OriginSpec artifact_rule_for_path
route that shadows it is newer but agrees). Proved empirically: built a
throwaway archive and ingested 9 REAL files pulled from
~/.claude/projects (1 top-level session, 3 real agent-*.jsonl subagent
transcripts, 4 real agent-*.meta.json sidecars, 1 standalone
meta+transcript pair) through LiveBatchProcessor (same primitives
polylogued run wires up) -- result: exactly 5 real sessions, 0 phantom
`.meta` rows.

**The actual live bug is a second, separate parse chokepoint**:
`sources/revision_backfill.py` (`_parse_one`/`_parse_stream`, driving
`polylogue ops reset --index` / the offline rebuild-index path via
`backfill_historical_revision_evidence`) calls
`dispatch.parse_payload`/`parse_stream_payload` on every retained raw
UNCONDITIONALLY -- no OriginSpec/artifact-taxonomy gate at all. Reproduced
live: rebuilding an index from the same 9-file real corpus through this
path (bypassing the daemon) produced 9 sessions, 4 of them phantom
`claude-code-session:agent-<id>.meta` rows with 0 messages/0 events --
the EXACT reported shape. `fallback_id = Path(source_path).stem` on
`agent-<id>.meta.json` strips only the trailing `.json`, leaving
`agent-<id>.meta` -- literally the observed native_id.

This means the bead's suggested remediation ("index.db is rebuildable,
prefer a rebuild") would have RECREATED the defect it was meant to fix,
not eliminated it -- this is now fixed (see below), so the plan below is
safe.

A structural gap also existed independent of both mechanisms:
`dispatch.py:_generic_messages_session` (the one payload-lowering branch
with zero provider-specific identity handling, reached both by genuinely
unknown providers and by the Drive-like generic fallback) fell back to
`fallback_id` -- a filename stem the *source-discovery walk* invented --
whenever a payload had a `messages` list but no `id` field. Didn't
reproduce with real `.meta.json`/`toolu_*`/`wf_*` fixtures (those are
covered by the OriginSpec/artifact-taxonomy path rules), but is exactly
the "next sidecar format" risk the bead is about, and closing it is what
implements the structural rule generically rather than per-shape.

## Fixes shipped (PR, branch feature/fix/provider-asserted-session-identity)

1. `polylogue/sources/dispatch.py`: `_generic_messages_session` now
   requires the payload to assert its own `id`; absent that it refuses to
   parse (returns None) instead of synthesizing an identity from
   `fallback_id`.
2. `polylogue/sources/revision_backfill.py`: `_parse_one`/`_parse_stream`
   now consult `artifact_rule_for_path` (same OriginSpec table batch.py
   already uses) and refuse to parse (return `[]`) when the declared
   artifact's `parse_policy` isn't `"session"`. One rule table, enforced
   at both entry points -- a rebuild and a live ingest now agree.

Both fixes proven with:
- Unit regression tests
  (`tests/unit/sources/test_source_laws.py::test_parse_payload_generic_messages_without_asserted_id_refuses_to_parse`,
  `tests/unit/sources/test_revision_backfill.py::test_parse_one_refuses_declared_fact_artifacts`)
  that fail before the fix and pass after (anti-vacuity verified by
  reverting each fix in isolation and re-running).
- The real 9-file fixture-corpus rebuild: 9 sessions / 4 phantom before
  fix #2, 5 sessions / 0 phantom after, with the 3 real subagent
  transcripts' message counts (96, 120, 164, 31... unaffected across the
  run) identical in both states -- no data loss to real content.
- `devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_source_laws.py
  tests/unit/sources/test_revision_backfill.py` -- 180 passed.

## AC: metadata retention (not data loss)

Already satisfied by existing, pre-existing code, unaffected by this fix:
`insights/claude_workflow_materializer.py` +
`insights/claude_workflow_evidence.py` read `agent_sidecar_meta` facts
from retained raw bytes (independent of whether a `sessions` row exists)
and materialize them into the `claude-workflow:*` work-evidence graph
(run/invocation/attempt nodes with sidecar-meta claims attached). This
fix only removes the DUPLICATE phantom `sessions` row; the raw bytes stay
in `raw_sessions` (admitted as "fact" artifacts) and the metadata content
keeps flowing into that graph exactly as before.

## `toolu_*` / `wf_*` (10 rows total, not separately reproduced)

`wf_*` (workflow_run_snapshot, `.json`) is covered by the same
OriginSpec-declared-fact gate as `.meta.json` -- fix #2 covers it
structurally, same mechanism.

`toolu_*` (3 rows) could not be reproduced with real fixture data: real
`tool-results/*.txt` sidecars are excluded from the live discovery walk
by suffix filtering (`artifact_suffixes_for_provider` only allows
`.json`/`.jsonl`/`.ndjson` for claude-code) and are NOT declared in
OriginSpec at all, so if a `raw_sessions` row for one of these 3 exists
in the live archive it's very likely a relic of an older
acquisition-scope bug already superseded by that suffix filtering. Given
there are only 3 (vs 4,945 `.meta`), recommend: after the rebuild below,
check whether they're gone; if any survive, file a narrow follow-up bead
with their actual `source_path`/payload shape rather than guessing
further blind.

## Verified live-data remediation procedure

index.db is the rebuildable tier; source.db (raw bytes) is durable and
untouched by this fix. With both fixes merged and deployed:

1. Stop anything writing to the live archive (already stopped per the
   session's safety rule).
2. `polylogue ops reset --index` -- wipes only the index tier (new
   generation), source.db/user.db/ops.db untouched.
3. `polylogued run` (or the offline `devtools`/maintenance rebuild-index
   path) -- replays EVERY `raw_sessions` row from source.db through the
   now-fixed `revision_backfill.py` path. Verified there is no
   `parsed_at_ms`-style skip: `all_index_rebuild_raw_ids` selects every
   raw unconditionally and `RebuildIndexRequest(only_missing=False)`
   forces a full non-incremental replay; content-hash idempotency only
   skips re-writing a session that ALREADY EXISTS in the target, which is
   moot against a freshly wiped, empty index.db. So no additional
   durable-tier invalidation beyond the code fix is needed -- the raws
   ARE the source of truth and will now be reparsed correctly.
4. Verify with `.agent/scripts/corpus-fidelity-audit.py` (or equivalent
   session-count query) that: claude-code session count drops by
   approximately 4,945+7(+ up to 3), absences do NOT rise (nothing real
   removed), and the 300-sample `.meta -> %:agent-<id>` resolution check
   from the original investigation still resolves (the real subagent
   sessions are untouched by this fix -- it only removes the duplicate).

Not run against the live archive per the session's explicit
instruction -- this is the procedure to execute, not evidence that it was
executed.

title: Collapse the failure taxonomy into three invariants that make the cases unrepresentable
description:
## The problem with the current shape

One day of investigation produced eleven separately-named defects and found four
existing special-case code paths. That is a taxonomy, not an architecture. Every
new provider quirk becomes another named category, another branch, another bead,
and the system's correctness becomes a function of how many cases someone
remembered. The goal is the opposite: make these failures unrepresentable, so
they are not known as anything at all.

Almost all of it collapses into three invariants.

## Invariant 1 -- comparison identity contains only content

**A conversation is a SET of messages keyed by stable provider identity, each
carrying only content-bearing fields. Nothing else may enter the value used to
compare two acquisitions of it.**

Collapses, as consequences rather than cases:

- polylogue-bu1i (attachment acquisition state in attachment identity) --
  acquisition state is not content.
- polylogue-c429 (message array order) -- a set has no order.
- polylogue-nuec (chatgpt elapsed_duration_ms) -- a measurement is not content.
- polylogue-hith (synthetic attachment id seeded on position) -- position is not
  identity.
- polylogue-d8al (real-id presence varies between vintages) -- identity must be
  derivable from content when the provider omits its own.
- polylogue-oycw (positional-prefix superset test) -- set containment, not
  sequence prefix.
- `_provider_ordered_browser_snapshots` -- exists only because DOM ordering
  differs from export ordering. Under a set, it has nothing to fix.
- The `superseded_prefix` / `superseded_equivalent` distinction -- both are just
  "contained or equal".

Superset-ness becomes total and decidable, with no residual category:

    equal       same id set, equal content per id
    contains    A's id set contains B's, equal content on the intersection
    conflict    content differs on the intersection

Ordering remains a stored, rendered property of a session. The claim is only
that it is not part of the comparison value. `_direct_export_precedence` (a real
export outranks a browser capture) probably survives as a genuine provenance
rule rather than a repair.

## Invariant 2 -- one chokepoint may write a session

**It must be structurally impossible to materialize a session without consulting
revision authority.**

polylogue-c737, PR #3397 and PR #3398 all exist because two write paths each
carried their own precedence logic, and one of them forgot. #3398 then had to
correct #3397's scope on one path while the other stayed wrong, which is the
signature of duplicated semantics rather than a missing check.

The fix is structural, not another check: one function through which every
session write passes, taking authority as a required argument, so a caller
cannot forget to ask. A predicate copied into two places is a bug that has not
happened yet.

## Invariant 3 -- derived state carries the version of the logic that derived it

**Any stored conclusion records which version of which computation produced it,
so a corrected computation invalidates its own stale outputs automatically.**

polylogue-9dxn is this, and its absence is what made polylogue-bu1i inert on
existing data: a persisted `ambiguous` verdict has no version, so a corrected
classifier cannot know which verdicts it now disagrees with. The two-component
design already recorded on 9dxn (separate identity and classification
fingerprints) is the mechanism.

With this, "stale verdict", "needs re-census", and "the fix does not apply to
existing rows" all stop being categories. Correction becomes self-healing by
construction.

## What this does to the current bead set

Reframe rather than close -- the individual fixes still ship, but as instances:

    bu1i c429 nuec hith d8al oycw        -> Invariant 1
    c737 (+ the shape behind #3397/#3398) -> Invariant 2
    9dxn                                  -> Invariant 3
    ck5v                                  -> not covered; genuinely separate
                                             (backfill coupled to acquisition
                                             route -- an availability rule, not
                                             an identity one)
    ey3r                                  -> a measurement defect, but its cause
                                             is Invariant 1: it counts
                                             `superseded_*` as missing because
                                             the vocabulary has redundant
                                             categories that Invariant 1 removes

## How to tell whether this worked

Not "the tests pass". The observable is that the vocabulary shrinks:

- The membership decision vocabulary loses `superseded_prefix` as distinct from
  `superseded_equivalent`.
- `_provider_ordered_browser_snapshots` is deleted rather than maintained.
- `HISTORICAL_NON_PREFIX_GOVERNANCE_DETAIL` and its legacy-detail variants stop
  needing to exist, because non-prefix growth stops being exceptional.
- No new provider quirk requires a new branch in the classifier.

If a change adds a case instead of removing one, it is going the wrong way even
if it makes a test pass. Per this repo's own surgical-renewal rule, the old path
is deleted in the same change that replaces it -- these special cases must not
survive as dead alternates beside the invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- The comparison value for a session is constructed from an explicit
  content-only allowlist, so adding a field to a parser cannot silently enter
  identity. Adding a volatile field and observing that comparison is unaffected
  is the test.
- Exactly one code path can write a session, and it cannot be called without
  authority.
- Every stored verdict carries a version; changing the logic invalidates the
  affected verdicts without an operator command.
- At least two existing special-case paths are DELETED, not merely bypassed.
notes:
VERIFICATION (group3 sweep): PARTIAL. Invariant 1 (comparison identity contains only content) substantially landed: PR #3401 'refactor(archive): collapse revision comparison into a content-only relation' (merged 2026-07-30T15:55) + PR #3405 'refactor(pipeline): route comparison identity through typed constructors' (merged 2026-07-30T17:50), both confirmed MERGED via gh pr view. PR bodies explicitly state deferred residuals within Invariant 1 itself: _maximal_evidence_fallback designed/tested but NOT wired (blocked on archive.py write-back invariant), _provider_ordered_browser_snapshots kept not deleted, 49 residual ambiguous cohorts unresolved. Invariant 2 (single write chokepoint) and Invariant 3 (versioned derived state) are EXPLICITLY stated as out of scope / not addressed in both PR bodies -- completely unstarted. This is a 3-invariant bead with 1 of 3 partially done; do not close. If the landing-check tool flagged this as stale off PR #3401/#3405 landing, that verdict is WRONG for the whole bead -- only ~1/3 of the AC surface is touched.
RECONCILIATION 2026-07-31: corroborates the bead's own 2026-07-30 PARTIAL verdict, independently re-verified. Confirmed PR #3401/#3405 merged and their Invariant-1 implementation (_axis_relation in session_revision_membership.py, set-based identity+content comparison) is real and live on origin/master. Invariant 2 (single write chokepoint) and Invariant 3 (versioned derived state / polylogue-9dxn) confirmed still untouched — no PR found addressing either. GENUINELY OPEN, 1 of 3 invariants landed. No change to prior verdict; do not close.
Dissection 2026-08-03 pricing (report /realm/data/derived/reports/polylogue-structural-dissection-2026-08-03.html): Invariant 2 (single write chokepoint with acquire-time authority resolution) is the highest-mass root reversal in the codebase — ~40K lines downstream (15,815 named-file prod + 87% of repair.py's function lines + 15,454 tests + 3,707 devtools proofs + 7 source.db tables). Live: 52% of raw_sessions quarantined (22,470 rows / 63.3GB). Sequencing: after 818fy reindex + lb39z/lkrc drain; the acquire path must read source files atomically (2t0vp mid-rewrite shape) or it recreates quarantine under another name. I1 is ~1/3 landed (#3401/#3405); I2/I3 unstarted.
OPERATOR REFRAMING 2026-08-03 (threat model): most of source.db is a CACHE of data still present at origin (~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions are not rotated; 25GB codex rollouts live on disk). Genuinely irreplaceable: browser-captured web chats, file states later truncated upstream (2t0vp mid-rewrite shape), user.db. Consequence for I2's design: 're-acquire on doubt' is a legitimate resolution arm alongside append/skip/supersede/refuse — the chokepoint may resolve ambiguity by re-reading the source instead of durably recording an ambiguous observation. This weakens the case for elaborate in-archive authority reconstruction further. ALSO (sequencing doctrine, operator-endorsed): aggz I1/I2 are the BATCH fix for most K/S-class reindex gates (vintage-volatile comparison axes and positional identity are I1's unrepresentability targets; side-door durable writes are I2's) — prefer landing the invariant over per-gate symptom fixes where the invariant is close.
close_reason: Invariant 2 (single session-write chokepoint) landed via PR #3505. Coordinator's grep hint was wrong (revision_governance.py vs archive.py is a legit already-extracted delegation, not duplication) — the lane found the REAL duplication instead: revision_governance.py's _write_parsed_precedence_result vs pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py's _write_session both independently hand-carried identical refusal logic (the exact shape PR #3397 fixed once and #3398 had to separately re-derive). Consolidated into one function revision_authority_refuses_write in storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/ingest_precedence.py; both write paths call it; duplicated inline blocks deleted. Anti-vacuity verified (mutation to if False: failed both regression tests). 127 tests passed, verify --quick green. Residual: full write-path merge (larger/riskier, deferred) and a third dead-in-production path (ArchiveStore.write_parsed/SessionRepository.save_parsed_session, zero authority consultation, no real caller today) flagged for a follow-up bead.

title: Coalescing rests on a positional-prefix superset test that real providers violate; 41% of the corpus depends on it
description:
## Scale first: this is the archive's normal condition, not an edge case

    logical identities with more than one raw   7,440
    total logical identities                   18,228
    -> 41% of the corpus is multi-raw

Cohort sizes by origin (raws in multi-member cohorts):

    chatgpt-export      3-member 5,817   4-member 551   +tail to 12
    claude-ai-export    4-member 3,592   3-member 258   +tail to 9
    codex-session       2-member 3,544   ... one cohort of 105
    claude-code-session 2-member 2,338   3-member 663   +tail to 25
    hermes-session      2-member 536
    aistudio-drive      2-member 302
    antigravity-session 2-member 232
    browser-capture raws            887  (786 chatgpt, 47 claude-ai, 38 unknown, 16 grok)

Correctness for nearly half the archive rests on the revision-arbitration layer.
It is not a rarely-exercised safety net.

## Where the multiplicity comes from

Not divergence. Repeated whole-account acquisition:

    claude-ai-data-2025-10-04    906 raws
    claude-ai-data-2026-04-23    973 raws
    claude-ai-data-2026-06-14  1,998 raws
    chatgpt-data-2025-10-20    2,072 raws
    chatgpt-data-2026-04-23    4,805 raws

Every GDPR export contains every conversation, so each conversation enters the
archive once per export vintage. 577 of the 587 claude-ai ambiguous cohorts have
exactly 4 members for this reason.

## Layer 1 -- identity. This one is sound.

`sessions.session_id` is a generated column, `origin || ':' || native_id`, where
`native_id` is the parser's `provider_session_id` -- the provider's own
conversation uuid. Measured: 34 of 35 sampled claude-ai cohorts have an
IDENTICAL provider_message_id set across all members, and the conversation uuid
is identical across all four export vintages.

Session identity is stable across acquisitions. The failures found on
2026-07-30 were narrower and are separately tracked: a dispatch bug appending a
spurious `-0` (fixed 2026-07-20, polylogue-eqnv), and unstable synthetic
*attachment* ids (polylogue-hith / polylogue-d8al) -- not session ids.

**Identity is not the problem, and a fix aimed at identity will not help.**

## Layer 2 -- coalescing. Two mechanisms that do not compose.

**(a) Content-hash idempotency** (`pipeline/ids.py:session_content_hash`).
Re-ingest with a matching hash is skipped. The hash deliberately excludes user
metadata, but it INCLUDES: message array order, attachment acquisition state,
volatile provider metadata, and synthetic ids. Across two exports of an
unchanged conversation, at least one of those always differs.

So idempotency never fires across export vintages -- by construction, not by
accident. Every re-export falls through to (b).

**(b) Revision membership arbitration.** Decides which raw is authoritative for
a session id when hashes differ. This carries the entire load that (a) fails to
absorb, for 41% of the corpus.

## Layer 3 -- superset determination. This is the actual defect.

`_strictly_dominates` (`archive/session_revision_membership.py`) requires:

    older.message_hashes == newer.message_hashes[: len(older.message_hashes)]

a POSITIONAL PREFIX. Three assumptions are embedded there, and all three are
violated by real providers:

1. *Messages keep a stable order across acquisitions.* Violated: 19 of 35
   sampled claude-ai cohorts differ only in array order, same ids, zero content
   differences. Claude.ai does not emit a stable sequence between exports.
2. *A message's hash is a function of its content alone.* Violated by volatile
   provider metadata (chatgpt `elapsed_duration_ms`, polylogue-nuec) and by
   acquisition state (Drive attachment bytes, polylogue-bu1i).
3. *Growth is append-only at the tail.* Violated whenever a provider edits or
   inserts mid-conversation, and structurally by browser-capture DOM snapshots.

When the test fails in both directions the cohort is quarantined ambiguous and
NOTHING is indexed -- so a conversation held complete, correct, and in four
identical copies is absent from the archive. That is the 1,009-1,027 absence
population.

## What the correct test looks like

Per-message ids are stable (34/35 measured), so superset-ness is decidable on
evidence we already hold, without ordering:

    equal      same provider_message_id SET, equal content per id
               -> semantically the same revision; `equivalent_raw_ids`,
                  no arbitration needed at all
    dominates  A's id set strictly contains B's, content equal on the
               intersection  -> A is authoritative
    fork       neither contains the other, OR content differs on the
               intersection -> genuinely ambiguous, and rare
               (0 of 35 sampled claude-ai; 1 plausible case archive-wide,
                in grok-export)

Ordering remains a real property of a session and must still be stored and
rendered -- the claim is only that ordering must not be the DOMINANCE key.
A conversation is a set of identified messages plus an ordering; which evidence
exists is a set question, and treating the sequence as identity makes every
provider-side reordering look like divergence.

Likewise a message's identity for comparison must exclude provider-volatile
measurement fields and acquisition state, for the same reason bu1i split
attachment identity from attachment acquisition.

## Browser capture

887 raws, 786 of them chatgpt. A DOM snapshot legitimately carries different
synthetic ids and a different ordering from the same conversation's export, so
it violates assumptions 1 and 3 by design. `_provider_ordered_browser_snapshots`
and `_direct_export_precedence` exist to special-case it, which is evidence that
the general test was already known to be too strict -- the special cases are
patches over the wrong primitive rather than genuine domain rules. Re-evaluate
both once the set-based test lands; `_direct_export_precedence` (a real export
outranks a browser capture) is probably a genuine rule worth keeping, while the
ordering special-case may become unnecessary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Superset determination is order-independent and decided on stable per-message
  identity plus per-id content equality.
- Equal-content cohorts resolve as `equivalent`, not `ambiguous`, and index one
  member -- no arbitration for the 34/35 case.
- Message comparison identity excludes provider-volatile measurement fields and
  acquisition state.
- Report how many cohorts still reach a genuine-fork verdict; it should be very
  small, and a large number means one of the above is wrong.
- Re-run `.agent/scripts/corpus-fidelity-audit.py`: absent_documents must fall
  to approximately zero from the 1,027 baseline.

Ref polylogue-bu1i, polylogue-c429, polylogue-nuec, polylogue-d8al, polylogue-f1vg
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (verified 2026-07-31): the core defect this bead describes
-- superset determination resting on a positional-prefix message-array test
-- is ALREADY FIXED, by #3401/#3405 (polylogue-aggz), merged ~1h15m after
this bead was filed the same day. Read current
archive/session_revision_membership.py + pipeline/ids.py directly: there is
no positional-prefix test anywhere in the current code. `_relation`/
`_axis_relation` compare messages/attachments/events as sets keyed by
content-derived identity (never array position, never a provider id whose
presence is unstable), with per-id content equality on the intersection --
exactly this bead's "what the correct test looks like" section, already
implemented.

AC verification:

1. Order-independent, per-message identity + per-id content equality: YES.
   `message_identity_hash(id=...)` keyed only on provider message id;

2. Equal-content cohorts -> equivalent, one member indexed: YES. First pass

     chatgpt-export:      125/136 (91.9%) resolve; 10/136 (7.4%) conflict

   upstream in session identity/lineage assignment, not in this module.
   Filed as polylogue-jc4q, out of scope for this bead.
   Traced the two small residual classes to real, NEW causes (follow-ups,
   not this bead's ask): polylogue-uqwd (ChatGPT generation_lifecycle
   events anchoring to a different message id across export vintages --
   extends nuec's fix to the anchor field, not just payload) and

5. corpus-fidelity-audit.py, run read-only against the LIVE archive (still

   bead targets (585 claude-ai-export, 173 claude-code-session, 135
   chatgpt-export, small tail). The reparse simulation shows most of the
   claude-ai/chatgpt share (718 cohorts) will resolve on rebuild; the
   claude-code-session share (173) mostly will not, per point 4.
   "Approximately zero" is optimistic for the full corpus, roughly right

CRITICAL CASE (never coerce genuine divergence into supersession): verified
correct. `_relation` returns `conflict` when content differs on a shared id,

Every write path consults this relation, not just one: `should_skip_stale_

title: Corpus acceptance gate: no absences and maximum fidelity, with the 2026-07-30 frozen baseline
description:
## What the operator asked for

"Ensure max fidelity as well as no absences, through the entire corpus." That is
a stronger bar than any existing check enforces, and nothing measured either
half until now.

## Why the existing checks cannot serve

`verify-archive`'s `source-index-coverage` counts superseded revisions as
missing work (polylogue-ey3r), so it cannot reach zero on any archive that ever
ingested a conversation twice, and therefore cannot gate a rebuild. Nothing at
all measures fidelity: an archive can report perfect coverage while every
attachment whose bytes it holds is recorded `unfetched`, which is precisely the
state measured on 2026-07-30.

## The gate

`.agent/scripts/corpus-fidelity-audit.py` (read-only, `mode=ro` throughout,
exits 1 on failure so it can gate a rebuild). Three measures:

1. **Absences** -- logical documents (origin + provider_session_id) the archive
   holds evidence for but does not surface, bucketed by cause so a fix's effect
   is attributable rather than a single number moving for unknown reasons.
2. **Attachment fidelity** -- acquired vs not-acquired refs, split by origin and
   upload_origin, because a Drive-hosted reference never fetched is actionable
   while a genuinely byte-less attachment kind is not.
3. **Revision fidelity** -- documents whose indexed evidence is smaller than the
   largest revision recorded for them.

## Baseline, live archive frozen 2026-07-30 (daemon stopped)

    ABSENCES  1,009 of 18,248 known documents
         587  claude-ai-export/ambiguous-only
         184  claude-code-session/ambiguous-only
         135  chatgpt-export/ambiguous-only
          71  aistudio-drive/settled-yet-absent
          20  unknown-export/settled-yet-absent
          12  gemini-cli / hermes / unknown / grok / codex

    ATTACHMENT FIDELITY  acquired=2,118  not-acquired=7,655
        3,684  chatgpt-export/oauth/unfetched
        2,391  chatgpt-export/<none>/unfetched
        1,975  aistudio-drive/drive/acquired
        1,119  aistudio-drive/drive/unfetched
          398  claude-ai-export/oauth/unfetched

    REVISION FIDELITY  94 documents below best recorded evidence
           76  hermes-session
           16  claude-code-session
            2  chatgpt-export

    VERDICT: FAIL

The `settled-yet-absent` buckets (71 drive, 20 unknown-export, 1 codex) are not
explained by any currently-tracked cause and want their own investigation --
these are documents with no ambiguous decision anywhere that are nonetheless
missing.

The 94 revision-fidelity documents are a residue after correcting a false
positive, and should be treated as a prompt to investigate rather than proof of
loss (see below).

## Measurement trap this already caught

The first version compared indexed *messages* against
`raw_session_memberships.message_count` and reported **474** shortfalls, 294 of
them codex-session. All false. `message_count` was recorded by whichever parser
censused that raw, and index v46 deliberately reclassified a large share of
Codex/Claude Code rows from chat turns into typed `session_events`. One codex
session read as "15 indexed vs 68,553 recorded" when it actually holds 15
messages plus 84,612 events. Counting `messages + session_events` drops the
figure to 94.

Anyone extending this must keep that in mind: cross-generation counts are only
approximately comparable, so a metric built on them needs its assumption stated
and checked against a real sample before its number is believed.

## Follow-up

Promote this into `devtools` as a first-class command with a `CommandSpec` (plus
`devtools render devtools-reference`) so it is an enforced gate rather than a
script, and wire it into the post-rebuild acceptance path alongside
`verify-archive`. Kept as a script for now because the fixes it measures are
still in flight and its thresholds will move as they land.

## Acceptance criteria

- Absences reach 0, or every residual is individually justified in writing.
- Attachment refs marked not-acquired are either acquired or shown to be
  genuinely unfetchable (deleted upstream, over the size cap, byte-less kind).
- Revision-fidelity residue is explained rather than merely small.
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03): the instrument exists (.agent/scripts/corpus-fidelity-audit.py, read-only, exit-1-gates); this bead's remaining work is (a) promotion into an enforced surface and (b) driving its three measures to an accountable PASS.

PROMOTION: lift the script into a devtools CommandSpec (devtools/command_catalog.py + devtools/<name>.py + `devtools render devtools-reference`) per the description's follow-up section — do this ONCE the in-flight fixes settle so thresholds stop moving. Per the 60gzo doctrine, its per-measure predicates should graduate into ARCHIVE_VERIFICATION_CHECKS (registry) so they run in both verification planes; the script's bucketed-by-cause reporting stays as the operator-facing wrapper. Wire into the 818fy post-rebuild acceptance path alongside verify-archive (818fy runbook step 6 already cites it).

CURRENT BASELINE MOVEMENT (2026-08-02 run): FAIL — 1,267 absent documents, 100 revision-shortfall sessions (fully explained: 76 hermes parser-staleness resolved by the reindex itself + quarantined claude-code cohorts resolved by the lb39z drain), 9,767 unacquired attachment refs. The blockers wired on this bead (4zqh3 hermes recovery, awy5 acquisition-failure representation, b4n2, yla8) are the fix lanes for the remaining buckets.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE (from the description's trap section, binding on any extension): cross-generation counts are only approximately comparable — any new metric must state its comparability assumption and check it against a real sample before its number is believed (the 474-vs-94 message_count false positive is the cautionary precedent).

SETTLED-YET-ABSENT: the 71 drive + 20 unknown-export + 1 codex settled-yet-absent documents have no tracked cause — that investigation is IN this bead's scope (it is the "no absences" half nobody else owns).
acceptance_criteria:
Formalizes the description's AC section with verify surfaces:
1. Absences == 0 in the corpus-fidelity audit, or every residual bucket individually justified in writing on this bead (incl. the settled-yet-absent 71 drive / 20 unknown-export / 1 codex investigation, which is in-scope here).
2. Every not-acquired attachment ref is either acquired or typed genuinely-unfetchable (deleted upstream / over size cap / byte-less kind) — bucketed by origin+upload_origin in the audit output.
3. Revision-fidelity residue explained, not merely small (hermes-76 resolves via reindex; quarantined cohorts via the lb39z drain — verify both post-818fy).
4. The audit is promoted from .agent/scripts/ to a devtools CommandSpec wired into the post-rebuild acceptance path, with its predicates graduated into ARCHIVE_VERIFICATION_CHECKS per 60gzo; devtools render devtools-reference clean.
5. Any metric extension states and sample-checks its cross-generation comparability assumption (the 474-vs-94 trap rule from the description).
notes:
