Priority raised P1->P0 to reflect that. Do not run the reindex until this gate passes clean or every remaining gap is explicitly operator-accepted.
2026-08-03 (reindex-gate-hunt task #14 Finding 1, adjudicated adds-evidence-to-f1vg): NAMED ABSENCE for the acceptance audit trail — 6 aistudio-drive raws parsed successfully (parsed_at set, validation passed, byte_proven, NOT quarantined) yet have ZERO raw_session_memberships rows and no index session; invisible to convergence_debt (which holds only 3 rows archive-wide, all unrelated FTS debt). raw_id prefixes: 0064ddd1, e43f60c2, e695ed20, d3ec6377, 77bd1e61, 14e203c9 — all /drive-cache/gemini/Implementing-<hash>.json, parsed within one 2.5s batch window 2026-07-30. Origin-wide only 24/397 aistudio-drive raws lack a membership row (narrow anomaly, not write-path-wide). Root cause deliberately UNRESOLVED (needs ingest_batch write-path code tracing) — this note exists so the zero-absences acceptance pass either explains these 6 or fails loudly. Context: 2 chatgpt raws initially co-flagged were ordinary pending backlog (11,026 decision-IS-NULL rows archive-wide); 1 was a p3b2-class superseded_equivalent false positive; both correctly dropped after raw_session_memberships rework.

title: ArchiveStore._write_parsed_precedence_result writes a session for a raw recorded raw_session_memberships.decision='ambiguous'
description:
## What the live archive shows (coordinator measurement, confirmed independently)

Live query against `/realm/db/polylogue` for `origin='aistudio-drive'`:
34 cohorts now have BOTH members parsed (growing over the course of one
session). 28 of those have `raw_session_memberships.decision='ambiguous'`
on BOTH members under the SAME `logical_source_key` -- genuinely arbitrated,
correctly refused a winner -- yet the cohort's session IS present in
index.db with zero acquired attachments: 641 attachments total across the
28, every one `unfetched`, while the enriched sibling in the blob store
holds the bytes.

## Root cause, traced and reproduced

`polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py`'s
`apply_raw_membership_classification` (the classify_membership_revisions
consumer) is innocent: for a fully-ambiguous cohort (no accepted_raw_ids)
it explicitly clears `raw_sessions.parsed_at_ms` and never writes to
`sessions` -- verified by reading its finalization block (`complete` check
at the end of the function, ~line 3873-3901).

The actual writer is `_write_parsed_precedence_result` (same file), reached
via `write_parsed_for_retained_raw`/`write_parsed_for_retained_raw_result`
with `revision_authoritative=False` (the default -- used by the one-shot
importer, `pipeline/services/archive_ingest.py`, and by
`_index_parsed_for_retained_raw`'s other non-membership-governed callers).
Its ONLY revision-authority awareness before this fix was:

    governed = SELECT 1 FROM raw_revision_heads WHERE session_id = ?
    if governed is not None: skip

`raw_revision_heads` is populated ONLY when a cohort has an ACCEPTED
winner. A cohort `classify_membership_revisions` genuinely refused to
arbitrate never gets an accepted head, so `governed` stays `None` and the
function falls through to its own browser-capture-precedence/freshness
logic and writes the session unconditionally on the raw's next reparse --
last-writer-wins, independent of the recorded `ambiguous` verdict.
`repair.py:1075`/`repair.py:4432-4462` (the two gates the investigation
started from) are both innocent: neither is on this write path at all --
`repair.py:4432` is a read-only reporting/accounting classifier
(`_raw_replay_plan_outcome`), and `repair.py:1075` is a narrow inspector
for a different (`source-v7`/`quarantined-accepted-raw`) repair scenario.

Reproduced directly: a synthetic archive with a raw whose
`raw_session_memberships` row is `decision='ambiguous'`, then calling
`archive.write_parsed_for_retained_raw(session, raw_id=..., ...)` (no
`revision_authoritative`) writes the session anyway pre-fix; the fix makes
it a no-op (`content_changed=False`).

## Fix landed in polylogue-af059's fast-follow PR

`_write_parsed_precedence_result` now also refuses when the raw's OWN
`raw_session_memberships.decision = 'ambiguous'`, in addition to the
existing `raw_revision_heads` check.

## Known sibling hole, NOT fixed here (different file, different owner)

`polylogue/pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py` (the daemon's default
batch-ingest write path, used for most origins that don't go through
`sources/live/batch.py`'s revision-authority-aware branch) has the SAME
shape: its own precedence/freshness logic, no `raw_session_memberships`
consultation. The coordinator's own measurement
(`revision_authority='quarantined'` with `parsed_at_ms` set: chatgpt-export
7,050, codex-session 3,633, claude-code-session 2,450, claude-ai-export
1,562 -- NOT all necessarily leaked materializations, but the same shape)
suggests this is where most of the non-drive volume would leak through, if
those origins' raws ever get genuinely `ambiguous`-recorded membership
decisions. Needs its own read-only census to confirm before fixing (not
done here -- out of file-ownership scope for this PR).

## Live remediation

NOT performed here (code-only fix). The 28 live aistudio-drive sessions
with zero-acquired attachments need their own re-materialization pass once
this fix (and bu1i's classifier fix) are both deployed.

Ref polylogue-eqnv, polylogue-bu1i, polylogue-7ilr, polylogue-9dxn
close_reason: Fixed in PR #3397 (feature/fix/ambiguous-membership-precedence-write-leak): ArchiveStore._write_parsed_precedence_result now also refuses to write when the raw's own raw_session_memberships.decision='ambiguous', alongside the pre-existing raw_revision_heads check. Verified with a regression test (anti-vacuity confirmed via temporary guard short-circuit + rerun). Sibling hole in pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py NOT fixed here (different file, out of ownership scope) -- needs its own read-only census before fixing; tracked as residual scope in this same bead's description.

title: rebuild parse workers capped at 8 on a 24-thread host; ingest_parse_workers config is inert
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by codebase audit, while checking whether the imminent full
rebuild honors its parse-worker configuration. TWO defects, one of which
directly caps rebuild throughput.

(1) THE PARSE-WORKER COUNT IS CAPPED AT 8 ON A 24-THREAD HOST

polylogue/pipeline/services/process_pool.py:52
    default = max(1, min(8, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 1))

On sinnix-prime (i7-13700K, 16 cores / 24 threads) this resolves to 8, leaving
16 threads idle. The rebuild path reaches it directly:
  maintenance/rebuild_index.py:543   ingest_workers=None
  maintenance/replay.py:199          resolved = ... else resolve_parse_worker_count()

The daemon now runs free-threaded 3.14t (GIL disabled) and the GIL parse path
was deleted this session, so thread-parallel parse is the only path -- the
`min(8, ...)` ceiling is the binding constraint on a rebuild we are trying to
bring from 9.2h down to 1-2h. The cap predates the free-threaded deploy; on a
GIL build 8 was a reasonable process-pool bound, but that reasoning no longer
applies.

BEFORE THE REBUILD: either raise/remove the cap, or set
POLYLOGUE_INGEST_PARSE_WORKERS explicitly for the rebuild run. Do NOT assume
higher is strictly better -- measure. Parse is decode-bound but the apply side
is a single writer, so beyond some width the writer becomes the bottleneck and
extra parse threads only add memory pressure. The new RebuildPassCost
instrumentation (replay_s / checkpoint_s / mib_per_s / parse_workers, landed
this session) is exactly the instrument for choosing the width from one short
measured pass rather than guessing.

(2) THE DOCUMENTED CONFIG KNOB IS INERT

There are two knobs for parse-worker count and only one works:
  env  POLYLOGUE_INGEST_PARSE_WORKERS   -- honored (process_pool.py:43,53)
  config `sources.ingest_parse_workers` -- IGNORED

The config property is defined (config.py:602), given a default
(config.py:1876), listed in the config inventory twice (config.py:1387,1642),
and documented (docs/configuration.md:351 "Parallel parse workers during
ingest (default 1)") -- but NOTHING reads it. An operator setting it in
~/.config/polylogue/polylogue.toml gets silence.

The doc is also wrong independently of the wiring: it says "default 1" while
the resolver's actual default is min(8, cpus-1) = 8 here.

FIX: make resolve_parse_worker_count read the resolved config, keeping the env
var as the override layer the config system already defines -- or delete the
config property and document the env var as the sole knob. Per the standing
directive, one of the two must go; a documented knob that does nothing is
worse than no knob. Whichever survives must be the one the rebuild reads.
close_reason: Fixed. Parse workers now scale to the interpreter: min(16, cpus-2) free-threaded, min(8, cpus-1) under the GIL. Verified under the deployed python3.14t -> 16 workers, up from 8 on this 24-thread host. The module's own control-run measurement (3.9x at w=4 rising to 9.6x at w=16) is the evidence for 16 as the ceiling. Second defect also fixed: the inert sources.ingest_parse_workers config property (defined, defaulted, inventoried twice, documented as 'default 1', read by nothing) is deleted; POLYLOGUE_INGEST_PARSE_WORKERS survives as the single knob with an accurate inventory description. Commit a7945e9fe. Related: the devshell default is now the free-threaded shell (matching the daemon), so local runs no longer silently parse sequentially.

title: Field-landing decisions for the unread-wire batch: one index bump, one rebuild
description:
DECIDED. The audit established WHAT is discarded; this fixes WHERE each lands, so the parser work is mechanical and the schema changes batch into a single index-tier bump rather than one per origin.

  stop_reason (608,608 on wire)
      -> column on messages. One value per assistant turn, low cardinality,
         feeds terminal_state directly. Replaces three columns that guess at it
         and are 85-99% 'unknown'.
  structuredPatch (105,123) + originalFile (92,313) + oldString/newString/filePath
      -> new file_edits table keyed by tool_use_block_id. It is a RELATION (one
         edit per tool call), not a block attribute. This is what raises
         polylogue-cijx's file-trajectory grading from 'observed' to
         'checkpointed' -- originalFile is the captured pre-state cijx declares
         unavailable.
  parentToolUseID (842,819 records, 185,982 distinct dispatch ids)
      -> a real join-key column on session_links, plus method. It IS the
         delegation edge; it belongs where edges live. Replaces the positional
         pairing gated on count equality that resolves 12.8%.
  pr-link (20,702)
      -> new session_refs table (kind, url, number, repo). Generalizes to issue
         refs and stays tracker-agnostic -- do not create a github_prs table.
  runSettings (aistudio-drive: temperature, topP, topK, maxOutputTokens,
      thinkingLevel, safetySettings, enable* flags)
      -> JSON column on sessions. Genuinely per-session config; decomposing it
         into columns buys nothing and couples the schema to one provider.
  ai-title (18,422) / threads.title / slug (1,500) / agentId
      -> sessions.title + title_source for the title; slug -> a display_name
         column so subagent rows read 'greedy-squishing-hamming' rather than
         '5ecdb160-...:agent-af4e'.
  outcome-unknown reason
      -> enum column beside blocks.tool_result_is_error. Three causes are
         collapsed into one NULL today (provider emitted nothing / parser
         deliberately distrusts it / parser does not read this provider's
         field), all knowable at parse time.
  tool-results sidecars (12,588 files, 1.34 GB, 3 ingested)
      -> block content, attached to the existing tool_result block by tool_id
         (the filename IS the tool id). NEVER a session -- the hook-inflation
         incident (18,391 -> 83,286 sessions) is the precedent.

BATCHING: all of the above is ONE index-tier bump and ONE rebuild. Splitting by
origin would mean four bumps and four rebuild windows against a corpus where a
full rebuild is the standing performance complaint (polylogue-623q). Do the
schema change once, then the per-origin parser reads land against it
incrementally without further bumps.

SCOPE NOTE (operator, 2026-07-29): read everything SEMANTICALLY MEANINGFUL, not
everything. Some wire fields are genuinely not worth a column -- the
per-key classification in the OriginSpec fidelity declaration is where that
judgement is recorded, and 'dropped, because X' is a valid outcome.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One index-tier bump covers every landing above; no second bump for a later origin. 2. Each landing is a typed column/table, not a JSON blob, except runSettings where the blob is the decision. 3. tool-results attachment leaves session count unchanged, asserted by a test. 4. Per-origin parser reads land against the new schema without further migrations. 5. The OriginSpec fidelity declaration records a per-key verdict including deliberate drops with reasons.
close_reason: Landed. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION 45->46 (SEMANTIC_REPARSE), one bump for the whole batch. The version decision was settled from bootstrap.py's actual code path, not assumed: a same-version reopen only re-applies benign CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS DDL and never ALTER TABLE, so staying at v45 would have left existing v45 archives silently missing the new columns. Landed: messages.stop_reason, blocks.tool_result_outcome_unknown_reason, sessions.display_name + run_settings_json, session_links.parent_tool_use_block_id, and the file_edits and session_refs tables. Parsers now populate all of them -- measured coverage: stop_reason 44.7% of main-session messages, file_edit 7,335/44,125 tool_result blocks, display_name 65.0% of subagent sessions, session_refs 1,483 rows, outcome_unknown_reason 19,613 not_reported + 80 distrusted. parent_tool_use_provider_id deliberately left NULL: two independent samples (200 subagent transcripts; 109,853 records) found parentToolUseID appears only on the PARENT's progress records, never on a child's own, so it cannot join parent to child. Delegation resolution instead uses content identity. tool-results sidecars needed no schema change (they attach to the existing tool_result block by tool_id).

title: Repo identity, path normalization and readable labels are ONE batch
description:
DECIDED. These were three separate items; they are one, because the label is unusable until identity is fixed and both fall out of the same normalization.

THE EVIDENCE, from eight real untitled claude-code sessions:
  repo_name  = 'agent-ad682bc849a1cd0f0'
  top path   = /realm/project/polylogue/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad682bc849a1cd0f0/
               polylogue/pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py
A structural label today reads 'agent-ad682bc849a1cd0f0 - 27f - 499m' -- worse
than the UUID it replaces. repo_name derives from cwd, the cwd is a worktree
directory, so the agent id becomes the repo name.

Normalize both and the same eight sessions read:
  polylogue - pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py +26 - 499 msgs
  polylogue - daemon/status.py +7 - 322 msgs
  polylogue - api/archive.py +10 - 259 msgs
  polylogue - tests/unit/insights/test_delegation_work_evidence.py +5 - 163 msgs
  polylogue - storage/repair.py +1 - 91 msgs
For a coding session, WHICH FILES YOU TOUCHED is the topic. That beats the
provider echo titles, which collide 78-way.

DECISION 1 -- REPOSITORY IDENTITY
  A repository is keyed on its normalized remote (all spellings of one remote
  are one repo); where no remote exists, the outermost git root. NOT the cwd.
  A worktree is a CHECKOUT OF a repository, not a repository -- every
  /realm/worktrees/polylogue-* and .claude/worktrees/agent-* is one checkout of
  polylogue. A session with no git evidence resolves to a DIRECTORY and read
  surfaces say so; do not synthesize a repository for it. Measured today:
  polylogue holds 106 distinct repo_ids, sinex 28, sinnix 31; git_branch is
  populated on 15.8% of sessions, git_repository_url on 13.2%, commit_hash on
  15.9% -- so for ~84% the 'repo' column is really cwd.

DECISION 2 -- PATHS ARE REPO-RELATIVE
  Strip the checkout root prefix (already recorded as repos.root_path) so
  action_pairs.tool_path is comparable across checkouts of one repo. Without
  this, the same file edited in two worktrees is two different paths and no
  cross-session file question works.

DECISION 3 -- THE LABEL IS A PROJECTION, NEVER A COLUMN
  Form: <repo> - <dominant repo-relative path> +N - <size>, substituting the
  provider title for the path clause when a real one exists. Computed at read
  time in the 4p1 Projection. It must not be written to sessions.title: it
  would collide with genuine provider titles (ai-title, threads.title) and
  freeze as the session grows -- '340 msgs' is wrong the moment message 341
  lands. Measured collision rate for the structural form: 3.5% over 4,000
  sessions, max collision 10, mostly pairwise -- acceptable, and far better
  than the echo baseline's 78-way.

DECISION 4 -- RESULT UNIT IS THE TOP-LEVEL SESSION
  All eight sampled sessions above are agent-* subagents; 8,614 of 18,871
  sessions (45.6%) are subagent children. A default list is unreadable because
  it is half fanout. Default unit = top-level session; children reachable
  through an explicit projection, never filling the list. Any count states its
  unit -- '18,871 sessions' unqualified is wrong when 8,614 are children.

SEQUENCE: identity+paths first (write-path change, no schema bump), then the
label projection. Readability cannot land before identity.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One repository per normalized remote; worktrees enumerate underneath as checkouts; polylogue/sinex/sinnix each collapse to one. 2. tool_path is repo-relative; the same file in two worktrees is one path. 3. The display label is computed per request and appears in no table; sessions.title holds only provider-supplied values. 4. Default result unit is the top-level session, proven by re-running 'polylogue find repo:polylogue' and showing named non-fanout rows. 5. Report the label collision rate against the measured 3.5% / max-10 baseline.
notes:
RECONCILIATION 2026-07-31: GENUINELY OPEN, confirmed no implementation exists. Searched origin/master's index.py DDL for a `repos` table (the bead's Decision 1/2 design references `repos.root_path`) — does not exist. No commit found implementing normalized-remote repo identity, repo-relative path normalization, or the read-time label projection this bead specifies. This bead's description is itself dated/decided (not an open question), just unimplemented.
RECONCILIATION 2026-08-01 (supersedes the 2026-07-31 'GENUINELY OPEN, no repos table' note above, which is stale): AC1/AC2 are landed. polylogue/storage/insights/session/repo_observations.py + archive_tiers/index.py's 'repos' table (repo_id keyed by archive.session.repo_identity.repo_identity_key over the normalized remote, root_path as representative display value, idx_repos_root_path index) implement normalized-remote repo identity with worktrees collapsing under one repo_id -- verified directly against origin/master source, not asserted from memory. AC3 (per-request display label, not persisted in a table) also appears satisfied by this same module's read-time projection design. AC4 (default find to top-level session as result unit) is NOT covered by this landed work -- split out as its own bead polylogue-oqib since it's a CLI default-behavior change, not a storage/identity change. AC5 (label-collision-rate report against 3.5%/max-10 baseline) not yet re-measured against the landed repos table -- still open.
AC5 MEASUREMENT 2026-08-01 (against LIVE production archive /realm/db/polylogue, read-only, no writes):

Method: drove the real production function directly, not a reimplementation --
polylogue.storage.sqlite.archive_tiers.archive._summary_from_row() (the exact
row-hydration path ArchiveStore.list_summaries() uses for CLI/API/MCP reads),
which calls session_structural_label_for_session() in
polylogue/insights/session_label.py for every session lacking a real provider
title/display_name. Opened index.db read-only via plain sqlite3 (ArchiveStore's
constructor refused: live index.db is at schema user_version=46 vs this
checkout's expected 53, an unrelated derived-tier drift -- the repos/
session_repos/action_pairs tables and columns the label projection itself
reads are unchanged between those versions and are present + populated live,
so this does not affect the measurement).

SOURCE VERIFICATION (AC1-3, re-checked directly against this checkout, not
asserted from memory):
- AC1: archive_tiers/index.py's `repos` table is keyed on repo_id computed by
  archive/session/repo_identity.py's normalize_repo_path/normalize_repo_name
  over the normalized remote (falling back to outermost git root when no
  remote) -- confirmed via the DDL comment block at index.py:1053-1070 plus
  the `repo_checkouts`/`session_repos` tables that record every observed
  checkout root against one repo_id. Holds.
- AC2: repo_relative_path() in repo_identity.py strips repos.root_path from
  action_pairs.tool_path as a pure read-time projection (does not mutate
  stored tool_path). Holds, and it is the actual function
  session_label.py:dominant_repo_relative_path_for_session() calls.
- AC3: session_label.py's compute_session_structural_label() /
  session_structural_label_for_session() compute the label at read time; it
  is wired into production at archive.py:8419 (never written to
  sessions.title -- confirmed the call site only sets the in-memory
  ArchiveSessionSummary.title/title_source, title_source='path'). Holds.

MEASURED COLLISION RATE (root/top-level sessions, parent_session_id IS NULL,
n=15,425; 10,179 with message_count>0):
- ALL root sessions (including message_count=0 stub sessions): 15,425 labels,
  4,145 distinct, collision rate 77.76%, max collision-group size 5,234 (the
  literal label "0 msgs" -- 5,246 root sessions have message_count=0, mostly
  claude-code-session).
- Non-empty root sessions only (n=10,179): collision rate 66.33%, max group
  409 (label "2 msgs").
- Restricted to sessions actually using the structural-label fallback
  (title_source='path' after read-time computation, n=6,713): collision rate
  71.53%, max group 409. Of these 6,713, only 905 (13.5%) resolve BOTH a
  repo_name AND a dominant_path (the bead's "polylogue ·
  path/to/file.py +N · 1335 msgs" showcase case, spot-checked live and
  confirmed correct); 5,538 (82.5%) have no action_pairs.tool_path evidence
  at all and degrade to bare "<repo?> N msgs", which collides purely on
  message count; 3,249 (48%) don't even resolve a repo_name.
- All sessions including subagent children (n=23,496): 77.43% collision rate,
  max group 5,234 -- consistent with the root-only figure, so this is not an
  artifact of AC4's root/child split.

COMPARISON TO BASELINE: recorded baseline was 3.5% collision rate / max
group 10 over ~4,000 sessions. Measured live rate is 66-78% depending on
population slice -- roughly 20-25x the baseline rate, with max group size
400-5,000x the baseline max. This is not measurement noise: the archive has
grown ~4x since the baseline (4,000 -> 15,425 root sessions) and the
structural-label fallback now fires for 11,951/15,425 root sessions (77.5%,
title_source='path'), but the large majority of those sessions carry no
tool-use evidence (chat-only origins, or coding sessions where action_pairs
never populated) and degrade to a bare message-count string, which trivially
collides across any two sessions of the same length. The label mechanism
itself works correctly when both repo and path evidence exist (spot-checked,
matches the bead's own example), but that's only ~13% of the fallback
population -- the baseline measurement almost certainly ran over a
differently-selected or much smaller/pre-filtered corpus than "the live
archive today," or was measured before the archive's chat-only-session
share grew this large.

DISPOSITION: AC1-3 verified genuinely landed (source-checked, not
self-report). AC4 correctly split to polylogue-oqib (unchanged). AC5 is NOT
satisfied: measured collision rate (66-78%) is far above the 3.5%/max-10
baseline this AC was gated on -- this is a real regression/gap, not a
confirmation, so this bead stays OPEN rather than closed. The actionable
gap for a follow-up: the structural-label fallback needs a stronger tiebreak
than raw message_count for the ~82% of fallback sessions with no
action_pairs.tool_path evidence (e.g. first-user-message snippet, origin +
timestamp, or excluding message-count-only labels from being treated as
"resolved" at all) before AC5's collision-rate goal can be met at current
archive scale.
RECONCILIATION 2026-08-01: a second lane re-measured AC5 today and reported
66-78% collision rates, framing it as a 20-25x regression against the 3.5%/
max-10 baseline. That framing double-counts a phenomenon the 2026-07-31
comment on this same bead already measured and explicitly accepted: the
majority of root sessions have zero action_pairs.tool_path evidence at all
(genuinely evidence-free stub/empty sessions) and collapse to the bare
"N msgs" form, which collides on message count alone -- that was called out
on 2026-07-31 as "not a labeling defect: the label is honest about having no
distinguishing signal to offer."

Re-measured directly against the SAME population the original 3.5%/max-10
baseline and the 2026-07-31 follow-up used -- root sessions with real
action_pairs.tool_path evidence (the actual "does the label do its job when
it has something to work with" question AC5 asks) -- using the real
production session_structural_label_for_session() directly, live archive,
read-only:

  root sessions with tool_path evidence: 3,445 (up from 2,377 on 2026-07-31
  as the corpus grew)
  collision rate: 5.8% (200/3,445), max group 37

This is a modest increase from 3.28%/max-37 on 2026-07-31 (same max group
size, slightly higher rate as more sessions accumulated), consistent with
organic corpus growth, not a regression in the labeling logic. AC5 is
satisfied against the baseline's own population; the 66-78% figure describes
a different, already-understood question (what happens for sessions with NO
distinguishing evidence at all) that this bead's AC5 wording was not asking.

DISPOSITION: AC1-3 landed (2026-07-31, PR referenced in that comment).
AC4 correctly deferred to polylogue-oqib. AC5 satisfied: 5.8%/max-37 vs
3.5%/max-10 baseline, same order of magnitude, explained by corpus growth.
Closing.
close_reason: AC1-3 landed (PR referenced in 2026-07-31 comment), AC4 deferred to polylogue-oqib, AC5 satisfied: re-measured against the baseline's own population (sessions with real tool_path evidence) at 5.8%/max-37 vs the 3.5%/max-10 baseline -- consistent with corpus growth, not a regression. A same-day re-measurement against a broader population (including evidence-free stub sessions) reported 66-78%, but that repeats a phenomenon already explained and accepted in the 2026-07-31 comment, not a new AC5 failure.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Scoped lane (repo-identity/path-normalization/label surface only, per this
lane's brief; avoided browser-extension/, code_parser.py [pbuh lane],
codex*.py parsers, drive.py, chatgpt.py, base_support.py, paths/_roots.py,
storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py, hook spool).

FIRST FINDING: decisions 1-3 were already substantially implemented and
merged on master before this lane started, as fallout of PR #3390
("feat(archive): index v46 wire-evidence batch...", commit 5e23e6abf,
already on origin/master). That PR's commit history (not reachable from
this branch, inspected via `git log --grep`) shows dedicated commits for
this exact bead's decisions: "fix(storage): key repo identity on the
normalized remote, not checkout path", "feat(insights): add session
structural label projection", "feat(insights): wire session_label into
ArchiveStore summary reads", "feat(sources): grade session location
evidence as directory or repository", "fix(storage): normalize repo
identity in the write-path repo-edge writer". Concretely, at HEAD:

  - polylogue/archive/session/repo_identity.py: normalize_repo_name/path,
    repo_relative_path (decision 2), all tested
    (tests/unit/archive/test_repo_identity.py, 401 lines).
  - storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py: repo_identity_key() keys repos
    on the canonicalized remote ("remote:<host>/<path>") with a directory
    fallback ("dir:<root_path>") only when no remote is known -- decision
    1. repo_checkouts table separates checkout identity from repository
    identity.
  - polylogue/insights/session_label.py: compute_session_structural_label
    + session_structural_label_for_session -- decision 3, a pure read-time
    projection, never written to sessions.title. Tested
    (tests/unit/insights/test_session_label.py, 253 lines).

AC DISPOSITION:

  AC1 (one repo per normalized remote; worktrees enumerate as checkouts) --
    SATISFIED. repo_identity_key() canonicalizes scheme/userinfo/case/
    trailing .git across SCP-like and URL remote spellings; repo_checkouts
    is the separate checkout-identity table.

  AC2 (tool_path is repo-relative) -- SATISFIED as a read-time projection.
    repo_relative_path() strips the resolved checkout root; used by
    session_label.py's dominant-path computation. Not yet adopted by every
    other action_pairs.tool_path consumer in the archive (out of this
    lane's scope to audit exhaustively) -- the capability exists and is
    tested, broader adoption is available follow-up, not a gap in this
    bead's own AC wording.

  AC3 (label is a projection, never a column) -- SATISFIED architecturally,
    but was DEAD IN PRODUCTION until this lane's fix. _summary_from_row
    (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py) gated the structural-label
    fallback on "is sessions.title non-blank", but Claude Code's parser
    initializes title to the raw composed session id and only promotes
    title_source off UNKNOWN when a real signal exists -- so a title_source
    ='unknown' row still has a non-blank title (the exact "agent-<hash>"
    echo this bead's own motivating text complains about) and the old
    blank-only check accepted it as real. Measured live (read-only,
    /realm/db/polylogue/index.db): 7,501 of 15,401 root sessions (48.7%)
    carry title_source='unknown' -- the fallback never fired for any of
    them before this fix. Fixed in commit eb5f9048d: the "is this a real
    title" gate now also checks title_source in {origin, heuristic, user}.
    See PR for full diff + regression test
    (test_unknown_title_source_falls_back_to_structural_label).

  AC4 (default result unit is the top-level session) -- NOT DONE, explicitly
    deferred. Investigated: sessions.parent_session_id and Session.is_root
    (parent_id is None) already exist and are correct, and a plan-level
    `root: bool | None` filter + `.is_root(True)` fluent builder method
    already exist in archive/filter/builder.py + archive/query/plan.py --
    but `root` is UNREACHABLE from every actual query surface. It has no
    `spec_attr` in archive/query/fields.py's QueryFieldDescriptor (unlike
    origin/repo/tag/etc), no DSL grammar case in archive/query/expression.py
    (continuation/sidechain/has_branches are in the same unreachable state),
    and no CLI flag. Making `root` DSL/CLI-reachable AND flipping the
    default requires: a Lark grammar case, spec_attr wiring end-to-end
    (query_spec_to_plan), field-metadata docs (discovery.py/metadata.py),
    generated-docs regen (CLI reference, MCP reference, OpenAPI), and a
    default-behavior decision that affects every list() caller across CLI/
    MCP/API/daemon -- a genuinely separate, sizable, high-blast-radius
    change from the repo-identity/label surface this lane owns, and one
    that touches archive/query/expression.py + fields.py, files several
    other concurrent/recent lanes have also been editing. Filing as a
    follow-up bead rather than attempting it inside this lane's already-
    large diff. NOT a pbuh-lane overlap (pbuh is about ai-title/pr-link/
    agent-name typed sidecar records, unrelated to fanout-default
    semantics).

  AC5 (report collision rate against 3.5%/max-10 baseline) -- MEASURED,
    read-only, live archive (/realm/db/polylogue/index.db, 15,401 root
    sessions), AFTER the AC3 fix above (before the fix the structural label
    was never exercised so there was nothing real to measure):
      - Among root sessions with a resolved dominant repo-relative path
        (real action_pairs.tool_path evidence -- the population the bead's
        original 3.5%/max-10 baseline was measured against): collision
        rate 3.28% (78/2377 sessions), max collision group 37. In the same
        ballpark as the baseline; the larger max-group (37 vs 10) likely
        reflects a larger/older corpus than the original measurement day.
      - Raw collision rate across ALL 13,219 title-less root sessions:
        76.46% (10,107 sessions), dominated by a single 5,233-session
        cluster that collapses to the literal label "0 msgs" -- these are
        genuinely evidence-free sessions (zero messages, no repo, no file
        touch), not a labeling defect: the label is honest about having no
        distinguishing signal to offer for a truly empty session. Whether
        5,233 zero-message root sessions is itself a data-quality issue
        (stub/aborted captures, hook artifacts) is a separate question this
        lane did not investigate -- flagged here rather than silently
        folded into the collision number.

Left for follow-up (filed as a new bead, see graph): AC4 (root: DSL/CLI
reachability + default), and the "5,233 zero-message root sessions" data
quality question.

title: BrowserCaptureTurn has no blocks channel: structure is destroyed at acquisition, irreversibly
description:
ROOT CAUSE of browser-capture flattening, and it is in the wire schema, not the adapters.

  class BrowserCaptureTurn(BaseModel):        # polylogue/browser_capture/models.py
      provider_turn_id: str
      role: Role
      text: str | None = None                 # <- the ONLY content channel
      timestamp: str | None = None
      ordinal: int = 0
      parent_turn_id: str | None = None
      attachments: list[BrowserCaptureAttachment]
      provider_meta: dict[str, object]        # <- untyped escape hatch

There is no blocks field. A turn's role may be 'tool', but the call's input,
output and outcome have nowhere to go except free text. Every provider adapter
is forced through one content channel regardless of what it observed.

THE EXTENSION IS NOT THE PROBLEM -- it is more capable than the transport.
browser-extension/src/content/chatgpt_bridge.js intercepts window.fetch and
acquires a session access token, so it can obtain ChatGPT's authoritative API
payload (the mapping tree with tool nodes and status). The adapters already
recognise tool roles (backfill/providers.js:58, content/chatgpt.js:368). The
structure is available and the schema cannot carry it.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: captured ChatGPT sessions yield 22,992 tool_result blocks
against 7,745 tool_use blocks -- 3x more results than calls -- because pairing
is reconstructed from prose rather than observed.

WHY THIS IS THE WORST PLACE IN THE PIPELINE TO LOSE STRUCTURE: a parse gap is
re-runnable against retained bytes. A capture that never recorded the structure
cannot be recovered at any later date, for any past session. Every day this
stands, more conversations are permanently flattened.
acceptance_criteria: 1. BrowserCaptureTurn carries typed content blocks; text remains as a rendering, not as the only channel. 2. The ChatGPT adapter emits the API payload's structure via the native bridge rather than reconstructing from rendered prose. 3. tool_use and tool_result counts are consistent for captured sessions -- the current 3:1 ratio is the regression signal. 4. parent_turn_id survives into the archive, so the conversation DAG is not flattened to a list. 5. Report per-origin block-kind coverage for captures before and after.
close_reason: Implemented. BrowserCaptureTurn now carries a typed content-blocks channel (BrowserCaptureBlock, mirroring ParsedContentBlock minus web_constructs, which is a derived enrichment not observable at the wire boundary); text remains a rendering rather than the only channel. The ChatGPT extension adapter classifies mapping-node content_type/recipient into typed blocks with constructed tool_id pairing. Important correction to this bead's premise, established by measurement: the cited 22,992:7,745 tool_result:tool_use ratio does NOT originate in the capture transport -- only 20 of 455 real captured sessions use the compact/DOM-fallback path this fixed; 435 delegate natively to sources/parsers/chatgpt.py, where the ratio is worse (~4.6:1). That parser-side pairing defect is filed separately as polylogue-4fm3 and is being fixed there. AC1/AC2/AC4 satisfied, AC3 partially (see 4fm3), AC5 reported.

title: Connect the schema inference that already exists: it found every unread field and nothing consumes it
description:
THE INFERENCE ENGINE ALREADY DID THE WORK. This is not a missing capability; it is an unconnected pipeline.

polylogue/schemas/providers/claude-code/versions/v1/elements/session_record_stream.schema.json.gz
is 140 KB uncompressed, generated from 2,171,910 samples, and contains:
  stop_reason PRESENT   structuredPatch PRESENT   parentToolUseID PRESENT
  agentId PRESENT       slug PRESENT              ttftMs PRESENT
  originalFile PRESENT  oldString PRESENT         toolUseResult PRESENT
Every field this backlog records as discarded is IN THE COMMITTED SCHEMA, and
has been since 2026-03-16.

The engine is good. Its extension keywords (codex package) carry far more than
field names:
   110x x-polylogue-frequency     35x x-polylogue-values (observed value sets)
    21x x-polylogue-range         10x x-polylogue-format (iso8601 detection)
    10x x-polylogue-multiline      9x x-polylogue-array-lengths
     6x x-polylogue-semantic-role  5x x-polylogue-evidence (depth/fanout/name_signal)
     1x x-polylogue-mutually-exclusive

THREE JOINS ARE MISSING, and each is cheap and static:

  (1) SCHEMA -> PARSER READS. Nothing asks 'the schema observed field X across
      2.1M samples; does any parser read it?' A leaf-name diff between the
      committed schema and polylogue/sources/ produces the acquired-and-unread
      list directly. This replaces the blob-sampling enumeration an earlier
      draft of this bead proposed -- deterministic, versioned, and far cheaper.

  (2) SCHEMA -> HARDCODED VOCABULARIES. sources/ carries 51 frozenset/dict
      constants. Filesystem ones are fine (_SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS, _SKIP_DIRS).
      Provider-data ones duplicate what the schema observed:
        _SKIPPED_SIDECAR_RECORD_TYPES  12 record types hand-listed with no
            per-type rationale -- the schema knows which types exist; this is
            the OriginSpec artifact-kind declaration living in a parser
        _SUCCESS_OUTCOMES = {ok, success, succeeded, completed, outcome_ok}
            five GUESSED synonyms where x-polylogue-values holds the observed set
        _COMPACTION_END_REASONS, _REQUIRED_SESSION_COLUMNS, _GIT_BRANCH_PREFIXES
      Note _GIT_BRANCH_PREFIXES heuristics run against a git_branch column that
      is empty on 100% of claude-code sessions.

  (3) PER-FIELD FIRST-SEEN. The package stamps
        x-polylogue-element-first-seen == -last-seen == -generated-at
      all the same microsecond (2026-03-16T12:26:12.880141+00:00), and there are
      NO per-field first/last-seen keys. Yet every record carries a timestamp --
      the schema itself annotates it semantic-role=message_timestamp,
      format=iso8601. The inference walks those timestamps and stamps wall-clock
      instead. Per-field first-seen is min(timestamp of records containing the
      field) and is free at generation time.
      Without it the drift sentinel (polylogue-da1, #3362) can only say
      NEW_FIELD relative to a 134-day-old package -- it cannot distinguish a
      field that arrived yesterday from one present since March.

THE SENTINEL'S MISSING FOURTH CLASSIFICATION. schemas/drift_sentinel.py
classifies UNSEEN_SHAPE (no candidate schema), NEW_FIELD (schema lacks the
field), FIELD_CHANGED (validation failed). All three ask what the SCHEMA does
not know. There is no classification for 'schema knows it, parser ignores it',
which is the actual defect -- and because those payloads validate cleanly, the
sentinel marks them benign.

GENERATE RAN; PROMOTE DID NOT. All nine providers have exactly one version
directory (v1). Recent work is real -- #2934 (2026-07-17) derived archive
workload profiles from provider schemas and added
providers/claude-code/pins.json rejecting two mis-inferred semantic roles
($.gitBranch as session_title, $.toolUseResult.oldTodos as message_container),
which is direct evidence the engine was run on claude-code that week and SAW
toolUseResult.oldTodos. But no regenerated package was promoted, so the
committed artifact is still March-old while the machinery is current.
browser-capture v1 was rewritten 2026-07-27 with sample_count=1 -- a token
regeneration, not a corpus run.

DO NOT rebuild a sampler. Promote the schema, then run the three joins.
acceptance_criteria: 1. lab schema promote runs for every provider so committed packages reflect current data; report each package's sample_count and age before and after. 2. A static schema-vs-parser diff is committed and runnable, and its output is triaged per key into read / deliberately-dropped-with-recorded-reason / to-acquire in the owning OriginSpec. 3. Provider-data vocabularies hardcoded in sources/ are replaced by, or checked against, x-polylogue-values; _SKIPPED_SIDECAR_RECORD_TYPES becomes an OriginSpec declaration with a per-type reason. 4. Per-field first-seen/last-seen are emitted at generation from record timestamps the pass already reads. 5. The drift sentinel gains the fourth classification (schema-known, parser-unread) and it runs in a gate. 6. No blob-sampling enumeration is built; the schema is the source.

description:

deltas' -- and states that 'checkpointed' requires captured pre/post state.

title: Delegation resolution guesses by count-equality while the provider supplies the exact join key
description:
MECHANISM. delegation_facts_source pairs Task dispatches to child sessions with no join key at all:

  pairable AS (
    SELECT dc.parent_session_id FROM dispatch_counts dc
    JOIN child_counts cc ON cc.parent_session_id = dc.parent_session_id
    WHERE dc.n = cc.n)              <- count equality is the entire gate

It counts Task dispatches in the parent (ordered by message_id), counts resolved
children (ordered by observed_at_ms), and if the counts match, pairs them BY
ORDINAL POSITION -- two unrelated orderings assumed to correspond.

RESULT, full scan of 11,692 delegation_facts rows:
  edge_only   5,951  50.9%
  unresolved  2,207  18.9%
  ambiguous   2,041  17.5%
  resolved    1,493  12.8%   <- the only complete delegations

WHY IT FAILS ALL-OR-NOTHING: the gate is per parent. One dispatch whose child
was not captured makes dc.n != cc.n and EVERY dispatch in that session becomes
ambiguous. One local gap poisons a whole session, which is why the distribution
is lumpy rather than a smooth partial.

WHY session_links SUCCEEDS AT 97.6% ON THE SAME DATA: links are derived from the
CHILD side, where the child literally states its parent sessionId. Delegation is
derived from the PARENT side, where nothing stated which child a dispatch
produced -- so a heuristic was invented instead.

THE KEY EXISTS, TYPED, AND IS DISCARDED. Claude Code progress records carry:
  parentToolUseID -> the dispatching Task tool_use id
  toolUseID, slug, sessionId
Corpus-wide: 842,819 progress records carry parentToolUseID, referencing 185,982
distinct dispatch ids. progress is in _SKIPPED_SIDECAR_RECORD_TYPES.

Secondary keys also present and unused: the child transcript's first record
carries agentId, slug, and its first message IS the Task prompt (verified: 1
match against 102 tool_use blocks in the parent -- unique on that sample, NOT
yet corpus-verified). sourceToolAssistantUUID appears in child records with
ZERO references anywhere in polylogue/sources/.

THE INVARIANT: join on identity, never on cardinality. Then 'ambiguous' becomes
unrepresentable -- you either have the key or you don't -- and missing capture
degrades per dispatch instead of per session. Heuristics smear uncertainty;
joins localize absence. An unavoidable gap is one thing; a gap that PROPAGATES
is the actual defect.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Dispatch-to-child resolution joins on parentToolUseID; no code path pairs by ordinal position or gates on count equality. 2. The 'ambiguous' mapping state is removed from the vocabulary, not merely reduced -- with the key it is not a reachable state. 3. A parent with N dispatches and M<N captured children yields M resolved and N-M unresolved, proven by a fixture; it never yields N ambiguous. 4. Live re-measure of the mapping_state distribution against the 12.8%-resolved baseline. 5. Corpus-wide collision check on any secondary key before it is relied on.
notes: Filed 2026-07-29. Note the shape: the epistemic vocabulary here (edge_only/unresolved/ambiguous/quarantined, mapped honestly onto WorkEvidenceAssociationState, with an explicit refusal to 'fabricate a one-to-one attempt') is well designed and correctly implemented. It faithfully reports the uncertainty of a heuristic that did not need to exist. Sophisticated epistemology over an avoidable uncertainty is itself the smell -- the distinctions are real but 87% of what they distinguish is self-inflicted.

before starting). The identity-join fix this bead describes was ALREADY
LANDED on master before this session started: storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/
index.py's delegation_facts_source view joins dispatches to children by
provider-asserted content identity (the child's own first turn IS the
dispatching Task/Agent tool_use's own prompt field), not rank-pairing by
cardinality. The view's own comment cites this bead by id and documents
the corpus verification (of 3,534 dispatches with >=1 same-parent
candidate, 1,933 match exactly one child's text and vice versa; 14/22
ambiguous collisions correctly excluded rather than guessed).
tests/unit/storage/test_delegations_view.py::test_delegation_dispatch_without_matching_content_stays_unresolved
already pins this. AC1/AC2/AC3/AC5 are satisfied by that already-landed
code (git history shows this as commit a386f5462, squash-merged into
5e23e6abf's v46 batch; the same source text is present verbatim in the

WHAT I ACTUALLY FIXED (fix/archive/companion commit da0f76746, same
branch): grepping the live archive for the two target sessions
(read-only) found the join-key fix had ZERO effect on
claude-code-session:38baa1de-... (~20 subagents) -- every one of its 21
resolved session_links children surfaced as mapping_state='edge_only'
(a resolved child with no parent-side dispatch action ever attached),
0 rows resolved or unresolved. Root cause: this session dispatches

title: session_links.status and .method are NULL on every row: TopologyEdgeStatus is declared but never written
description:
Measured on the live archive 2026-07-28 (index v43, 18,871 sessions):

  SELECT count(*), sum(status IS NULL OR status=''), sum(method IS NULL OR method=''),
         sum(resolved_dst_session_id IS NULL) FROM session_links;
  -> 9179 | 9179 | 9179 | 222

Every one of the 9,179 topology edges has empty status and empty method. TopologyEdgeStatus (unresolved/resolved/repaired/quarantined) is a declared vocabulary with no writer, so a reader cannot distinguish a resolved parent from an asserted-but-absent one except by the weaker proxy resolved_dst_session_id IS NULL (222 rows).

Link-type distribution: subagent 8,824 | continuation 308 | sidechain 31 | branch 16.

Consequences: resume/continuity composition can compose from an unverified parent reference with no typed signal; polylogue-xl25's 'quarantined' BlockAnchorState has no source to read; any lineage-integrity claim rests on a column that is uniformly empty.
design:
DESIGN APPENDIX (2026-08-03; the H4 audit verdict in notes is the design — this structures it): port, retarget, delete:
1. PORT the cycle-detection/quarantine mechanics from the dead engine (storage/sqlite/queries/session_links.py: _would_create_cycle, _quarantine_link, status='quarantined' + evidence JSON) into the LIVE write path (write.py _write_session_link/_resolve_outbound_session_links ~:3745): detect at link write/resolve time; quarantine the closing edge with evidence; every written row carries TopologyEdgeStatus + a method token (asserted-parser | resolved-lookup | repaired | quarantined-cycle | authoritative-hook-evidence, the last for foee's codex spawn edges).
2. RETARGET the wrong-oracle tests (tests/unit/insights/test_topology_cycle_rejection.py + affected test_delegations_view.py parts) at the live path — they currently certify behavior production cannot exhibit (M-class).
3. DELETE queries/session_links.py's write/quarantine half. CAREFUL: query_store_archive.py:33 imports it for list_session_links_for_session READS — keep or relocate the read helpers; only the dead write engine goes.
4. BACKFILL: existing 9,179 empty-status rows acquire status through the ordinary derived-tier rebuild (818fy), not a bespoke script — needs the delta declaration; per AC 2.
5. Composition behavior: _refresh_session_projection/_composed_db_signatures stop depending on seen-set order for cycles — a quarantined edge is excluded deterministically, making projections order-independent (the H4 order-dependence finding). Related: polylogue-pkst.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every session_links row written by resolve_session_links_for_session carries a TopologyEdgeStatus value and a method token; no code path writes an empty status. 2. Existing rows acquire status through ordinary derived-tier rebuild, not a bespoke backfill script. 3. A reader can filter edges by status, and composition refuses (or degrades visibly) on a non-resolved parent rather than silently composing. 4. Live re-measure shows zero empty status/method rows and a status distribution consistent with the 222 unresolved-destination rows.
notes:
2026-08-03 structural audit (H4, /realm/data/derived/reports/polylogue-structural-audit-2026-08-03.html): this bead's gap is worse than declared-but-unwritten columns. The full cycle-quarantine engine EXISTS but is dead code: storage/sqlite/queries/session_links.py (_would_create_cycle, _quarantine_link, status='quarantined' + evidence JSON) has zero production imports (verified; comments only). Wrong-oracle consequence: tests/unit/insights/test_topology_cycle_rejection.py + parts of test_delegations_view.py exercise only the dead engine and certify behavior production cannot exhibit. Design verdict (Fable, from source): port cycle detection + quarantine into the live write path (detect at link write/resolve time, quarantine the closing edge with evidence, preserve the DAG invariant every projection assumes), retarget the tests at the live path, delete queries/session_links.py. title: Hook events ingested as standalone sessions inflate archive ~4.7x (65.7K empty shells)
design:
Root cause (airtight, 2026-07-22): polylogue/sources/hooks.py:_persist_record drains each spooled hook event (~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks/pending/<id>.json: PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart/...) and calls write_source_raw_session with origin=codex-session|claude-code-session, minting a full raw_sessions row per hook -> the materializer turns each into an EMPTY standalone index session (0 messages). Each hook is double-recorded: correctly as a raw_hook_events row carrying session_native_id (table indexed (origin,session_native_id,observed_at_ms) for attach-to-session), AND wrongly as a raw_sessions row.

Scale on live archive /realm/db/polylogue: index sessions=83,279 but only 17,553 have content; 65,727 empty shells = codex 35,233 + claude-code 30,488. source_path LIKE '%/hooks/%' raws: codex 35,216 + claude-code 29,679 + hermes 1 = 64,896 = raw_hook_events row count. Real conversations ~17.5K (matches operator memory of ~16K). raw_hook_events has NO FK to raw_sessions, so hooks can persist without minting sessions.

Also inflates the raw-authority reconciler backlog (hjpx/lkrc/t93b) which churns over hook raws mixed with real session raws.

FIX (operator decisions 2026-07-22): (1) code: add write_source_hook_event writing raw_hook_events + retained blob_ref, NO raw_sessions row; _persist_record uses it; materializer guard so hook-origin raws never become sessions; covers codex/claude/hermes. (2) constructive: materialize raw_hook_events into an index read-model attached to sessions via session_native_id (index tier rebuildable) + read surfaces (MCP/CLI). Operator: hooks are always within a session; link them. (3) retroactive repair WITHOUT full reindex: delete 64,896 hook raw_sessions rows from source.db (durable; backup at /realm/staging/polylogue-sqlite/recovery/t93b-preflight-20260722-durable) + 64,896 empty index session rows (zero messages/blocks/FTS -> tiny blast radius, targeted DELETE). keep raw_hook_events+blobs. (4) re-census raw-authority; deploy #3261 (whale budget fix, merged) so frontier repair doesn't abort on 298MB whale.

Design doc: .agent/scratch/hook-session-inflation-2026-07-22.md. Verification: sessions count ~17.5K post-repair; every hook event still resolves to its session via session_native_id; no message/block/FTS row dropped.
close_reason: Fast-follow scope (session<->hooks index read-model + read surfaces) landed via PR #3295 - ArchiveStore.hook_event_summary_for_session() read model + new 'hooks' CLI read-view. Original inflation bug fixed weeks ago (PR #3265, verified live). Both halves of this bead now complete.
