title: Untested shipped defaults: _archive_facet_buckets(include_deferred=True) plus a 17-item sweep
description:
FALSE-GREEN AUDIT 2026-07-31 (findings F4 + F13). Generalises the correlation_view github_api defect.

THE SEED DEFECT'S SHAPE: run_correlation_view(github_api=True) at
polylogue/insights/correlation_view.py:14 shipped a NameError on its DEFAULT path because
every test (tests/unit/cli/test_correlate_view.py:60,80,90) passed github_api=False.

I built an AST sweep to find the class mechanically: walk every polylogue/ function with a
boolean default param, walk every tests/ call site, and flag params where the DEFAULT value is
never passed and never omitted while the opposite value IS passed.
  388 production functions carry bool defaults
  265 of them are called from tests
   17 have a default that is never exercised
    2 of those 17 have default=True (i.e. the SHIPPED behaviour is the untested one)
The sweep rediscovered run_correlation_view without being told it existed -- that is the
calibration proving it detects the class.

NEW FINDING, the second default=True case:
  polylogue/api/archive.py:735  _archive_facet_buckets(..., include_deferred: bool = True)
  tests/unit/api/test_facade_contracts.py:738 is the only test, and passes include_deferred=False.
  The False branch returns HARD-CODED EMPTY DICTS for repos/role_counts/material_origins/
  message_types/action_types/has_flags. The True branch (the shipped default) calls
  _archive_aggregate_facet_families(archive._conn, ...) and does all the real SQL work.
  The test constructs its archive stub with _conn=None -- so it STRUCTURALLY CANNOT exercise
  the default; passing True would crash on the None connection.
  Production callers at api/archive.py:4771-4774 all forward an operator-supplied
  include_deferred, so the default path is live in real use.

The remaining 15 are default=False with tests passing only True (force, detail,
require_overlays, exclude_none, include_rows, ...). Lower risk -- the untested default is
usually the inert path -- but each is an untested shipped default and worth a triage pass.

A mirror sweep found 235 flags never passed explicitly by ANY test (the non-default branch
untested). That list is noisy: matching is by bare function name, so generic names (list,
count, to_payload, model_copy) collide across classes. Treat it as a candidate pool.

AC:
- A test exercises _archive_facet_buckets with include_deferred=True against a real
  connection, asserting the SQL facet families are populated.
- The 17-item list is triaged: each either gets default-path coverage or a recorded reason
  the default is not worth testing.
- Consider whether this sweep is worth a devtools lab policy check. NOTE the operator's
  standing 'no completeness-check theater' rule: only add the gate if the known debt is
  migrated first, not as a substitute for migrating it.
notes: Fixed via PR #3445, commit a9eed07fd. Added test_archive_facet_buckets_include_deferred_default_populates_sql_families exercising _archive_facet_buckets(include_deferred=True) against a real seeded ArchiveStore connection; asserts role_counts/message_types are SQL-populated, not the include_deferred=False branch's hardcoded empty dicts. Triaged the remaining ~15-item sweep in the commit body rather than adding 15 individual tests: reproduced the AST sweep locally and confirmed it is structurally noisy exactly as the bead's own text warns -- it false-flags storage/blob_gc.py's run_blob_gc(dry_run=False) as untested even though a dozen tests exercise that default by omitting the kwarg. title: Origin misclassification: gemini-cli chats and Drive-cached transcripts detected as claude-code-session (6 native-id collisions)
description:

This session's real, shipped deliverable: consolidated the three duplicated skip-stale-replace freshness-tie implementations (archive_tiers/write.py, pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py, archive_tiers/revision_governance.py) into one should_skip_stale_replace() in archive_tiers/ingest_precedence.py. comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Follow-up forensics 2026-07-31 (session-identity/rebuild-safety audit, polylogue-lyr2 sibling task). This extends -- does not duplicate -- the hs3y content-shape audit, which correctly ruled out "misclassified non-Claude-Code content" but never cross-checked the 12 drive-cache/gemini claude-code-session rows against LOCAL raw native_ids for actual session_id collisions. Cross-checked now, read-only against the live archive.

CONFIRMED (live index.db/source.db, read-only):
- 19 raw_sessions rows with origin='claude-code-session' AND capture_mode IN ('gemini','gemini-cli') (4 gemini-cli -- already fixed at the code level by hs3y/PR#3436, stale data only; 15 drive-cache/gemini).
- Those 15 drive-cache raws parse into 14 sessions total (one raw yields 2 sessions: raw 0964ee2c.../0213d48f-....jsonl.txt.json -> both native_id 0213d48f-5b7a-4241-b77a-eb714672dc3b AND 997aa5cf-5b4a-4605-b79b-59fd9ddafc40).
- Of those 14, exactly 6 native_ids ALSO exist as a genuinely-local ~/.claude/projects/... raw_sessions.native_id: 0213d48f-5b7a-4241-b77a-eb714672dc3b, 063a6885-8d6a-4f91-80b2-7f67fa06d680, 705f1fcb-8953-4b8b-92f1-9244fcf9db91, 8c9f8c3d-4859-44cf-be9c-338803a8e7de, a952ffa4-73b0-48bd-a212-ebe5b9772d1e, cf3404fa-89e0-400a-af3e-ff1450eecef4 -- real session_id collisions, confirmed by SQL join, not inference.
- In EVERY ONE of the 6, sessions.raw_id currently points at the DRIVE-cache raw, not the local one -- the drive duplicate is the live archive's current winner for all 6.
- Byte-diffed one pair directly (blob store, read-only): drive raw 0964ee2c... (856028 bytes) is an EXACT byte-for-byte PREFIX of local raw b8282869... (856165 bytes) for native_id 0213d48f-...; the local file has one extra trailing `{"type":"summary","summary":"Sinex: Abstraction & Testing Infrastructure Refactoring",...}` record the drive copy lacks. This is the SAME conversation, drive is a stale/truncated snapshot -- not a distinct identity.
- Concrete, already-live consequence: sessions.title for claude-code-session:0213d48f-5b7a-4241-b77a-eb714672dc3b currently reads "continue" (a generic fallback) instead of the correct "Sinex: Abstraction & Testing Infrastructure Refactoring" the local file's summary record would have produced, because the stale drive copy won the write.

ROOT CAUSE, precisely: these are genuinely the SAME conversation (same conversation branch), so per the task framing "coalesce by content" is the right conceptual answer -- content-hash idempotency exists for exactly this. But it doesn't actually protect here: `write_parsed_session_to_archive`'s skip-stale-replace check (archive_tiers/write.py ~L414-422; near-duplicate logic also lives in pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py ~L537-552 and storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/revision_governance.py ~L364-373 -- three copies of the same freshness gate) compares message-derived timestamps with a STRICT `<`. Both raws derive the SAME last-message timestamp (`_derive_session_timestamps_from_messages`, since the summary record isn't a conversational message), so the check treats them as a tie and does NOT skip -- whichever raw is (re)ingested/replayed LAST wins outright, even when it is strictly less complete. That's a real gap, but it's a freshness-tie policy question across three duplicated gates, not a session-identity bug -- session_id is computed correctly and consistently for these rows.

WHY THIS ISN'T FIXED IN THIS PR: the AC on this bead ("drive-cache re-acquisitions must not claim claude-code-session identity") points at a different, deeper fix -- acquisition-provenance-aware gating in `_detect_provider_from_raw_bytes`/dispatch.py so a fallback_provider=GEMINI/DRIVE acquisition channel doesn't get silently overridden by a coincidental CLAUDE_CODE content-shape match. Traced the plumbing: `detect_provider()`'s `path` parameter is already accepted but discarded (`del path`, dispatch.py:291); `fallback_provider` reaches `_detect_provider_from_raw_bytes` from several call sites (live/batch.py:1698/1751/2619, live/batch_support.py:513, source_acquisition_components.py:326) but is only used as a last-resort fallback, never as an override signal. A correct fix must be scoped to DRIVE_LIKE_PROVIDERS acquisition channels specifically -- a blanket "prefer fallback_provider over content-shape" rule would break legitimate mixed-content/inbox directories that intentionally rely on content-shape detection winning regardless of watched-directory config. Getting that scoping wrong under time pressure risks silently breaking real detection elsewhere; did not attempt it without being able to verify the actual drive-cache OriginSpec/source config (not in source, config-driven) within this session's effort budget.

REBUILD IMPACT: unchanged by the sibling PR (polylogue-lyr2 fix). A rebuild replays every raw for these 6 (and any future) collisions and will pick whichever raw its replay order processes last for that native_id -- exactly today's live, order-dependent behavior, now precisely diagnosed rather than merely suspected. No SEMANTIC_REPARSE declaration applies since no detection/parsing code changed here.

RECOMMENDATION for whoever picks this up: implement acquisition-provenance gating narrowly in `_detect_provider_from_raw_bytes`, keyed on `fallback_provider in DRIVE_LIKE_PROVIDERS` and `detected is Provider.CLAUDE_CODE` (or CODEX) specifically -- not a general fallback-wins policy -- and decide the target outcome for the losing/duplicate raw explicitly (quarantine vs. merge-as-revision via the existing `logical_source_key`/`predecessor_raw_id` chain vs. attachment-of-the-enclosing-session per the hs3y work-evidence-material design) rather than silently promoting it to a colliding standalone session.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:

this is NOT an identity/detection bug and NOT a provenance-classification problem. The 15 drive-cache
`<uuid>.jsonl(.txt)?.json` raws ARE genuinely, byte-for-byte Claude Code session transcripts -- content-shape
detection is CORRECT to call them claude-code-session. They reach the archive because the operator uploaded
those transcript files into AI Studio conversations as attachments, and Drive sync re-downloaded them
unmodified. Treating that as a category error (PR #3436's "naming coincidence, not a bug" verdict) or as a
provenance class needing admission-time gating (both explored and reverted in this session) both aim at the
wrong layer.

ROOT CAUSE, precisely: session_id is `origin || ':' || native_id`, a generated column, so a local raw and a
drive-cache raw sharing a native session UUID legitimately collide on identity -- correctly, because they ARE
the same session. Which raw should WIN is a revision-arbitration question, not an identity question, and the

Claude Code JSONL messages for native_id 0213d48f-5b7a-4241-b77a-eb714672dc3b) -- an EARLIER, incomplete state

  confirmed via `raw_session_memberships`: both raws for logical_source_key
  `claude-code:0213d48f-5b7a-4241-b77a-eb714672dc3b` are recorded `decision='ambiguous'`,
  `revision_authority='quarantined'`, `decided_at_ms` = 2026-07-30 05:05/05:13 UTC.
- That `decided_at_ms` PREDATES the actual fix: PR #3401 "collapse revision comparison into a
  content-only relation" (commit 9fc5220ef, merged 2026-07-30 15:55 UTC) and PR #3405 (a9f2f307d,
  17:50 UTC). The live archive's membership rows are simply STALE, computed by the old
  positional/volatile-field-sensitive comparison this same day's earlier PRs replaced.

  confirming #3401/#3405 already resolves this exact case; the live archive just hasn't
  recomputed it yet.

SELF-HEALS ON REBUILD, verified from source (not assumed): `daemon/bulk_rebuild.py` documents that
the daemon itself, with zero operator involvement, routes a bulk-scale backlog (e.g. the one
`polylogue ops reset --index` creates) into `maintenance/rebuild_index.py:rebuild_index_from_source`,
which calls `sources/revision_backfill.py:backfill_historical_revision_evidence` ->
`classify_membership_revisions` -- the current, fixed, content-only relation. So the operator's
already-planned `polylogue ops reset --index && polylogued run` will recompute these 6 (and any
other stale pre-#3401 cohorts) correctly, with the local, complete transcript winning as the
accepted revision head. No further code change is needed for the collision resolution itself.

WHAT THIS PR ACTUALLY SHIPS (real, needed regardless of the above):
Consolidated the three independently-duplicated skip-stale-replace freshness-tie checks
(`archive_tiers/write.py`, `pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py`,
`archive_tiers/revision_governance.py`) into one `should_skip_stale_replace()` in
`archive_tiers/ingest_precedence.py`, called from all three. This tie-break was never the layer
that should decide "which raw wins when one is a content subset of the other" (that's revision
membership, see above) -- it is the narrower per-write timestamp fallback for cohorts revision
membership hasn't classified (single-raw sessions, or older data), and it's now one implementation
instead of three that could silently drift apart.

WHAT WAS TRIED AND REVERTED this session, recorded so the next reader doesn't re-derive it: an
OriginSpec artifact-rule refusing session admission for drive-cache Claude-Code-shaped paths
(kind=foreign_session_transcript, parse_policy=raw-only), plus a matching
`pipeline/services/ingest_worker.py:_build_stream_parse_plan` path-classification short-circuit.
Both were fully implemented and verified working (classify_artifact_path correctly refused the 15
files, real Claude Code local paths and real AI Studio export files were unaffected) before being
reverted per operator instruction: it would have permanently prevented these files from ever being
recognized as the real Claude Code sessions they are, which is wrong for the 6 non-colliding raws
(no local counterpart exists to supersede them -- they'd become inert, un-queryable raw_artifacts
rows instead of correctly-attributed real content) and unnecessary machinery for the 6 colliding
ones (revision membership already resolves this once the data catches up).

PR #3436's RECORD CORRECTED: it verified these 12 drive-cache/gemini rows were content-shape-correct
("naming coincidence, not a bug") but never cross-checked native_id collisions against local raws --
that's genuinely true and remains true (the content-shape classification was never wrong), but it
did not catch that 6 of the 12 were silently shadowing a fuller local transcript. That shadowing
was a data-staleness artifact of a bug fixed the same day this bead's forensics ran, not a defect
in #3436's own change.

gemini-cli part of the original AC (4 sessions colliding via a `.jsonl` stub detector gap) was
already fixed by PR #3436 (`local_agent.looks_like_gemini_cli` widened, `_detect_provider_from_sequence`
trust ordering) -- unaffected by anything in this comment.

Closing this bead: detection is correct, the collision-resolution defect already has a landed fix
elsewhere (#3401/#3405), the automagic rebuild path already wires it in, and this PR's own
deliverable (freshness-tie consolidation) is real, verified, shipped. Follow-up if the operator
wants proactive confirmation rather than relying on self-heal: re-run
`polylogue ops maintenance rebuild-index` (or the daemon's automagic bulk path after
`ops reset --index`) and re-query the 6 native_ids above to confirm `sessions.raw_id` now points at
the local raw.

title: shipped-but-dead: raw-authority ledger has never converged — 587,576 carried_forward plans vs 24 executed across 256 censuses
description:
Audit 2026-07-31 (shipped-but-dead census). MEASURED on the live archive. This is
the largest computed-then-discarded surface in the system by volume.

  select outcome_status, count(*) from raw_authority_census_plans:
      carried_forward   587,576
      executed               24

  select mode,lifecycle_status,fixed_point,count(*) from raw_authority_censuses:
      apply    | completed   | 0 | 84
      apply    | interrupted | 0 |  2
      apply    | planned     | 0 |  1
      census   | completed   | 0 | 84
      dry_run  | completed   | 0 | 85

fixed_point = 0 for ALL 256 censuses. Not one pass has ever reached a fixed point.
84 apply-mode passes completed and 24 plans total were ever executed (0.004% of
planned work).

Storage cost of the non-convergence: raw_authority_census_plans 570,216 rows and
raw_authority_census_post_plans 570,216 rows in source.db (a DURABLE tier), over
45,053 distinct plans in raw_authority_plans -- i.e. the same plan set is
re-planned and carried forward every pass and re-persisted each time.

Dominant blocker (raw_authority_blockers, 4,420 rows):
  4,393  "accepted raw authority remains quarantined pending exact refinement proof"
     12  "byte-proven browser rekey requires no retained membership census"
      7  "accepted revision head and materialized session select different raw authority"

So ~99.4% of blockers are one condition. The ledger is functioning as designed --
it plans, blocks, and carries forward -- but the refinement proof that would let
plans execute does not exist, so the machinery runs every pass and produces
nothing but rows.

Unlike the other census findings this is not "no reader" -- raw_reconciler.py and
raw_authority.py do read these tables. It is the sharper variant: the output is
read only by the machinery that regenerates it, and never reaches a state change.

Relevant code: polylogue/storage/raw_authority.py:1109 (plan insert), :1577
(post-plan insert), :2057/:2124 (outcome_status updates), raw_reconciler.py:1120,1515.
acceptance_criteria: Either the 'accepted raw authority remains quarantined pending exact refinement proof' blocker gets the proof path that lets its 4,393 plans execute, or the census loop stops re-persisting a carried-forward plan set it cannot act on (plan once, reference thereafter). Success is measurable the same way this was: fixed_point reaches 1 on at least one census, or census_plans row growth per pass drops to the number of genuinely new plans.
close_reason: Merged PR #3559 (with polylogue-f4z9). Real root cause: prune_raw_authority_census_history's plan-row retention window was gated on every blocker attached to a census being resolved, but the dominant blocker reason is structurally permanent (a quarantined raw with no logical source key to refine against) -- it never resolves, so continuous ingestion keeps minting new instances, each pinning whichever census first observed it, forever. Fix: the plan-row window now prunes unconditionally by the retention floor (a blocker's own expected_json/observed_json already snapshots the plan; resolve_raw_authority_blocker never reads census_plans/_post_plans); the header window's real FK-driven guard is unchanged. No schema/migration needed. Does not resolve the underlying quarantine pile itself (u19l's territory) or the RawAuthorityReconciler rewrite (lkrc/hjpx/yla8, operator-gated) -- explicitly out of scope.

title: The schema-versioning gate is version-keyed and cannot see parser-content drift: PR #3428 shipped a reparse-requiring classifier fix green
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ASSERTED. The gate is keyed to a version integer; the failure mode does not
change a version integer.

Related, do not duplicate: polylogue-9rw0 (its description already concedes
"parser-content drift is NOT covered") and polylogue-zqph (the ~5,257-row repair
pass deferred out of PR #3428). This bead is the missing GATE, not the repair.

CLAIM (CLAUDE.md, Schema regimes): every index bump above the compatibility
floor declares a delta class; "Only a SEMANTIC_REPARSE delta -- one whose result
depends on parser semantics -- routes to polylogue ops reset --index &&
polylogued run. A bump without a declaration is a policy violation."

WHAT THE LINT CHECKS. devtools/verify_schema_upgrade_lane.py, main() at :243-281,
does exactly four things:
  1. _collect_upgrade_helpers (:98-114)  AST name-pattern scan for legacy
                                          upgrade-helper function shapes
  2. _invalid_migration_paths (:174-188) durable migration file naming/location
  3. index_delta_declaration_report(INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION) (:253 ->
     storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py:473-493) -- the version-gap check
  4. _invalid_benign_ddl_entries (:144-171) benign-DDL registry shapes
Check 3 has real teeth: expected = range(FLOOR+1, INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION+1) and it
fails on any version in that range with no IndexDeltaDeclaration. It is wired
into the REQUIRED per-PR lint job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:36) -- confirmed, it
is not skipped the way the heavy `test` job is. This half works.

THE STRUCTURAL BLINDNESS. Check 3 reads one integer and diffs it against a static
table. It has zero visibility into polylogue/sources/parsers/** or
polylogue/archive/artifact_taxonomy/**. A change that alters classification
output FOR IDENTICAL INPUT BYTES needs a reparse but produces NO version bump at
all -- so the gate that would fire never fires.

THE CONCRETE CASE, merged 2026-07-31T07:33Z. PR #3428, "fix(sources): require
positive conversation evidence before session classification":
  archive/artifact_taxonomy/support.py   looks_like_record_entry() -- removed
      bare "type" as sufficient evidence, added _TYPE_ENVELOPE_MARKERS
      co-occurrence. Identical bytes now classify differently than yesterday.
  sources/parsers/claude/code_detection.py  looks_like_code() -- same shape
  sources/revision_backfill.py           unified the rebuild-replay gate with
      the live-ingest gate
INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION stayed 46; lifecycle.py untouched; the PR body itself says
"No schema change" and "This PR only stops NEW phantoms going forward", deferring
~5,257 already-misclassified rows to polylogue-zqph.
`devtools lab policy schema-versioning` ran and was GREEN -- correctly, per its
contract, and uselessly for this defect.

RUNTIME MAKES IT PERMANENT, and this corrects CLAUDE.md's wording. CLAUDE.md says
an undeclared bump means "the archive silently falls back to full raw replay".
Measured: it does not. bootstrap.py:226-229 raises a loud RuntimeError and no
caller swallows it (checked all 18 initialize_archive_database call sites for
except RuntimeError -- none). The genuinely SILENT path is the one PR #3428 took:
same version -> bootstrap.py:174-192 applies only the benign-DDL registry and
opens as-is. No error, no log line, no debt row. Stale classification persists
indefinitely.

HOW ANYONE FOUND OUT: they didn't, automatically. bead polylogue-9ykn came from a
manual live-archive audit, not a signal.

BLAST RADIUS: every archive generation at the same index version keeps stale
derived rows forever. This is aggz Invariant 3 -- "derived state carries the
version of the logic that derived it" -- and its absence is exactly what makes a
corrected classifier inert on existing data.

AC:
- A parser/classifier fingerprint exists such that changing classification logic
  invalidates the rows it produced, without an operator command. (aggz Invariant 3
  / polylogue-9dxn is the mechanism; this bead is the gate that consumes it.)
- The gap is stated where a developer will hit it: the schema-versioning lint or
  its docs say in one line that parser-content drift is out of its scope, so a
  green run is not read as "no reparse needed".
- A test or lint fails when a file under sources/parsers/ or
  archive/artifact_taxonomy/ changes classification-affecting logic with no
  corresponding reparse declaration -- or, if that is judged infeasible, the
  decision and its reasoning are recorded on this bead rather than left implicit.
close_reason: Merged PR #3532 (feature/devtools/classifier-fingerprint-gate): devtools lab policy classifier-fingerprints AST-fingerprints classify_artifact*/looks_like* functions and diffs against a committed manifest; undeclared drift fails the gate. Regression test proves it would have caught PR #3428's classifier drift retroactively. Fixed 2 real CodeRabbit findings post-hoc (decorator-exclusion, UnicodeDecodeError) before merge.

title: Lineage truncation signal is computed then discarded: polylogue read and HTTP silently return partial transcripts
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ASSERTED on 2 of 3 read call chains; the signal is computed and then discarded.

CLAIM: forks/resumes/subagents/auto-compaction store only the child's divergent
tail plus branch_point_message_id + inheritance; "reads recompose parent-up-to-
branch + child-tail" (CLAUDE.md, Lineage normalization).

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE BRANCH POINT IS DANGLING. Composition does not raise and
does not fall back to the whole parent. It returns ONLY the child's own tail --
i.e. the operator sees a conversation that silently begins mid-thread.

The system knows this. Both composition implementations compute an explicit
truncation signal:
  storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:1271-1287
      sets lineage_complete=False,
      lineage_truncation_reason=LINEAGE_TRUNCATION_DANGLING_BRANCH_POINT
  storage/sqlite/queries/message_query_reads.py:226-238
      computes the identical DANGLING_BRANCH_POINT / DEPTH_LIMIT reasons

THE SIGNAL IS THROWN AWAY. message_query_reads.py:134-137:

    messages, _completeness = await get_messages_with_lineage_completeness(
        conn, session_id, _compose_in_position_order=_compose_in_position_order
    )
    return messages

No caller outside that module invokes get_messages_with_lineage_completeness
directly (verified: grep -rln for the symbol excluding tests returns only its own
file). Every real consumer uses the signal-dropping get_messages:
  storage/repository/archive/sessions.py:79,98,112   (repository .get/.get_messages)
  storage/sqlite/queries/message_query_reads.py:393  (inside get_messages_paginated)

And the Session domain model carries no completeness field at all
(archive/session/domain_models.py, storage/hydrators.py: zero "lineage" matches),
so the CLI's own descriptor builder hard-codes it away:
  rendering/semantic_cards.py:288-312  lineage_descriptor_from_session()
      returns LineageDescriptor(..., lineage_complete=None, ...)

AFFECTED SURFACES:
  cli/messages.py:108-114        polylogue read / messages -- the primary human
                                 surface. Neither the markdown render nor the
                                 json/ndjson payloads carry a truncation flag.
  daemon/http.py:3429, 4628-4647 GET /api/sessions/:id/messages -- same blind call.
SAFE SURFACE (for contrast, proving the plumbing is possible):
  mcp/archive_support.py:676-677 propagates lineage_complete +
                                 lineage_truncation_reason onto the MCP payload;
  rendering/semantic_cards.py:1174-1175 renders "composed transcript is truncated".

LIVE DATA (measured, file:/realm/db/polylogue/index.db?mode=ro):
  sessions with non-null branch_point_message_id                       537
  branch_point_message_id NOT present in messages.message_id (dangling)  0
  session_links total / unresolved / quarantined / repaired    9333 / 1426 / 0 / 0
  deepest live prefix-sharing chain                                    60 hops
The bug is DORMANT today (0 dangling), not firing. It is a real gap, not a
hypothetical: the moment any branch point falls out of sync the CLI and HTTP
surfaces render a short conversation with no indication.

WHAT KEEPS IT DORMANT, and why that is thin: two repairs exist and neither is a
periodic sweep.
  write.py:2746 -> :4756  _repair_stale_prefix_branch_points_db -- inline, per
      save, scoped to impacted sessions; repairs ONLY the stale-parent-id-suffix
      shape, skips ambiguous matches silently (write.py:4732-4733,4751).
  daemon/lineage_startup.py:31 (via daemon/cli.py:215) -- the full unscoped scan,
      called exactly once per daemon process START. It is NOT a DaemonConverger
      stage (grep of daemon/convergence*.py for the symbol: no matches), so a
      branch point that goes dangling between restarts is never re-checked.

BLAST RADIUS: silent data-fidelity loss on the two surfaces a human actually
reads. A truncated transcript is indistinguishable from a short conversation.
Ranked above the layering/doc findings because it corrupts what the user is
shown, not merely what a report claims.

AC:
- polylogue read and GET /api/sessions/:id/messages surface lineage_complete /
  lineage_truncation_reason, in both human and machine output.
- The signal reaches those surfaces from the same computation the MCP path uses;
  get_messages either propagates it or its signal-dropping wrapper is deleted.
- A test composes a session with a deliberately dangling branch_point_message_id
  and asserts the CLI/HTTP output is marked truncated (fails against current code).
- Decide explicitly whether the startup-only full repair should become a periodic
  convergence stage, and record the decision either way.
close_reason:
Fixed on branch feature/storage/surface-lineage-truncation-signal (commit
5fd73c478). AC disposition:

1. Satisfied -- lineage_complete/lineage_truncation_reason now appear in
`polylogue read --format json` (SessionMessagesResponsePayload gained the
fields, docs/schemas/cli-output/session-messages-response.schema.json
regenerated) and GET /api/sessions/:id/messages (both the DB-backed
_do_get_messages and the archive-root-backed _do_archive_get_messages
handlers), plus the markdown/card-placement render for both surfaces
(overlaid onto lineage_descriptor_from_session's previously hard-coded
lineage_complete=None).

2. Satisfied -- message_query_reads.get_messages_paginated (the function
`polylogue read`/HTTP actually call) now composes via
get_messages_with_lineage_completeness directly instead of the
signal-dropping get_messages() wrapper, and returns
(messages, total, LineageCompleteness) instead of a 2-tuple. The plain
get_messages() wrapper itself was left in place -- other callers
(get_messages_batch, iter_messages, etc.) don't need the signal and
deleting it would be a wider, unrelated refactor.

3. Satisfied -- new fixtures in tests/unit/storage/test_lineage_normalization.py
and tests/unit/cli/test_messages.py compose a session with a hard-deleted
parent (dangling branch_point_message_id) and assert
get_messages_paginated / the CLI JSON output are marked truncated; both
fail against the pre-fix 2-tuple signature.

4. Decision recorded, not silently dropped: daemon/lineage_startup.py's
full repair still runs once per daemon START only, not as a
DaemonConverger stage. Live measurement (0 dangling of 537 branch points)
means nothing is actively broken today, but a branch point going dangling
between restarts would go unrepaired until the next restart. Making it a
convergence stage is a distinct, non-trivial change (bounded scan cost,
session-scoped retry semantics matching other stages) -- deliberately
left as a decision-recorded gap, not folded into this fix's scope.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/storage/test_lineage_normalization.py
tests/unit/cli/test_messages.py tests/infra/mcp.py
tests/unit/api/test_facade_contracts.py tests/unit/core/test_facade_api.py
tests/unit/core/test_sync_surface_runtime.py

a known "clock freeze_clock does not patch" gap, not touched by this
change). devtools verify --quick: exit 0.

title: Codex sidecar discovery failure is frozen forever as an empty enrichment snapshot
description: Silent-degradation audit 2026-07-31. pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py:1336-1351: 'except Exception: logger.exception(...); discovered = {}' then persists {} via write_history_sidecar. Because read_earliest_history_sidecar_for_path (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/source_write.py:888) freezes the FIRST persisted snapshot per (origin, source_path) by design (polylogue-ih67 AC#3/4), a transient disk/parse error during discovery becomes a durable, uncorrectable data-quality defect: every future ingest of that source_path replays the empty snapshot and enrichment is never retried. Same shape at ingest_worker.py:583-596 (per-record path, falls back to unenriched sessions, logged but not counted in summary). Fix: do not persist a snapshot when discovery raised — only persist genuinely-empty looked-and-found-nothing results; add a sessions_unenriched counter to the ingest summary. Verdict: MUST-FAIL-LOUD.

Fixed root cause: on a discovery exception, ingest_batch/_core.py now uses the empty {} only for that ingest attempt and never passes it to write_history_sidecar -- ih67's first-snapshot-freeze stays intact for genuinely-empty discovery results, only the exception path stops persisting, so the next attempt for the same source_path retries discovery from disk. Regression test confirms fails-before/passes-after. Sibling instance found and fixed too: ingest_worker.py's per-record on-demand enrichment fallback had the same silent-degradation shape -- added IngestRecordResult.sessions_unenriched, threaded through and counted in _IngestBatchSummary.

title: Session native_id is stored raw but its FK is computed stripped -- the ab5bad1f bug class, unfixed at session level
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict: ASSERTED
at the session level; the identical bug class is ENFORCED at the message level.

CLAIM: "Identity is computed, never stored redundantly -- every id is a SQLite
generated column" (CLAUDE.md, docs/internals.md). sessions.session_id is
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (origin || ':' || native_id) STORED UNIQUE
(polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:164).

THE DIVERGENCE. There are two Python implementations of the session-id formula
and they disagree on whitespace:

  polylogue/core/identity_law.py:33     session_id()  -> STRIPS native_id
                                        (via _required_text, line 20-24)
  polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:153         session_id()  -> does NOT strip; it only
                                        checks non-emptiness after strip (line 168)
                                        then interpolates the RAW value (line 171)

polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py binds the raw value into the
sessions row but computes the child FK from the stripped one, inside the same
function:

  write.py:375   native_id = session.provider_session_id        # RAW
  write.py:376   session_id = archive_session_id(origin.value, native_id)  # STRIPPED
  write.py:553   ... INSERT INTO sessions (...) VALUES (native_id, ...)    # RAW

So for provider_session_id = "  abc  ":
  sessions.session_id (SQL generated column, from the RAW stored native_id)
      = "codex-session:  abc  "
  the session_id bound as the FK into messages (from identity_law, STRIPPED)
      = "codex-session:abc"
-> FOREIGN KEY violation; the write/rebuild transaction aborts.

WHY THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. This is the exact bug class of incident ab5bad1f,
which killed a 10-hour rebuild. It was fixed AT THE MESSAGE LEVEL by introducing
a single-source-of-truth normalizer whose docstring names the incident:

  write.py:5218-5245  _stored_message_native_id()
    "This is the single source of truth for message identity (polylogue rebuild
     ab5bad1f FK-failure fix): both the _write_messages INSERT and _message_id
     ... MUST route through this helper, or the two computations can diverge and
     a later blocks insert can reference a message_id that was never written."

That fix is guarded by tests/property/test_message_identity_normalization.py
(test_db_generated_message_id_matches_python_identity_law).

THE SESSION LEVEL HAS NEITHER. Confirmed with two independent greps:
  git grep -n "_stored_session_native_id"          -> no matches
  git grep -n "provider_session_id" -- 'polylogue/**/*.py' | grep -i strip
      -> only pipeline/ids.py:168, an emptiness CHECK, not a normalization
polylogue/sources/parsers/base_models.py:300 declares
ParsedSession.provider_session_id as a plain Pydantic str with no strip
validator, so nothing upstream prevents a padded native id reaching the writer.

LIVE DATA (measured, file:/realm/db/polylogue/index.db?mode=ro):
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE native_id != trim(native_id);   -> 0
  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE instr(native_id,':') > 0;       -> 8781
The defect is LATENT, not active. Colon-bearing native ids are common (8781) and
are safe by construction (Origin enum values contain no ':' and sessions.origin
carries a CHECK against that enum, so the first ':' always terminates the origin).
Whitespace is the unguarded axis.

BLAST RADIUS: narrow but loud. Fails as an aborted transaction, not silent
corruption -- same shape as ab5bad1f, which cost a 10-hour rebuild. Any parser
that derives provider_session_id from a filesystem path segment, an external
identifier, or a scraped field can emit padding.

AC:
- A _stored_session_native_id-equivalent normalizer exists and is the single
  value used by BOTH the sessions INSERT and the archive_session_id call in
  write.py, mirroring the message-level fix.
- A session-level sibling of tests/property/test_message_identity_normalization.py
  asserts the SQL-generated sessions.session_id equals the Python identity_law
  computation for whitespace/empty/surrogate-bearing provider_session_id inputs,
  and fails against the current code.
- The two divergent implementations are reconciled or one is deleted: either
  pipeline/ids.py:session_id routes through core.identity_law, or the audit
  records why two intentionally-different functions must coexist.
close_reason: Verified SATISFIED (storage triage 2026-07-31): commit decca43ab (#3450, merged 2026-07-31T14:13Z) explicitly fixes polylogue-lyr2 per PR body. write.py:5817 _stored_session_native_id() (docstring names the bead) used at write.py:378 and write.py:3043 (session-link parent matching). New test tests/property/test_session_identity_normalization.py exists.

title: Repair pass for existing empty-session phantom rows (polylogue-9ykn dataset cleanup)
description:
Follow-up to polylogue-9ykn: the ingest-time classifier fix (looks_like_record_entry / looks_like_code
type-only overmatch, and unifying the live-ingest classify_artifact gate with the
revision_backfill.py replay/rebuild gate) stops NEW phantom sessions of the
conversation_relationships.jsonl / problems_index.jsonl / graph-edge-index shape from being
created going forward, on both the live daemon path and any polylogue ops reset --index rebuild.

It deliberately does NOT delete or touch any of the existing ~5,257 empty-session rows already in
the live archive (per explicit operator scoping: dataset repair is a separate, carefully-scoped
concern). This bead tracks that repair pass.

What the repair needs to do, precisely (do not blanket-delete via repair_empty_sessions /
`polylogue check --cleanup` -- see polylogue-ne6k, which found that predicate cannot distinguish
a legitimately-empty session, e.g. the 832 the 2026-07-22 hook-inflation postmortem chose to
retain, from corruption debris):

1. Re-run classification (the now-fixed classify_artifact / looks_like_record_entry /
   looks_like_code) against each existing empty session's ORIGINAL raw_sessions source_path +
   raw bytes to determine: would this record be admitted as a session under the current
   classifier, or refused?
2. For rows the current classifier would refuse (the conversation_relationships.jsonl-shaped
   phantoms, and any other now-caught non-conversational content): these are safe candidates for
   targeted reclassification/removal from index.db (rebuildable tier) -- NOT source.db (durable
   raw evidence must be retained per the repo's schema regime).
3. For rows the current classifier would still admit (genuinely-empty-but-valid sessions, e.g. a
   real Claude Code/Codex session that has zero turns so far, or the 832 retained browser-capture
   stubs): leave untouched.
4. Needs explicit operator sign-off before running against the live archive (per CLAUDE.md's
   destructive-operation and schema-regime discipline) -- this bead should NOT be closed by an
   agent unilaterally running the repair.

Evidence base: polylogue-9ykn's own measurement (5,255 zero-message sessions, 22.6% of the
23,296-session archive at measurement time; 5,193 claude-code-session, 46 claude-ai-export, 17
codex-session) plus polylogue-gvgi's single dominant phantom (conversation_relationships.jsonl,
96,748 empty messages, ~95% of the archive's zero-block messages -- tracked/repaired separately
per gvgi's own AC, coordinate rather than duplicate).
notes: RECONCILE 2026-08-02: same conclusion as gvgi. The classifier fix (#3428, ab8a92c1a) this bead's own text calls 'now-fixed' is confirmed deployed (ancestor of live nix pin 513e8f85a). This bead's own AC4 already says it 'should NOT be closed by an agent unilaterally running the repair' against the LIVE archive via a targeted script -- but the planned full 'polylogue ops reset --index' reindex is not a targeted repair script, it's a full from-scratch reparse using current (already-fixed) classifiers, so it will naturally admit only genuinely-valid sessions and never recreate the ~5,257 phantom shape rows, without any separate operator-authorized live-mutation step. Recommend: treat the reindex itself as satisfying this bead's repair goal; verify post-rebuild (re-run the 9ykn zero-message-session count query) rather than building a separate repair script.

title: Declare SEMANTIC_REPARSE index bump for Claude Workflow artifact classification (PR #3088)
description:
Investigation 2026-07-31 (worktree agent-a7335b82eed35c7cf), triggered by
operator report that Claude Code Workflow artifacts appear BOTH normalized
AND independently ingested raw as empty sessions.

FINDING: the classification code is already correct. polylogue/archive/
artifact_taxonomy/runtime.py:classify_artifact_path consults OriginSpec's
artifact_rules (polylogue/sources/origin_specs.py, added by 1e0246d77 / PR
#3088, "admit Claude Workflow artifacts through OriginSpec", 2026-07-18) and
correctly returns parse_as_session=False for workflow_run_snapshot,
workflow_journal, agent_sidecar_meta, and adopt_manifest artifact kinds.
Verified directly against the live paths (python3 -c
"classify_artifact_path(...)") -- current code classifies them correctly.

But 1e0246d77 changed session/fact classification semantics for an already-
running archive WITHOUT declaring an INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in
polylogue/storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py (checked: no lifecycle.py/index.py
change in that commit, and no v33-v47 IndexDeltaDeclaration references
polylogue-2qx.2 or the Workflow admission PR). Per docs/architecture ("Schema
regimes"), only a declared SEMANTIC_REPARSE delta routes an index.db through
`polylogue ops reset --index && polylogued run`; a semantic parser change
with no declared bump leaves already-materialized wrong-classification rows
untouched forever, because the daemon's fast-forward convergence has no
signal that anything changed.

MEASURED LIVE IMPACT (index.db read-only query, 2026-07-31):
  zero-message claude-code-session rows total: 5,193
  of these, joined to a source_path under a `workflows/` artifact family: 172
    agent_sidecar_meta (subagents/workflows/*/agent-*.meta.json): 164
    workflow_run_snapshot (workflows/wf_*.json):                    7
    other (workflow_journal / adopt_manifest):                      1
  acquired_at_ms range for these 172: 2026-07-14 10:52 UTC .. 2026-07-26
  19:18 UTC -- i.e. ALL acquired while the deployed daemon build predated
  the fix. The sinnix flake's polylogue input only advanced to a revision
  containing 1e0246d77 on 2026-07-29 (flake.lock lastModified
  1785367887 = 2026-07-29 23:31 UTC; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms
  1e0246d77 is an ancestor of the pinned rev 5e23e6a). So this is deploy-lag
  contamination the fix code cannot self-heal without a reparse trigger, not
  a currently-active defect in the shipped classification logic.

Separately, polylogue-omsw's tool-result-sidecar and file-history-snapshot
populations are a DIFFERENT, still-open acquisition-scope gap (not covered
by this bead) -- do not conflate the two when scoping remediation.

DO NOT execute the reset live from this investigation; this bead exists to
make the repair describable and consented rather than silent. Per this
repo's ops.db/index.db durability rules, `polylogue ops reset --index` is a
disposable-tier rebuild, not durable-data loss, but it is still a
consequential live-daemon action (extended downtime rebuilding ~20K
sessions) that needs explicit operator scheduling, not an agent-triggered
version bump buried in an unrelated PR.
acceptance_criteria: 1. polylogue/storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py gets a new IndexDeltaDeclaration bumping INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION with classes=(SEMANTIC_REPARSE,), whose comment names 1e0246d77/#3088 as the retroactive semantic change being captured and cites the measured live-impact counts. 2. The bump lands in a PR whose body explicitly tells the operator a 'polylogue ops reset --index && polylogued run' is now required, so it is scheduled deliberately (not silently triggered by routine deploy). 3. After the rebuild, the 172+ contaminated sessions reclassify to their correct non-session disposition (verified by re-running the same index.db query this bead's evidence used and confirming zero remain). 4. devtools lab policy schema-versioning stays green.
close_reason: Declared the missing v48 SEMANTIC_REPARSE IndexDeltaDeclaration for #3088/1e0246d77 (storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py + INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bump in archive_tiers/index.py), citing the measured live-impact counts (172 zero-message sessions: 164 agent_sidecar_meta + 7 workflow_run_snapshot + 1 other). AC1-2 satisfied (declaration lands, PR body states the operator command required). AC3 (172 rows reclassify to zero) is explicitly deferred -- NOT executed per this bead's own DO-NOT-EXECUTE instruction; the operator must run 'polylogue ops reset --index && polylogued run' deliberately. AC4 (devtools lab policy schema-versioning stays green) verified. Also investigated why the lint didn't catch PR #3088's original undeclared bump: it only checks declaration-table completeness against the CURRENT INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION constant, never inspects classification source files, so it structurally cannot detect a missing bump, only an undeclared existing one. Filed polylogue-qs4b to design a real fix (content-fingerprint of classification tables) rather than rushing one in; explained in PR body.

title: FTS invariant violated: ops status says 100% indexed while queries fail as incomplete
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31 on the live archive.

CONTRADICTION between two surfaces:
  polylogue ops status        -> 'FTS: 100.0% indexed'
  polylogue find <anything>   -> exit 1, DatabaseError,
                                 'Search index is incomplete. Run polylogued run.'
Both were run minutes apart against /realm/db/polylogue with the daemon RUNNING.
So either the status surface measures something the query path does not require,
or one of them is wrong. A user-facing error telling the operator to run a daemon
that is already running is itself a broken contract.

WHY THIS IS AN INVARIANT VIOLATION, not just a bug: the automagic-invariants
doctrine (bd memory 'automagic-invariants') states that FTS coherence belongs to
daemon convergence/startup/write-path invariant enforcement, NOT to routine
operator maintenance commands. Search being degraded while the daemon runs means
the convergence path either is not running the FTS stage, is failing it silently,
or completed it against a different index generation than the query path opens.

CONTEXT that may be causal, all measured tonight:
- The daemon was livelocked for hours (raw materialization yielding to a pending
  browser-capture spool every 60s while ingesting nothing) and was restarted
  around 06:20. The index may have been left mid-convergence.
- An index-generation swap happened 2026-07-30 (.index-generations/, active
  pointer gen-1785377665711-06297b00). A dataset lane separately measured 4,186
  embeddings rows (2.2%) pointing at message_ids no longer in index.db, which it
  attributed to that swap with no cross-tier reconciliation (bead polylogue-feu0).
  An FTS table left behind by the same swap would present exactly this way.
- A dataset lane also measured 10,837 blocks with real text missing from
  messages_fts (down from 36,757), spot-checked directly (appended to
  polylogue-5vbs). That is a real gap, but 'incomplete' as a hard query-path
  failure is a different symptom from 'partially indexed'.
- Concurrent stderr warning on every CLI call: 'format drift: origin
  aistudio-drive 100% of 302 records since 2026-07-01 carry unseen shapes'.

AC: the two surfaces agree; a degraded FTS either self-heals via convergence or
reports the SAME state through both surfaces; and the error message does not
instruct the operator to start a daemon that is already running.
close_reason: Root cause: daemon/convergence_stages.py::repair_messages_fts_surface recorded state=ready with a fabricated source_rows=1,indexed_rows=1 placeholder (detail='bounded global messages_fts repair completed; exact counts skipped') after its exhaustive (not partial) reconcile pass, purely to dodge two cheap COUNT(*) probes. cli/commands/status.py then defaulted the resulting None coverage_pct to a hard-coded 100.0% whenever messages_ready was true -- the '100% indexed' the operator saw was never a measurement. The query path (storage/fts/freshness.py) independently trusts/distrusts the same ledger row via freshness_ready_record_trusted with no knowledge of the placeholder, so the two surfaces could show different confidence for the same state. Live evidence: /realm/db/polylogue/index.db carried exactly this poisoned row at investigation time; live messages_fts_docsize already matched the real indexable block count (0 missing) -- convergence HAD actually finished, it just lied about verifying it. Fix (PR #3429): repair_messages_fts_surface now records real post-repair counts via two plain COUNT(*) probes instead of the placeholder; removed the now-dead BOUNDED_MESSAGE_FTS_REPAIR_DETAIL/counts_available special-casing in fts_status.py; CLI no longer defaults an unmeasured coverage_pct to a fabricated percentage (prints 'coverage unknown'); centralized and reworded the FTS repair-hint text so it never tells the operator to start a daemon that might already be running. New regression test proves status and query-path readiness agree post-repair (verified it fails against the pre-fix code). All three AC items satisfied: surfaces derive from the same ledger check; repair now honestly self-heals (real counts recorded, not a lie); error text no longer presumes the daemon is down. devtools verify --quick green; devtools test on all touched/adjacent modules green (44+181+23 tests).

title: Non-transcript JSONL under ~/.claude/projects/ ingested as claude-code-session: 96,748 empty phantom messages
description:
Adversarial dataset investigation (H7) found a single phantom claude-code-session with native_id literally 'conversation_relationships' and message_count=96,748, all zero-block/zero-word (role=user, material_origin=human_authored, message_type=message, no user_context_text). It accounts for 96,748 of the archive's 101,765 total zero-block messages (95.1%).

Traced to source: raw_sessions.raw_id=aa5e35075a0c0b809ae70811c2e5515a4b02e1890518078028149c4258ea3e93, source_path=/home/sinity/.claude/projects/-realm-project-sinex/analysis/index/conversation_relationships.jsonl (251,568 lines, 52MB blob). This file is NOT a Claude Code transcript -- it is a sinex analysis-index artifact recording parent/child/conversation graph edges (each line: conversation/parent/child/type/timestamp keys, type is assistant or user). It happens to live under a directory tree shaped like ~/.claude/projects/PROJECT/... and its per-line type field was apparently enough to satisfy a loose provider-shape check, causing dispatch to lower it as a claude-code-session with one empty message per JSONL line.

Distinct root cause from the already-tracked polylogue-b508 (agent-star.meta.json sidecars, fixed PR 3403): that class is Claude Code own sidecar files; this is a third-party tool artifact that merely sits in the scanned directory tree and pattern-matches a provider detector.

Blast radius (verified 2026-07-31 on live archive): 1 phantom session, 96,748 phantom messages (about 2 percent of the archive total 4,900,553 messages), 52MB wasted raw blob. Also the leading contributor to the C4 metric (sessions with created_at_ms NULL) growing from 1,117 (post-de-inflation) to 5,382 -- 97.8 percent of those NULL-created_at_ms sessions have word_count=0, consistent with this and similar phantom-ingestion artifacts accumulating.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Root-cause: identify the exact detector/heuristic that accepted this file as a claude-code-session, tighten it to require genuine Claude Code transcript shape evidence (sessionId/uuid/message envelope), not just a bare type key. 2. Purge the phantom session and its 96,748 messages/blocks from index.db via targeted delete, not full rebuild (rebuild would recreate it per the b508 lesson about the parse chokepoint in sources/revision_backfill.py). 3. Quarantine or reclassify the source raw so ops reset --index does not resurrect it. 4. Add a regression test: a JSONL file with type-assistant/user shaped lines but no session/message envelope must not be classified as any chat-transcript origin.
notes: RECONCILE 2026-08-02: AC1 (root-cause detector fix) ALREADY MERGED -- PR #3428 (ab8a92c1a, 2026-07-31) rewrote looks_like_code() to require a genuine record-envelope marker (uuid/cwd/version/message) alongside an ambiguous role-word type; conversation_relationships.jsonl's shape (bare conversation/parent/child/type/timestamp keys) has none of those and is now refused. Verified: this commit is an ancestor of the currently-deployed nix pin (513e8f85a, live since 2026-08-01 17:05). AC3 (quarantine raw so ops reset --index doesn't resurrect it) is satisfied for free: a full index reset always reparses from source.db with current parser code (no fast-forward path involved), so the fixed classifier naturally refuses this file on rebuild -- no separate quarantine/reclassify step needed. AC2 (targeted delete of the 96,748 existing phantom messages) becomes MOOT once the planned full reindex runs, since that rebuilds index.db from scratch and simply never recreates the phantom. Net: this bead needs no further code work -- closeable after the reindex, pending a post-rebuild verification that the session is actually gone.
close_reason: Duplicate/superseded by polylogue-21qj, which covers this exact conversation_relationships.jsonl case as one of 6 named non-transcript-artifact-as-session shapes. gvgi's own AC1 (root-cause detector fix) was already confirmed merged in its own notes (PR #3428, ab8a92c1a). AC2/AC3/AC4 (purge + quarantine + regression test) are completed as part of polylogue-21qj's closure: the empty_sessions maintenance-repair target (polylogue/storage/repair.py) was widened to also flag content-empty-but-message-bearing sessions (word_count=0), which now catches conversation_relationships specifically -- verified read-only against the live archive that this session is flagged for purge via the existing dry-run-gated `polylogue maintenance repair --target empty_sessions`. See polylogue-21qj's closing notes for full detail and the PR.

title: Decision: remove Origin.BEADS_ISSUE — Beads data belongs in the work-evidence graph, not sessions
description:
DESIGN INVESTIGATION VERDICT (2026-07-31, design doc: .agent/scratch/live/beads-handling-design-2026-07-31.html). The operator challenged BEADS_ISSUE-as-Origin ("beads is not a chatlog"). Investigation confirms the doubt with measurements:

1. interactions.jsonl is 100% field_change rows (polylogue: 2,249 rows / 862 issues = priority 1124 + status 1071 + assignee 54), actor constant "Sinity" in 2,249/2,249. The parser synthesizes English prose from these ("Sinity changed priority from 3 to 2") into Role.USER messages with MaterialOrigin.RUNTIME_PROTOCOL — ~924 projected sessions containing zero human or assistant content. Same structural shape as the hook-event inflation incident (polylogue-31r1, 83,286→18,391 sessions).
2. The rich Beads artifact — issues.jsonl (1,260 issues, 907 with notes, 1,857 dependency edges, descriptions/design/AC) — is NOT ingested by the Origin route at all. The Origin captures the least informative beads file.
3. The architecturally correct home already exists in code: insights/work_effects.py BeadsIssueEffectAdapter reads the SAME interactions.jsonl as ObservedRepositoryEffect facts, and devtools/mandate_continuity_replay.py build_repository_claim_graph builds claim nodes from it. docs/internals.md 688-733 documents both. BEADS_ISSUE-as-Origin is a redundant second representation of data the archive already models correctly as effects/claims.
4. Revealed preference: fully wired for months (parser/detector/dispatch/OriginSpec), acquired nothing, nobody noticed. #3416's sources.beads_roots defaults to () — still zero ingested (measured: 0 beads-issue sessions among 23,296 in the live index).
5. Scaffolding rot: origin_specs.py:796 references stream_parser_path "beads.py:parse_beads_stream" — that function does not exist anywhere (dangling reference). Completeness mode is "proposed", never harvested from a real sample.

REMOVAL PATH (no shims, no deprecation theater — nothing ingested, zero migration risk): delete Origin.BEADS_ISSUE + Provider.BEADS, sources/parsers/beads.py + its tests, dispatch branches (dispatch.py 44/46/56/198/239/1033/1159/1260), _beads_spec + completeness mode (origin_specs.py 787-805, 997-1030), core/sources.py mappings (126-129, 158, 236, 254, 300); drop "beads-issue" from session_links dst_origin CHECK (derived-tier index bump, declare delta class — 0 affected rows measured, in-place fast-forward safe); remove #3416 beads_roots acquisition wiring (no users exist; hard removal is policy-compliant per no-compat-pre-adoption). Keep artifact-taxonomy shape classification (looks_like_beads_interaction) keyed off shape, so a stray uploaded ledger classifies as a non-session artifact instead of unknown-export sessions — same treatment hook events got in 31r1. BeadsIssueEffectAdapter and the claim-graph builder are untouched and become the sole consumers of the ledger.

WHAT IS NOT LOST: ledgers are git-tracked in their repos (durability is git's, not polylogue's); issue state-transition evidence (timestamps, old→new, close reasons carrying commit hashes) stays reachable via the effect adapter for 1vpm.6 reconciliation; bead ids in real sessions remain FTS-searchable (phrase "polylogue-x4s" already matches 248 real messages). What ingestion WOULD have added: +4% sessions, all synthetic protocol prose polluting exactly the FTS queries used to find real work on a bead.
notes: Follow-on filed: polylogue-5jnq (issues.jsonl as work-evidence issue nodes, 1vpm.6 adapter). Related open beads: polylogue-37t.13 (beads<->assertions boundary revisit — its premise 'beads-history ingestion landed (#2800)' refers to the Origin route this decision removes; re-anchor it on the work-evidence graph), polylogue-pbuh (typed pr-link records = the session↔PR leg of the three-way join).

title: session_commit.py ignores typed claude_pr_link/claude_bridge_session events and Claude-Session git trailers, regex-scans instead
description:
Two independent typed-signal-ignored gaps in polylogue/insights/session_commit.py, found during the 2026-07-31 heuristics audit (parallel to polylogue-pbuh/polylogue-1vpm.7's exemplars).

GAP 1 -- GitHub PR/issue refs. extract_github_refs() (session_commit.py:26-142) regexes raw session message text for https://github.com/.../pull/N, owner/repo#N, and bare #N -- acknowledged in its own comments as a false-positive-prone heuristic (bare #N can match heading anchors / arbitrary numbers). Meanwhile polylogue-pbuh's fix (already landed on this branch, commit 5e23e6abf / index v46) now persists the Claude Code pr-link sidecar record as a typed claude_pr_link session_event, and bridge-session as claude_bridge_session. VERIFIED live: sqlite3 index.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_events WHERE event_type='claude_pr_link'" -> 18,967 rows (167 distinct sessions); claude_bridge_session -> 12,154 rows. VERIFIED zero readers: grep -rn claude_pr_link polylogue/ (excluding the writer in code_parser.py) returns nothing -- session_commit.py, correlation_view.py, and every consumer of build_correlation_result still regex-scan text instead of reading these typed events. This is a fresh instance of the pbuh pattern that survived the pbuh fix landing: the parse-side fix shipped, the read side never got updated to use it.

GAP 2 -- session-to-commit attribution. detect_session_commits() (session_commit.py:256-363) attributes a git commit to an authoring session via time-window scan (+-2h around session timestamps) plus file-overlap scoring (score_file_overlap, confidence thresholded at 0.3) or an in-text commit-SHA regex match (explicit_ref, confidence 0.95 hardcoded). It never reads git commit trailers. This repo's own commit convention (CLAUDE.md, global agent instructions) appends 'Co-Authored-By: Claude ... ' plus 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_<id>' to every agent-authored commit -- a typed, zero-ambiguity session-authorship signal. VERIFIED: git log --all --format=%B | grep -oE 'Claude-Session: [^ ]+' | wc -l -> 116 commits in this repo alone carry the trailer; grep -rn 'Claude-Session\|Co-Authored-By' polylogue/ --include='*.py' returns zero hits anywhere in the codebase. Stronger evidence the fix was anticipated but never wired: the session_commits table schema itself (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:922) already declares detection_type TEXT CHECK(... IN ('time_window','file_overlap','explicit_ref','origin_reported')) -- 'origin_reported' is a live CHECK-constraint value with ZERO rows using it (VERIFIED: sqlite3 index.db "SELECT detection_type, COUNT(*) FROM session_commits GROUP BY detection_type" -> only explicit_ref, 2,990 rows). The schema slot for a typed session-commit link has existed, unused, while a scored heuristic fills the table instead.

NOT EVALUATED: no test in tests/unit/insights/test_session_commit.py asserts accuracy of file_overlap/time_window scoring against ground truth -- only the arithmetic of score_file_overlap() itself is unit-tested (confidence math, not hit-rate).

BLAST RADIUS: session_commits backs the PF-D1 receipts demo (polylogue-212.2/xyel), the provenance-carrying-PRs bead (polylogue-kph), and the Hermes forensics report (polylogue-fs1.4) -- all four read session-to-PR/commit linkage through this exact machinery. 2,990 live session_commits rows, all detection_type=explicit_ref (VERIFIED); repo breakdown polylogue=1,060, sinex=879, sinnix=495, sinity-lynchpin=104 (VERIFIED).
acceptance_criteria: 1. detect_session_commits (or a new higher-priority step ahead of it) parses git commit trailers (Co-Authored-By: Claude / Claude-Session: <url>) via git log --format=%B%n---%n and, when a trailer's session id matches an archived session, records a session_commits row with detection_type='origin_reported' and confidence=1.0, superseding time_window/file_overlap for that pair. 2. build_correlation_result (or its caller) reads claude_pr_link/claude_bridge_session typed session_events before falling back to extract_github_refs' text regex; the regex path is kept only as a fallback for sessions with no typed event, and its results are labeled distinctly from typed results in the output payload. 3. A live re-measure reports the before/after split of session_commits by detection_type, and the before/after count of PR/issue refs sourced from typed events vs regex. 4. tests/unit/insights/test_session_commit.py gains a fixture asserting the trailer-parse path takes priority over file_overlap/time_window for a commit carrying a matching Claude-Session trailer.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (self-correction, keep both versions visible per audit discipline): the original description implied the PERSISTED session_commits table (2,990 rows, all detection_type='explicit_ref') is filled by detect_session_commits()'s file-overlap/time-window scoring. VERIFIED that is wrong -- storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:4039-4063 shows session_commits is actually populated straight from session.git_commit_hash (a typed field the agent-runtime parser already reports, method='parser-git-meta', confidence hardcoded 1.0). This is a narrow but honest fact (HEAD at session capture time, not 'commit this session produced') and is NOT itself an instance of the audited pattern -- it already prefers a typed field.

The real, still-live gap is the ON-DEMAND correlation surface: build_correlation_result (session_commit.py:387-449) IS wired live -- api/archive.py:5406 and insights/correlation_view.py:60 both call it, reachable via the 'analyze correlation' CLI/API path (VERIFIED via grep, both call sites exist outside session_commit.py/its tests). THIS is where detect_session_commits' file-overlap/time-window scoring and extract_github_refs' text regex actually run, live, on every invocation -- and neither reads git commit trailers nor the typed claude_pr_link/claude_bridge_session session_events. The bead's AC1-AC4 stand unchanged: they target this on-demand path, not the persisted table. cijx.1's own notes (read after filing this bead) independently confirm session_commits has 0 readers and stores a different, narrower fact than commit attribution -- consistent with this correction, not contradicting it.
