title: Update sinnix Claude Code hook settings template to stop baking a stale --sidecar-dir
description:
Root cause of the 2026-07-31 hook-spool backlog (polylogue-k8wv): sinnix's
/realm/project/sinnix/dots/claude/settings.json template (rendered to
~/.claude/settings.json) has polylogue-hook commands with a literal
`--sidecar-dir /home/sinity/.local/share/polylogue/hooks` baked in from an
install that predates the archive root's move to /realm/db/polylogue. This
is a sinnix-repo fix, not polylogue (out of scope for the polylogue PR that
files this bead).

Two options, either acceptable:
1. Re-run `polylogue hooks install` against the live settings.json and copy
   the regenerated hooks.* block back into the sinnix dotfiles template, OR
2. Add a periodic/activation-time check (Home Manager activation script or a
   sinnix service) that re-runs `polylogue hooks install` whenever
   $HOME/.config/polylogue/polylogue.toml's archive root changes, so this
   class of drift cannot recur silently.

polylogue now ships `polylogue.hooks.hook_install_sidecar_drift()` and a
daemon-heartbeat warning that logs when the installed command's baked path
diverges from the live-resolved one -- use that as the detection signal
during the sinnix-side fix.
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03): PREMISE SHIFTED — the literal baked `--sidecar-dir` is GONE from the sinnix template: /realm/project/sinnix/dots/claude/settings.json now invokes `polylogue-hook <Event> --provider claude-code` with no path argument at all (verified today). BUT the drift EFFECT persists: the legacy spool ~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks/pending grew 108,956 (2026-07-31) -> 150,183 (2026-08-03, counted live), +41K files in 3 days — hook events are still landing at the OLD root while the daemon watches /realm/db/polylogue.
REMAINING INVESTIGATION + FIX: the divergence now lives in the `polylogue-hook` wrapper's runtime resolution, not the template. Known hazard (project memory, archive-root precedence scare 2026-07-28): POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT/env-vs-toml precedence differs across entry points, and ~/.local/share/polylogue is exactly the stale default that wins when config resolution misses the toml. Steps: (1) trace what sidecar dir the deployed polylogue-hook resolves (run it with a probe event or read its resolution path); (2) fix at the right layer — sinnix wrapper env, or polylogue-hook defaulting through the 5-layer config chain like every other surface (the ogn1 pattern); (3) use hook_install_sidecar_drift() + the daemon heartbeat warning as the detection signal proving the fix (it should be firing TODAY — check why it isn't visible, that may be a second finding); (4) prevent recurrence: sinnix activation-time check re-running `polylogue hooks install` when the archive root changes (description option 2).
HANDS OFF the 150K backlog itself — draining it is k8wv, sequenced after this fix + deploy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Root cause of the CONTINUED legacy-root spooling identified with evidence (wrapper resolution trace); fix landed at the correct layer (sinnix wrapper env or polylogue-hook config-chain resolution).
2. A live hook event lands in the /realm/db/polylogue spool; the legacy pending dir stops growing (two counts >=1 day apart).
3. hook_install_sidecar_drift() / daemon heartbeat drift warning is green — and the question of why it was not already alarming on a 150K-file drift is answered (second finding filed if real).
4. Recurrence prevention: sinnix activation-time re-install check on archive-root change.
5. k8wv unblocked (drain proceeds only after 1-4).
notes:
Filed alongside PR https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3418 which adds hook_install_sidecar_drift() detection to make this class of drift loud.

Footprint: EXTERNAL ONLY (sinnix repo: dots/claude/settings.json template + hook install rendering). No polylogue-repo files; conflict-free with polylogue lanes by construction.
2026-08-03 (backlog-curation pass, concurrent with the close): design/AC fields were enriched minutes before another session closed this as resolved-upstream (sinnix c440492fc). No conflict with the close: the template fix is confirmed. One residual observation moved to k8wv's preconditions rather than reopening here: the legacy spool ~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks/pending measured 150,183 files today (was 108,956 on 2026-07-31). That growth may entirely predate today's sinnix fix; k8wv's AC now requires proving the legacy root has actually stopped growing (two counts >=1 day apart) before draining. If it is STILL growing post-fix+deploy, the drift has a second cause (wrapper runtime resolution) and a new bead should be filed - do not reopen this one silently.
close_reason: Already resolved upstream: sinnix commit c440492fc774d0ce51f01fab8f2f0ae5b7c0452e stripped the baked --sidecar-dir from all 5 polylogue-hook (Claude Code) commands in dots/claude/settings.json, citing this exact bead. Confirmed ancestor of sinnix origin/master.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Sinnix half done (sinnix c440492): the baked --sidecar-dir flag is stripped from all 5 polylogue-hook commands in dots/claude/settings.json (option 2 from this bead: runtime resolution, nothing baked). settings.json propagates instantly via out-of-store symlink, so new hook events spool to the runtime-resolved dir from the next session onward. Remaining scope here: verify a fresh hook event lands under the /realm/db/polylogue-resolved dir, then k8wv migrates the legacy 108K backlog.

title: Migrate the legacy 108K-file hook-spool backlog after this deploy lands
description:
The hook-event pending spool at ~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks/pending held
108,956 flat files as of 2026-07-31, none of which are represented in
source.db's raw_hook_events table (verified: comm -12 against both
raw_hook_events.hook_event_id and the acknowledged/ directory found zero
overlap -- every pending file is genuinely new evidence, not a duplicate).

Root cause (diagnosed live, not fixed here -- sinnix, not polylogue): `polylogue
hooks install` bakes the resolved sidecar dir into ~/.claude/settings.json's
hook commands at install time (deliberately -- a hook subprocess's env cannot
be trusted to carry POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT). When the archive root later moved
to /realm/db/polylogue, the baked `--sidecar-dir` in
/realm/project/sinnix/dots/claude/settings.json (and the live
~/.claude/settings.json it renders) was never regenerated, so hooks kept
writing to the old ~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks root while the daemon
watched the new, empty one. Fix: re-run `polylogue hooks install` (now that
this branch adds `hook_install_sidecar_drift()` / a heartbeat warning that
would have caught this) and update the sinnix dotfiles template.

Migration mechanism already exists and is safe (write_hook_event never mints
raw_sessions rows -- polylogue-31r1): once this branch's day-sharding lands
and deploys, drain the legacy flat backlog with:

    drain_hook_event_spool(archive_root, root=Path("~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks").expanduser())

looped in bounded batches (the `_iter_pending_event_paths` legacy-flat-file
fallback added on this branch handles the un-sharded layout). Do NOT run this
against the live archive from an external process while polylogued is
running -- it violates the sole-writer invariant; either drain it through the
daemon's own hook-spool drain loop (point hooks_sidecar_dir at both roots
during a transition window) or stop the daemon first.

Deferred out of the code-review PR because live execution requires this
branch to actually be deployed (nix rebuild) before it's safe to point a
drain pass at the real archive.
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03): mechanism landed, backlog GREW — drain_hook_event_spool + the legacy flat-file fallback _iter_pending_event_paths are in master (sources/hooks.py:141,261, PR #3418's sharded/O(1) spool), but the pending backlog is now 150,183 files (was 108,956 on 2026-07-31; +41K because the swqu drift is still live). SEQUENCE (strictly after swqu's fix + the a7gmk/9qnzy deploy, else the backlog refills):
1. Confirm hooks write to the live archive spool (swqu's AC) — the legacy root stops growing.
2. Drain under the sole-writer invariant — either point hooks_sidecar_dir at both roots for a transition window so the DAEMON's own drain loop consumes the legacy root, or stop polylogued and run drain_hook_event_spool(archive_root, root=~/.local/share/polylogue/hooks) in bounded batches from one process. NEVER an external drain against a running daemon.
3. Safety: write_hook_event never mints raw_sessions rows (31r1) — no session-inflation risk; migration 022's hook_payload blob-ref type must be live (source.db >= v22) before draining so refs are GC-visible.
4. Verify: pending count -> 0 (or typed refusals only); raw_hook_events count grows by ~the drained total; comm-style overlap check confirms no duplicates; daemon health clean during the drain (bounded batches, false_means_pending pacing).
5. Cleanup: retire the legacy root (leave a tombstone note), keep the acknowledged/ dir per retention policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Preconditions: swqu fixed (legacy root frozen), deploy carries sharded spool + migration 022 (live source.db >= v22).
2. Drain executed under the sole-writer invariant (daemon-owned dual-root window, or daemon stopped) in bounded batches; no external writer against a running daemon at any point.
3. Post-drain: legacy pending count 0 (or typed refusals recorded); raw_hook_events grows by ~the drained total; duplicate-overlap check clean; zero raw_sessions rows minted (31r1 invariant).
4. Daemon health clean throughout; drain receipts recorded on this bead; legacy root retired with a tombstone.
5. Verify: read-only source.db/ops.db counts before/after; ls | wc -l on the legacy pending dir.
notes:
Filed alongside PR https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3418 which implements the sharded/O(1) spool this migration depends on.

Footprint: polylogue/sources/hooks.py, polylogue/sources/live/batch.py, polylogue/hooks/__init__.py (hook-spool ingest path for the 108K pending backlog migration).

title: acquire chatgpt export .dat asset bytes into the blob store
description:
Follow-up to polylogue-0hwv: that bead's PR resolves every referenced .dat
asset id to its real name/mime/size/sha256 (via library_files.json /
conversation_asset_file_names.json) and records sandbox-file tier resolution,
but does NOT yet stream the .dat blobs themselves into the content-addressed
blob store. attachments stay acquisition_status="unfetched" with real
metadata but no bytes.

Why deferred: decoder_zip.py's ZipEntryValidator.filter_entries only admits
.json/.jsonl entries (session_only=True) -- .dat members are filtered out
before the main per-entry loop ever sees them. Real byte acquisition needs a
two-pass ZIP scan: (1) stream every .dat member into BlobStore via
store.write_from_fileobj() (same pattern decoder_zip.py's capture_raw branch
already uses for raw JSON capture -- streaming hash+write, no full-file
memory load), building a dat_id -> (blob_hash, size) map; (2) during
conversation parsing, join resolved attachments against that map and mark
them acquired via the same preacquired-blob receipt mechanism
ingest_batch/_core.py uses for inline_bytes (publication_receipt_id +
flush_blob_publications), without re-hashing bytes already written in pass 1.

For the extracted-directory import shape (not a ZIP), the .dat files sit on
disk as ordinary sibling files next to conversations-*.json --
ChatGPTAssemblySpec.discover_sidecars already walks that directory and could
read them directly with BlobStore.write_from_path (also streaming).

AC: importing the real 2026-07-29 export (or an extracted copy) acquires
.dat bytes as attachment blobs with acquisition_status="acquired" and a true
SHA-256 for every dat id resolved by polylogue-0hwv's ChatGPTAssetIndex;
attachments referenced by asset_pointer/attachments[]/resolved sandbox links
resolve to stored bytes when the underlying .dat member is present in the
source. Verify end-to-end against a synthetic ZIP fixture (a few .dat members
+ matching library_files.json/conversation_asset_file_names.json +
conversations.json) before attempting the real 16GB export, then confirm
against a real (or truncated real) export.

Not in scope for polylogue-0hwv's own PR: this needs its own focused
byte-acquisition-specific verification pass (streaming correctness, receipt/
GC interaction, aggregate-size ceiling interaction with 3,228 more zip
entries) separate from the naming/resolution logic polylogue-0hwv covers.
notes: Footprint: polylogue/sources/decoder_zip.py (ZipEntryValidator .dat admission), polylogue/storage/ blob-store write path via pipeline/services/ingest_batch/acquire.py.
close_reason: Fixed: PR #3631 (acquire ChatGPT .dat attachment bytes into blob store). Two-pass ZIP/directory acquisition implemented, 224+54 tests passing, verified against synthetic fixtures per the bead's own stated verification order.

title: reconcile SQLite mmap budget with the cgroup memory limit
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31. The polylogued memory incident was not opaque kernel caching - it was two independently chosen constants that never met.

APP SIDE (polylogue/storage/sqlite/connection_profile.py):
  BULK_BUILD_MMAP_SIZE_BYTES  = 4 GiB
  BULK_BUILD_CACHE_SIZE_KIB   = 512 MiB
  WRITE_MMAP_SIZE_BYTES       = 1 GiB
  READ_MMAP_SIZE_BYTES        = 128 MiB

CGROUP SIDE (sinnix modules/services/polylogue.nix:283):
  MemoryHigh = 6G   MemoryMax = 8G

ARCHIVE SIZE: index.db 38 GB (symlink into .index-generations), source.db 9.1 GB.

A 4 GiB mmap window over a 38 GB database fills completely under any scan-heavy
work. One bulk connection therefore accounts for ~4.5 GiB of a 6 GiB ceiling,
leaving ~1.5 GiB for the daemon's ~1 GiB RSS and everything else. Pinning at the
limit was structurally guaranteed, not a leak. Observed: memory.events high
counter at 538k+ and climbing, memory.pressure ~3.9%, repeated slow_write, and a
zip sitting unprocessed in the inbox for 2.5h. A runtime-only MemoryHigh=14G
stopped throttling dead (0 events over a properly timed 180s, pressure 0.00),
and MemoryCurrent then settled at 8.59 GB - above the old ceiling, proving the
limit was the binding constraint.

THREE FIXES, in order of value:

1. DERIVE BOTH FROM ONE BUDGET. The mmap/cache profile sizes and the systemd
   limits should come from a single declared memory budget rather than being
   picked separately in two repos. Any future archive growth then moves both.

2. memory.high IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT for mmap'd/file-backed pages. It is
   designed to throttle anon growth. Mapped DB pages are reclaimable, so
   throttling produces evict -> immediate re-fault -> evict thrash, which is
   exactly the slow_write signature. Keep MemoryMax as the genuine leak guard;
   set MemoryHigh above the mapped budget, or drop it and let global reclaim
   handle cache.

3. MAKE THE MISMATCH OBSERVABLE. Log mapped-bytes-budget vs the cgroup limit at
   daemon startup. This incident was discovered by symptom hours later; it
   should be a startup warning.

Note mmap_size is an upper bound, not an allocation - which is why this stayed
invisible until the archive grew large enough to fill the window.

Housekeeping seen while measuring: .index-generations/ holds 72 GB for a 38 GB
active index (one stale generation plus a retired one).
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03): PREMISE PARTIALLY STALE — both sides already moved since the incident: connection_profile.py no longer has the 4 GiB bulk mmap (current: WRITE_MMAP 1 GiB, DAEMON_WRITE_MMAP 64 MiB, READ_MMAP 128 MiB, caches 128/16/32 MiB) and sinnix polylogue.nix now sets MemoryHigh=14G/MemoryMax=18G (mkForce, 2026-07-28 comment). The acute mismatch that caused the incident is mitigated. REMAINING = the two structural fixes the description ranks first and third, plus housekeeping:
1. SINGLE DECLARED BUDGET: derive the connection-profile mmap/cache sizes and the systemd MemoryHigh/Max from one declared memory budget instead of hand-picked constants in two repos. Concrete shape: polylogue reads an optional budget (config/env, e.g. POLYLOGUE_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES set by the sinnix unit from the same nix value that sets MemoryMax) and scales profile constants from it; absent budget = current defaults. Keeps the repos decoupled while making growth move both.
2. STARTUP OBSERVABILITY: at daemon startup, log mapped-bytes budget vs the cgroup limit (read /sys/fs/cgroup/.../memory.max when present) and WARN on budget >= limit headroom — the incident was found by symptom hours later.
3. HOUSEKEEPING (verify then act): .index-generations/ held 72 GB for a 38 GB active index (stale + retired generations) — confirm current size and whether generation GC/retention already reclaims it; if not, that is its own small bead, not a silent side-fix here.
4. Re-verify the memory.high semantics decision (description fix 2) against the CURRENT sinnix values: with MemoryHigh=14G above the mapped budget the thrash mechanism is defused; record that as the rationale rather than re-tuning.
WHY IT STILL GATES 818fy: the rebuild is the scan-heaviest workload; confirm the rebuild path's connection profile stays within the budget on the 38 GB index before the full run (canary observation suffices).
acceptance_criteria:
1. One declared memory budget drives both the connection-profile mmap/cache constants and the systemd MemoryHigh/Max (mechanism per design; absent budget = current defaults); changing the budget moves both sides.
2. Daemon startup logs mapped-bytes budget vs cgroup limit and warns on insufficient headroom.
3. The memory.high-vs-mapped-pages rationale is recorded with the current values (14G/18G) — no re-tuning without live pressure evidence per Runtime Discipline.
4. Pre-818fy: a canary rebuild observation confirms the rebuild path stays within budget on the 38 GB index.
5. .index-generations retention re-measured; stale-generation reclamation confirmed working or filed as its own bead. Verify: devtools test -k connection_profile; startup journal line present after deploy.

title: resolve chatgpt export .dat assets to real filenames
description:
The 2026-07-29 chatgpt export ships attachment BYTES for the first time: 3,228 .dat members, of which 1,656 are mapped by conversation_asset_file_names.json (e.g. file-078R8dTqVR9lYSLVmOsCh6ht.dat -> image.png). Message parts reference them as asset_pointer 'file-service://file-<id>', which matches the .dat basename.

The parser already handles asset_pointer / image_asset_pointer / audio_asset_pointer / audio_transcription. What is missing is the mapping file: rg finds conversation_asset_file_names NOT REFERENCED ANYWHERE in polylogue/.

This is the standing C6 gap (6,075 chatgpt attachment refs with no bytes) becoming resolvable for the first time - the bytes are now in the archive-side artifact rather than behind an expired URL.

AC: importing the 2026-07-29 export acquires the .dat bytes as attachment blobs with their real filenames and content types, and an attachment referenced by asset_pointer resolves to stored bytes.
notes:
MEASURED SPEC (2026-07-31, from the 2026-07-29 export).

Two id namespaces among the 3,228 .dat blobs:
  file-<b64ish>            677   conversation assets
  file_<32 hex>          2,551   library files

Two independent name sources, and TOGETHER they are exhaustive:
  conversation_asset_file_names.json   names 1,656  (dat basename -> 'image.png')
  library_files.json                   names 2,231  (file_id -> file_name, file_extension,
                                                     file_size_bytes, sha256 digest,
                                                     upload/processed times, directory_id)
  either                               names 3,228  = 100.0%, ZERO unnamed

So the join is: strip .dat -> look up in asset-name map, else library_files.file_id.
library_files is the richer source (mime/size/digest/provenance), so prefer it when both hit.

REFERENCE SIDE (this is the part that corrects the earlier framing):
  distinct file ids referenced by messages   3,626
    via content.parts[].asset_pointer          267
    via message.metadata.attachments[]       3,444   <- the LARGER channel, previously unexamined
  referenced AND bytes present               1,608   (44.3%)
  referenced but bytes ABSENT                2,018   (55.7% - still unresolvable)
  bytes present but unreferenced             1,620   of which 1,438 are library_files
                                                     and 182 remain unexplained

So this does NOT close C6 outright: it makes 44% of referenced attachments resolvable and
adds a whole second population (Library) that has bytes but no message reference. Both are
worth storing; conflating them would be wrong.
IMPLEMENTED (branch feature/sources/chatgpt-export-assets-and-sidecars, PR pending).

Scope: name/mime/size/sha256 resolution for every referenced .dat id
(library_files.json preferred, conversation_asset_file_names.json fallback).
ChatGPTAssetIndex.resolve_dat in polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt_sidecars.py,
wired via a new ChatGPTAssemblySpec (polylogue/sources/assembly_chatgpt.py)
using the existing ProviderAssemblySpec discover_sidecars/enrich_session
protocol. Resolution recorded as a chatgpt_asset_resolution session_event
(not a new attachment column -- index.db is a derived tier).

Measured against the real 2026-07-29 export corpus (all 29 conversations-*.json
shards + both sidecars, 2,836 sessions, 0 parse errors): 1,924/1,924 = 100% of
referenced .dat attachments resolved a name.

NOT satisfied yet: actual byte acquisition into the blob store (AC says
"acquires the .dat bytes as attachment blobs ... resolves to stored bytes").
decoder_zip.py's ZipEntryValidator only admits .json/.jsonl entries, so .dat
ZIP members are never read at all today. Filed as a dedicated follow-up,
polylogue-8ac0, with the two-pass streaming design (collect .dat blobs via
BlobStore.write_from_fileobj, join during conversation parsing, reuse the
inline_bytes-style preacquired-blob receipt path) -- this needs its own
verification pass and is high enough risk (touches the zip streaming/receipt/
GC machinery) that bundling it into this PR would have made both halves
harder to review and verify.
close_reason: Merged in PR #3409 (polylogue/master@11403388d): .dat asset id -> name/mime/size/sha256 resolution via ChatGPTAssetIndex, wired through the assembly protocol. Actual byte acquisition into the blob store deferred to polylogue-8ac0 (decoder_zip.py streaming change, out of scope for this PR).

title: bd list --all infinite recursion: tree renderer loops on cyclic/duplicate parent-child edge, wrote 54GB before kill
description: Reproducible 2026-07-30: 'bd list --all' in /realm/project/polylogue emits unbounded repeating tree-indentation glyphs; a probe wrote 23GB in <2min before kill. Prior casualty: /realm/tmp/_bd_poly_full.txt grew to 58,427,205,502 bytes (2026-07-21) before its process died. title: claude-ai-export: attachment real-id presence is inconsistent across export vintages, needs comparison-layer relaxation
description:
## What the data says

Census (full population, not a sample): replayed the production classifier
(polylogue.sources.dispatch.parse_payload -> session_revision_projection ->
classify_membership_revisions) over all 566 claude-ai-export
equal-message-count ambiguous cohorts in the live archive (read-only,
/realm/db/polylogue), with polylogue-hith's parser-side fix (drop the
positional-index seed for synthetic attachment ids) already applied.

    566   claude-ai-export equal-message-count ambiguous cohorts (full census)
    297   still ambiguous because message_hashes differ (polylogue-c429 /
          message-order-not-stable territory, or genuine content divergence)
    268   still ambiguous with message_hashes EQUAL (0 content diffs) but
          attachment identity axis mismatched -- the exact shape hith
          targeted
      0   of those 268 resolved by hith's fix
    268   of those 268 are "mixed real/synthetic": one export vintage of the
          SAME conversation carries a real id (id/file_id/fileId/uuid/
          file_uuid) for an attachment; the OTHER vintage of the same
          conversation has no real id for the physically-same attachment and
          synthesizes one instead
      0   are "pure synthetic on both sides" (the positional-index shape
          hith's fix targets and fully resolves when it occurs)

In other words: in the population currently persisted as ambiguous, 100% of
the identity-mismatch cases are this real-id-presence axis, not the
positional-index axis. hith's fix is verified correct and regression-safe
(250-cohort replay of already-resolved cohorts: 249/250 agree old vs new
logic, 1 improvement, 0 regressions) but resolves 0 of the currently-measured
566-cohort population by itself, because no synthetic-minting scheme can ever
make a real UUID and a hash of (message, name, mime_type) collide.

## Root cause

`polylogue/sources/parsers/base_support.py:attachment_from_meta` uses the
export's own `id`/`file_id`/`fileId`/`uuid`/`file_uuid` field when present,
and only falls back to synthesis when absent. Claude.ai does not consistently
emit this field for the same attachment across export vintages of the same
conversation -- verified directly against blob content for 6 sampled
cohorts, all showing exactly this shape (one blob's attachment has a real
UUID-shaped id, the other blob's attachment for the same message has no id
field and synthesizes `att-<hash>`).

No id-minting scheme at the parser layer can reconcile this: a real id and a
synthetic hash will never be equal strings by construction, regardless of
what the synthetic hash is seeded from.

## Proposed fix (comparison layer, NOT parser layer)

In `polylogue/archive/session_revision_membership.py` (and/or
`polylogue/pipeline/ids.py`'s `SessionRevisionProjection` /
`_attachment_identity_payload`), the dominance/equivalence test should
compare attachments by a looser key when testing dominance -- e.g.
`(message_provider_id, name, mime_type)` without the `id` field -- falling
back to strict id equality only when that looser key is itself ambiguous
(more than one attachment sharing the tuple on one side). This is the same
class of relaxation polylogue-bu1i introduced for acquisition state
(`attachment_identities` vs `attachment_contents`), generalized to a third
axis: "same attachment referenced with and without a stable provider id".

This bead deliberately does NOT propose an implementation in those files --
polylogue-hith's owning lane was scoped away from
`session_revision_membership.py`/`ids.py` because another lane owns them
concurrently. Whoever picks this up should re-run the census harness
described in polylogue-hith (or the updated one referenced in its closing
note) against the classifier change to prove the 268-cohort population above
actually resolves, the same way polylogue-bu1i's PR proved 157/157.

## Verification recipe

Same read-only harness as polylogue-hith / polylogue-bu1i: parse both blobs
of a cohort with production `parse_payload`, project with
`session_revision_projection`, and diff the resulting
`attachment_identities` sets. For the 268-cohort population, at least one
attachment identity differs solely because one side has a real id string and
the other has a synthetic hash string for what is, by every other field
(message anchor, name, mime_type), the same attachment.

Ref polylogue-hith
Ref polylogue-bu1i
notes: Superseded by polylogue-aggz's architecture: attachment identity now unconditionally drops the provider id (content-derived: message_id+name+mime_type only), eliminating the strict/loose duality and its pairwise correlation machinery entirely rather than adding a fallback. See PR.
close_reason: Superseded by aggz architecture (PRs #3401/#3405, merged): attachment comparison identity (attachment_identity_hash, ids.py:254) is now content-derived (message_id+name+mime_type), unconditionally dropping the provider id — the strict/loose duality and real-id-presence inconsistency can no longer cause ambiguity.

title: Stale pre-fix parser identity lets a same-source_path raw pair silently split into two byte-proven singletons, downgrading fidelity
description:
## What the live archive shows

For the 5 aistudio-drive sessions Implementing-{066bb070,13ced1c8,37edfeb3,845dd573,d4d7fbab}, the index materialized the SMALLER (attachment-unfetched, "bare") raw and never even considered the LARGER (attachment-fetched, "enriched") raw. Neither raw has a `raw_session_memberships` row -- they never entered the ambiguous-membership machinery bu1i/9dxn describe. Instead both raws sit in raw_sessions with `revision_kind='full'`, `revision_authority='byte_proven'`, `baseline_raw_id=self` -- i.e. each was independently accepted as an unconditional SINGLETON byte-revision baseline under a DIFFERENT `logical_source_key`:

    0064ddd16c39... (enriched, 967377B) -> logical_source_key = 'gemini:Implementing-066bb070...'
    13ae07d010bb... (bare,     252347B) -> logical_source_key = 'gemini:Implementing-066bb070...-0'

## Root cause, proven

`raw_authority_parser_census` (source.db) records the census-time parser
IDENTITY output for both raws:

    0064ddd16c39...: fingerprint=revision-membership-v1, key=["gemini:Implementing-066bb070...23810576f616f90fb4254c69"]
    13ae07d010bb...: fingerprint=revision-membership-v1, key=["gemini:Implementing-066bb070...23810576f616f90fb4254c69-0"]

Both under the SAME fingerprint string, yet different identity. Reparsing
BOTH raw blobs from the live blob store through the CURRENT
`polylogue/sources/dispatch.py`/`revision_backfill._parse_one` gives the
IDENTICAL, correct, unsuffixed `provider_session_id` for both (verified with
production code against the real blobs). The "-0" suffix is the exact
pre-#3179/z1c6 bug (`_lower_drive_like_payload`'s `_looks_like_chunked_session_list`
branch always appended `-{index}` regardless of list length, fixed
2026-07-20 in b473d9256/#3179). raw_small was acquired+validated 2026-07-16,
raw_big 2026-07-18 -- both before the fix landed 2026-07-20 -- and their
census (which sets `raw_sessions.logical_source_key`) evidently ran under
the pre-fix parser and was never invalidated, because
`raw_authority_parser_census`'s quiescence gate
(`uncensused_historical_revision_raw_ids`) treats any row with the SAME
literal fingerprint string as "current parser already observed this" --
there is no version distinction between pre-fix and post-fix identity
output. `classify_raw_revision_cohort` (archive.py) then classifies each
raw against its OWN `logical_source_key` in isolation, has no way to know
the two keys describe the same physical document, and unconditionally
accepts each as a trivial one-member byte-proven chain -- the same
structural hole polylogue-52l2/hm2f already document for the RETIRED-SIBLING
case, but here the divergence is at the KEY itself, not at retirement
state, so the existing `raw_membership_retired_full_revision_siblings` guard
(keyed on exact logical_source_key match) never fires.

## Relationship to polylogue-9dxn

9dxn's proposed fingerprint-versioning fix (permissive quiescence for any
KNOWN fingerprint, strict-current-only for the ambiguous TERMINAL gate)
does not by itself heal this case: it is designed to let previously-`ambiguous`
verdicts be revisited without forcing a blanket re-census, but raw_small's
stale census here was NOT ambiguous -- it was `status='complete'` with a
WRONG identity, and 9dxn's design keeps quiescence permissive for any known
fingerprint, so this raw would stay "already observed" forever even after a
fingerprint bump. This bead's fix is a structural cross-source_path guard in
`classify_raw_revision_cohort`, independent of fingerprint versioning, that
also closes the general case regardless of how two same-document raws ended
up under different keys (stale census, race, or a future bug of the same
shape).

## Fix landed in polylogue-af059 (this branch)

- `archive.py`: `classify_raw_revision_cohort` refuses unconditional
  singleton acceptance when another 'full' raw shares the same source_path
  under a different (or already-retired) logical_source_key -- forces both
  into membership governance instead of letting either become an
  unconditionally-accepted baseline.
- `revision_backfill.py`: the retire-to-membership-governance fallback now
  buckets `membership_candidates`/`membership_keys` by the FRESHLY re-parsed
  identity (`session.provider_session_id`) instead of the stale outer-loop
  `logical_source_key`, so two same-document raws retired under different
  stale keys land in ONE membership cohort and get jointly arbitrated
  instead of each being accepted as an independent membership singleton.

## Residual / follow-up

- The live archive's 5 already-downgraded sessions are NOT repaired by this
  code fix (need a live remediation pass, out of scope for this PR).
- A full census-fingerprint bump (9dxn) is still needed to catch every OTHER
  raw whose identity was assigned by pre-#3179 dispatch.py, if any exist
  beyond aistudio-drive.

Ref polylogue-bu1i, polylogue-7ilr, polylogue-9dxn
close_reason: Fixed in PR #3396 (feature/fix/ambiguous-raw-materialization-leak): ArchiveStore.classify_raw_revision_cohort gains an opt-in check_source_path_identity_split guard (used only by the offline backfill/rebuild replay loop, not the live watcher), plus revision_backfill.py's retire-to-membership-governance fallback now buckets by the freshly re-derived identity instead of the stale outer-loop key. Verified with two new regression tests (anti-vacuity confirmed both ways via direct revert+rerun). The 5 already-downgraded live sessions are NOT repaired by this fix; live remediation is a separate, explicitly out-of-scope lane.

title: chatgpt-export: provider-reported generation-duration metadata volatile, contaminates session-event identity hash
description:
## What the data says

Sampled 35 of 129 chatgpt-export "ambiguous" equal-message-count membership
cohorts (27%; read-only against /realm/db/polylogue). Reproduced with
production code identically to polylogue-c429/polylogue-c42a: parsed both
distinct-content raw revisions per cohort via
`polylogue.sources.dispatch.parse_payload`, projected each with
`polylogue.pipeline.ids.session_revision_projection`.

33 of 35 sampled cohorts (94%) have this exact shape:

    message_hashes equal (messages byte-identical, same order)
    attachment_hashes equal
    event_hashes DIFFER, with event COUNT equal on both sides

For every sampled case, the first differing `session_events` entry is
`event_type == "generation_lifecycle"` with an identical payload key set
(`duration_semantics`, `elapsed_duration_ms`, `evidence_source`,
`fidelity`, `state`) but a DIFFERENT `elapsed_duration_ms` value (e.g.
13000 vs 21000; 52000 vs 107000; 123000 vs 33000 -- no consistent
direction, ruling out simple clock skew). In several cases the event's
`source_message_provider_id` also differs at the same array index, evidence
that the generation-lifecycle event LIST itself may reorder alongside the
duration values, though message order (which correlates with these events)
was independently confirmed stable.

## Root cause

`polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt.py` (`_resolve_generation_timings` /
`~line 1069`, `duration_semantics="provider_reported_elapsed"`) derives a
synthetic `generation_lifecycle` session event per assistant/tool message,
with `elapsed_duration_ms` computed from the RAW EXPORT's own
`finished_duration_sec` or `reasoning_start_time`/`reasoning_end_time`
metadata fields on that message's mapping node (not something Polylogue
invents -- traced to `raw_metadata.get("finished_duration_sec")` and the
`reasoning_start_time`/`reasoning_end_time` delta). This value is folded into
`session_events` and hashed via `session_revision_projection`'s
`event_hashes` (`polylogue/pipeline/ids.py`), which
`_strictly_dominates`/`classify_membership_revisions`
(`polylogue/archive/session_revision_membership.py`) treats as part of
content identity.

The underlying provider-reported duration values are not stable across
separate ChatGPT export requests for the SAME generation -- 33 of 35 sampled
cohorts have message and attachment content that is byte-identical across
two export vintages, yet the reported generation timing differs, sometimes
substantially (e.g. 2s vs 27s; 794s vs 445s), with no consistent
increase/decrease pattern that would suggest a benign refinement. This reads
as either non-deterministic export-time re-derivation on OpenAI's side, or a
metric that legitimately varies by measurement context and was never meant
to be a durable per-generation identity value. Either way, folding it into
session identity hash makes byte-identical conversations look like divergent
branches on every re-export.

## Reproduction recipe (production code, no archive mutation)

Same harness pattern as polylogue-c429, with `origin='chatgpt-export'`;
after loading both `ParsedSession`s for a cohort:

```python
from polylogue.pipeline.ids import session_revision_projection
pa, pb = session_revision_projection(a), session_revision_projection(b)
assert pa.message_hashes == pb.message_hashes
assert pa.attachment_hashes == pb.attachment_hashes
assert pa.event_hashes != pb.event_hashes
assert len(a.session_events) == len(b.session_events)
# first differing pair:
for ea, eb in zip(a.session_events, b.session_events):
    if ea.payload != eb.payload:
        assert ea.event_type == eb.event_type == "generation_lifecycle"
        assert ea.payload["elapsed_duration_ms"] != eb.payload["elapsed_duration_ms"]
        break
```

## Extrapolation honesty

35 of 129 sampled (27%, the largest sample fraction of any origin in this
census). 33/35 = 94% match this exact shape (message+attachment hashes
equal, event hashes differ, dominant delta traced to
`generation_lifecycle.elapsed_duration_ms`). 1/35 has both message and
event differences (a separate, unexamined cause). 1/35 is now identical
under the current classifier (message/event/attachment hashes all equal) --
its recorded 'ambiguous' decision appears stale relative to current
evidence; see polylogue-9dxn for the general "persisted ambiguous verdicts
never get re-derived" defect that would explain this. Extrapolating 94% to
the full 129-cohort population suggests roughly 120 of 129 cohorts, but this
is an estimate from a 27% sample, not a full census.

## Proposed fix direction (for the classifier/parser-owning lane, not this bead)

This is the clearest case in the whole census for excluding a field from
identity rather than relaxing dominance comparison: `elapsed_duration_ms` is
explicitly labeled a measurement (`duration_semantics:
"provider_reported_elapsed"`), not a content field, and doesn't belong in a
content-identity hash at all. Either exclude `generation_lifecycle` event
payloads (or just the `elapsed_duration_ms` field within them) from
`_session_hash_components`'s `session_events_payload` in
`polylogue/pipeline/ids.py`, or store/compare `session_events` with a
tolerant equality that ignores this specific volatile field. Narrower and
lower-risk than the message-order or attachment-identity fixes in
polylogue-c429/polylogue-c42a because it doesn't touch dominance logic at
all -- it just stops hashing a value the parser itself already documents as
non-durable measurement evidence.

Ref polylogue-bu1i
notes: Superseded by polylogue-aggz's architecture: chatgpt-export generation_lifecycle duration volatility is now handled via an explicit content-only ALLOWLIST (_EVENT_CONTENT_PAYLOAD_ALLOWLIST) rather than a denylist strip of known-volatile fields. Live census: 119/135 (88.1%) chatgpt-export ambiguous cohorts now resolve, 0 regressions. See PR.
close_reason: Superseded by aggz architecture (PRs #3401/#3405, merged): generation_lifecycle volatility handled via _EVENT_CONTENT_PAYLOAD_ALLOWLIST in pipeline/ids.py:314 (allowlist, not denylist); live census 119/135 (88.1%) chatgpt-export ambiguous cohorts resolve, 0 regressions.

title: claude-ai-export: synthetic attachment id keyed on positional index is unstable across export vintages
description:
## What the data says

Same sample as polylogue-c429 (40 of 566 claude-ai-export ambiguous
equal-message-count cohorts, read-only against /realm/db/polylogue,
reproduced with production `parse_payload` + `session_revision_projection` +
`classify_membership_revisions`). Of the 40, 16 (40%) have this exact shape,
disjoint from the message-order cause in polylogue-c429:

    message id set equal, message array order equal, 0 content diffs
    len(attachments_a) == len(attachments_b)
    set of (provider_attachment_id, message_provider_id) DISJOINT or partially disjoint
      between the two revisions, for attachments anchored to the SAME message

Example (cohort with 4 attachments, 2 anchor messages, `key` starting
`claude-a...`):

    A: att_id=e950263f-063d-495d-b0c0-61e9330d3a14  msg=7f1cf6ff-...
    B: att_id=att-ce21cd12d650                       msg=7f1cf6ff-...   (same message anchor)

    A: att_id=66a7a163-d488-4320-8129-19ad43f64a43  msg=c38e86ac-...
    B: att_id=att-cd01a39eb65c                       msg=0d3a13b8-...  (different message anchor too)

mime_type/size_bytes/inline-presence/name-length are identical between the
paired attachments in every sampled case -- this is not
polylogue-bu1i's acquisition-state pattern (`inline_bytes`/`size_bytes`
flipping None->real). The IDENTITY STRING itself differs, and sometimes so
does the message it's anchored to.

## Root cause

`polylogue/sources/parsers/base_support.py:152-197`
(`attachment_from_meta`/`_make_attachment_id`), used by the Claude.ai parser
via `attachment_from_meta` (`polylogue/sources/parsers/claude/ai_parser.py`,
`_merge_session_attachments` at line ~191, iterating `("attachments",
"files")`):

```python
def _make_attachment_id(seed: str) -> str:
    return f"att-{hash_text(seed)[:12]}"

def attachment_from_meta(meta, message_id, index):
    attachment_id = (
        meta.get("id") or meta.get("file_id") or meta.get("fileId")
        or meta.get("uuid") or meta.get("file_uuid")
    )
    ...
    if not attachment_id:
        if not name:
            return None
        seed = f"{message_id or 'msg'}:{name}:{index}"
        attachment_id = _make_attachment_id(seed)
```

Two independent failure modes both traced in the sample:

1. **Real-id presence is inconsistent across export vintages.** When
   Claude.ai's own export payload carries a real `id`/`file_id`/`uuid` for an
   attachment, that string is used directly (stable). When it's absent, the
   parser falls back to a SYNTHETIC id hashed from
   `f"{message_id}:{name}:{index}"`. The two export vintages of the same
   conversation don't consistently include the real id -- one carries it,
   the other doesn't -- so the same physical attachment gets a real UUID in
   one revision and a synthetic `att-...` id in the other.
2. **`index` is positional, and attachment order is not guaranteed stable.**
   Even when BOTH revisions fall back to synthesis, `index` is the
   attachment's position in the merged `attachments`+`files` iteration for
   that message. If that per-message ordering shifts between export
   vintages (plausible given polylogue-c429's proof that the surrounding
   MESSAGE array order is itself unstable across Claude.ai exports), the
   synthesized id changes even though the underlying attachment didn't.

Either way, attachment identity is accidentally keyed on transient
export-shape details (real-id presence, list order) rather than a property
of the attachment itself, so `_attachment_hash_payload`
(`polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:152`) hashes the same physical attachment to two
different identities across export vintages -- the same general shape as
polylogue-bu1i (acquisition/export-time noise contaminating an identity
hash), but a DIFFERENT concrete defect (id synthesis, not acquisition-state
flip) requiring a different fix.

## Reproduction recipe (production code, no archive mutation)

Same harness as polylogue-c429's reproduction recipe; after loading both
`ParsedSession`s for a cohort where message ids/order/content are identical:

```python
atts_a = {(at.provider_attachment_id, at.message_provider_id): at for at in a.attachments}
atts_b = {(at.provider_attachment_id, at.message_provider_id): at for at in b.attachments}
assert len(atts_a) == len(atts_b)
assert set(atts_a) != set(atts_b)          # disjoint identity despite same count
```

## Extrapolation honesty

40 of 566 sampled (7%). 16/40 = 40% match this exact shape (message
content/order fully identical, attachment key sets disjoint at equal
count). Extrapolating to the full population suggests roughly 220-230 of the
566 cohorts, but this is an estimate from a 7% sample, not a census.

## Proposed fix direction (for the classifier/parser-owning lane, not this bead)

Two independent levers, either alone reduces the blast radius:

- Parser-side: derive the synthetic attachment id from content-stable
  material only (e.g. a hash of `(message_provider_id, name, mime_type,
  size_bytes)` without positional `index`), so re-ordering the export's
  attachment list doesn't change identity. Does not fix mode (1)
  (real-id-present-in-one-export-only).
- Classifier-side (in the files this investigation lane does not edit):
  compare attachments by a looser key (e.g. `(message_provider_id, name,
  mime_type, size_bytes)`) when testing dominance, falling back to id
  equality only when that tuple is ambiguous -- the same class of relaxation
  polylogue-bu1i proposes for acquisition-state, generalized.

Ref polylogue-bu1i
Ref polylogue-c429
close_reason: Superseded by the same aggz comparison-identity change as d8al: attachment_identity_hash (ids.py:254) reads neither the real provider id nor the synthetic positional att-* id, so both failure modes (inconsistent real-id presence, positional-index instability) can no longer produce ambiguous membership cohorts. The synthetic id still exists in base_support as a storage/display artifact but is no longer identity-bearing.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Parser-side fix landed (PR pending, branch feature/fix/synthetic-attachment-id-stability):
attachment_from_meta's synthetic-id seed no longer includes the positional
`index`; mime_type is used as the one extra structural disambiguator instead
(id/name/mime_type). The now-unused `index` param was removed from
attachment_from_meta and all 3 call sites (ai_parser.py x2,
claude/common.py's _message_attachments).

Verified: 250-cohort regression replay (old vs new minting logic) over
already-resolved claude-ai-export cohorts -- 249/250 agree, 1 improvement,
0 regressions.

Honest disposition on the 566-cohort measured population: 0 resolved by this
fix alone. Full census (not sample) shows all 268 message-hashes-equal
ambiguous cohorts are "mixed real/synthetic" (failure mode 1: real-id
presence varies across export vintages of the same conversation) -- 0 are
"pure synthetic on both sides" (the positional-index shape this fix
targets). Failure mode 1 needs a comparison-layer relaxation in
session_revision_membership.py/ids.py, which this lane was scoped away
from. Filed as polylogue-d8al with the full census breakdown and a proposed
design (loosen dominance comparison to (message_id, name, mime_type) when
provider ids disagree, id-equality fallback only when that's itself
ambiguous). polylogue-c429 (message order) accounts for the other 297.

Leaving this bead open pending the comparison-layer fix -- the fix in this
PR is real and durable (protects any future/other-origin case of the
positional-index shape) but does not itself resolve the currently-measured
population; polylogue-d8al is the actionable remainder.

title: claude-ai-export: message array order is not stable across export vintages, breaking prefix-dominance
description:
## What the data says

Sampled 40 of 566 claude-ai-export "ambiguous" equal-message-count membership
cohorts (7%; read-only against /realm/db/polylogue). Reproduced with
production code: parsed both distinct-content raw revisions of each cohort
via `polylogue.sources.dispatch.parse_payload` (routed through
`provider_from_origin`/`capture_mode` exactly as `_parse_one` does in
`polylogue/sources/revision_backfill.py`), projected each with
`polylogue.pipeline.ids.session_revision_projection`, and ran the production
`classify_membership_revisions`.

21 of 40 sampled cohorts (52.5%) have this exact shape:

    n_messages_a == n_messages_b
    set(provider_message_id for a.messages) == set(provider_message_id for b.messages)
    [a.provider_message_id for a in a.messages] != [... for b.messages]   # order differs
    for every shared id: (role, text, timestamp) identical between a and b

That is: the SAME messages, byte-identical per-message content, just in a
DIFFERENT SEQUENCE in the two exports. Concretely reproduced on cohort
`claude-ai:944d1095-51ea-4063-abe9-719d9971e281` (raws
`aa0990572bb833d4...` vs `ebe3a4f95f45b235...`): 36/36 messages, identical
`{role,text,timestamp}` for every one of the 36 shared `provider_message_id`s,
0 content diffs, but `ids_a != ids_b`. One revision's message array is sorted
chronologically; the other is not (its role sequence pairs adjacent
user/user, assistant/assistant messages -- looks like Claude.ai's own tree
flattening interleaving edited-message siblings rather than a strict
timestamp sort).

## Root cause

`polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:session_revision_projection` builds
`message_hashes` as an ORDER-SENSITIVE tuple (`_message_hash_payload` per
message, in array order). `polylogue/archive/session_revision_membership.py`
`_strictly_dominates` requires
`older.message_hashes == newer.message_hashes[: len(older.message_hashes)]`
-- an exact positional prefix match. When Claude.ai's own export emits the
same conversation's message array in a different sequence across two export
requests (same message set, same content, different order), this prefix
check fails in BOTH directions even though there is no real content
divergence, and the cohort is quarantined ambiguous.

No parser code sorts messages by timestamp before this hash is computed
(`polylogue/sources/parsers/claude/ai_parser.py` preserves whatever order the
export's `chat_messages` array carries; see `_merge_session_attachments`
iterating `("attachments", "files")` for the analogous merge-order case in
attachments). Claude.ai's own export ordering for a given conversation is
apparently NOT guaranteed stable across separate export requests -- this is
upstream non-determinism polylogue must tolerate, not something polylogue's
own acquisition controls.

## Reproduction recipe (production code, no archive mutation)

```python
from pathlib import Path
from polylogue.sources.decoders import _iter_json_stream
from polylogue.sources.dispatch import parse_payload
from polylogue.core.enums import Origin
from polylogue.core.sources import provider_from_origin
from polylogue.pipeline.ids import session_revision_projection
import io, sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("file:/realm/db/polylogue/source.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
rows = con.execute(
    "select rs.raw_id, rs.source_path, rs.blob_hash, rs.capture_mode "
    "from raw_session_memberships m join raw_sessions rs on rs.raw_id = m.raw_id "
    "where m.decision='ambiguous' and rs.origin='claude-ai-export' "
    "and m.logical_source_key = ?",
    ("claude-ai:944d1095-51ea-4063-abe9-719d9971e281",),
).fetchall()

def load(row):
    h = row["blob_hash"].hex()
    raw = (Path("/realm/db/polylogue/blob") / h[:2] / h[2:]).read_bytes()
    provider = provider_from_origin(Origin.CLAUDE_AI_EXPORT, family_hint=row["capture_mode"])
    fallback_id = Path(row["source_path"].split(":")[-1]).stem
    name = Path(row["source_path"].split(":")[-1]).name
    records = list(_iter_json_stream(io.BytesIO(raw), name))
    return parse_payload(str(provider), records, fallback_id, source_path=row["source_path"])

sessions = {r["raw_id"]: load(r)[0] for r in rows}  # cohort has exactly 1 session per raw here
ids = list(sessions)
a, b = sessions[ids[0]], sessions[ids[1]]
assert {m.provider_message_id for m in a.messages} == {m.provider_message_id for m in b.messages}
assert [m.provider_message_id for m in a.messages] != [m.provider_message_id for m in b.messages]
```

## Extrapolation honesty

40 of 566 sampled (7%), stratified randomly (seed fixed). 21/40 = 52.5% match
this exact shape; 3 more sampled cohorts show this pattern layered with a
second delta (attachment count or session-event differences) in addition.
Extrapolating the 52.5% rate to the full population suggests roughly 280-300
of the 566 cohorts, but this is an ESTIMATE from a 7% sample, not a census --
unlike polylogue-bu1i's 100%-verified aistudio-drive population, this has not
been checked against every cohort.

## Proposed fix direction (for the classifier-owning lane, not this bead)

`_strictly_dominates` and `session_revision_projection` currently treat
message sequence as part of content identity. A safe fix compares the
message SET (by `provider_message_id` + content) rather than requiring an
exact positional prefix when a provider's export ordering is not
authoritative -- i.e. treat "same message ids/content, different array
order" as equivalent, not as a branch. This is a distinct code path from
polylogue-bu1i's attachment-acquisition-state fix (different failure
mode, different field: sequence vs. attachment identity) and should not be
folded into the same patch without separate verification, since a naive
order-insensitive compare would also need to preserve real append-order
detection (`older.message_hashes == newer.message_hashes[:len(older)]`) for
genuinely growing sessions.

Ref polylogue-bu1i
Ref polylogue-hith
Ref polylogue-nuec
notes: Superseded by polylogue-aggz's architecture: message array order is now handled as a byproduct of set-based (identity, content) comparison (message_contents), not a dedicated positional-prefix fix. Live census (full population): 554/587 (94.4%) claude-ai-export ambiguous cohorts now resolve, 0 regressions against previously-resolved cohorts. See PR.

title: A persisted 'ambiguous' verdict is terminal with no classifier version, so classifier corrections are inert on existing data
description:
## Problem

`polylogue-bu1i` fixes the classifier so that acquiring an attachment's bytes is
read as a fidelity upgrade rather than a branch. Verified: all 157 live
aistudio-drive cohorts now resolve to an accepted chain with the enriched
revision at its head, where previously 157/157 were ambiguous.

That fix cannot heal the archive it was written for. The verdicts it corrects are
already persisted, and a persisted `ambiguous` verdict is TERMINAL:

    polylogue/storage/repair.py:4432-4462
      SELECT 1 FROM raw_session_memberships
       WHERE raw_id IN (...) AND decision = 'ambiguous'
      -> RawReplayPlanStatus.TERMINAL,
         "component ended in explicit ambiguous or parse-terminal authority state",
         "inspect durable authority debt; do not replay without new evidence"

`raw_session_memberships` has no fingerprint column, so nothing distinguishes
"ambiguous under the current classifier" from "ambiguous under a classifier we
have since corrected". Every improvement to `classify_membership_revisions` is
therefore inert on existing data and only affects newly-acquired raws, while the
existing debt sits terminal forever and reads as though it needed operator
judgment.

Live scale of the inert-fix problem: 3,875 ambiguous membership rows across
~1,079 cohorts (587 claude-ai-export, 191 claude-code-session, 151
aistudio-drive, 136 chatgpt-export, and a tail).

## Second defect: a bump would not propagate

`RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT = "revision-membership-v1"` exists as a proper
constant in `polylogue/storage/raw_authority.py:27`, but
`polylogue/sources/revision_backfill.py` hardcodes the literal string eight
times instead of importing it (lines 318, 348, 438, 475, 552, 565, 596, 919),
including inside an f-string. Bumping the constant today would half-apply: the
writer would stamp the new value while the quiescence gate still matched the old
one. The constant is not load-bearing, which makes the versioning mechanism
non-functional exactly when it is first needed.

## Proposed fix

1. Make the constant load-bearing: `revision_backfill.py` imports
   `RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT` rather than repeating the literal.
2. Separate two questions the single fingerprint currently conflates:
   - *Was this raw ever observed by a real parser?* -- the quiescence gate
     (`uncensused_historical_revision_raw_ids`, `revision_backfill.py:321`).
     Any known fingerprint should satisfy this, so a bump does NOT trigger an
     archive-wide re-census of all 41,363 raws.
   - *Is this verdict still authoritative under current semantics?* -- the
     terminal gate. Only the CURRENT fingerprint should satisfy this.
   Concretely: keep a `SUPERSEDED_MEMBERSHIP_FINGERPRINTS` set alongside the
   current one, and have the terminal check treat an `ambiguous` decision as
   stale (replayable) when the raw's census fingerprint is superseded rather
   than current. Absent census row -> treat as current, i.e. stay conservative.
   `index_tier.raw_revision_applications` carries the same `decision='ambiguous'`
   check and needs the same treatment.
3. Bump `RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT` to `revision-membership-v2`, because
   `polylogue-bu1i` genuinely changed classification semantics.

With (2) in place the healing is targeted: roughly 3,875 raws re-derive their
verdict, instead of re-censusing the whole 99 GB archive. Without (2), a bump
is correct but costs a full reparse (~4h20m measured on this archive).

## Why this is the general fix, not a one-off

The value here is not unblocking one origin. It is that a classifier correction
becomes self-healing: today, improving `classify_membership_revisions` requires
manual archive surgery to have any effect on existing data, which is precisely
the shape that leaves corrected logic silently inert and debt looking legitimate.

## Acceptance criteria

- `RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT` is the single source of the fingerprint
  string; no module hardcodes it.
- An `ambiguous` verdict recorded under a superseded fingerprint is replayable,
  and one recorded under the current fingerprint remains terminal. Both
  directions covered by tests.
- A bump does not force re-census of raws whose verdict is unaffected; assert
  this against a fixture archive rather than by reasoning.
- Anti-vacuity: state the production line mutated and the resulting failure.

Ref polylogue-bu1i
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-30, from the lane that traced polylogue-eqnv: the 'Proposed fix' item (2) above is wrong for identity-class staleness, and I am recording that before anyone implements it.

I proposed splitting the fingerprint's two jobs so that the QUIESCENCE gate accepts any *known* fingerprint (avoiding an archive-wide re-census on a bump) while only the TERMINAL gate requires the current one. The motive was cost: targeted healing of ~3,900 raws instead of reparsing 99 GB.

That does not work when the stale thing is the raw's derived IDENTITY rather than its verdict. polylogue-eqnv is the concrete counterexample: two raws of one document were censused under the same fingerprint string but recorded different logical_source_key values, one carrying a pre-#3179 '-0' suffix from a dispatch bug fixed 2026-07-20 (b473d9256) that their 2026-07-16/18 acquisition predates. Reparsing both blobs through current dispatch yields the identical correct key. Permissive quiescence is exactly what keeps that raw from ever being re-derived, so it preserves the corruption it was meant to be cheap about.

Consequence for this bead's scope: re-census (a reparse) is the honest price for any change that alters derived identity, and the cost cannot be engineered away by making the gate permissive. The split between 'was this observed' and 'is this verdict current' may still be worth having for pure VERDICT changes, where the recorded identity is unaffected -- polylogue-bu1i is that shape, since it changed only how revisions are COMPARED. State which class a change falls in before choosing the cheap path.

Possible middle path, not yet evaluated: re-census only raws whose recorded identity disagrees with a cheap re-derivation, which needs a parse but not a full projection/materialization. Whether that is meaningfully cheaper than the full reparse is unmeasured -- do not assume it is.
DESIGN 2026-07-30, from the polylogue-eqnv/c737 lane, supersedes the correction note above with something actionable.

Split the single parser fingerprint into two independently-versioned components:

  identity fingerprint       -- covers dispatch.py's provider_session_id /
                                logical_source_key derivation
  classification fingerprint -- covers session_revision_membership.py's
                                dominance rules

Then each class of fix pays only its own price:

- A CLASSIFICATION fix (polylogue-bu1i's shape: dominance rules changed, the
  stored identity is unaffected) bumps only the classification component.
  Quiescence stays permissive on identity, so no reparse is forced, and the
  terminal-ambiguous gate re-runs classification against the already-known
  identity. Cheap, and it makes classifier corrections self-healing, which is
  this bead's original ask.
- An IDENTITY fix (polylogue-eqnv's shape and the z1c6 dispatch bug: the stored
  logical_source_key itself was wrong) bumps the identity component. Quiescence
  goes strict for it, forcing exactly the reparse that is unavoidably the honest
  price -- you cannot know an identity is still correct without recomputing it,
  since recomputing IS how you discover it changed.

This is strictly better than the single fingerprint in both directions: today a
classification fix cannot heal existing data at all (the terminal gate has no
version to compare), and an identity fix would force a full 99 GB reparse even
when only classification changed.

Implementation note carried over: RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT must first
become load-bearing -- sources/revision_backfill.py still hardcodes
'revision-membership-v1' at eight sites (318, 348, 438, 475, 552, 565, 596,
919) instead of importing the constant, so any bump half-applies until that is
fixed.

Each class of fix then pays only its own price:

- A CLASSIFICATION fix (polylogue-bu1i's shape: dominance rules changed, stored
  identity unaffected) bumps only the classification component. Quiescence stays
  permissive on identity so no reparse is forced, and the terminal-ambiguous
  gate re-runs classification against the already-known identity. Cheap, and it

- An IDENTITY fix (polylogue-eqnv's shape, and the z1c6 dispatch bug: the stored
  logical_source_key itself was wrong) bumps the identity component. Quiescence
