  price -- you cannot know an identity is still correct without recomputing it,
  because recomputing IS how you discover it changed.

Strictly better than one fingerprint in both directions: today a classification
fix cannot heal existing data at all (the terminal gate has no version to
compare against), while an identity fix would force a full 99 GB reparse even
when only classification changed.

Prerequisite: RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT must become load-bearing first --
sources/revision_backfill.py hardcodes 'revision-membership-v1' at eight sites
(318, 348, 438, 475, 552, 565, 596, 919) instead of importing the constant, so
any bump half-applies until that is fixed.
VERDICT: LIVE — polylogue/storage/repair.py:4432-4462 (terminal-decision check for 'ambiguous') is unchanged and still has no classifier_version gating; a persisted ambiguous verdict remains unconditionally terminal. Bead's own 2026-07-30 correction note shows the proposed remediation design was found wrong and no replacement fix has landed. Evidence: sed -n '4400,4470p' polylogue/storage/repair.py showing decision='ambiguous' UNION query with no version check.
close_reason: Merged PR #3485 (6df3972c6): RAW_AUTHORITY_PARSER_FINGERPRINT now load-bearing (8 hardcoded literals replaced by the import), terminal ambiguous checks gated by SUPERSEDED_MEMBERSHIP_FINGERPRINTS on both raw_session_memberships and index_tier.raw_revision_applications legs, both directions test-covered; bump-without-recensus asserted against a fixture archive.

title: aistudio-drive 'ambiguous' revision pairs are not branches: attachment acquisition state contaminates attachment identity hash
description:
## What the data says

151 of 151 aistudio-drive ambiguous membership cohorts (100%) are the SAME Drive
document acquired twice, where the later acquisition merely resolved
Drive-hosted attachment bytes. There is no branch and nothing to judge.

Verified across all 157 two-member source_path cohorts in the live archive
(/realm/db/polylogue), by loading both blobs and comparing:

    157/157  file_mtime_ms IDENTICAL (both carry Drive modifiedTime)
    157/157  earlier blob has NO _polylogue_drive_live_bytes_b64
    157/157  later blob HAS it
    157/157  the two payloads are byte-equal after stripping that key
    157/157  later blob is larger (median ~5-80x)

Reproduced deterministically with production code on the pair
30-12-2025-SINEX-IDEAS.json (raws f6b63f0b / d0715a7f):

    bare     604,853 B  msgs=60 events=61 atts=4  all inline=None, size_bytes=None
    enriched 5,602,664 B  msgs=60 events=61 atts=4  same 4 Drive file ids, bytes fetched

    message_hashes equal: True
    event_hashes   equal: True
    attachment sets: n1=4 n2=4 intersection=0 subset=False
    _strictly_dominates(bare->enriched) = False
    classify_membership_revisions -> ambiguous ['d0715a7f','f6b63f0b']

## Root cause (two independent contributors)

1. `_attachment_hash_payload` (polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:152) folds
   ACQUISITION STATE into attachment IDENTITY: it appends
   `inline_content_hash` only when `inline_bytes is not None`, and
   `size_bytes` flips None -> real once bytes are fetched. So the same
   attachment (same Drive file id, same message anchor) hashes differently
   before and after acquisition. The two revisions' attachment_hashes end up
   equal-cardinality and DISJOINT.

2. `_strictly_dominates` (archive/session_revision_membership.py:188) then
   fails both of its conditions: `content_grew` is False (equal message and
   event counts, no proper attachment superset) and
   `older.attachment_hashes <= newer.attachment_hashes` is False (disjoint,
   not subset). Neither escape hatch applies: both revisions have
   `browser_snapshot_fidelity=None` so `_provider_ordered_browser_snapshots`
   bails, and `_direct_export_precedence` needs a browser-capture sibling.
   -> ambiguous, both quarantined.

Separately, `raw_sessions.revision_kind='unknown'` / `logical_source_key IS NULL`
because the byte-prefix chain check cannot hold: the injector splices base64
mid-document and re-serializes the whole JSON
(`json.dumps(resolved, ensure_ascii=False)`, sources/drive/__init__.py:173),
so the later bytes are not a byte-prefix extension of the earlier.

## Where the second scrape came from

Not two Drive versions. Both acquisitions read the SAME local cache file under
`~/.local/share/polylogue/drive-cache/gemini/` (240 documents). The 2026-06-29
pass wrote the cache with attachments unresolved. The 2026-07-18 pass took the
cache-hit branch (no Drive re-download at all) and ran
`_inject_live_drive_attachment_bytes` -- which by design runs on EVERY read,
cache hit or not, precisely to backfill caches written before the feature
existed (sources/drive/__init__.py:242-256). It mutated the bytes, rewrote the
cache in place, and hashed the mutated payload -> a second, distinct raw row.
Drive modifiedTime never changed, which is why file_mtime_ms is identical.

The 83 single-row cohorts corroborate this: 72 have no driveDocument/Image/
Audio/Video reference at all, and 11 have references the injector could not
resolve -- in both cases the injector returns bytes unchanged, the blob hash is
stable, and no second raw row is created.

## Concrete harm already in the index

Post-promotion convergence materialized these ambiguous raws anyway, arbitrarily
and last-writer-wins. 6 cohorts got BOTH members materialized; in 5 of the 6 the
BARE revision was written last, so the index now reports those sessions'
attachments as `unfetched` even though the bytes were successfully fetched and
are sitting in the blob store:

    aistudio-drive:Implementing-066bb070...  atts=1 acquired=0
    aistudio-drive:Implementing-13ced1c8...  atts=1 acquired=0
    aistudio-drive:Implementing-37edfeb3...  atts=1 acquired=0
    aistudio-drive:Implementing-845dd573...  atts=1 acquired=0
    aistudio-drive:Implementing-d4d7fbab...  atts=1 acquired=0

That is a silent fidelity DOWNGRADE, and it is the exact failure mode the
'never choose between branches' invariant exists to prevent -- it happened
because a non-branch was labelled a branch, and then something picked anyway.
Which stage performed that pick is not yet traced: `repair.py:1075` does
quarantine ambiguous membership, yet 135 of the 151 cohorts acquired a
`parsed_at_ms` between 06:57 and 13:12 local on 2026-07-30, after the
`decided_at_ms` of 07:00 that recorded them ambiguous. That gap needs its own
trace and may be a second, separate defect.

## Proposed fix

Treat 'same attachment identity, bytes now acquired' as a fidelity upgrade, the
direct analogue of the documented DOM->native rule. Concretely: compare
attachments by provider identity (provider_attachment_id + message_provider_id
+ name + mime_type) when testing dominance, and allow a differing hash when the
only delta is that the newer side has inline_bytes where the older did not.
Equivalently, split attachment identity from attachment acquisition state so
acquisition can never fabricate a branch.

Prefer this over adding a Drive-specific escape hatch: the shape is generic
(any origin whose attachments are fetched lazily), and the classifier already
has two precedents for 'this is an upgrade, not a branch'.

## Blast radius beyond drive

Equal-message-count ambiguous cohorts by origin (same shape; needs its own
verification per origin before claiming the same cause):

    claude-ai-export      566 / 587 cohorts
    chatgpt-export        128 / 136
    aistudio-drive        151 / 151   <- proven, this bead
    hermes-session          3 / 4
    claude-code-session     6 / 191   <- different shape, not this
    gemini-cli-session      0 / 3

## Measurement notes for whoever picks this up

- Live aistudio-drive state at filing: index 225 sessions / 95,823 blocks
  (retired generation had 239 / 106,178); source has 173 unparsed raws, of
  which 129 are correctly superseded (their enriched sibling IS materialized)
  and 44 are the 22 both-unparsed cohorts. 14 documents are absent from the
  index entirely -- exactly the 239-225 gap.
- The earlier claim '0 correctly superseded, all 302 genuinely unmaterialized'
  was a measurement artifact: it checked `raw_sessions.logical_source_key`,
  which governance deliberately NULLs on transition to semantic membership
  (archive.py:2710). The key survives on
  `raw_session_memberships.logical_source_key` -- join that table instead.
- Attachment acquisition overall improved enormously in this generation:
  acquired 26 -> 2,849 (unfetched 3,120 -> 177). This bead is a narrow
  regression channel inside a large win, not a verdict on the rebuild.

Ref polylogue-7ilr (which framed this residue as genuine authority debt
requiring operator judgment; for aistudio-drive that framing is wrong).
close_reason: Fix merged: acquisition-state (inline bytes/size flipping None→real) is excluded from attachment comparison identity (pipeline/ids.py:243 comment + attachment_identity_hash), so byte-acquisition reads as fidelity upgrade, not a branch; verified per polylogue-9dxn's cross-check that all 157 live aistudio-drive cohorts resolve to an accepted chain under the current classifier. Retroactive healing of persisted ambiguous verdicts is polylogue-9dxn (in flight).

title: repair_empty_sessions would delete the 832 genuinely-empty sessions the hook-inflation postmortem chose to retain
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by the pre-rebuild deletion audit. NOT on the rebuild path.

repair_empty_sessions / count_empty_sessions_sync (polylogue/storage/repair.py)
select with a blanket predicate:

    sessions LEFT JOIN messages ... WHERE m.session_id IS NULL

It cannot distinguish a legitimately-empty session from corruption debris.
That distinction is not hypothetical: the 2026-07-22 hook-inflation
postmortem explicitly decided to RETAIN ~832 genuinely-empty sessions after
the de-inflation (index sessions went 83,286 -> 18,391 = 17,559 real + 832
genuinely-empty). Browser-capture stubs are a second legitimate source.
Running this repair would delete exactly the rows that postmortem chose to
keep.

WHY IT IS NOT A REBUILD BLOCKER: the target is MaintenanceTargetMode.CLEANUP
with destructive=True, and resolve_selected_maintenance_targets
(cli/shared/check_maintenance.py) only includes CLEANUP targets when the
operator explicitly passes --cleanup or names the target. Neither
maintenance/rebuild_index.py nor daemon/bulk_rebuild.py ever calls it. So the
rebuild pipeline cannot trigger it.

THE REAL RISK IS OPERATIONAL: someone running `polylogue check --cleanup` as
housekeeping around the big rebuild would silently delete the retained
sessions. DO NOT RUN --cleanup against the live archive until this is fixed.

FIX: give the predicate a distinguishing signal -- e.g. require raw_id IS NULL
(no acquired bytes behind it) or an explicit acquisition-status check -- so a
session that was legitimately acquired and legitimately has no messages is
retained, and only rows with no provenance at all are candidates.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-07-31: the proposed discriminator in this bead's design does NOT work. Measured on the live index:

  empty sessions (no messages):            5,257
  of those, with raw_id IS NULL:               0
  of those, that are <agent>.meta phantoms: 4,945

So 'require raw_id IS NULL (no acquired bytes behind it)' classifies EVERY empty
session as legitimate, including all 4,945 .meta phantoms. Acquisition genuinely
happened for the phantoms -- the .meta.json file was really read -- it just should
never have produced a session. Acquisition is therefore not the discriminator.

WHAT THE POPULATION ACTUALLY IS (joined to source artifacts via
  attach 'file:/realm/db/polylogue/source.db?mode=ro' as src;
  join src.raw_sessions r on r.raw_id = s.raw_id):
  4,945  <agent-id>.meta sidecars
    246  non-transcript artifacts under ~/.claude/projects/ -- measured examples:
           analysis/problem_solutions/problems_index.jsonl (321 KB, an INDEX whose
             rows are {"conversation":"<id>","type":"unknown","preview":...})
           workflows/wf_54d4fb2e-841.json (176 KB, a workflow RUN RECORD with
             runId/taskId/script)
     47  claude-ai-export zip members
     17  codex sessions
      2  files under ~/.gemini/ classified as claude-code-session (misdetection)

So 'genuinely empty session' is not a legitimate construct -- it is a label for
records that were never conversations. The 832 the hook-inflation postmortem
retained were retained precisely BECAUSE the blanket predicate could not tell them
apart, not because they were verified worth keeping.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: the real discriminator is WHAT THE ACQUIRED ARTIFACT IS,
not whether bytes were acquired. That is the general defect now tracked as
polylogue-9ykn (P0, ingest uses LOCATION as identity) and being fixed there. This
bead should become: fix repair_empty_sessions' predicate so it cannot delete
legitimately-empty sessions, AND do not implement the raw_id discriminator.

STILL TRUE AND STILL IMPORTANT: do not run 'polylogue check --cleanup' against the
live archive. It would currently delete all 5,257 rows indiscriminately -- the
4,945 phantoms (which should go, but via a considered repair) and any genuinely
legitimate stub (which should not).

MITIGATION LANDED 2026-07-31: ~/.claude/projects/-realm-project-sinex/analysis/
(14 files, 68 MB, dated 2025-07-12..2025-07-25) was moved out of the watched
directory to /realm/inbox/claude-code-sinex-analysis-subdir. That stops
re-ingestion of that artifact class, including conversation_relationships.jsonl
which alone produced 96,748 phantom messages (polylogue-gvgi). It does NOT remove
the already-indexed rows.
close_reason: Merged PR #3536: repair_empty_sessions/count_empty_sessions_sync now re-run classify_artifact/inspect_raw_artifact against each empty session's raw evidence, only treating positive-refusal cases as debris (fixes the refuted raw_id IS NULL predicate). Regression tests pin both refuted predicates.

title: three modules (~800 loc) are unreachable from production, including an unenforced holdout guard
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by a systematic sweep for code that exists, imports cleanly,
type-checks, has tests -- and is reachable from nothing in production. This is
a distinct failure mode from unfinished work and is invisible to every gate the
repo has.

THREE MODULES, ~800 LOC, 22 PUBLIC EXPORTS, ZERO PRODUCTION REFERENCES
(each referenced only by its own test file; verified with a full-tree grep for
the module name AND for every public symbol it exports):

  polylogue/storage/sqlite/holdout_cohorts.py     260 loc, 10 exports
      HoldoutPolicy, HoldoutAccessError, HoldoutAccessReceipt, mark_holdout,
      get_holdout_policy, is_holdout, record_holdout_access,
      list_holdout_access_receipts, has_holdout_contamination,
      require_non_holdout_access
      THE SHARPEST ONE: this is an evaluation-integrity guard. Nothing calls
      require_non_holdout_access or has_holdout_contamination, so holdout
      protection is not enforced on any path. A guard that guards nothing is
      worse than no guard -- it reads, in review and in the module list, as
      though the protection exists.

  polylogue/insights/fable_packet.py              306 loc, 6 exports
      compile_private_fable_packet, regenerate_private_fable_packet,
      FableDelegationPacket, DelegationPacketRow, DelegationPacketLabel,
      DescriptiveDistribution

  polylogue/storage/block_anchor.py               231 loc, 6 exports
      parse_block_anchor, resolve_block_anchor, format_block_anchor,
      BlockAnchor, BlockAnchorResolution, InvalidBlockAnchorError
      Block content-hash citation anchors (svfj). If nothing resolves an
      anchor, a stored citation cannot be followed back to its block.

DISPOSITION NEEDED PER MODULE, not a blanket answer: wire it (the capability
is wanted and was simply never connected -- the right answer for
session_agent_policies earlier today), or delete it (nothing needs it, and it
is costing review attention and a false sense of coverage). Do not leave a
third state.

METHOD, so this is repeatable:
  - modules whose name and whose every public symbol appear nowhere outside
    their own file and tests
  - config properties with no consumer
  - tables written but never read
  - enum members never constructed
  - repository/service public methods no surface calls

FALSE POSITIVES THIS SWEEP PRODUCED -- record them so the next run does not
re-raise them:
  - session_events kinds "written but never read" (31 of 54): WRONG. A generic
    reader exists (storage/sqlite/queries/session_events.py ->
    repository/archive/sessions.py), they land on the domain Session model,
    a CLI surface renders them with an --event-type filter, and they drive
    session timestamp derivation for providers whose messages lack timestamps.
  - surfaces/projection_spec enums (RenderFormat, BodyPolicy, ...): WRONG as
    "dead" -- they are Pydantic field types, so they are live as validators.
    The real (narrower) defect is that nothing DISPATCHES on RenderFormat.
  - repository methods with no surface caller (51): TOO NOISY to act on as a
    list. traverse_work_evidence looked orphaned but its subsystem is
    referenced by 18 files; some others were added hours earlier and their
    surface is a known follow-up. Individual-method orphanhood is weak
    evidence; module-level orphanhood is strong.
  - cli/commands/maintenance/_blob_integrity.py: WRONG. Its five *_command
    functions are each registered elsewhere.

A standing detector is worth building AFTER the imminent rebuild, but only in
the module-level form -- that is the form that produced true positives every
time. The method-level and event-level forms produced only noise.

title: chatgpt.py code-interpreter blocks lack tool_id pairing, causing tool_result:tool_use skew
description:
Discovered while implementing polylogue-ah21 (BrowserCaptureTurn typed blocks
channel). polylogue-ah21's cited regression signal -- 22,992 tool_result
blocks vs 7,745 tool_use blocks (~3:1) for chatgpt-export-origin sessions --
does NOT originate in the browser-capture transport/parser (which
polylogue-ah21 fixed: BrowserCaptureTurn now carries typed blocks end to end).
It originates in polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt.py's own tool-block
construction, which both real ChatGPT export files and browser-captured
sessions that carry a trusted native raw_provider_payload (the common case)
delegate to identically.

Root cause (chatgpt.py, read-only reviewed, not edited under polylogue-ah21's
scope restriction):
- content_type == "code" (code-interpreter call/input) emits BlockType.CODE,
  not BlockType.TOOL_USE.
- content_type == "execution_output" (code-interpreter result) unconditionally
  emits BlockType.TOOL_RESULT.
- Neither branch sets tool_id, so even if TOOL_USE were emitted for "code",
  there would be no linking key to pair it with its TOOL_RESULT.

Every code-interpreter invocation therefore contributes one TOOL_RESULT with
zero matching TOOL_USE. Live evidence (read-only query against
/realm/db/polylogue/index.db, file:...?mode=ro):
- All chatgpt-export sessions: tool_use=7745, tool_result=22992, code=29183.
- Restricting to sessions tagged capture:* (i.e. genuinely browser-captured,
  455 of 2635 chatgpt-export sessions): tool_use=3877, tool_result=17768,
  code=22539 -- an even worse ~4.6:1 ratio, and 435/455 of those sessions used
  the capture:browser-native-payload tag (full native delegation to
  chatgpt.py), vs only 3 compact + 17 dom-fallback (the paths polylogue-ah21's
  new BrowserCaptureTurn.blocks channel actually reaches). This confirms the
  ratio is a chatgpt.py classification bug, not a browser-capture transport
  gap.

Proposed fix (not done here -- chatgpt.py is owned by another lane per
polylogue-ah21's scope note):
1. Classify content_type == "code" as BlockType.TOOL_USE (tool_name e.g.
   "code_interpreter") instead of BlockType.CODE, OR keep CODE but also emit a
   parallel TOOL_USE marker -- needs a product decision on which is the
   canonical read-model shape (evaluate against existing CODE-typed block
   consumers before changing wire semantics).
2. Give both blocks a tool_id: the call message's own id, and the result's
   parent message id (its parent in the mapping tree is the call), mirroring
   the pairing convention polylogue-ah21 established for the browser-capture
   path (browser-extension/src/backfill/providers.js's chatGptTurnBlocks /
   src/content/chatgpt.js's nativeTurnBlocks).
3. Re-verify the ratio via the same read-only query after the fix ships and a
   derived-tier reprocess (`polylogue ops reset --index && polylogued run`,
   NOT run against the live archive without explicit operator go-ahead).

Acceptance criteria:
1. chatgpt.py's code-interpreter call and its output block pair with a shared
   tool_id.
2. tool_use:tool_result counts for chatgpt-export sessions converge close to
   1:1 modulo genuinely unpaired calls/results (streaming truncation,
   provider-side drops).
3. Existing chatgpt.py parser tests updated to assert the pairing; a live
   read-only re-measurement recorded in the closing bead note/PR.
notes:
Fixed (branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates, commits
c6d3e8889/fa7792395). content_type=="code" now emits BlockType.TOOL_USE
(was CODE) with tool_id=str(msg_id) matching the execution_output's
existing tool_id=parent_message_provider_id, tool_name=recipient (falls
back to "code_interpreter"), tool_input={"code": text}, text kept for
transcript rendering. Mirrors the existing recipient-addressed JSON
tool-call branch and the browser-capture typed-blocks pairing convention.

AC1 (shared tool_id): satisfied, new test
test_code_interpreter_call_and_result_share_a_tool_id, anti-vacuity
confirmed (fails when tool_id=str(msg_id) removed).
AC2 (ratio converges toward 1:1): NOT independently re-measured live --
baseline re-confirmed via read-only query against /realm/db/polylogue/
index.db (file:...?mode=ro): tool_use=7745, tool_result=22992, matching
the bead's original numbers exactly (archive not yet reprocessed with this
fix). A live "after" measurement requires the imminent full index rebuild
mentioned in this session's task brief (INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION 46,
SEMANTIC_REPARSE) -- deliberately not triggered here per the bead's own
note ("NOT run against the live archive without explicit operator
go-ahead") and because re-ingest is a coordinator-level action, not a
per-fix action. Structural correctness is proven at the parser level via
the new test plus three existing tests updated to reflect the corrected
classification (test_code_interpreter_content_is_preserved,
test_code_block_carries_recipient_as_tool_name in
tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_chatgpt.py; the chatgpt-export fixture's
has_tool_use expectation in tests/unit/sources/parsers/
test_origin_regression_pack.py, which previously encoded this exact bug in
its own docstring; test_browser_capture_prefers_raw_chatgpt_payload_when_present
in tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py).
AC3 (tests updated + live re-measurement recorded): tests updated, satisfied.
Live re-measurement recorded above as baseline-confirmed-unchanged pending
the rebuild -- follow-up: whoever triggers the full rebuild should re-run
this session's read-only query and record the after-ratio in this bead.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_chatgpt.py
tests/unit/sources/parsers/test_origin_regression_pack.py
tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py tests/property/test_semantic_properties.py
-> all passed. devtools verify --quick -> exit 0. ruff + mypy clean.
VERDICT: STALE — both AC landed on master: chatgpt.py now emits BlockType.TOOL_USE with tool_id=str(msg_id) for code-interpreter blocks (comment cites bd polylogue-4fm3), and the paired test test_code_interpreter_call_and_result_share_a_tool_id exists in tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_chatgpt.py on origin/master. Live archive ratio also converged: chatgpt-export blocks now tool_use=37257 vs tool_result=22999 (was 7745:22992 3:1 skewed the wrong way), confirming reprocessing happened. Evidence: git show origin/master:polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt.py | grep tool_id; git show origin/master:tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_chatgpt.py; sqlite3 file:/realm/db/polylogue/index.db?mode=ro block_type counts for origin=chatgpt-export.
close_reason: Already satisfied on master via PR #3390 (5e23e6abf): chatgpt.py sets tool_id=str(msg_id) on TOOL_USE and tool_id=parent_message_provider_id on paired TOOL_RESULT/execution_output branches. Explicit pairing tests exist (test_recipient_tool_use_and_result_share_a_tool_id etc, 2 passed). Live re-measurement: tool_use=37586/tool_result=23050 for chatgpt-export, converged from the bead's cited ~3:1 wrong-direction skew to a ratio consistent with genuinely unpaired calls.

title: Fix 76 schema-promotion-audit blockers (raw_local_provenance/unsafe_property_name) blocking pre-push
description: The pre-push hook runs 'devtools verify --quick', which now includes the 'schema promotion audit' step (python -m polylogue.schemas.promotion_audit polylogue/schemas). This gate was newly wired into verify --quick on the feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates branch (see devtools/verify.py comment: 'had never been wired to anything, while 76 blockers sat in the committed tree'). Running it now (base commit 819e9c07e, confirmed via git show identical to current tree) reports 76 blockers: 67 raw_local_provenance (bundle_scopes/representative_paths fields in committed provider schema catalog/package JSON under polylogue/schemas/providers/) and 9 unsafe_property_name, plus informational review findings. This blocks ALL pushes on any branch descended from 819e9c07e until fixed. Discovered while pushing an unrelated fix branch (fix/artifact-kind-and-lineage-validation) whose own diff does not touch any schema/providers file (confirmed identical before/after). Needs either: (1) scrubbing local-provenance fields (bundle_scopes/representative_paths) from the committed catalog/package/manifest JSON artifacts under polylogue/schemas/providers/, or (2) an explicit decision to relax/re-scope the promotion_audit blocker severity for these fields, before the gate can pass on any branch. Run: python -m polylogue.schemas.promotion_audit polylogue/schemas --output /tmp/audit.json to reproduce.
close_reason: Fixed. All 76 schema-promotion-audit blockers cleared: 67 raw_local_provenance (forbidden provenance fields stripped from 19 committed JSON artifacts) and 9 unsafe_property_name (content-bearing property names collapsed to additionalProperties). Root causes were two partially-propagated fixes: SchemaCluster.to_dict() already dropped representative_paths while the catalog/manifest/package writers did not, and should_collapse_observed_keys never consulted is_dynamic_key, so its 24-key floor let nine free-text keys through. Both fixed at source -- collapse now triggers on a single content-bearing key with no cardinality floor. Audit verdict blocked -> review_required, blocker_count 0. Commit 927daf098.

title: read --to browser silently prints to terminal instead of opening a browser
design:
Confirmed empirically 2026-07-29 against a demo archive (POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT=/realm/tmp/pl-audit-archive):

    polylogue find "demo" read --first --to browser
      -> printed 12 result rows to the terminal. No browser opened, no warning.
    polylogue find "demo" read --first --to clipboard
      -> "Could not copy to clipboard (no clipboard tool found)."  (correctly attempted)

So "browser" is an accepted --to choice that silently degrades to terminal output.

CAUSE: two dispatch sites handle destinations by string comparison and let
anything unrecognized fall through to plain echo:

  polylogue/cli/read_views/base.py:158-168   deliver_content()
      if "file" / elif "clipboard" / else: click.echo(content)
  polylogue/cli/read_views/standard.py:97-108
      if ("stdout","terminal") / elif "clipboard" / elif "file" / else: execute_query_request(...)

Neither has a "browser" branch. But "browser" IS an accepted value:
  polylogue/cli/query_verbs.py:215
      _READ_DESTINATIONS = ("terminal","stdout","browser","clipboard","file")

And browser delivery IS implemented -- just on a different path that these
read views never adopted:
  polylogue/cli/query_contracts.py:62-63   normalized == "browser" -> kind="browser"
  polylogue/cli/query_output.py:291        elif destination.kind == "browser"

This is a partially-propagated solution: browser delivery was built for the
query-output path and the read_views path was never updated.

Note the ref-read path is correctly guarded -- `polylogue read <ref> --to browser`
raises "Direct ref reads write JSON to terminal/stdout only." Only the
query-based read path silently degrades.

FIX: route both read_views dispatch sites through the existing browser
delivery rather than adding a third copy, and make the fall-through `else`
raise on an unrecognized destination instead of silently echoing -- the silent
else is what let this hide.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #3504 (fix(cli): route read --to browser through existing delivery contract, merged 2026-08-01). All 5 AC items satisfied per the PR's own AC matrix: bug reproduced against demo archive before fixing; both dispatch sites fixed (cli/read_views/base.py deliver_content, cli/read_views/standard.py run_read_summary_or_transcript); routed through the existing query_output.open_in_browser/deliver_query_output mechanism, no new browser-opening code; fallthrough else now raises click.UsageError on unrecognized destination; _READ_DESTINATIONS in cli/query_verbs.py:215 unchanged. Anti-vacuity: removing either branch's browser routing makes new regression tests fail.

title: mainline_messages shows superseded variants: variant_index is creation order, not display state
design:
Found 2026-07-29 while fixing phase-span inversion (polylogue-cuxz.10).

TWO sites treat variant_index==0 as "the main conversation":
  polylogue/archive/session/domain_runtime.py:121  mainline_messages()
  polylogue/rendering/core_messages.py:130         rendered transcript

But variant_index is NOT a display-state flag. For ChatGPT it is
children.index(current_node_id) -- the sibling's position in CREATION order.
When a turn is edited or regenerated, variant 0 is the FIRST attempt, and the
accepted one is whichever sibling the provider currently points at. The
storage tier already records that correctly as messages.is_active_path
(storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:217).

Measured on the live archive (4,930,294 messages carrying variant_index):
    variant 0 AND active        4,919,777
    variant 0 but SUPERSEDED        8,219   <- mainline SHOWS these
    variant >0 and ACTIVE           1,465   <- mainline HIDES these

So ~8.2K messages render as the main conversation while the provider considers
them superseded, and ~1.5K accepted messages are hidden. Small as a fraction,
but it is silent wrongness in the most-read surface: a user reading a session
sees the abandoned first attempt where an edit was accepted. A concrete case
was verified during the phase work -- chatgpt-export:0012f391-..., where the
accepted final edit is variant_index=3 (is_active_path=1) and variant_index=0
is the superseded original.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED THERE: is_active_path exists only in the storage tier and
was never threaded through archive/query/archive_execution.py into Message /
MessageSemanticFacts, so the domain model has no access to it. That file was a
concurrent lane's write scope. The phase lane deliberately did NOT substitute
branch_index==0 for "accepted", precisely because it would have produced
differently-wrong output while looking authoritative.

DO: thread is_active_path from storage into the domain Message, then switch
both call sites to it. Keep variant_index for what it actually is (creation
order / lineage), and do not conflate the two again -- a comment at each site
saying which one means what would have prevented this.

Not rebuild-blocking on its own (is_active_path is already materialized
correctly), but the domain-model plumbing is read-path work that should land
before anyone trusts mainline reads.
close_reason: Fixed: threaded messages.is_active_path through MessageRecord/Message domain models, both ArchiveMessageRow->Message hydrators (archive_execution.py and the actual api/archive.py route behind Polylogue.get_session()), and message_query_reads.py's SELECT list. Session.mainline_messages() and rendering/core_messages.py's attach_rendered_message_branches now select on is_active_path (falling back to branch_index==0 only when unknown/None). Verified with new tests: variant_index=3-accepted vs variant_index=0-superseded selects the accepted one; is_active_path=None retains all messages; reverting to a bare branch_index==0 check fails the new tests. devtools verify --quick green; devtools test on affected dirs shows only pre-existing unrelated failures. Commit 093e6185d on branch work-9qq7 (pushed to shared feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates).

title: Codex file paths are invisible to tool_path and FTS: 0.07% coverage vs 44% for Claude Code
design:
Measured 2026-07-29 on the live archive (index.db, read-only).

action_pairs.tool_path coverage by origin:
  claude-code-session   ~44%
  codex-session         0.07%   (654 of 995,202 rows)

tool_path is a GENERATED column on blocks
(storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:307):
    COALESCE(json_extract(tool_input,'$.file_path'), json_extract(tool_input,'$.path'))
and the same two keys feed search_text (:310-317), which is what FTS indexes. So
whatever Codex puts file paths in is invisible to BOTH structured path queries
and full-text search.

Consequence beyond search: the readable session label
(insights/session_label.py, polylogue-cijx.4) derives its dominant path from
action_pairs.tool_path, so Codex sessions cannot get a path-bearing label at
all. That is why label collisions are dominated by Codex sessions today.

CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED -- do not guess it. What is known: sampling 4,000 Codex
tool_use blocks, the dominant tool_input key is `arguments` (2,984), then
project/repository_full_name/issue_number/body/pr_number/repo. Attempting to
parse `arguments` as a nested JSON object yielded ZERO dicts across 6,000
sampled rows, so paths are not simply one level deeper under
`$.arguments.file_path`. Either `arguments` is a non-JSON string, or Codex file
operations store paths under a different key entirely, or the sampled
population is skewed toward MCP/GitHub tool calls that genuinely have no path.
Establish which before changing the generated column.

Note the 2026-07-29 Codex parser lane found the dominant exec bucket
(exec_command/write_stdin/shell_command/exec) emits a CLI text envelope rather
than JSON -- if file operations follow the same pattern, the path may not be in
tool_input as structured data at all, and the fix would be parser-side rather
than a generated-column change.

DO: (1) determine where Codex actually records the operated-on path, sampling
by tool_name rather than in aggregate; (2) if it is structured, widen the
generated column -- which is an INDEX-TIER change and must ride the same
rebuild as v45, not a later one; (3) if it is not structured, extract it in
sources/parsers/codex.py so it lands in a field the column already reads.

Both routes are rebuild-blocking: a generated-column change and a parser change
each require the rebuild to take effect.
notes:
2026-07-29 FIXED (b8ac74fc4), cause established.

apply_patch carries its whole payload as a PATCH-FORMAT STRING under 'arguments' -- not
JSON. The path is in '*** Update File: <path>' header lines, so no json_extract could ever
reach it; my earlier note's 'nested arguments dict' hypothesis was wrong because there is
no dict at all. Sampling BY TOOL NAME rather than in aggregate is what showed it:
apply_patch is 18,984 of 20,000 Codex tool_use blocks (95%) and its only key is 'arguments'.

The batched code-mode child path already extracted these via _patch_touched_paths; the
standalone function_call path -- where the 95% lands -- did not. _tool_input_from_arguments
now runs the same helper, setting path/paths/patch, gated on _PATCH_TOOL_NAMES so a
non-patch tool containing that text is never scanned.

11% of patches touch multiple files (554 of 5,000), so 'paths' keeps the full set while
'path' feeds the single generated column. Realised on the next rebuild.
close_reason: Parser fix landed in b8ac74fc4: standalone apply_patch now exposes the operated path where the tool_path/search_text generated columns read it. Not a generated-column change -- the path is unstructured text in the payload, so no json_extract expression could find it.

title: ParsedContentBlock.metadata is parse-time-only and never persisted (no blocks.metadata column)
description:
Discovered while triaging polylogue-5o05 (hermes/gemini-cli JSON-snapshot
wire-field triage): ParsedContentBlock.metadata (base_models.py) is a
parse-time-only scratch field. The `blocks` table (storage/sqlite/
archive_tiers/index.py CREATE TABLE blocks) has NO metadata column -- every
read path selects a literal `NULL AS metadata` (see
storage/sqlite/queries/attachment_blocks.py's `NULL AS metadata` in its
SELECT), and storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:5057 only ever reads
block.metadata to extract a "language" key (folded into the real `language`
column) -- everything else in the dict is silently discarded at write time.

Confirmed-affected call sites (not exhaustive):
- hermes_state.py:_reasoning_metadata() attaches codex_reasoning_items/
  codex_message_items/reasoning_details to a THINKING block's metadata --
  dropped.
- local_agent.py's shared _tool_metadata() (status/timestamp/description/
  displayName/renderOutputAsMarkdown) attached to TOOL_USE/TOOL_RESULT blocks
  for both gemini-cli and hermes -- dropped, except is_error/exit_code which
  are separate real ParsedContentBlock fields (unaffected).
- local_agent.py's gemini "thought" blocks (subject/timestamp metadata) --
  dropped.
- chatgpt.py / codex.py / claude/*.py -- not yet audited for similar
  metadata-dict usage; needs a repo-wide grep of `metadata=` in
  ParsedContentBlock(...) construction across sources/parsers/.

This is a real, live data-loss gap (has been silently true since block-level
metadata was introduced), not something introduced by polylogue-5o05's fix
(which routes its own new captures through session_events instead, since
that tier IS persisted).

Fix shape: either (a) add a real `metadata` TEXT column to `blocks` (additive
index-tier schema change, needs a schema-versioning bump + rebuild plan per
docs/schema.md's derived-tier regime), or (b) audit every current
ParsedContentBlock(metadata=...) call site and migrate genuinely-valuable
fields to session_events (message-scoped) or dedicated ParsedMessage/
ParsedSession fields, then remove the dead metadata field/column plumbing
entirely rather than leave a write-only illusion of persistence.

Needs an index-tier schema decision -- out of polylogue-5o05's no-schema-bump
scope.
notes:
2026-07-29 COORDINATOR DECISION: do NOT add a generic blocks.metadata JSON column.

Scope confirmed. Six parser sites construct ParsedContentBlock.metadata:
  sources/parsers/base_support.py:122        (CODE blocks)
  sources/parsers/hermes_state.py:708        (_reasoning_metadata)
  sources/parsers/drive_support_blocks.py:104
  sources/parsers/browser_capture.py:186
  sources/parsers/claude/common.py:497       (claude-ai web tool evidence)
  sources/parsers/claude/code_parser.py:756
storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:5057 reads exactly ONE key back --
`language`, via _block_language. The blocks table has no metadata column
(verified against the live index: 14 columns, none named metadata), and read
paths select a literal `NULL AS metadata`. Everything else these six sites
write is dropped at write time.

Concretely inert today: the claude-ai web tool evidence landed 2026-07-29
(integration_name/icon_url, approval_key/options, start/stop_timestamp,
display_content, is_mcp_app, mcp_server_url) -- 17 keys at 85-99% document
coverage, parsed and then discarded.

WHY NOT JUST ADD THE COLUMN. A generic JSON metadata column on a 5,042,564-row
table is precisely the shape polylogue-ei0d just removed:
session_provider_usage_events.payload_json was 1.28 GiB of write-only JSON
whose every field was already a typed column beside it. Adding
blocks.metadata would recreate that anti-pattern at ~5M rows, in a tier we are
about to rebuild, with no consumer designed for it. "It is dropped, so persist
it" is the wrong inference; the right question is where each field belongs.

DECISION: route block-scoped evidence through session_events, keyed to the
block/message it describes. session_events.event_type has no CHECK vocabulary,
so this needs NO schema change and no index bump. polylogue-5o05 took exactly
this route for the Hermes tool-availability and message-wire-extras evidence
and it works; that is the precedent to follow.

Where a field is genuinely block-scoped, high-volume AND queried, it earns a
TYPED column (as tool_result_is_error/tool_result_exit_code already did) --
decided per field with evidence, never as a catch-all blob.

FOLLOW-UP WORK: migrate the five non-`language` sites above to session_events
(or typed columns where justified). The claude-ai one is highest value at
85-99% coverage. This is rebuild-blocking: evidence not extracted before the
rebuild needs another rebuild.

Follow-up pass (branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates, commits a0e8ee28b/dec636bde/840b70802/0c563f7d3/199871134):

Discovered that the coordinator-decision comment's cited commits
(3147872f5/90cec3afe/731a08061/1c5e98cbd) were only PARTIALLY present on the
branch tip: 731a08061 (browser_capture.py's session_events routing) had been
silently dropped by a later merge bringing in the typed-blocks-channel
refactor (bb5b7f2ff) that rewrote the same function -- git history
simplification hid the loss from `git log -- path`. Restored it, adapted to
the new turn.blocks-based loop, plus its test.

Remaining 19-site audit (operator's grep count matched exactly):
- browser_capture.py: RESTORED (was lost, now re-fixed) -- routes via
  browser_capture_block_metadata session_events.
- hermes_state.py, drive_support_blocks.py, claude/code_parser.py,
  claude/common.py, base_support.py:132 (CODE language): already correctly
  dispositioned by the prior pass, verified still intact.
- codex.py (_code_mode_child_result_blocks) -- NEW: routed via
  codex_functions_exec_child_result_evidence session_events.
- chatgpt.py (6 sites: content_type on TOOL_USE/THINKING/CODE/TOOL_RESULT/
  CONTEXT text + asset_pointer on IMAGE) -- NEW: one generic
  chatgpt_block_metadata helper, all six sites share it.
- local_agent.py (5 sites: shared _tool_metadata for gemini-cli+hermes
  tool_use/tool_result, gemini "thought" metadata, generic content-index
  metadata) -- NEW: local_agent_block_metadata helper, wired into both
  parse_gemini_cli and parse_hermes.
- base_support.py:88 (image/document segment metadata, shared across Claude
  Code/Claude common/Codex) -- NOT routed to session_events. Disposition:
  the remaining keys after type/media_type are dominated by `source` (the
  base64 payload or an attachment-pipeline-duplicate reference);
  verbatim-copying this into session_events risks embedding large binary
  data into a table meant for small JSON evidence. Stopped building the dead
  dict at all (behavior-neutral: it was already write-time-dropped).

DECISION CONFIRMED: no schema bump. Everything landed in the rebuildable
index tier via session_events (no fixed vocabulary needed --
session_events.event_type has no CHECK). devtools lab policy
schema-versioning stayed "Schema evolution policy intact" throughout.
devtools verify --quick kept exit 0 (also fixed one pre-existing,
unrelated topology-projection drift found broken at the branch tip before
my own changes -- a prior lane's merge added
polylogue/cli/read_views/events.py without regenerating the projection).

All sites verified via anti-vacuity: each new test asserted to fail when
its wiring call is removed, then restored to green. Round-trip production
coverage where warranted (browser_capture has a full receiver -> parser ->
materialize -> index.db test).
Verification (group2 sweep, 2026-07-30): STALE, safe to close. All 19+6 cited sites verified present on origin/master via git log --grep 9x22 (commits 3147872f5/90cec3afe/731a08061/1c5e98cbd/a0e8ee28b/840b70802/dec636bde/0c563f7d3/199871134); git show origin/master:polylogue/sources/parsers/base_support.py confirms the deliberate-drop disposition for the one non-routed site matches the notes exactly. Closing bookkeeping commit 184a4e0be already records the implementation trail. Full scope is on master.
close_reason: Verified complete on origin/master (group2 sweep 2026-07-30 + lane-brief evidence 2026-07-31): all 19+6 cited metadata call sites landed via commits 3147872f5..199871134; base_support.py records the deliberate-drop disposition for the one non-routed site; bookkeeping commit 184a4e0be carries the trail.

title: Census plan bookkeeping is 89% of the durable tier and grows ~1 GB/day with rows recording that nothing happened
design:
Measured on the live archive 2026-07-29 (/realm/db/polylogue/source.db, 6.6 GiB by dbstat).

WHERE THE DURABLE TIER ACTUALLY GOES
  raw_authority_census_plans          (table) 1730.1 MB
    sqlite_autoindex_..._plans_1      (index) 1047.2 MB
    idx_raw_authority_census_plans_status     505.6 MB
    sqlite_autoindex_..._plans_2      (index)  391.0 MB
  raw_authority_census_post_plans     (table)  926.3 MB
    sqlite_autoindex_..._post_plans_1 (index) 1047.0 MB
    sqlite_autoindex_..._post_plans_2 (index)  392.3 MB
  --------------------------------------------------------
  census plan bookkeeping                     6039.5 MB   ~89% of the tier

For comparison, the evidence this archive exists to hold:
  raw_sessions                        (table)   22.3 MB
  blob_refs                           (table)   30.0 MB
  raw_hook_events                     (table)  364.5 MB

source.db is 50% index bytes overall, and the census-plan autoindexes are
essentially the whole reason.

WHAT THE ROWS SAY
  6,621,562 raw_authority_census_plans rows, of which
  6,619,986 (99.98%) have outcome_status='carried_forward'
     reason: "bounded scheduler carried this complete plan forward unchanged"
  executed 1,422 | retryable 139 | terminal 9 | deferred 5 | rejected_stale 1
  raw_authority_census_post_plans: 6,621,527 rows (a near-exact mirror)

Every census re-records the entire pending plan set as carried_forward. The
current census carries 16,890 plans of which 15,691 are residual, so each tick
writes ~16,890 plan rows plus ~16,890 post-plan rows plus seven indexes' worth
of updates, to record that nothing changed.

RATE
  593 censuses in 6.1 days (~97/day), 13.2M rows total.
  ~2.17M rows/day, ~990 MB/day of durable, backed-up, never-rebuilt storage.

There is NO retention. `grep -rn "DELETE FROM raw_authority_census"` over
polylogue/ returns nothing; there is no census-retention config key and no
pruning path anywhere. This is source.db -- the tier that is never rebuilt and
IS backed up -- so it inflates borg backups at the same rate.

WHY RETENTION IS SAFE
Every read of these tables is scoped to a single census:
`storage/raw_authority.py:433` and `:446` both filter `WHERE census_id = ?`
with ORDER BY ordinal / LIMIT / OFFSET -- a per-census inspection pager. No
query aggregates across censuses, and `:2065` only COUNT(*)s for a status
figure. Keeping the last N censuses preserves every actual read pattern.

COMPOUNDING
This is downstream of polylogue-ktwa: the 15,691 residual plans are stuck
because refine_quarantined_raw cannot discharge its proof, so the same plans
are re-recorded ~97 times a day and will keep being re-recorded until that
lands. Fixing ktwa slows the bleed; it does not reclaim the 6 GB or remove the
unbounded-growth property.

DO
1. Add census retention (keep last N, default small) with a pruning path, and
   prove it against the per-census read pattern above.
2. Reconsider recording carried_forward at all. A plan carried forward
   unchanged is derivable from "present in census N, unchanged in N+1" -- the
   99.98% majority may not need a row per census per plan.
3. Decide whether census plan/post-plan history belongs in the DURABLE tier at
   all. It is scheduler bookkeeping, not acquired evidence; ops.db is the
   disposable tier and this is exactly disposable-shaped. Moving it would take
   ~6 GB out of the backup set permanently.
Sequence 1 before 3: retention is cheap and immediately reclaims; the tier move
is a schema decision.
notes:
2026-07-29 — relationship to the m6tp phase (d) deletion plan, checked against docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md and live source.

Censuses are NOT slated for deletion. Phase (d)'s inventory has six items and none is
the census records or the census concept: (1) process-pool machinery, (2) pool-amortization
heuristics, (3) the 64 MiB parse envelope, (4) census BURST-ESCALATION constants, (5)
per-pass candidate REQUERY, (6) the CLI bulk importer's operator-surface status. Item 4 is
the 16/64 batch limits and the census_mode switch; item 5 is the full-backlog recompute.
Both are about the per-tick orchestration AROUND censuses, not the records.

But items 4 and 5 are what generate this bead's growth rate, and neither has landed:
  _RAW_MATERIALIZATION_CONVERGENCE_BATCH_LIMIT = 16   daemon/cli.py:80
  _RAW_MATERIALIZATION_CENSUS_BATCH_LIMIT      = 64   daemon/cli.py:88
  census_mode escalation switch                       daemon/cli.py:838, 898-900
  _raw_materialization_candidate_ids() requery        storage/repair.py:3758,
                                                      called at :4064 and :4235
Only items 1 and 2 are deleted (2026-07-29, this branch). Item 5's stated endpoint is a
persistent in-daemon backlog iterator replacing the per-pass full recompute -- landing it
removes the mechanism that makes every tick recompute and re-record the whole plan set,
which is the ~97 censuses/day driving ~990 MB/day here.

So this bead is complementary, not redundant: item 5 slows or stops the bleed, but it
reclaims none of the accumulated 6,039 MB, and there is still no retention and no DELETE
against these tables anywhere in the tree. Retention is worth landing independently of
whether phase (d) proceeds.
RECONCILE 2026-08-02 (worktree lane, no PR needed): already resolved on master via PR #3390 (prune_raw_authority_census_history, wired unconditionally into record_raw_authority_census) + PR #3530 (_delete_orphaned_raw_authority_plans, composes safely with #3390). Verified live against /realm/db/polylogue: raw_authority_censuses=256 (retention floor holding), census_plans/post_plans=761,602 each (down ~89% from the 6.6M measured 2026-07-29), blockers=4,848. PRAGMA freelist_count shows ~8.1GB reclaimable via VACUUM (SQLite DELETE doesn't shrink the file; freed pages sit on the freelist). Remaining: (1) operator should run 'polylogue check --repair --vacuum' when convenient to physically reclaim the ~8GB -- not run automatically, it's a live single-writer-daemon operation; (2) DO items 2/3 from this bead (stop recording carried_forward rows at all; move census bookkeeping to disposable ops.db tier) are open architectural decisions, not bugs -- bigger schema-regime calls, not part of this pass. Recommend closing the retention-mechanism ask and re-scoping any remainder to a design bead if wanted.
close_reason:
Investigation confirms this bead's urgent ask -- unbounded census-plan/post-plan
growth (89% of source.db, ~1GB/day, no retention) -- is already fixed and
verified live in this session, independent of and prior to the w6hql/lb39z
raw-authority redesign track:

  - PR #3390 (merged 2026-07-29) wires prune_raw_authority_census_history
    into record_raw_authority_census, so retention runs automatically at
    every census tick rather than needing an operator-run maintenance step.
  - PR #3530 (merged 2026-08-01) adds _delete_orphaned_raw_authority_plans,
    composing safely with the above.
  - Live verification against /realm/db/polylogue (2026-08-02): 256 censuses
    (retention floor holding), raw_authority_census_plans/post_plans steady
    at 761,602 rows each (down from the 6,621,562/6,621,527 measured
    2026-07-29 -- an 88.5% reduction), source.db file size 6.6GB -> 1.48GB,
    PRAGMA freelist_count=0 (fully vacuumed, no reclaimable-but-unshrunk
    freelist backlog remains).

This bead's DO item 1 (add retention) is DONE. DO items 2/3 (stop recording
carried_forward rows at all; reconsider whether census bookkeeping belongs
in the durable tier vs disposable ops.db) are real but non-urgent
architectural decisions, not part of the original growth emergency -- split
out to polylogue-ubdxf so they survive independently rather than being lost
when this bead closes. They are related to but not subsumed by
polylogue-w6hql (Phase 2: collapse the verdict vocabulary to a closed enum,
which has no AC/description content yet and is blocked on lb39z items 3-5) --
cross-referenced there.

No code changes made this session; this was a verification-only close after
confirming a previous session's work already shipped the fix.

title: The 2026-04-23 ChatGPT export is not ingested: six months of history absent
description:
Two GDPR exports sit in ~/.local/share/polylogue/inbox:
    chatgpt-data-2025-10-20-06-01-07.zip   -> ingested (6,904 raws reference it)
    chatgpt-data-2026-04-23-20-21-52.zip   -> NOT referenced by any raw_sessions row

So ChatGPT history between 2025-10 and 2026-04 is absent from the archive, and
the 43 browser-captured-only conversations are the extension filling a gap a
sitting export would close.

LIKELY CAUSE, to verify first: the newer export is SHARDED. Its json entries are
conversations-000.json through conversations-024.json plus
shared_conversations.json, message_feedback.json, user.json, user_settings.json,
export_manifest.json. The older export may have used a single conversations.json.
A detector matching the singular filename would skip the sharded layout
entirely and silently.

Check the shard-name assumption before writing any import code -- if it is
wrong, the cause is elsewhere and the fix differs.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The cause is identified by evidence, not assumed from this note. 2. The 2026-04-23 export ingests, and sharded exports are handled as a declared artifact shape in the ChatGPT OriginSpec. 3. Report sessions and date-range added. 4. A future export layout change fails loudly at acquisition rather than being skipped.
close_reason: Root cause: bead premise was stale — export already fully ingested (2402 sessions, acquired 2026-07-02..07-14, before this bead was filed). Shape-based detection already handled the shard layout; fixed real residual gap (silent total-format-drift) in PR #3391.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text:
Investigated. The bead's premise was stale by the time it was filed, not a live bug:

- polylogue import <export.zip> --explain against the real 2026-04-23-20-21-52.zip
  (via a scratch POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT, real export only read) shows current
  master's shape-based ChatGPT detection already parses every one of the 25
  conversations-NNN.json shards correctly (2421 candidate sessions). Detection
  was never filename-based, so the shard split was never actually a parser gap.
- The live archive (/realm/db/polylogue, read via mode=ro) already has 2402 real
  sessions from this export, acquired 2026-07-02 through 2026-07-14 (source.db
  raw_sessions.acquired_at_ms) -- before this bead was filed 2026-07-29. 373 of
  those sessions fall in the claimed Oct 2025-Apr 2026 gap with real content
  (e.g. native_id 68f5735b-... "Declarative NixOS setup", 4 msgs, 2416 words).
- The "NOT referenced by any raw_sessions row" claim doesn't hold against
  `source_path LIKE '%2026-04-23-20-21-52%'` (4815 rows). Likely an earlier
  check assumed a literal "conversations.json" filename and missed the
  shard-suffixed paths.

Real residual gap found and fixed in PR #3391: _lower_bundle_payload's ChatGPT
branch admitted every bundle item unconditionally, so a total-shape-drift
failure (every real conversations-NNN.json record failing shape validation,
e.g. from a future OpenAI format change) was indistinguishable from routine
non-conversation siblings (message_feedback.json etc.) silently producing
empty sessions. Added _chatgpt_bundle_record_specs, which filters via
chatgpt.looks_like_fragment and logs a warning when >=5 mapping-bearing
"near miss" records all fail shape validation, without warning on legitimate
metadata siblings (which never carry a mapping key at all).

AC disposition:
1. Cause identified by evidence -- satisfied (see above).
2. Sharded exports handled as declared OriginSpec shape -- satisfied as
   pre-existing: _chatgpt_spec() in origin_specs.py has no filename-based
   artifact rules; detection was already shape-based. No OriginSpec change
   needed.
3. Sessions/date-range added -- 2402 real sessions from this export are
   already in the archive (acquired before this bead existed), spanning
   native create_time 2022-12-12 through 2026-04-23; 373 in the claimed gap.
   No sessions were added by this PR -- they were already there.
4. Future layout change fails loudly -- satisfied by PR #3391's warning.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_dispatch_payloads.py
(13 passed, 3 new), devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_chatgpt.py
(101 passed), devtools verify --quick (exit 0), byte-identical --explain
output on the real export before/after the change.

No live re-acquisition was run or is needed -- the export is already fully
ingested. Ref PR #3391.

title: ChatGPT outcome is a parser gap: the export is ingested and its status field is read past
description:
CORRECTION to an earlier reading in this batch. chatgpt-export at 100% unknown tool outcome is NOT an acquisition gap -- the official GDPR export IS ingested. 6,904 of 7,690 chatgpt raws have source_path under ~/.local/share/polylogue/inbox/chatgpt-data-2025-10-20-06-01-07.zip.

The export carries exactly the missing data. Sampled from
chatgpt-data-2026-04-23 conversations-NNN.json, 1,705 messages:

  status:  finished_successfully 1,660
           finished_partial_completion 23
           in_progress 22
  recipient (tool targets): python 116, browser 54, myfiles_browser 4,
           chat_consensus_app__jit_plugin.search_papers 4, dalle.text2im 3

finished_partial_completion and in_progress are precisely the terminal states

ChatGPT execution_output status now maps structurally: finished_successfully -> is_error=False, finished_partial_completion -> is_error=True, in_progress and anything else stay NULL as an honest unknown. recipient now stamps tool_name. No outcome inferred from prose. Live baseline was 22,992/22,992 chatgpt-export tool_result blocks with tool_result_is_error IS NULL (100%); projected ~1.3% unknown after rebuild using the bead's own real-sampled proportions. Commit 6d476bd1b.

title: analyze tools raises KeyError('source_name'): the provider->origin retirement is not complete on surfaces
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-07-29 against the deployed CLI and live archive:

  $ polylogue analyze tools
  Error: unexpected error: KeyError: 'source_name'
  Tool call counts
  origin              tool                                    kind              calls
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  (empty)

One of only six analyze subcommands, and it returns nothing.

EXACT CAUSE. storage/sqlite/queries/tool_usage.py defines ToolUsageRow with
field 'origin' (line 30). cli/commands/diagnostics.py:777 reads
    source_name = str(row["source_name"])
and again at 784, 793, 801. The provider->origin retirement renamed the field in
the query layer; the CLI display code was never updated. The stale docstring at
tool_usage.py:60 still reads 'The grouping key is (source_name,
normalized_tool_name, action_kind)', matching the stale code.

WHY THE TYPE CHECKER DID NOT CATCH IT -- the architectural half. row["key"] is
string-key access into a mapping, invisible to mypy --strict. The typed
ToolUsageRow dataclass EXISTS; row.source_name would have been a compile error.
The codebase has the typed model and the surface bypasses it.

SCOPE OF THE CLASS:
  untyped row["..."] / record["..."] / item["..."] access
    polylogue/cli      35 sites
    polylogue/daemon   57
    polylogue/mcp      28
    polylogue/api      28
                      ---
                      148 sites where a rename cannot be type-checked
  references to the retired source_name on surfaces:  66

CLAUDE.md states the provider->origin retirement 'is complete for normalized
archive identity: sessions, messages, actions, insights, query filters,
CLI/API/MCP/daemon read payloads ... There is no payload-rewrite shim.' A live
KeyError on a core CLI surface contradicts that claim; the doc should be
corrected along with the code.

  $ grep -rn 'row\["' --include='*.py' polylogue/cli polylogue/daemon polylogue/mcp polylogue/api | wc -l
  $ grep -rn 'source_name' --include='*.py' polylogue/cli polylogue/daemon polylogue/mcp polylogue/api | wc -l
acceptance_criteria: 1. analyze tools returns rows against the live archive. 2. The fix routes through the typed ToolUsageRow rather than repairing the string key -- repairing the key leaves the class intact. 3. The 66 surface references to source_name are triaged: converted, or shown to be legitimately raw-wire. 4. A regression test invokes analyze tools through the real CLI route, not a mocked row mapping -- the current tests pass while the command is broken, so state which mutation makes the new test fail. 5. The completeness claim in CLAUDE.md is corrected or substantiated.
notes:
RESOLVED on branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates (worktree agent-a4445dcb35874fb25).

ROOT CAUSE: cli/commands/diagnostics.py's `_tools()` text-rendering loop
(the `analyze tools` command) read `row["source_name"]` at four call sites
(orig. lines 777/784/793/801) against raw dict rows returned by
`ArchiveStore.list_tool_call_count_rows` / `list_tool_observed_event_count_rows`
/ `list_tool_action_evidence_count_rows` (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py),
all of which only ever emit an "origin" key. The `--format json` branch of the
SAME function already built a typed `ToolCountRowPayload` (surfaces/payloads.py)
per row via a `row_payload()` helper -- that payload model has no
`source_name` field -- so JSON output was never broken, only the default
text output was.

FIX (AC1+AC2): text loop now calls the SAME `row_payload(row)` helper the JSON
branch already used, and reads `.origin`/`.normalized_tool_name`/`.action_kind`/
`.call_count`/`.event_count`/`.status`/`.evidence_kind` off the typed Pydantic
payload instead of re-indexing the raw dict a second time. This makes the class
of bug mypy-checkable: `ToolCountRowPayload` has no `source_name` attribute, so
a regression here is now an AttributeError caught at review/mypy time in spirit
(payload construction is fully typed) rather than surviving to a runtime
KeyError. Also fixed the matching stale docstring in
storage/sqlite/queries/tool_usage.py:60 (unrelated ToolUsageRow used by
`analyze insights tool-usage`, not this bug's code path, but same stale
"source_name" wording).

AC3 (66 references triaged): grepped `source_name` across cli/daemon/mcp/api
(~50 direct hits at investigation time). All classified:
- Legitimate raw-wire / config-Source-name (not the Origin vocabulary at all):
  cli/shared/helpers.py, helper_source_selection.py, helper_source_state.py,
  formatting.py:format_source_label, daemon/convergence_debt_alert.py
  (watchsource_name_to_family -- config watch-source, unrelated concept),
  cli/messages.py:158 (raw_sessions artifact metadata via
  get_raw_artifacts_for_session -- genuinely raw-tier, not normalized origin),
  daemon/events.py, daemon/http.py, daemon/cli.py, daemon/similarity.py,
  daemon/status.py, api/ingest.py, api/archive.py's explain_import_path /
  QueryFieldRef.source_name (SQL-column-source metadata, different concept
  entirely), watchsource_name_to_family re-export.
- Correct conversion pattern (evidence the doc's intended shape already
  exists elsewhere): daemon/provenance.py SQL `c.source_name AS origin`;
  mcp/payloads.py `origin=source_name_to_origin(record.source_name)`.
- ONE additional genuine same-class leak found (not a crash, a naming leak):
  polylogue/storage/search/models.py's `SearchHit.source_name` field is
  populated with a normalized Origin value (query_builders.py SQL literally
  does `s.origin AS source_name`), backing the public `Polylogue.search()` /
  `PolylogueSync.search()` API. Filed as polylogue-gody (separate, smaller,
  ~4-file fix) rather than fixing in this PR: storage/search/** isn't in this
  bead's owned surface (insights/cli/api) and search_messages_impl itself
  turned out to be dead code (no callers), so it's lower urgency and cleanly
  separable.

AC4 (regression test, real route): added
tests/unit/cli/test_diagnostics.py::test_tools_renders_against_real_archive_backed_store.
Unlike the pre-existing test_tools_renders_tool_usage_insight (which
monkeypatches ArchiveStore.open_existing with a fake store whose fixture rows
carry BOTH "source_name" and "origin" keys -- that's exactly why it passed
while the command was broken in production), the new test seeds a real
index.db via SessionBuilder + a real tool_use block and invokes `_tools()`
against a real ArchiveStore/SQL read path. Verified the mutation: reverting
`item.origin` back to `row["source_name"]` in diagnostics.py reproduces
`KeyError: 'source_name'` in exactly this new test (11 pre-existing tests in
the file stay green under that mutation -- proof they could never have caught
this).

Also reproduced live: reflink-copied /realm/db/polylogue/index.db (v43,
36GB) to /realm/tmp/ (deleted after use), ran
`POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT=... polylogue analyze tools` (default tool-use-blocks
basis) and `--basis observed-events` against it -- both now return real rows
(codex-session/exec_command, claude-code-session/bash, etc.) with no
KeyError. `--basis actions` hit a 120s command timeout on this basis's heavier
bucket-aggregation query over the full 36GB corpus (unrelated perf
characteristic of that basis, not this bug -- it never reached the display
loop that raised).

AC5 (CLAUDE.md completeness claim): grepped for the bead's exact quoted
sentence ("is complete for normalized archive identity ... no
payload-rewrite shim") across CLAUDE.md and docs/*.md in the current
worktree -- it is not present verbatim; the current "Vocabulary: Provider vs
Origin vs Source" section's actual wording ("Normalized archive identity
carries Origin; source_name in rebuildable storage rows is a persistence
detail converted while hydrating typed models, never a second public
identity vocabulary") is accurate now that this bug is fixed and modulo the
one tracked exception (polylogue-gody). Not editing CLAUDE.md further since
I could not find the over-broad literal claim to correct in this checkout.

VERIFICATION:
- nix develop --command mypy polylogue/cli/commands/diagnostics.py
  polylogue/storage/sqlite/queries/tool_usage.py -> Success: no issues found
  in 2 source files
- nix develop --command devtools test tests/unit/cli/test_diagnostics.py ->
  19 passed
- nix develop --command ruff check / ruff format --check on the 3 changed
  files -> all clean
- Live archive repro/verify as above (read-only reflink copy, deleted after).

Changed files: polylogue/cli/commands/diagnostics.py,
polylogue/storage/sqlite/queries/tool_usage.py (docstring only),
tests/unit/cli/test_diagnostics.py.
close_reason: Fixed: routed analyze tools text rendering through the existing typed ToolCountRowPayload; added real-archive regression test; triaged source_name surface leak (66 refs), filed one follow-up (polylogue-gody) for a non-crashing instance out of this bead's owned scope

title: The schema constrains values but never relationships: 13,743 rows end before they start
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 (every number below carries the command that produced it -- RE-RUN, do not trust).

SHAPE
  516 columns in index.db, 231 nullable (45%), 34 JSON-blob TEXT columns, 17 generated columns
  $ grep -cE '^\s+[a-z_]+\s+(TEXT|INTEGER|REAL|BLOB)' polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py
  $ grep -cE 'GENERATED ALWAYS' polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py

DEFECT 1 -- no intra-row relationship constraints anywhere.
  sqlite3 -readonly index.db "select count(*) from session_phases where ended_at_ms < started_at_ms;"
    -> 11,129 of 29,432 (37.8%)
  sqlite3 -readonly index.db "select count(*) from session_work_events where ended_at_ms < started_at_ms;"
    -> 2,614 of 21,190 (12.3%)
  grep -c 'ended_at_ms >= started_at_ms' polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py
    -> 0
Rows end before they begin, and duration_ms is clamped by max(0, ...) in the
consuming code, so the defect is arithmetic-honest and invisible.

The schema uses CHECK well for VALUE ranges (>= 0, enum membership, json_valid)
and almost never for RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN COLUMNS IN A ROW. The technique is
known and used exactly once: raw_authority_blockers has
  CHECK((resolved_at_ms IS NULL) = (resolution IS NULL))

DEFECT 2 -- same-row derivations stored as independent columns.
  duration_ms could be GENERATED ALWAYS AS (ended_at_ms - started_at_ms)
  session_provider_usage_events.total_tokens is stored beside its own components

session_provider_usage_events.payload_json (700 MB, zero readers -- polylogue-c3ip),

session_profiles.

Same-row derivations (duration_ms, total_tokens) become generated columns or are dropped. 4. NULL semantics are split: unknown carries a reason, not-applicable is expressed structurally. 5. Projected inverted rows after rebuild: 0 (was 13,743).
