That mis-conflation is real and live (~8.2K superseded messages shown as mainline, ~1.5K accepted hidden); filed as polylogue-9qq7.

title: A representation is computed or generated, never written
description:
The archive stores several REPRESENTATIONS of an entity as if they were the entity, then needs machinery to keep each honest. One surface already does it correctly and is the model to copy.

CORRECT, and the template: blocks.search_text is a GENERATED ALWAYS column. It is a search projection over block content that cannot drift, cannot go stale, and needs no refresh tracking. Same for session_id, message_id, block_id, repo_id, tool_command, tool_path -- twelve generated columns proving the technique is available and used.

WRITTEN COPIES that should be computed or generated:
  sessions.title            a LABEL projection. Provider titles are real and
                            belong here; a structural/derived label does not --
                            it would collide with them and freeze ('340 msgs')
                            the moment the session grows. Belongs in 4p1's
                            Projection, computed per request.
  action_pairs              a RELATIONAL projection over blocks that copies six
                            columns (tool_name, semantic_type, tool_command,
                            tool_path, is_error, exit_code), two of which are
                            themselves GENERATED on blocks. 1,870,733 rows.
  delegation_facts          a JOIN projection materialized while its own
                            derivation view returns 0 rows -- the failure mode
                            this invariant prevents.
  session_profiles          a STATISTICS projection carrying five versioning
                            columns (materializer_version, enrichment_version,
                            enrichment_family, inference_version,
                            inference_family), all constant across 18,871 rows,
                            existing only to date a copy.
  insight_materialization   seven freshness proxy columns tracking whether other
                            copies are current.

THE GENERAL FORM: an entity has ONE identity and MANY representations --
transcript, relational, rendered, searchable, statistical, labelled. Multiplicity
is correct and necessary. The error is materializing one representation and
treating it as the entity, which then requires freshness tracking, refresh
scopes and guards to keep it honest.

Test to apply per case: if the underlying evidence changed, would this value be
wrong? If yes it is a representation, and it must be computed at read or
expressed as a generated column -- never written and tracked.

Performance materialization remains legitimate, under one condition: it is keyed
by the hash of its inputs (see the content-addressed derivation bead), so a
stale row is a cache miss rather than a lie.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Each written representation above is converted to a read-time projection, a generated column, or a hash-keyed cache -- with the choice justified per case. 2. No new column is added whose value could be wrong if untouched evidence changed. 3. Freshness-tracking columns are deleted as their representations convert, not maintained in parallel. 4. blocks.search_text is cited as the reference implementation in whatever doc records this.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-01, evidence split into two follow-ups per the parent cuxz epic's own precedent (already split into cuxz.1/.2/.3/.10). Disposition: (1) sessions.title is NOT a defect — no structural-label freeze found, title only populated from real parser-asserted evidence; no action. (2) action_pairs is ALREADY the correct pattern — fully DELETE+INSERT-rebuilt per content-hash lifecycle (refresh_action_pairs), prior fix polylogue-2i2w already removed the duplicated payload text; the remaining join/rank/outcome columns exist because the tool_use<->tool_result windowed self-join is too expensive per-read at 1.87M rows — exactly the bead's own stated carve-out, not a violation. (3) insight_materialization is MISCHARACTERIZED by the bead — its 7 columns are the primary input to the materializer_version/high_water_mark staleness machinery DaemonConverger is built on (documented deliberate design), not a freshness-proxy anti-pattern. (4) delegation_facts is a genuine defect, split to new bead (view-vs-table design decision needed). (5) session_profiles has 4 confirmed-dead versioning columns, split to new bead (concrete, shippable, contract-versioned removal).

title: Pick content-defined chunking over durable cursors and delete the classification it makes irrelevant
description:
DECISION, not a fork. Two paths were available for the append/prefix problem; they are mutually exclusive and one is clearly better.

  (A) make the ingest cursor durable (polylogue-aex0's current framing)
      -- fixes the symptom; the cursor remains a thing that can be wrong, wiped,
         or disagree with the bytes
  (B) content-defined chunking (rolling hash, as Borg and restic use)
      -- prefix growth leaves every prior chunk byte-identical, so dedup is
         automatic. No cursor. No offset. No append-vs-full distinction.

Pick (B). It does not merely solve the problem, it removes three concepts:
  - the ingest cursor (and its durability question, and ops.db's role in it)
  - revision_kind classification -- the 35.2% of raws currently 'unknown'
    (14,561 of 41,363) stop mattering, because chunk identity does not care
  - append_end_offset, which is 100% NULL across all 18,730 raw_revision_heads
    rows anyway

MEASURED PRIZE: 2,703 logical sources hold 8,482 full snapshots totalling
17,055.5 MB where 2,444.2 MB would do -- 14,611.3 MB (85.7%) is redundant
prefix. The blob store is whole-file SHA-256 (storage/blob_store.py), so
content-addressing dedupes EQUALITY and gives nothing on CONTAINMENT, which is
the dominant pattern for append-only transcripts.

CHEAP INTERIM, available now and compatible with (B): when a new blob for a
logical source is a strict byte-prefix extension of a retained one, drop the
older after proving containment. Captures most of the 14.3 GB with no chunker.

WHY THIS SHAPE MATTERS BEYOND STORAGE: it is the clearest available example of
the pattern worth seeking elsewhere -- do not improve a classification, remove
the need for it.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A decision record states (B) and retires (A)'s framing on aex0 rather than leaving both open. 2. Chunk-level dedup is implemented and measured against the 14,611.3 MB baseline. 3. revision_kind and append_end_offset are deleted, not merely unused -- if either survives, state what still reads it. 4. Ingest wall-clock is measured before and after against the 623q envelope. 5. The interim prefix-containment reclaim may ship first; it does not close this bead.
notes:
2026-07-29 (polylogue-623q measurement lane): deprioritized per operator direction for today's real-rebuild decision. Recording a compose/conflict assessment since it was asked for, without implementing (schema/storage-sqlite changes this bead needs are outside this lane's write scope: storage/sqlite/** is owned by a different lane on this branch).

COMPOSE, DO NOT CONFLICT, with the already-landed blob_hash rebuild paging (IndexGenerationStore.next_raw_page, ORDER BY blob_hash, raw_id): they operate at different layers. blob_hash paging is a READ-TIME SCHEDULING optimization over already-stored raw_sessions rows -- it exploits WHOLE-FILE equality (identical full snapshots share one blob_hash and get scheduled adjacently so the existing per-page/cross-page dedup cache catches them). Content-defined chunking (CDC) would change how raw bytes are STORED/hashed at ingest time -- a per-chunk identity enabling CONTAINMENT dedup (append growth reuses earlier chunks), which whole-file hashing structurally cannot express. Landing CDC does not require touching next_raw_page's ordering logic; it would, however, make MUCH of blob_hash paging's current benefit moot for the append-only-file case specifically, because the 8,482-full-snapshot/2,703-logical-source duplication this bead's own numbers cite would mostly stop existing as separate raw_sessions rows in the first place -- CDC ingest would produce new incremental chunks instead of near-duplicate whole-file snapshots. blob_hash paging remains valuable post-CDC for genuinely accidental whole-file duplicates (re-exports via different acquisition paths), just a smaller slice of the corpus.

Relevance to 623q's measurement: CDC is upstream of the writer-bound apply_s cost 623q measured (54-77% of wall-clock) only insofar as it would shrink the number of raw_sessions rows/logical sources census has to walk and the writer has to replay in the first place (fewer near-duplicate full-snapshot rows -> fewer index_parsed_write/full_replace calls). It does not change the PER-ROW writer cost. Given 623q's measurement shows the writer, not decode parallelism, as the binding constraint, this bead is a legitimate lever for a FUTURE rebuild's corpus size but is not something today's imminent rebuild can benefit from (the corpus is what it is; CDC would need to run first and reduce it before the next rebuild). Not attempted this session: full implementation (schema changes to raw_sessions/blob storage, revision_kind/append_end_offset deletion) is out of this lane's write scope and is a multi-day epic in its own right, matching this bead's own AC scope (5 ACs including chunk-level dedup implementation and measurement against the 14,611.3 MB baseline).

title: Every outcome field is dominantly unknown while the provider supplies stop_reason 608,608 times
description:
A sweep for fallback buckets that dominate their own column found one coherent family: the archive cannot say how anything ended.

  delegation_facts.result_status          'unknown'   99%  of 11,692
  delegation_facts.parent_terminal_state  'unknown'   96%  of 11,692
  session_profiles.terminal_state         'unknown'   85%  of 18,871
  delegation_facts.child_terminal_state   'unknown'   56%  of 11,692
  delegation_facts.result_is_error        NULL      98.6%; success recorded 0 times
  blocks.tool_result_is_error             NULL        72%  of 1,844,545

Three separate derived columns guess at terminal state and fail 85-99% of the
time. Meanwhile the wire carries the answer on every assistant message:

  "stop_reason":"tool_use"        583,171
  "stop_reason":"end_turn"         21,666
  "stop_reason":"stop_sequence"     3,684
  "stop_reason":"refusal"              70
  "stop_reason":"max_tokens"           17
                                    -------
                                    608,608

And the parser's OWN model already declares the field --
sources/providers/claude_code_models.py:206 has 'stop_reason: str | None = None'
-- but nothing persists it. The only other references in polylogue/ are in
cli/commands/embed.py and cli/shared/embed_stats.py, which concern the
EMBEDDING JOB's stop reason and are unrelated.

The two rarest values are the most valuable and are entirely invisible today:
70 refusals and 17 max_tokens truncations across the whole corpus. A truncated
or refused turn is precisely the thing a postmortem needs to find, and no
surface can express it.

RELATED FALLBACK DOMINANCE from the same sweep, different cause:
  repos.origin_url            empty 89% of 1,623   (see the repo-identity bead)
  session_repos.branch_name   empty 81% of 16,341
  session_events.summary      empty 97% of sample
acceptance_criteria: 1. stop_reason is persisted per assistant message from the provider record. 2. terminal_state and result_status derive from persisted provider evidence, or are deleted -- three columns guessing the same fact do not survive. 3. 'unknown' ceases to be the dominant value of any outcome column; where genuinely unknown it carries the reason (see the outcome-NULL-reason bead). 4. refusal and max_tokens are queryable: a query for truncated or refused turns returns the 17 and 70 cases. 5. Re-measure each percentage in the table above.
close_reason: Merged PR #3535: stop_reason threaded through ArchiveMessageRow/ArchiveBlockRow to the query path (closing the gap a prior PR left open), MessageSemanticFacts gained stop_reason, and _terminal_state now derives refused/truncated from it before falling back to unknown. AC1-3 satisfied for the query path; AC4 (query-grammar field predicate) and re-measurement against live archive explicitly deferred as follow-up.

title: Git support is inference over prose while typed git records are discarded
description:
Measured 2026-07-29.

WHAT EXISTS: branch/url/sha snapshotted at session start (13-16% coverage, see
the repo-identity bead); a repos table keyed on two unreliable fields;
session_commits holding HEAD-at-session-start with ONE writer and ZERO readers
(2,989 rows, detection_type/method/confidence all constant); and
insights/session_commit.py shelling out to git log on demand via an
on-demand view that materializes nothing.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: any commit corpus, diff, authorship, branch lineage, or
merge/PR outcome.

WHAT IS DISCARDED: Claude Code emits typed pr-link records --
  {"type":"pr-link","prNumber":3126,
   "prUrl":"https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3126",
   "prRepository":"Sinity/polylogue","sessionId":"cdaf1c01-..."}
20,702 of them in the live corpus, dropped by _SKIPPED_SIDECAR_RECORD_TYPES.

So the archive infers git from prose (regex ref extraction, time-window and
file-overlap scoring in derive_scan_window/score_file_overlap) while deleting
the structured git records the provider hands it. The correlator exists to
reconstruct, badly, a join that arrives typed and free.

file-history-snapshot records (34,132, also discarded) carry trackedFileBackups
plus a timestamp -- the 'checkpointed' tier of polylogue-cijx's trajectory
grading, above 'observed'. Captured by the provider, never read.

SEQUENCE: read the records before building the correlator. This may reduce
cijx.1 and its four blocked consumers (212.2, xyel, kph, fs1.4) from an
inference problem to a parse problem.
acceptance_criteria: 1. pr-link records are persisted as typed session->PR evidence and become the producer those four consumer beads read. 2. file-history-snapshot is persisted and raises file-trajectory grading from observed to checkpointed where present. 3. session_commits either gains a reader against honest semantics or is deleted -- it does not survive as a write-only table. 4. Any retained heuristic correlator emits graded candidates, never rows indistinguishable from provider-supplied fact. 5. Report coverage: sessions with a typed PR link, before and after.
notes: VERIFICATION (group3 sweep): LIVE. Recent (2026-07-29) finding, no notes since filing. Checked: session_commits table and pr-link record handling -- description states pr-link records are dropped by _SKIPPED_EVENT_TYPES and session_commits has zero readers; no evidence of a persisted PR-link table or session_commits reader landing since. Genuinely open, not stale.
close_reason:
Most of this bead's AC were already satisfied by prior sessions before
this one started (verified against current master, not assumed):

AC1 (pr-link records persisted as typed session->PR evidence): satisfied
-- session_refs table (kind=pull_request) + claude_pr_link session_events,
landed in the v46 batch (5e23e6abf). Live measurement: 18,949 session_refs
rows, all pull_request; both target sessions carry them (49 and 139
rows respectively).

AC2 (file-history-snapshot persisted, raises file-trajectory grading
observed->checkpointed): satisfied, via a more precise mechanism than the
AC's literal wording anticipated -- file_edits.original_file (v46,
polylogue-2qx.4) captures the actual pre-edit file state per edit tool
call, which is what the index.py DDL comment identifies as raising the
grading (not the coarser file-history-snapshot whole-session backup
list, which is ALSO persisted as claude_file_history_snapshot events but
is the "observed" tier, not the promotion mechanism itself).

AC4 (heuristic correlator emits graded candidates, never indistinguishable
from provider fact) and AC5 (report coverage before/after): satisfied by
polylogue-l9su (PR #3425, closed 2026-07-31 same day): GitHubRef gained a
`source` field (typed_session_ref vs heuristic_regex), a
CorrelationDisagreement surface flags conflicts instead of silently
preferring one signal, and detect_session_commits now parses git commit
Claude-Session trailers against a session's own claude_bridge_session
events (detection_method="origin_reported"). Live re-measure from that PR:
167 sessions carry typed pull_request session_refs (1,690 PR-number rows);
regex-only extraction over the same sessions finds 1,934 PR mentions (102
agree exactly, 65 would have surfaced extra/different numbers -- now
surfaced as disagreements instead of silent).

AC3 (session_commits either gains a reader or is deleted -- the one
genuinely still-open item, verified false-absence two ways: grep for
`FROM session_commits` and for any reader module before concluding it was
missing): fixed on this branch (commit 04ec36f28). New SessionCommitRecord
model + async/sync readers (storage/sqlite/queries/session_commits.py,
following the session_refs precedent), threaded through
query_store_archive/repository, wired into BOTH existing correlation
entrypoints (api/archive.py::session_correlation_payload, the HTTP
GET /api/sessions/:id/correlate surface; and
insights/correlation_view.py::run_correlation_view's JSON output, the CLI
`read --view correlation --format json` surface) as a `checkout_commits`
field, explicitly separated from the heuristic `commits` list rather than
merged into it. This is a narrow, honest fact (repo checkout HEAD at
session-capture time, method='parser-git-meta', confidence=1.0) distinct
from the on-demand commit-authorship correlator -- it was never claimed to
subsume that mechanism.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/api/test_facade_contracts.py
tests/unit/cli/test_correlate_view.py tests/unit/insights/test_session_commit.py
(all pass except the pre-existing, unrelated clock-gap failure). mypy
(repo-wide, new module needs topology projection regen): 0 issues.

title: Repository identity is really cwd: 84% of sessions have no git evidence and one path yields conflicting repo names
description:
Measured 2026-07-29 on the live archive.

GIT EVIDENCE COVERAGE across 18,871 sessions:
  git_branch          2,989   15.8%
  git_repository_url  2,495   13.2%
  commit_hash         3,003   15.9%
For the other ~84%, repo assignment comes purely from working_directories. The
column named 'repo' is therefore 'cwd'. A session in /home/sinity is recorded as
being in the 'sinity' repo.

THE KEY IS TWO UNRELIABLE FIELDS. write.py:5150
  _repo_id(origin_url, root_path) = f'{origin_url}\x1f{root_path}'
and write.py:5143 _repo_name takes the URL basename when a URL exists, else the
path basename. So the same directory produces multiple rows with DIFFERENT names:
  /realm/project/sinex                  -> sinex
  /realm/project/sinex                  -> sinnix
  /realm/project/sinex                  -> polylogue
  /realm/project/sinex-gateway-shutdown -> sinnix
and one repository splits across spellings: polylogue holds 106 distinct
repo_ids, sinex 28, sinnix 31.

THREE ENTITIES ARE COLLAPSED INTO ONE COMPOSITE KEY:
  Repository -- stable identity. The right key is the ROOT-COMMIT SHA
      (git rev-list --max-parents=0): content-addressed, survives renames,
      remote changes, mirrors and forks. Remote URLs are ALIASES of a
      repository, not its identity -- which is exactly why three spellings
      produced three repos. This is the same philosophy the archive already
      applies to embeddings (input hash) and blocks (content hash).
  Checkout -- a filesystem path bound to a repository at a branch. Every
      /realm/worktrees/polylogue-* is a checkout of ONE repository, not fifteen.
  Observation -- a session seen in a checkout, at a commit, at a time.

A directory with no git evidence is honestly A DIRECTORY. Do not synthesize a
repository for it.

OPEN DECISIONS, not measurements -- resolve explicitly rather than assuming:
  (a) root-commit identity is unavailable for repos polylogue never had
      filesystem access to (an imported ChatGPT session merely mentioning a repo)
  (b) a path reused across projects over time belongs to different repositories
      in different intervals
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03; AC already set — this is the how): three typed entities replacing the composite _repo_id (write.py:5150 f"{origin_url}\x1f{root_path}"):
- Repository: identity = root-commit SHA (git rev-list --max-parents=0) where obtainable; remote URLs are ALIASES (normalized: strip .git, unify ssh/https/scp forms) recorded as evidence, never identity.
- Checkout: filesystem path bound to a Repository over a time interval (resolves open decision (b): path reuse across projects = different intervals, keyed by observed root-commit at observation time).
- Observation: session seen in a checkout at a commit/time.
Open decision (a) resolution: for sessions with no filesystem access (imported ChatGPT mentions), do NOT synthesize a Repository — resolve to a normalized remote-URL alias cluster when a URL exists, else a plain directory entity; read surfaces say which kind they got (AC 4).
IMPLEMENTATION PATH: this is index-tier derived identity — new/changed columns + resolution logic in write.py (_repo_id/_repo_name successors) with an IndexDeltaDeclaration (SEMANTIC_REPARSE: identity of derived rows changes); the reindex is the backfill, no bespoke migration. repo: query field resolves through the normalized identity (archive/query lowering). Root-commit capture: for LIVE local checkouts, capture at ingest time from the session's cwd git evidence when present; never shell out at query time.
PITFALL: do not let alias normalization merge genuinely distinct repos (forks share no root commit — safe; mirrors share it — intended merge); test over the observed spelling set (AC 2 names the shapes).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Repository, checkout and observation are separate entities; repo identity does not include a filesystem path. 2. Remote-URL spellings that denote one remote resolve to one repository, with tests over the observed spelling set (empty/https/ssh/.git). 3. Live re-measure: polylogue/sinex/sinnix collapse to one repository each, with checkouts enumerable underneath. 4. A session with no git evidence resolves to a directory, not a repository, and read surfaces say which. 5. The repo: query field resolves through normalized identity -- a session recorded under one spelling matches a query using another.
notes:
VERIFICATION (group3 sweep): LIVE. Recent (2026-07-29) structural finding with no notes recorded since filing -- no rg evidence of a Repository/Checkout typed-entity refactor landing (git log --grep cijx shows no matching commit). repo: field still resolves through _repo_id/_repo_name path-based logic per description. Genuinely open architectural work, not stale.

Footprint: polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py (_repo_id derivation), read-surface repo columns in polylogue/storage/sqlite/queries/sessions.py.

comments.text:
Scoped lane (sources/**+insights/**, no storage/sqlite/**) on
feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates, commit 243bfb3ea.

Verified live: the storage-side identity rework this bead calls for
(content-addressed repo_id via root-commit SHA, repo_checkouts,
repository/checkout/observation split) is NOT landed on this branch despite
the task brief describing it as "partially addressed already" --
repos.repo_id in storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:732 is still the
plain SQL GENERATED `origin_url || char(31) || root_path` column, and there
is no repo_checkouts table anywhere in this checkout. That work either
belongs to a different, not-yet-merged lane, or has not started; either way,
storage/sqlite/** is out of this lane's write scope this cycle (a concurrent
lane owns it), so it was correctly left untouched here.

What I did instead (the parser/attribution half, per the mission's scope
split): _append_repo_identity_evidence in polylogue/sources/emitter.py, run
at _SessionEmitter._maybe_enrich (the single point every session from every
provider passes through after provider-specific sidecar enrichment, before
leaving sources/** for storage). It grades each session's location evidence
without touching any table:
  grade="git_evidence"    when git_branch/git_repository_url/commit_hash is
                           non-empty
  grade="directory_only"  when only working_directories is non-empty
  (no event)               when there is no location evidence at all
persisted as a session_event (event_type "repo_identity_evidence",
event_type has no CHECK vocabulary so this needed no migration), payload
{grade, root_paths, git_repository_url, git_branch, git_commit_hash}.

MEASURED (read-only, file:...?mode=ro against /realm/db/polylogue/index.db,
NOT written to -- confirms this bead's own baseline exactly):
  sessions total: 18,871
  sessions with ANY git evidence (branch/url/commit): 3,003 (15.9%)
  sessions with NO git evidence (the "directory, not repository" case,
    per cijx.4 decision 1): 15,868 (84.1%)

AC disposition:
  AC1 (repository/checkout/observation separate entities, no filesystem path
    in repo identity) -- NOT done here; storage-side, out of scope.
  AC2 (remote-URL spellings resolve to one repository) -- NOT done here;
    storage-side, out of scope.
  AC3 (live re-measure: polylogue/sinex/sinnix collapse to one repo each) --
    NOT applicable without AC1/AC2 landing first.
  AC4 (a session with no git evidence resolves to a directory, read surfaces
    say which) -- SUBSTRATE SATISFIED at the parser layer: every session now
    carries a typed repo_identity_evidence grade a reader can consult without
    re-deriving it from working_directories. The storage-side repos/
    session_repos tables still synthesize a repo row keyed on root_path
    regardless of grade (write.py:_write_repo_edges, out of this lane's
    scope) -- so today's read SURFACES (CLI/API/MCP) do not yet expose the
    distinction end-to-end. That wiring is the remaining half, blocked on the
    storage-side identity rework landing.
  AC5 (repo: query field resolves through normalized identity across
    spellings) -- NOT done here; storage-side, out of scope.

Writer contract left for the storage-side lane: session_events rows with
event_type="repo_identity_evidence" (one per session, not per-record) carry
{grade: "git_evidence"|"directory_only", root_paths: [str],
git_repository_url, git_branch, git_commit_hash}. This is exactly the signal
the storage rework needs to decide "synthesize a repository row" vs "this is
a bare directory" without re-deriving it from raw session columns.

title: Titles must describe what a session did: prompt echoes collide 78-way and do not distinguish sessions
description:
THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES THE DESIGN. Codex state_5.sqlite threads, full scan:
  2,771 threads carry a title
  2,185 distinct titles
    166 titles are shared by more than one thread
  worst: 78x 'take over claude's session 755b624d-074f-4d4f-b2fa-02d3a9e...'
         78x 'familiarize yourself with the repo and its full beads-set'
         36x 'find, using whatever means, either direclty ~/.codex or po...'

A title you cannot select by is not a title. BOTH providers produce
first-prompt echoes, so copying the provider does not solve this:
  - Claude Code ai-title records exist but cover ~12% (64 of 520 session files
    in the polylogue project dir; 2026-05: 8, 06: 25, 07: 31 -- recent feature)
  - Codex threads.title covers 2,771 of 3,054 but the values ARE the echoes above

Current archive state: 13,611 of 18,871 sessions (72.1%) titled with a raw UUID,
plus 2,369 (12.6%) with >60-char echo titles = 84.7% unusable.

DESIGN: derive the title from what the session DID. Every input is already in
the index, measured against untitled claude-code sessions:
  repo                     100%  (3,000 of 3,000 sampled)
  work_events              82%
  file paths               382,940 action_pairs rows carry tool_path
  timestamps               after m3p9
DEFINED AND MEASURED 2026-07-29, so the executing agent does not have to invent
it. Label = repo | distinct files touched | message count | date:

  sqlite3 -readonly index.db "with pl as (select s.session_id, s.message_count,
    (select r.repo_name from session_repos sr join repos r
       on r.origin_url=substr(sr.repo_id,1,instr(sr.repo_id,char(31))-1)
      and r.root_path=substr(sr.repo_id,instr(sr.repo_id,char(31))+1)
     where sr.session_id=s.session_id limit 1) repo,
    (select count(distinct ap.tool_path) from action_pairs ap
      where ap.session_id=s.session_id and ap.tool_path is not null) nfiles,
    date(s.created_at_ms/1000,'unixepoch') d
    from sessions s where s.origin='claude-code-session' and s.title=s.native_id limit 4000)
    select ...;"

  4,000 untitled sessions -> 3,862 distinct labels
  collisions            138 (3.5%)
  max collision size     10
  labels used twice      62
  labels used 3+ times   24

Contrast the echo baseline: 166 colliding titles with a SEVENTY-EIGHT-way worst
case. Structural collisions are small and mostly pairwise, and the 10-way case
is a batch of near-identical subagent spawns -- sessions that genuinely are
alike. Adding one more discriminator (top file path, or a duration bucket) cuts
it further; 3.5% pairwise is already usable.

Inputs are all present: repo on 100% of untitled sessions, message_count on
100%, 382,940 action_pairs rows carrying tool_path, dates on 94%.

Prose synthesis is a worthwhile ADDITION, not the base: ~10,157 sessions x ~2K
head tokens is a few dollars on a small model, and the budgeted-external-call
pattern already exists (embeddings, embedding_max_cost_usd ceiling, batching,
progress, reconcile). Claude Code's ai-title is itself an LLM summary, so this
reproduces the provider's own method for the residual.

sessions.title_source already models provenance as
('origin','path','heuristic','user','unknown'); add a synthesized value and
stamp which tier produced each title so a mixed corpus stays honest.
acceptance_criteria: 1. sessions.title holds ONLY provider-supplied titles, or NULL. A derived label is never written to it. 2. The display label is computed at read time from repo, work shape, duration and size -- it is a projection, not a column, so it cannot go stale as a session grows. 3. title_source distinguishes provider-supplied from absent; it does not need a value for the derived label because the derived label is not stored. 4. Un-skipping ai-title and acquiring threads.title are inputs, not the plan -- neither closes this bead alone. 5. Re-run 'polylogue find repo:polylogue' and show the before/after rows. 6. Report the collision rate of the derived label on a sample -- collisions are acceptable, silent staleness is not.
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (operator, 2026-07-29). An earlier draft of this bead proposed storing structural titles as a field. That is wrong for two reasons and the correction is the actual point:

  (a) it would collide with genuine provider titles, which now exist for Claude
      Code (ai-title) and Codex (threads.title);
  (b) a serialized structural label goes STALE the moment the session grows --
      'polylogue - implementation - 340 msgs - 2h' freezes at 340 while the
      session continues. Storing a computed value and then needing machinery to
      keep it honest is the precise pattern this backlog is trying to remove.

So this is not a titles problem, it is an IDENTITY AND REPRESENTATION problem:
  - a session's identity is provider-supplied and stable;
  - its display label is a projection over current state and belongs in the read
    algebra (polylogue-4p1), computed per request;
  - the archive stores what the provider said, not what a renderer would say.

Also caution: the 'implementation/research/review/planning' work-event label
proposed as a title input is itself heuristic -- constant per-type confidence,
and classifications like 'Create my holiday video' -> implementation. See the
session_work_events bead. Prefer structural facts that are not themselves
inferred (repo, file paths, duration, message count, token spend).
Codex closed-PR audit 2026-08-06: PR #3846 merged freshness and non-persistence behavior but still omits duration from the read-time structural label required by AC2. Keep open until duration is derived and tested through the read route.

title: Codex SQLite state is never acquired: 5 databases, 706 MB, including spawn topology and 2,771 titles
description:
Measured 2026-07-29. ~/.codex holds five SQLite databases; raw_sessions contains no row whose source_path is any of them.

  state_5.sqlite     39 MB   threads (3,054 rows, 2,771 with a non-empty title),
                             thread_spawn_edges (1,030), thread_dynamic_tools,
                             remote_control_enrollments, external_agent_config_imports
  logs_2.sqlite     627 MB   logs (47,060 rows: ts, level, target, module_path,
                             file, line, thread_id, process_uuid, estimated_bytes)
  memories_1.sqlite 456 KB   stage1_outputs, jobs
  goals_1.sqlite     44 KB   thread_goals, thread_goal_continuation_deferrals
  codex-dev.db       36 KB

THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS AND IS USED FOR A DIFFERENT ORIGIN: Hermes .db
files ARE acquired (/home/sinity/.hermes/state.db and verification_evidence.db
appear in raw_sessions). SQLite-source acquisition is built, applied to one
provider, and not propagated -- the same shape as content-addressing being
applied only to embeddings and OriginSpec declaring a detector order nothing
reads.

WHAT IS BEING RECONSTRUCTED BY INFERENCE INSTEAD:
  threads.title 2,771     -> all 3,201 Codex sessions are UUID-titled
                             (polylogue-ih67 builds a resolution ladder; the
                             ladder's own notes cite this table as 'richer than
                             session_index.jsonl on live installs')
  thread_spawn_edges 1,030 -> Codex delegation topology, which polylogue-1vpm
                             and polylogue-4ts derive from transcript inference
  thread_goals             -> stated task intent, unavailable anywhere else
  memories_1 stage1_outputs-> Codex-side memory, no archive representation

logs_2 is 627 MB of runtime logging (level/target/module_path/file/line) rather
than session evidence -- classify it deliberately rather than acquiring by
default. It may be the right home for runtime-observability questions, or it may
be correctly out of scope; the point is that nobody has decided.

NOTE state_5.sqlite is live-locked on a running install; ih67's notes already
prescribe copy-first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Each of the five databases is classified as acquire / acquire-partially / out-of-scope, with the reason recorded in the Codex OriginSpec fidelity declaration. 2. Acquisition reuses the Hermes sqlite path rather than adding a second mechanism. 3. threads.title and thread_spawn_edges reach the archive as typed evidence and are consumed by title resolution and topology respectively. 4. Live-locked databases are copied before reading; a running Codex is never blocked. 5. Report the before/after UUID-title census for codex-session and the count of spawn edges that replaced inferred ones.
notes:
Implemented on branch feature/sources/acquire-sidecars-and-codex-sqlite (commits
8e9778209 wiring, a70bd9257 tests), within OWNS: sources/live/batch.py,
sources/live/watcher.py, sources/origin_specs.py (storage/sqlite untouched,
per the concurrent schema-lane constraint on this branch).

WHAT WAS UNACQUIRED AND WHY: sources/parsers/codex_state.py (classification +
parsers) already existed but was completely unwired -- zero references from
dispatch.py/batch.py/watcher.py, exactly as its own docstring stated. The root
cause was never "not implemented" at the parser level; it was that
sources/live/batch.py's ~2900-line acquire/parse loop special-cased Hermes by
name (`provider is Provider.HERMES`) at three tail sites and had no equivalent
branch for a second sqlite-snapshot provider.

WHAT CHANGED:
- sources/live/batch.py: acquire loop gains a filename-gated (no I/O for the
  common case) + structurally-verified (codex_state.is_in_scope_codex_sqlite_path)
  branch for state_5.sqlite/goals_1.sqlite/memories_1.sqlite, snapshotting via
  the SAME snapshot_sqlite_to_blob (SQLite backup API, never a raw read of a
  live-locked file) Hermes already uses, minting a raw_id via
  codex_state_raw_id (AC2: no second mechanism). logs_2.sqlite/codex-dev.db
  are excluded by filename before any bytes are read (AC1's out-of-scope
  classification enforced at runtime, not just documented).
- The three `provider is Provider.HERMES` special cases in the acquire-loop
  tail are generalized to `path in raw_source_revisions` / `record.blob_hash
  is not None` -- the real distinguishing signal (sqlite-snapshot acquisition
  vs. content-hash acquisition) rather than a Hermes-specific one, since Codex
  now shares Provider.CODEX with its own JSONL rollout acquisition.
- Parse stage: a new elif (gated on provider is Provider.CODEX AND a
  structural re-check of the acquired blob, mirroring Hermes's own two elifs)
  routes thread_state to _write_codex_thread_state_evidence and admits
  goals_1/memories_1 raw bytes only (acquire-partial, no derived parse, per
  CODEX_STATE_FIDELITY) -- both bypass session materialization entirely via
  the same "fact artifact" continue idiom the codebase already uses.
- sources/live/watcher.py: a SECOND WatchSource ("codex-state", root ~/.codex,
  suffixes .sqlite/.db) rather than widening the existing "codex" JSONL
  source's root -- avoids ever reasoning about history.jsonl/config.toml/log/
  under the shared root.
- sources/origin_specs.py: _codex_spec() fidelity_notes now carries all 5
  databases' classification+reason (AC1), mirroring codex_state.py's
  CODEX_STATE_FIDELITY (that module explicitly names this file as the
  canonical home for the text).

WHERE EVIDENCE LANDS: threads.title and thread_spawn_edges reach
source.db's raw_hook_events (event_type=codex_thread_title /
codex_thread_spawn_edge), keyed to the EXISTING codex-session row via
session_native_id=thread_id -- the SAME mechanism sources/hooks.py already
uses for hook events (ArchiveStore.write_hook_event), read at query time via
the ALREADY-WIRED ArchiveStore.hook_event_summary_for_session /
Polylogue.get_hook_event_summary_for_session (live in the CLI's message/read
view). No index schema change: raw_hook_events.event_type is unconstrained
TEXT, exactly the documented cheap route.

MEASURED (read-only, real live ~/.codex install, scratch archive under
/realm/tmp, never touched /realm/db/polylogue):
  state_5.sqlite     40,116,224 bytes  acquired  (backup took ~121s -- live
                                                   WAL contention with the
                                                   running Codex install;
                                                   correctness unaffected,
                                                   noted as an operational
                                                   observation, not a bug)
  goals_1.sqlite         45,056 bytes  acquired  (0.5s)
  memories_1.sqlite     466,944 bytes  acquired  (0.3s)
  logs_2.sqlite     657,100,800 bytes  excluded by name, 0 bytes read
  codex-dev.db                    --  absent on this install, skipped
  total blob bytes acquired: 53,023,051
  raw_sessions rows (raw-tier admission, NOT sessions): 3
  raw_hook_events: 4,085 total -- codex_thread_title=3,055, codex_thread_spawn_edge=1,030
    (1,030 matches the bead's own original spawn-edge count exactly)
  index.db sessions rows after ingest: 0 -- confirms the hard constraint
    (thread_spawn_edges/titles never mint a session)

AC DISPOSITION:
1. Classify each of 5 dbs with reason in Codex OriginSpec fidelity -- SATISFIED
   (origin_specs.py _codex_spec() fidelity_notes, all 5).
2. Reuse the Hermes sqlite path, no second mechanism -- SATISFIED
   (snapshot_sqlite_to_blob shared; codex_state_raw_id mirrors
   hermes_profile_raw_id exactly).
3. threads.title/thread_spawn_edges reach the archive as typed evidence --
   SATISFIED (raw_hook_events, verified against real data above). "...and are
   consumed by title resolution and topology respectively" -- NOT done in
   this lane; deliberately deferred (codex_state.py's own docstring already
   named assembly_codex.py/topology consumption out of scope to avoid
   colliding with the still-in-flight ih67 ladder). Follow-up filed:
   polylogue-foee.
4. Live-locked databases copied before reading, running Codex never blocked --
   SATISFIED, verified against the REAL live install (state_5.sqlite was
   actively WAL-written during acquisition; backup succeeded, no lock
   contention errors, Codex itself was not blocked).
5. Report before/after UUID-title census + spawn-edge replacement count --
   PARTIAL. Spawn-edge count IS reported above (1,030, matching the bead's
   original measurement exactly). The UUID-title census does NOT change in
   this PR: the acquired titles sit in raw_hook_events as typed evidence but
   nothing yet folds them into the session's own displayed title (that is
   exactly polylogue-foee's scope) -- so the honest report is "evidence
   acquired, consumption and the resulting census change are the follow-up."

title: Claude Code tool-results sidecars unacquired: 1.34 GB across 12,588 files, 3 ingested
description:
Measured 2026-07-29 against ~/.claude/projects and the live source tier.

  ON DISK                                    ACQUIRED (raw_sessions.source_path)
    *.jsonl        11,540 files  13,275.9 MB   projects/ root  5,559
    subagents/        572 dirs    2,933.2 MB   subagents/     13,916
    tool-results/     582 dirs    1,339.6 MB   tool-results/       3
    memory/            14 dirs        0.8 MB   --

Claude Code writes a tool result to <session>/tool-results/<tool_id>.<ext>
whenever the output exceeds the inline limit, leaving only a stub in the
transcript. 3,058 tool_result blocks already in the archive contain the literal
text 'Full output saved to' -- the archive is storing its own admission that the
content is elsewhere, and the elsewhere is never read.

THE JOIN IS TRIVIAL: the filename IS the tool id. Verified by intersecting
10,545 distinct tool ids from disk filenames against a 400k-row sample of
blocks.tool_id -- 2,813 matched on the sample alone.

CONSEQUENCES: FTS cannot match anything that lived in a large tool output, so
'polylogue find X' silently misses it; and outcome/exit-code evidence carried in
a truncated result is unavailable, which is one contributor to the 72%-unknown
tool_result_is_error measured on this archive.

HARD CONSTRAINT (operator, 2026-07-29): these are BLOCK CONTENT, not sessions.
The hook-event inflation incident is the precedent -- standalone ingestion of
non-session records inflated the archive from 18,391 to 83,286 sessions before
being reverted. A tool-results file must attach to its existing tool_result
block by tool_id and must never create a session, a raw session row that parses
as a session, or a new top-level unit of any kind.
acceptance_criteria: 1. tool-results content attaches to the existing tool_result block via tool_id; session count is unchanged before and after, asserted by a test. 2. Its text is searchable -- a term that appears only inside a large tool output is findable via FTS. 3. Unmatched files (a tool id with no block) are recorded as typed acquisition debt, not silently dropped. 4. Blob storage is content-addressed and deduplicated; report bytes added. 5. Ingest wall-clock impact is measured against the polylogue-623q envelope before this is enabled by default.
notes:
Investigation + scoped implementation landed (worktree-agent-a6730c39cc2369360, commit 9b37431fd on feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates):

MEASUREMENT (read-only against live ~/.claude/projects, sampled ~330MB across 80 sessions):
- Genuinely-truncated "output too large" overflow sidecars: ~12% of files, ~60-65% of bytes, ~99% new content beyond the inline preview.
- Never-truncated "full mirror" sidecars (Claude Code unconditionally persists many small Read/Grep/Edit results too): ~85% of files, <2% of bytes, ~97% already-duplicate of inline block text.
- Orphan sidecars with no owning tool_result block left in the retained transcript (compaction pruned the referencing turn): ~1-5% of files, real acquisition debt, not a bug in the join.
- Filename scheme (toolu_<id> vs internal short-slug vs call_NN_<id> vs mcp-<server>-<tool>-<ts>) does NOT predict which bucket a file is in -- both truncated-overflow and full-mirror sidecars use both toolu_ and non-toolu_ names. The reliable join key is always the owning block's tool_use_id, recovered directly (filename stem) or via the "Full output saved to"/"Output has been saved to" pointer in that block's own preview text -- including for Task subagent transcripts, whose sidecars persist to the session-level tool-results/ dir under the subagent's own (non-toolu_) tool id, not a per-subagent dir.
- hook-*.txt files under the same directory (185 of 12,588 sampled) are a separate, already-tracked mechanism (raw hook stdout, polylogue-qqyg/#2781) -- correctly excluded from both acquisition and debt.

RECOMMENDATION: acquire, but content-aware (replace-when-truncated), not blanket-copy-the-directory. This is what was built.

BUILT (within OWNS: sources/live/**, sources/parsers/claude/**):
- polylogue/sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py: join_tool_result_sidecars(payload, tool_results_dir) -> SidecarJoinResult(matched, debt). Read-only, no writes.
- polylogue/sources/parsers/claude/code_parser.py: apply_tool_result_sidecars() attaches the join result to an already-parsed ParsedSession -- replaces truncated tool_result block text (AC2: FTS indexes block content, so this makes large-output terms findable), leaves full-mirror blocks untouched, and emits a bounded claude_tool_result_sidecar session_event per file (matched or debt) -- id/filename/size/content_hash/status only, never raw bytes in the event (no schema bump needed, per constraint). parse_code/parse_code_stream take tool_result_sidecars as an optional kwarg; omitting it is a no-op (verified).
- tests/unit/sources/test_tool_result_sidecars.py: 5 tests, synthetic fixtures only. Verifies AC1 (session/message count and ids unchanged with sidecars attached), AC2 (a term only in the full sidecar becomes findable in block text; anti-vacuity confirmed -- nulling the replacement dict makes this assertion fail, not a self-validating mock), AC3 (unmatched file becomes a typed debt event; hook-*.txt never does).

AC DISPOSITION:
1. Attaches by tool_id, session count unchanged, asserted by test -- SATISFIED (test_apply_tool_result_sidecars_replaces_truncated_block_text_only).
2. FTS-findable -- SATISFIED at the block-content layer (block.text is what FTS indexes); not verified end-to-end through a live FTS query in this pass since that requires the dispatch.py wiring below to actually run during ingest.
3. Unmatched -> typed acquisition debt, not silently dropped -- SATISFIED (SidecarDebt -> claude_tool_result_sidecar event, acquisition_status=debt, reason=no_owning_tool_result_block).
4. Blob storage content-addressed + deduplicated, bytes-added report -- PARTIAL. content_hash is computed and recorded per sidecar (SHA-256 via core.hashing.hash_text) but there is no dedicated blob_refs-tier write here; the acquired text rides into the existing blocks table via the block's own text field, which already participates in the archive's session-level content-hash idempotency. True cross-session blob dedup needs storage-tier work (storage/repair.py or a raw_authority.py-adjacent path), explicitly outside this lane's OWNS list. Not implemented; flagged as a real gap, not silently declared done.
5. Ingest wall-clock vs polylogue-623q envelope, default-off until measured -- NOT DONE. This lane never got as far as running ingest, because the acquisition path isn't wired into dispatch.py yet (see polylogue-wjgf). Cannot honestly claim this AC without that wiring existing to measure.

FOLLOW-UP: polylogue-wjgf (dispatch.py wiring: derive tool-results dir from source_path, call the join, pass result into parse_code; plus the default-on-vs-flagged decision needing config.py/CLI, and the streaming-path equivalent). AC4's blob-store dedup and AC5's wall-clock measurement both depend on that wiring landing first.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_tool_result_sidecars.py tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_claude_code_artifacts.py -> 31 passed. mypy --strict clean on both changed modules. ruff check/format clean. devtools render topology-projection + topology-status regenerated and committed (new module under polylogue/). devtools render all --check: no "out of sync" lines.

[2026-07-29, polylogue-wjgf follow-up] Wiring landed (branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates, commit 2237e8a82). AC5 (ingest wall-clock vs polylogue-623q envelope, default-off until measured) is now resolved: measured join_tool_result_sidecars against the FULL population of real ~/.claude/projects sessions with a tool-results/ dir (525 sessions) -- total added join time 8.2s (704MB matched + 708MB debt bytes, 9,421 matched files / 3,012 debt files), ~23% on top of just those sessions' own JSONL read time but those sessions are ~3% of the corpus, so well under 1% of a <60min full-rebuild budget. Decision: default-on, no flag. AC4 (blob-store dedup) remains PARTIAL/deferred as originally noted -- still needs storage-tier work outside sources/live and sources/dispatch scope; not addressed by wjgf.
VERIFICATION (group4 stale-sweep, 2026-07-31): PARTIAL. AC1-3 and AC5 satisfied (attach-by-tool_id, FTS-findable, typed debt events, wall-clock measured/default-on per the 2026-07-29 wjgf follow-up note). AC4 (content-addressed, deduplicated blob storage with bytes-added report) explicitly marked PARTIAL/deferred in the bead's own notes -- content_hash is computed but there is no blob_refs-tier write. Confirmed on master: polylogue/sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py has no blob-store/dedup logic. Evidence: git show origin/master:polylogue/sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py | grep -n 'blob_ref|content_addressed|dedup' -> no matches.
2026-07-31 acquisition-completeness audit recount: class has grown to 12,744 files / 1,450,338,905 bytes (12,741 unacquired; 3 stray .json ingested; 30/30 random sha256 samples have no blob_hash match). Oldest 2026-01-19, newest same-day as audit - ACTIVE unbounded growth. Same pattern exists for gemini-cli: ~/.gemini/tmp/*/tool-outputs = 218 files / 78,496,025 bytes, 100% unacquired (dormant since 2026-04) - whatever capture-or-ledger decision lands here should cover that analog class too. Also unaccounted nearby: memory/*.md 249 files/814KB and ~5 large gemini chats/*.json checkpoints 76.9MB of REAL session content (sessionId/messages/summary verified) with no raw rows.
close_reason: Merged PR #3533 (c61db58af): content-addressed dedup for Claude Code tool-result sidecar text via the existing blob store, wired into _write_session. All 5 ACs satisfied per PR body's AC-disposition table.

title: Subagent children are 45.6% of the archive and rank equal to real sessions in every result list
description:
Measured 2026-07-29: 8,614 of 18,871 sessions (45.6%) are subagent children; 8,824 session_links rows carry link_type='subagent'.

They are presented at equal weight in default result sets. Actual output of the
deployed CLI against the live archive:

  $ polylogue find repo:polylogue
  claude-code-session:5ecd  2026-07-27  5ecdb160-...-a3a24886af8cc:agent-af4e...  (342 msgs)
  claude-code-session:5ecd  2026-07-27  5ecdb160-...-a3a24886af8cc:agent-ad73... (1098 msgs)
  claude-code-session:5ecd  2026-07-28  5ecdb160-...-a3a24886af8cc:agent-ad68...  (499 msgs)

Three rows, one parent, differing only by an agent suffix -- and the same shape
fills . Combined with the title defect, a default query returns a
list that is ~46% fanout and ~85% UUID-labelled.

This is not a correctness bug and not a latency bug. The queries are right and
fast (2.8-7.6s measured). It is the reason the archive cannot be read by a
human, and therefore the practical gate on the operator using the product at
all -- ahead of every substrate program in the backlog.

NON-GOAL: hiding subagent evidence. It is real work and must stay queryable and
citable. The default result UNIT should be the top-level session, with its
delegation fan available on request, rather than one row per spawn.

Related: polylogue-4ts (lineage truth: counted once) is the storage-side
statement of the same problem; this bead is the read-side one. polylogue-fcyf
wants fanout as a first-class live view, which is the deliberate opposite
presentation and stays valid.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The default result unit is the top-level session; subagent children are reachable through an explicit projection, not by filling the list. 2. Session counts on read surfaces state which unit they count -- an archive of 18,871 rows containing 8,614 fanout children must never present '18,871 sessions' unqualified. 3. Subagent evidence remains fully queryable and citable; a query that asks for children still gets them. 4. Re-run the exact dogfood commands and show before/after output in the closing note.
close_reason: Merged PR #3495: default session-query result unit is the top-level session across CLI/MCP/daemon/API (root filter pushed to SQL in all four builders — three were missing it entirely); counts unit-labeled via total_unit; children fully recoverable via --no-root / root:false (live dogfood: 5161 mixed → 1906 top-level + 3255 children, arithmetic exact); lineage: predicates exempt.

title: 84.6% of Claude Code sessions are titled with a raw UUID: 10,157 of 12,001
description:
Measured on the live archive 2026-07-29 (full scan, 18,871 sessions):

  origin                  total   title = native_id   pct
  claude-code-session    12,001            10,157    84.6%
  codex-session           3,201             3,201   100.0%   <- owned by polylogue-ih67
  hermes-session            279               157    56.3%
  aistudio-drive            239                88    36.8%
  gemini-cli-session         17                 7    41.2%
  chatgpt-export          2,635                 0     0.0%
  claude-ai-export          377                 1     0.3%
  antigravity-session       116                 0     0.0%
  grok-export                 6                 0     0.0%

  archive-wide: 13,611 of 18,871 (72.1%) titled with a UUID,
                plus 2,369 (12.6%) with titles over 60 chars (prompt echoes)
                -> 84.7% of the archive has no usable title.

The split is exactly provider-generated vs locally-captured: web exports arrive
with titles because the provider makes one; local coding-agent sessions do not,
because nothing generates one. The two origins that dominate the archive
(15,202 of 18,871 = 80.6%) are the two with essentially no titles.

Only 1,241 of the UUID-titled rows are subagent children, so this is NOT a
fanout artifact: roughly 8,900 TOP-LEVEL Claude Code sessions -- the operator's
own primary work -- are unlabelled.

polylogue-ih67 owns the Codex 3,201 and has already built the resolution
ladder (thread name -> authored history -> first HUMAN_AUTHORED message ->
native id). Nothing owns the Claude Code 10,157, which is 3.2x larger. This
should reuse ih67's mechanism rather than invent a second one; polylogue-30h
owns the separate first-prompt-echo case.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A Claude Code session's display title is derived from authored content, never its UUID, using ih67's existing resolution ladder rather than a parallel mechanism. 2. Title provenance is recorded (title_source/title_ref), so a synthesized title is distinguishable from a provider-supplied one. 3. Live re-measure: UUID-titled claude-code-session count falls from 10,157 toward zero, reported as a before/after census like ih67 AC#6. 4. Existing rows acquire titles through ordinary reprocess, not a bespoke backfill script.
notes:
2026-07-31 re-measurement (H6, adversarial dataset investigation, full live scan, 23,280 sessions):

  origin                  total   title = native_id   pct
  claude-code-session    16,374            14,626    89.3%   (was 84.6% / 10,157 of 12,001)
  codex-session           3,203             3,203   100.0%
  chatgpt-export          2,637                 0     0.0%
  claude-ai-export          425                95    22.4%   (was 0.3% / 1 of 377)
  hermes-session             279               157    56.3%
  aistudio-drive             239                88    36.8%
  antigravity-session        116                 0     0.0%
  gemini-cli-session          17                 7    41.2%
  grok-export                  6                 0     0.0%

claude-code-session got WORSE, not better, despite the intervening b508/#3403 phantom-sidecar fix -- total session count grew 12,001->16,374 (+4,373) and the untitled fraction grew with it. Of the 14,626 title=native_id claude-code-session rows, 8,631 (59%) are subagent-shaped (native_id LIKE '%:agent-%', i.e. the real parent:agent-* subagent transcripts from C1 -- arguably expected, since these are dispatched-task transcripts without their own human-authored opening prompt) and 5,995 (41%) are top-level sessions with a bare native_id as title. Of those 5,995: 5,191 have message_count=0 (empty, arguably don't need a title) but 551 have message_count>5 (substantive sessions, e.g. 6,059 messages / 536,011 words) with zero human-readable title -- these are the sharpest instances of this bead's defect. claude-ai-export's jump (0.3%->22.4%) tracks its session count nearly doubling (377->425); worth checking whether the new claude-ai-export rows are a distinct ingestion batch with different title-resolution coverage.
PROGRESS 2026-08-01: root cause found — NOT in the single-pass parser (already correctly resolves ai-title/custom-title/agent-name -> heuristic -> raw-id via polylogue-pbuh). The defect is in dispatch.py's merge_parsed_session_chunks (the ONLY caller of Claude Code's memory-bounded multi-chunk streaming path): 'whichever chunk resolves a non-UUID title first wins, forever' — discards a stronger later ai-title in favor of an earlier weak heuristic guess, and never propagates title_source/title_ref/title_confidence. Confirmed live on a real raw file (490 ai-title records) whose archived row still showed title_source='unknown'. Fixed via _claude_code_title_rank in PR #3506 (not merged): merge_parsed_session_chunks now moves all four title fields as one unit picked by rank. AC1/AC2 satisfied by this fix; AC3 (live before/after census: 16,552 total / 14,801 UUID-titled / only 273 title_source=origin, measured read-only) requires an operator-authorized live reprocess, not attempted. AC4 unaffected (parse-time fix, ordinary reprocess picks it up).
close_reason: Root cause fixed via PR #3506: merge_parsed_session_chunks (dispatch.py, the sole caller of Claude Code's memory-bounded multi-chunk streaming path) discarded stronger later ai-titles in favor of earlier weak heuristic guesses and never propagated title_source/title_ref/title_confidence. _claude_code_title_rank now moves all four title fields as one ranked unit. AC1/AC2 satisfied (mechanism+provenance already existed via prior polylogue-pbuh; this fixes the one bypass). AC3 (live before/after census) requires operator-authorized reprocess of the live archive — not yet run; AC4 unaffected (parse-time only, ordinary reprocess picks it up). 194 tests passed, verify --quick green.

title: Landed capability is dark by default: feature flags defer decisions nobody made
description:
Measured 2026-07-29: polylogue/config.py declares 18 boolean feature flags. The live ~/.config/polylogue/polylogue.toml sets only the [embedding] section, so every other flag runs at its default.

Flags that are False by default and gate work that has already landed and merged:
  daemon_parse_stage_split      m6tp phase (a), PR #3168
  live_watcher_parse_stage_split  same mechanism for the watcher
  daemon_bulk_rebuild_routing   m6tp phase (c), PR #3189/#3197, bead gd6v CLOSED
  mcp_write_enabled             MCP write role
  mcp_judge_enabled             MCP review role
  mcp_maintenance_enabled       MCP admin role
  judgment_automation_enabled   judgment automation
  embedding_enabled             (this one IS set live, to false)

The compounding case is m6tp: three of its four phases are landed, the fourth
is inventoried, the runtime precondition is satisfied in production -- and the
redesign is entirely dark because two flags default False. The daemon therefore
runs the slowest available configuration (serial parse, trickle conveyor) on a
free-threaded interpreter that measured 3.9x-9.6x parallel parse.

THE PRINCIPLE AT STAKE: a flag on a landed capability is a decision nobody
made. It defers the decision to configuration, where the default silently
becomes the decision -- and the default is always the previous behaviour, so
shipping is decoupled from taking effect. A bead can close, CI can be green,
the PR can merge, and nothing changes for the operator.

This directly contradicts the project's own automagic-invariants doctrine:
'if Polylogue can maintain a condition fully automatically, it generally
should ... there is NO break-glass tier. Once the automatic path maintains an
invariant, the redundant manual surface is DELETED, not demoted.'

NON-GOAL: removing genuinely necessary configuration (archive root, ports,
credentials, embedding model/dimension/cost ceiling -- the last gates real
money). This is about flags whose only function is to keep landed code from
running.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every boolean feature flag is classified as: rollout-scaffolding for landed work (delete the flag, make the behaviour unconditional), genuine deployment choice (keep, document why config is the right home), or unshipped-work gate (keep until the work lands, with the bead that removes it named). 2. No flag gating already-merged work survives without a named reason. 3. For each flag deleted, the removal is unconditional -- not a default flip that leaves the knob in place. 4. m6tp's two flags are resolved first and their removal is the worked example. 5. A landed-but-dark capability is treated as not shipped: the closing bead's definition of done includes the behaviour being active.
notes:
Filed 2026-07-29 from the convergence audit. The trigger was discovering that the fix for a standing operator complaint ('why is import not within 1h') was built, merged, bead-closed, and switched off -- and that the daemon logs its own correct diagnosis hourly while doing the slow thing anyway.
[Verification sweep 2026-07-31, bead-landing-check group5] Verdict: LIVE. Filed 2026-07-29 same day as audit; explicitly describes current unaddressed state (18 flags, all defaulting False/off) with zero remediation notes.
close_reason: Full classification complete, no code change warranted (honest no-op outcome). 3 of 8 named flags already deleted by prior PRs (#3390/#3455/#3468), confirmed via repo-wide grep — AC4's 'm6tp worked example' already satisfied. The 4 remaining candidates (mcp_write_enabled, mcp_judge_enabled, mcp_maintenance_enabled, judgment_automation_enabled) each trace to an explicit, dated operator decision (polylogue-800m, closed 2026-07-20/07-31: independent config opt-ins over unconditional behavior) — the opposite of 'a decision nobody made'. Remaining boolean flags (observability_enabled, api_allow_no_auth, browser_capture_allow_*, CLI UX toggles, SMTP TLS) are all genuine security/blast-radius/protocol config, out of the bead's literal scope. No flag in current config.py matches the rollout-scaffolding pattern this bead targets.

title: Supersession receipts go stale when heads advance: 10,518 raws unreleasable despite proven supersession
design:
ROOT CAUSE (corrected 2026-07-29 after querying the live archive; the earlier framing
"codex appends are not detected" named the symptom, not the mechanism).

revision_kind='unknown' is exactly equivalent to logical_source_key IS NULL. Verified on
the live source.db: all 13,713 unknown rows have a NULL logical_source_key, and every one
of them is revision_authority='quarantined'. The correlation is perfect, both directions.

  kind=unknown  authority=quarantined   13,713 rows   50.33 GiB
  kind=full     authority=byte_proven   13,478 rows   30.30 GiB
  kind=full     authority=quarantined    9,869 rows    1.85 GiB
  kind=append   authority=byte_proven    2,403 rows    3.55 GiB
  kind=append   authority=quarantined    1,900 rows    6.20 GiB

A raw cannot be typed 'full' or 'append' without a logical_source_key, because those kinds
are defined RELATIVE to a predecessor in a logical chain. No key means no chain means no
append detection is even attempted -- so the raw is stored and replayed as a whole blob
every time. Append detection is not broken; it is never reached.

Why the key is missing. sources/revision_backfill.py:437 assigns a logical key directly
only when a raw parses to exactly ONE session (len(sessions) == 1 -> bind_raw_revision with
kind=FULL, authority=QUARANTINED). Multi-session raws take the branch at :453 instead, which
records a membership census and defers to state.membership_candidates -- resolution then
requires a raw-authority census plan to execute. Codex sessions are large multi-session
JSONL streams, so they systematically take the deferred branch. That is why 72% of all
archive bytes are codex while codex is only 22% of rows.

Why the deferred branch never completes. The census IS running and reaching quiescence
(raw_authority_censuses sequence 545, lifecycle_status=completed, quiescent=1), but:
    plan_count            16,890
    executable_plan_count  1,199
    residual_plan_count   15,691   <- carried forward unchanged, every pass
and 5,445 of the 5,474 blockers carry one reason: "accepted raw authority remains
quarantined pending exact refinement proof" (actuator refine_quarantined_raw). Frontier
state counts: proven_current 12,271, superseded 10,431, unresolved_provenance 5,247,
duplicate_alias 1,189, conflicting_authority_needs_judgment 7, corrupt 6.

So the actual defect is that refine_quarantined_raw cannot discharge its proof obligation
for these raws, and the scheduler carries the same 15,691 plans forward on every census
without progress. This is the raw-authority convergence degradation already suspected
(hjpx/lkrc/t93b) landing on real bytes.

Also: 4,938 of the 13,713 unknown rows have parsed_at_ms IS NULL -- never parsed at all --
and 98 carry a parse_error.

SCOPE. The fix is upstream of anything append-shaped: make refine_quarantined_raw able to
discharge (or explicitly fail) its proof so multi-session raws acquire a logical_source_key.
Do NOT start by touching append detection. Start by taking one stuck plan and determining
why its exact-refinement proof cannot be produced.

Independent, separable lever (still valid, unchanged): 41,363 raws carry 92.22 GiB but only
32,673 distinct blob_hash / 66.10 GiB. 8,690 raws are byte-identical re-acquisitions the
rebuild parses individually. Skipping re-parse for a hash already materialized in the
current generation is worth ~26 GiB and does not depend on any of the above.
notes:
2026-07-29 ROOT CAUSE COMPLETED (corrects this bead's earlier note, which said refine_quarantined_raw 'cannot discharge its proof' -- true for one population, wrong for the one holding the bytes).

There are TWO stuck populations, and they are stuck for different reasons:

  quarantined WITH a logical key   12,089 raws    8.04 GiB
  quarantined WITHOUT one          13,393 raws   50.33 GiB   <- the bytes

Population 1 (keyed, 8 GiB) is the one the earlier note describes: it reaches the frontier,
classifies as UNRESOLVED_PROVENANCE with actuator REFINE_QUARANTINE, and
inspect_quarantined_accepted_raws finds it ineligible. Those are the 5,247 frontier items
and 5,445 blockers.

Population 2 (keyless, 50 GiB) never reaches the mechanism at all:
  - _strategy_overrides' quarantine branch filters
     (storage/raw_reconciler.py:686), so a
    keyless raw is never even inspected for eligibility.
  - 9,402 of the 13,393 have no raw_revision_heads row whatsoever (18,730 heads exist), so
    they cannot appear as an accepted head in the frontier query
    (storage/raw_authority.py:648) either.
  - REFINE_QUARANTINE's only route to becoming executable is that override promoting it to
    SAFELY_REKEYABLE (_EXECUTABLE_STATES = {SAFELY_REKEYABLE, DUPLICATE_ALIAS};
    UNRESOLVED_PROVENANCE is not executable). No override, no execution -- ever.

And the reason they are keyless is upstream, in the census: sources/revision_backfill.py:437
assigns a logical key directly ONLY when a raw parses to exactly one session
( -> bind_raw_revision). Multi-session raws take the branch at :453,
which records a membership census and defers to state.membership_candidates. Codex sessions
are large multi-session JSONL streams, so they systematically take the deferred branch.

Complete chain, each link verified against live data:
  multi-session raw -> no direct key (revision_backfill.py:437 vs :453)
    -> no key -> excluded from the quarantine override (raw_reconciler.py:686) and absent
       from raw_revision_heads
    -> never refined -> revision_kind stays 'unknown'
    -> stored and replayed as a whole blob every acquisition -> 50.33 GiB

IMPLICATION FOR THE FIX: do not start at refine_quarantined_raw. It is downstream of the
actual gap and only governs the 8 GiB population. The 50 GiB needs the membership-candidate
path to actually resolve a logical key for multi-session raws -- or an explicit decision
that a multi-session raw gets a key by a different rule than a single-session one.

2026-07-29 CORRECTION #2 -- this bead's premise is largely wrong, including the root cause
I recorded earlier today. Retracting both.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I claimed multi-session raws "never acquire a logical_source_key" and
that this left 50 GiB unclassified. But raw_sessions.logical_source_key being NULL is
CORRECT BY DESIGN for a multi-session raw: one raw belongs to MANY logical keys, so a
single scalar column cannot represent it. Its per-key state lives in
raw_session_memberships (raw_id, logical_source_key, decision, revision_authority) --
30,921 rows. Reading NULL there as "unclassified" was a schema misreading on my part.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (live source.db, 13,393 keyless raws):
  census status:   complete   11,826 raws   43.34 GiB
                   failed        375 raws    6.97 GiB
                   non_session    29 raws    0.02 GiB
  membership decision, by raw:
                   superseded_equivalent  4,464 raws  34.13 GiB
                   applied                3,854 raws  33.65 GiB
                   ambiguous              3,654 raws   7.95 GiB
                   superseded_prefix        154 raws   0.81 GiB
                   (null)                    43 raws   0.40 GiB
(GiB columns are per membership ROW, so they double-count a raw belonging to several keys;
raw counts are exact.)

So the membership mechanism is largely WORKING: 88% censused complete, and most raws carry
a definite decision. This is not a stuck pipeline.

THE GENUINELY STUCK SET is much smaller than 50 GiB:
  ambiguous          3,654 raws   ~8 GiB   classification could not decide
  census failed        375 raws   ~7 GiB   the census itself errored
  ~15 GiB total, not 50.

THE REAL OPPORTUNITY IS RETENTION, NOT CLASSIFICATION. ~4,600 raws are decided
superseded_equivalent / superseded_prefix -- the system has already PROVEN an accepted
chain supersedes them -- and their blobs are still retained in full. That is a
raw_retention question (storage/raw_retention.py), not a parser or census bug. Note its
existing predicate at :181 matches `application.decision = 'superseded'` against
raw_revision_applications, whereas membership decisions use the distinct vocabulary
`superseded_equivalent`/`superseded_prefix` in raw_session_memberships -- worth checking
whether decided-superseded members are reachable by any release path at all.

RESCOPE THIS BEAD to two separable pieces of real work:
  1. Why 3,654 raws classify ambiguous and 375 censuses fail (~15 GiB).
  2. Whether decided-superseded membership raws are eligible for blob release, and if the
     retention vocabulary mismatch above means they are currently unreachable.
The earlier "don't start at refine_quarantined_raw" advice still holds, but for a plainer
reason than I gave: the 50 GiB was never blocked on it, because it was never blocked.
2026-07-29 DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE (supersedes correction #2's "retention vocabulary mismatch"
lead, which was also wrong -- 8,923 of 8,924 membership-superseded raws DO have a
'superseded' raw_revision_applications row, so the two vocabularies meet fine).

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM, measured end to end on the live archive:

  raws with decision='superseded'                     11,700
  raws the retention path deems eligible for release   1,182
  ineligible                                          10,518

_active_index_raw_authority (storage/raw_retention.py:148) admits a raw for release only
when its application receipt still joins the CURRENT head on eight columns --
accepted_raw_id, accepted_source_revision, accepted_content_hash, acquisition_generation,
append_end_offset, decided_at_ms, plus key/session -- and the head is frontier_kind='byte'.

Why the 10,518 fail (11,977 superseded receipt rows):
     2   no head row for that key/session
 2,027   head has ADVANCED to a different accepted_raw_id
 7,166   same accepted_raw_id, but decided_at_ms differs

I hypothesised the last group was a spurious timestamp-only mismatch and that
decided_at_ms should be dropped from the join. TESTED AND REFUTED: of those 7,166, only 4
are substantively identical on the proof columns; 7,162 genuinely differ in
accepted_source_revision / accepted_content_hash / acquisition_generation /
append_end_offset. The head really did change content under the same accepted_raw_id (an
append extending it). The strict join is CORRECT -- it is refusing to release a raw whose
supersession was proven against a head state that no longer holds. Do not weaken it.

THE REAL GAP: receipts are immutable by construction
(archive_tiers/revision_application.py:148 record_revision_application_sync -- INSERT OR
IGNORE keyed on decision_id, and a mismatch against an existing decision_id raises). That
is right. But NOTHING re-issues a supersession receipt when a logical head later advances.
So a raw superseded against head state N keeps a receipt naming N forever, the head moves
to N+1, and the raw becomes permanently unreleasable even though it is now MORE superseded
than when the receipt was written.

The blobs are therefore retained not because supersession is in doubt, but because its
proof went stale and nothing refreshes it. This accumulates monotonically: every append to
a logical source strands the previously-superseded raws behind it.

THE FIX (well-scoped, and deliberately NOT attempted in this pass -- see risk below):
re-evaluate already-superseded raws against the current head and write a FRESH receipt
(new decision_id) when supersession still holds against the current head state. Append-only,
no mutation of existing receipts, no weakening of the retention predicate. Natural home is
the census/apply path that already computes head advancement.

RISK NOTE: this is the deletion-authority path -- a wrong receipt makes an
evidence-bearing blob deletable. My analysis of this bead was wrong twice before reaching
the above, so the implementation wants an independent adversarial check that a re-issued
receipt is only ever written when the current head genuinely supersedes the raw, plus a
dry-run reporting how many blobs would become eligible before any of them are released.
2026-07-29 implementation landed (commit 6ca25bd3b, worktree-agent-a73601249e0a08f56): plan_stale_supersession_reissue/reissue_stale_supersession_receipts in raw_retention.py, proof is 'current head is a byte-proven full reset' (append-chain heads never authorize reissue for a different raw -- ancestors are protected not superseded, verified via anti-vacuity test). Live dry-run against /realm/db/polylogue: already_current=2640, stale=2 (both correctly ineligible), eligible=0. The bulk of the original 10,518 ineligible count (9,320+) is semantic-frontier heads (antigravity multi-file sessions), structurally excluded from release by active_raw_retention_authority's own byte-only join regardless of receipt freshness -- filed polylogue-hgsq to track that separate open question. 63/63 tests pass, ruff+mypy clean. PR not yet opened.
