title: Parse Gemini CLI JSONL chat-log checkpoint format (turn-per-line, no embedded messages)
description:
Gemini CLI has TWO on-disk checkpoint shapes for its "chats" feature:

1. Single JSON document per session (`.json`): {"sessionId","projectHash",
   "startTime","lastUpdated","kind","messages":[...]} - the messages list is
   embedded. This shape has a working detector+parser (`local_agent.
   looks_like_gemini_cli` / `parse_gemini_cli`).

2. A genuinely different multi-line `.jsonl` checkpoint log: a session-open
   stub record (same envelope fields, but NO "messages" key at all) followed
   by one JSON object per turn/event on subsequent lines, shaped
   {"id","timestamp","type":"user"|"gemini"|"error"|"info",...} interleaved
   with {"$set":{"lastUpdated":...}} patch lines. There is currently NO
   parser for this shape at all.

polylogue-hs3y's fix (dispatch.py + local_agent.py) taught detect_provider
to recognize the stub record so it no longer misclassifies as
claude-code-session (bare "sessionId" collided with Claude Code's
_STRONG_SESSION_KEYS). But _lower_payload_specs's GEMINI_CLI branch only
knows _single_document_record - a multi-line event-log stream still lowers
to zero specs, so these sessions are correctly tagged gemini-cli-session in
raw_sessions but never become a queryable sessions row (0 messages, by
design - no forced empty session).

Confirmed live in the archive: 4 raw_sessions rows under
~/.gemini/tmp/*/chats/*.jsonl carry real turn content (user questions,
gemini responses with thoughts/token usage, tool calls) that is currently
unrecoverable from the archive.

Scope: write a stream-record parser for the event-log shape (turn-per-line,
$set patches folded into session metadata, first-line stub as session
identity), wire it into GROUP_PROVIDERS/STREAM_RECORD_PROVIDERS or an
equivalent per-line lowering path, add real-fixture-shaped tests.

title: Attachment backlog: 7,376 of 9,289 attachments (79%) still acquisition_status='unfetched'
notes:
PR https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3590 (feature/storage/attachment-reacquisition-backfill): built the classifier + actuator pair the AC calls for.

polylogue/storage/attachment_reacquisition.py, mirroring attachment_relink.py (ref-linkage backfill, same real-ingest_record-reparse pattern) and blob_integrity.py's raw actuators:
- plan_attachment_reacquisition(): classifies every unfetched attachment into reacquirable (re-parsing its still-durable raw_sessions payload with today's parser via the real ingest_record entry point reproduces its content-identity hash -- write.py:_attachment_id, independent of session/message -- with inline bytes), unrecoverable (static source_url startswith 'sandbox:' signature, no reparse needed -- chatgpt.py's own comments document Code Interpreter output as never carrying bytes), or undetermined (left exactly as unfetched -- most commonly Drive/OAuth attachments needing a live authenticated fetch, polylogue-ck5v's separate scope; zero network I/O here, never guesses).
- apply_attachment_reacquisition(): dry-run by default; --apply requires an immutable JSONL manifest + a verified backup manifest for the index tier (same gate durable-tier migrations use). Publishes reacquired bytes through the same ArchiveBlobPublisher/blob store every other acquisition path uses. Marks unrecoverable attachments 'unavailable' -- the schema (archive_tiers/index.py:1238-1239) already declares this value in its CHECK constraint but nothing in production code had ever written it; no schema migration needed.
- Two devtools commands: `devtools workspace attachment-reacquisition` (report) / `...-apply` (actuator), mirroring the raw-live-source-reconciliation report/apply pair.

AC check: "backfill pass over unfetched attachments where the source payload still contains the bytes" -- satisfied by plan_attachment_reacquisition's reparse-based reacquirable class. "unrecoverable ones marked distinctly from 'unfetched'" -- satisfied via the existing-but-unused acquisition_status='unavailable' value, applied to the sandbox_file class.

Duplicate: polylogue-7r6u is the same measurement/AC as this bead (same forensics session, same suggestion) -- recommend closing 7r6u as duplicate of pfdf once this PR merges.

LIVE EVIDENCE (read-only, /realm/db/polylogue, no mutation -- ran the new `devtools workspace attachment-reacquisition` report against production): of 7,394 unfetched attachments, 1,904 (25.8%) are the ChatGPT sandbox_file class -- classified instantly, zero reparse needed, all definitively unrecoverable by chatgpt.py's own documented semantics. Of the remaining 5,490, a 300-row raw_sessions reparse scan (newest-first) found 0 reacquirable in that sample -- real per-row parse cost on large session payloads (some multi-GB Claude Code JSONL files) made a full 43,124-row corpus scan too slow to complete in-session (a 3000-row scan ran 7+ CPU-minutes without finishing before I stopped it). This is consistent with the live channel census on 7r6u/pfdf (oauth 4,136 + drive 3,094, both requiring polylogue-ck5v's live-fetch mechanism this module deliberately never invokes) dominating the undetermined bucket -- i.e. the reparse-recoverable slice this bead's own AC targets may be small or zero on THIS archive's actual data, with the bulk of real recoverability work living in polylogue-ck5v (live Drive fetch) instead. The mechanism is proven correct (7 passing tests against real ingest_record/blob-store/index.db plumbing) and will backfill any case where it does apply (e.g. a future parser fix analogous to 60d93b618), even though this session's live sample did not surface a large reacquirable cohort. Recommend an operator-supervised full-corpus run of `devtools workspace attachment-reacquisition --json` (no --raw-row-limit, expect a long run given real parse cost) to get the exact live ratio before deciding whether to invest further here vs. prioritizing polylogue-ck5v.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/storage/test_attachment_reacquisition.py (7 passed). devtools verify --quick clean.

title: test_web_reader agent-coordination test is order-dependent: passes alone, fails in a wide selection
description:
FALSE-GREEN AUDIT 2026-07-31 (finding F6). MEASURED.

tests/unit/daemon/test_web_reader.py TestReaderSearchState::test_agent_coordination_endpoint_uses_shared_payload
fails with KeyError 'root' at test_web_reader.py:894 when run as part of a 31-file selection,
and PASSES when run alone.

  isolated:  pytest tests/unit/daemon/test_web_reader.py -k agent_coordination
             -> 3 passed, 174 deselected in 4.50s
  in a 31-file selection (all tests/unit files referencing MaterialOrigin)
             -> FAILED with KeyError 'root'; reproduced 5 consecutive times

This is cross-test state leakage, not a flake: deterministic in both directions.

WHY IT MATTERS: the default gate is devtools verify with pytest-testmon affected-selection,
which rarely runs this file together with that set, so the pollution is invisible to the
normal pre-merge gate. It surfaces only in a broad run.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: it produced a FALSE RED in my own mutation harness. v1 ran pytest with -x
and read the exit code; this pre-existing failure tripped -x on every run, so all five planted
mutations looked caught when the runs proved nothing. The harness auditing for false greens
generated a false red.

STANDING RULE: a mutation-testing or bisect harness must difference against a measured
baseline set of failing node ids. An exit code is not evidence, and -x makes any pre-existing
failure masquerade as the signal.

AC:
- Identify the polluting module/fixture (bisect the 31-file selection).
- Fix the leak at its source, not by reordering or by adding a fixture-reset to the victim.
- Check whether the 'root' key comes from module-global or process-global state another test
  mutates.
- Record whether other order-dependent failures exist in a broad run.
close_reason: Misframed/stale: reran the exact cited repro (test_agent_coordination_endpoint_uses_shared_payload) both alone and in a 33-file broad selection (both file orders) — passed every time; the described KeyError 'root' order-dependent failure does not reproduce on current master (0b33b1c5b). The real, deterministic bug in the same test file (test_archive_filter_kwargs_cover_every_storage_lowerable_spec_field / _archive_filter_kwargs_from_spec missing 'root' key) is unrelated to the order-dependence this bead described and is now tracked separately as polylogue-c379. Verified 2026-07-31 verify-first triage.

title: Tautological assertions: three tests that cannot fail
description:
FALSE-GREEN AUDIT 2026-07-31 (findings F7, F8, F9). Read-verified, not mutation-checked.

1) tests/unit/core/test_json.py:169  test_loads_malformed_json_never_silent
   Docstring: 'loads either raises or returns a non-None value; it never silently returns None
   for a non-null JSON input.'
   Body:
       try:
           result = core_json.loads(text)
           _ = result  # No assertion needed - successful parse is fine
       except Exception:
           pass  # Expected for malformed input
   There is NO assertion. The exact regression the docstring names -- loads() silently
   returning None -- passes. Note the contrast with the test immediately above it (:163),
   which uses pytest.raises and carries an explicit 'Anti-vacuity:' docstring, so the concept
   was understood in this very file.
   FIX: assert result is not None (the docstring's actual claim), keeping the documented
   carve-out that literal JSON 'null' legitimately returns None.

2) tests/unit/core/test_filters_props.py:505  test_provider_filter_exclusion_disjoint
   Docstring: 'Provider inclusion and exclusion should be mutually exclusive.'
   Body computes  result = included - excluded  over two plain Python sets built from the
   Hypothesis inputs, then asserts members of the difference are not in excluded. That is a
   property of set.__sub__. No SessionFilter, no archive code, nothing from polylogue is
   invoked -- in a module whose subject is production filter properties.
   FIX: build a SessionFilter with those origins/exclusions and assert on .list() output, or
   delete the test.

3) tests/unit/core/test_filters_props.py:791, :804, :816
   test_exclude_provider_and_exclude_tag / test_provider_with_exclude_tag /
   test_multiple_exclude_providers
   These DO call real SessionFilter(...).exclude_origin(...).list(), but every assertion sits
   inside 'for conv in result:' with no cardinality guard. Currently non-vacuous (the
   filter_repo_advanced fixture leaves 1-2 rows), so they are not silently passing today --
   but a regression that made the filter return [] (the total-failure mode) keeps all three
   green.
   FIX: add assert len(result) >= 1 before each loop.

CONTEXT -- suite-wide AST sweep over 12,513 test functions (upper bounds on CANDIDATES, not
defect counts; manual sampling found only ~15-20% of each bucket genuine, because this
codebase legitimately delegates assertions to shared helpers such as _assert_structured_error):
  186 functions with zero bare-assert statements
  137 with only weak asserts (is not None / isinstance / len>=0)
  238 with all asserts inside a possibly-empty loop   <- bucket (3) above
   63 mock-assert only
   17 with a swallowing try/except                     <- bucket (1) above

AC: the three tests above assert something that can fail; the loop-only cluster gets
cardinality guards; consider whether a cardinality-guard convention belongs in TESTING.md.
notes:
PR opened (not merged): https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3528 (branch feature/test/fix-tautological-assertions-3a61).

Fixed all three findings:
1. test_json.py:169 test_loads_malformed_json_never_silent -- added `assert result is not None` on the success path, kept the null carve-out (unreachable given the alphabet, kept anyway for robustness). Mutation-proof: changed json.py's stdlib fallback to `return None` instead of `raise exc from None` -> test failed with `assert None is not None`; reverted -> green.
2. test_filters_props.py:505 test_provider_filter_exclusion_disjoint -- rewrote (did not delete) as a parametrized async test building a real archive and asserting on SessionFilter(...).origin(...).exclude_origin(...).list(), including a contradictory include==exclude case. Mutation-proof: made builder.py's exclude_origin() a no-op (`return self`) -> 3 of 4 parametrized cases failed; reverted -> green.
3. test_filters_props.py:791/804/816 -- added `assert len(result) >= 1` before each loop (documented expected fixture composition inline). Mutation-proof: made SessionFilter.list() always `return []` -> all three tests failed at the new guard; reverted -> green.

Also added a short "Cardinality guards on loop-only assertions" convention to TESTING.md (scoped narrowly, right after the Test Patterns section) per the bead's own suggestion. Did NOT audit or fix the broader 238-candidate loop-only-assertion sweep -- out of scope per this bead's AC, and manual sampling already showed most are legitimate shared-helper delegation.

Verification: `devtools test tests/unit/core/test_json.py tests/unit/core/test_filters_props.py` -> 187 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (TestSessionFilterBranching::test_parent_filters_by_parent_id, confirmed failing identically on unmodified master via git stash, unrelated fixture/area). `devtools verify --quick` -> exit 0, all steps green.

Leaving open per instruction; PR awaiting review/merge.

title: 234 stale workflow-artifact sessions (coordinator_session_stream 226 + workflow_run_snapshot 7 + journal counted separately) never reparsed after classification fix
schema-versioning lint cannot catch an undeclared semantic classification change (only declaration-completeness)
description:
Investigation triggered by polylogue-lzh8 (PR landing the missing v48
SEMANTIC_REPARSE declaration for #3088/1e0246d77). The bead asked: PR #3088
shipped a semantic classification change (origin_specs.py artifact rules,
changing parse_as_session for four Claude Workflow artifact kinds) with no
INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bump at all, and `devtools lab policy schema-versioning`
did not stop it. Why not, and can it be made to?

FINDING: the lint (devtools/verify_schema_upgrade_lane.py) checks THREE
things: (1) no legacy upgrade-shaped helper functions exist under
storage/sqlite/, (2) `index_delta_declaration_report(INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION)`
-- every version from the compatibility floor up to the CURRENT
INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION constant has exactly one valid IndexDeltaDeclaration,
(3) every INDEX_BENIGN_DDL_REGISTRY entry is an idempotent, non-mutating
DDL shape. All three are structurally scoped to "is the declaration table
internally consistent with the current version constant" -- none of them
ever inspect polylogue/sources/origin_specs.py, artifact_taxonomy/, or any
other classification/parser source file, and none of them fire on a diff
that changes classification semantics without touching
INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION. A commit that changes what parse_as_session resolves
to for a given artifact kind, without incrementing the version constant, is
therefore invisible to this lint by construction: index_delta_declaration_
report still reports "ok" because the (unchanged) current version still has
its (already-declared) coverage. The lint can only catch an UNDECLARED
BUMP, never a MISSING bump.

Why not fixed inline in polylogue-lzh8's PR: a real fix needs some notion of
"this source file changing without a version bump is itself a policy
violation" -- e.g. a content-fingerprint of the classification decision
table (origin_specs.py's artifact_rules, artifact_taxonomy's classify_
artifact) stored per INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION and diffed at lint time, or a
git-diff-based check flagging commits that touch known classification-
semantic files without touching lifecycle.py/index.py in the same commit.
The former is a genuine architecture addition (a new declared invariant,
not a quick patch); the latter is close to the "fossilized-diff" check
shape this repo's testing philosophy explicitly rejects (CLAUDE.md
Verification section: don't gate on a changed file list). Neither is a
small, local fix -- both need design work and a real value case, not a
rushed addition riding on an unrelated bead.

Does NOT block polylogue-lzh8: that bead's job was to declare the missing
v48 delta for the already-shipped classification fix, which is done
regardless of whether the lint that should have caught the original miss
gets strengthened.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Either (a) a designed, low-false-positive mechanism exists that would have caught #3088's undeclared classification change (e.g. a stored content-fingerprint of origin_specs.py/artifact_taxonomy classification tables, versioned and diffed by the lint), and is implemented + wired into devtools lab policy schema-versioning, or (b) the investigation concludes no low-false-positive mechanism is worth building at this time, with the reasoning recorded here and the gap documented in docs/internals.md's Schema Versioning Model section so a future contributor doesn't assume the lint already covers this case. 2. If implemented, devtools lab policy schema-versioning must still pass on the current archive state (post polylogue-lzh8) and a regression test proves it fails when a classification-table change lands without a version bump.

Investigation complete, no new code needed: this exact mechanism was already

title: shipped-but-dead: repair.py stale_supersession_receipts capability is built but unregistered — silently unreachable
description:
Audit 2026-07-31 (shipped-but-dead census). MEASURED, handler dicts opened and read.

polylogue/storage/repair.py builds a complete stale-supersession-receipts repair
capability:
  :5777  count_stale_supersession_receipts_sync
  :5786  repair_stale_supersession_receipts   (constructs RepairResult("stale_supersession_receipts", ...))
  :5851  preview_stale_supersession_receipts

None of the three is a key in either dispatch table. REPAIR_HANDLERS and
PREVIEW_HANDLERS each enumerate exactly these eight targets:
  empty_sessions, message_type_backfill, orphaned_attachments, orphaned_blobs,
  orphaned_messages, session_insights, session_timestamp_backfill,
  superseded_raw_snapshots

run_safe_repairs dispatches only through REPAIR_HANDLERS, so no CLI or daemon path
can reach the capability. It has zero test coverage as well -- fully unexercised.

The underlying primitive it wraps, raw_retention.py:815 reissue_stale_supersession_receipts,
IS tested (tests/unit/storage/test_raw_retention.py:2019,2047,2155) and has other
callers -- so this is specifically the orchestration/registration layer that was
never connected.

This differs from the other findings in consequence: it is not wasted writes, it
is a repair the operator believes exists and cannot run.

Related dead single functions found in the same sweep (lower value, fold in or
split):

      live sibling count_orphaned_messages_sync:5140 has 6+)
  polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/ops_write.py:1383  read_mcp_call (zero callers;
      sibling list_mcp_calls:1352 is wired to cli/commands/diagnostics.py:850,866)
acceptance_criteria: stale_supersession_receipts is registered in REPAIR_HANDLERS and PREVIEW_HANDLERS with a test that reaches it through run_safe_repairs (not by direct import), or the three functions are deleted. has_orphaned_messages_sync and read_mcp_call are deleted or given a caller.

title: shipped-but-dead: v2mg kept price_catalogs on a justification that is false in all three named particulars
description:
Audit 2026-07-31 (shipped-but-dead census). CORRECTION to a closed bead.

polylogue-v2mg (CLOSED) dropped model_prices and session_reported_costs as
zero-consumer tables, and kept price_catalogs. Its justification is quoted
verbatim in production source at
polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index_convergence.py:74-77:

  "The sibling price_catalogs table genuinely is read (session_model_usage.
   priced_with FK, active_price_catalog_id) and is kept."

MEASURED -- all three named particulars are false:

1. session_model_usage.priced_with -- zero production SELECTs. Every reference is
   an INSERT/UPDATE/NULL-clear in write.py (946,955,962,971,3711,3745,3783,
   3911,3929,3938,3960), the DDL FK line index.py:1033, or prose. The only
   SELECTs in the entire repo are in tests/unit/storage/test_pricing_chain_roundtrip.py
   (162,283,305).
2. session_model_usage.priced_at_ms -- same shape; write-only.
   (session_profiles.priced_with / priced_at_ms are write-only too.)
3. active_price_catalog_id -- pricing_seed.py:105, exported at :155. Its only
   caller in the whole repo is tests/unit/storage/test_pricing_chain_roundtrip.py:146.

A FOREIGN KEY declaration is not a read. price_catalogs itself is read only by
pricing_seed.py, the module that writes it (a seeded-already check).

Live data confirms the column carries no information: of 18,655
session_model_usage rows, 10,222 have priced_with set and there is exactly

title: FTS identity ledger catches the class counts cannot see, but no periodic consumer of it was found
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
DETECTED within ~60s for the count class; the identity class has a purpose-built
ledger whose periodic consumer was not found.

CLAIM (CLAUDE.md): FTS5 is contentless over blocks.search_text, "kept in sync by
three triggers". architecture-spine.md: "FTS freshness is an invariant".

THE TRIGGERS ARE REAL. Measured live (SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE
type='trigger'): exactly three on blocks -- messages_fts_ai / _ad / _au, defined
at storage/fts/sql.py:117-134. The _au arm handles search_text moving to and from
''. All three are gated by a derived_refresh_guard row rather than DROP TRIGGER,
deliberately (write.py:4463-4471: so "the trigger-presence half of
assert_session_fts_exact_sync never observes a trigger-less window"). Every
guard set/clear pair traced (write.py:501/792, :2206/2268, _bulk_fts_session_guard
:4433-4520, archive.py delete_sessions) sits INSIDE the same transaction as the
work it suppresses, so a kill mid-guard leaves an uncommitted txn that WAL
discards -- the guard cannot durably survive a crash. Measured:
derived_refresh_guard has 0 rows live. This design is sound.

THE BLIND SPOT, in the code's own words (storage/fts/sql.py:44-58): messages_fts
is contentless, so its UNINDEXED block_id is write-only and unreadable by SELECT;
SQLite reuses freed rowids (a full-session-replace commonly gets the SAME rowid
back). Therefore:
    "Count-only reconciliation (source_rows == indexed_rows) is blind to this:
     both sides still balance even when a stale rowid has silently rebound to a
     different block."
i.e. the FTS row count is perfect while rowid N's postings index the WRONG
block's text -- searches for the old block's terms hit, terms for the current
block miss, and every count check reports healthy.

THE SYSTEM ALREADY BUILT THE ANSWER. messages_fts_identity (storage/fts/sql.py:
63-71) is a rowid -> (block_id, source_hash, recipe_id) shadow ledger written in
the SAME trigger body as each messages_fts write, precisely so exact
reconciliation can join on rowid AND block_id. FTS_MESSAGES_IDENTITY_RECIPE_ID
(:39) even lets a tokenizer/fold change invalidate ledgered rows without a table
shape change.

WHAT RUNS PERIODICALLY IS THE COUNT CHECK. make_fts_stage
(daemon/convergence_stages.py:83-139) compares FTS_INDEXABLE_MESSAGE_COUNT_SQL
against messages_fts_docsize on the ~60s convergence tick (daemon/cli.py:75,218).
A count mismatch is caught fast. An identity-ledger-based exact reconciliation
was NOT found wired into that periodic stage in this pass -- flagged honestly as
not-fully-verified rather than asserted absent; the follow-up read is
_fts_repair_needs_for_sessions and callers of message_identity_mismatch_sql
(referenced from docs/internals.md:238 as fts_invariant_snapshot_sync).

LIVE MEASUREMENT (file:/realm/db/polylogue/index.db?mode=ro):
    blocks WHERE search_text IS NOT NULL AND search_text <> ''   4,961,305
    messages_fts                                                 4,961,305
    messages_fts_identity                                        4,961,305
    distinct recipe_id      1 (messages_fts.v1:unicode61-remove_diacritics2+pl_fold)
    derived_refresh_guard                                        0 rows
The archive is coherent today by every measure available read-only. The
rowid-rebind class was not probed (it needs a rowid+block_id join over 5M rows).

BLAST RADIUS: wrong search results with a green health check -- the failure mode
that motivated building the ledger in the first place. Currently unmeasured, not
currently known-bad.

AC:
- Determine whether an identity-join reconciliation runs on a periodic cadence,
  a repair-only cadence, or not at all; record the answer here with file:line.
- If it is repair-only, decide whether a bounded periodic identity sample is
  worth its cost, and either wire it or record why not. A ledger built to catch a
  class that nothing periodically checks is a detector that never fires.
- The fts_freshness_state row for messages_fts distinguishes "counts agree" from
  "identity verified", so an operator can tell which guarantee they have.

title: writer_modules DML lint scans only archive_tiers/: 11+ DML sites elsewhere own tiers with no declaration
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ENFORCED, but only inside one directory; ASSERTED everywhere else.

CONTEXT: docs/plans/layering.yaml declares a writer_modules inventory -- which
module owns which tier, with durability and interruption semantics -- and the
repo treats it as the audited authority ("the policy is the audited inventory",
layering.yaml:14).

THE GOOD NEWS, established first so this is not read as a teardown:
devtools/verify_layering.py:243-286 (_mutation_calls / _mutation_sql /
_mutation_table) is REAL AST analysis. It parses execute/executemany/
executescript arguments for INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|REPLACE and resolves the target
table to a tier via ARCHIVE_DDL_BY_TIER. It genuinely fails a file that performs
DML with no matching "Writer module:" docstring (writer_module_unmarked_mutation,
:464-470) and fails a declared module whose OBSERVED tiers diverge from its
DECLARED tiers (writer_module_observed_tier_mismatch, :524-534). This is not
docstring ceremony.

THE SCOPE PROBLEM: _writer_module_files (verify_layering.py:321-334) walks only
policy.mutation_roots, and layering.yaml:22 sets that to exactly one path:
    mutation_roots: [polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers]
Nothing else in the repository is scanned. Modules that execute BEGIN IMMEDIATE
+ DML outside that root are invisible to the lint:
    annotations/write.py:316            user.db governed-ontology writes
    storage/raw_reconciler.py           5 sites
    storage/raw_authority.py
    storage/blob_gc.py:436              blob deletion bookkeeping
    storage/blob_publication.py         reservation insert/delete
    storage/embeddings/reconcile.py
    storage/sqlite/migration_runner.py
    browser_capture/capture_jobs.py     4 sites
    sinex/service.py                    5 sites
    daemon/backup.py:335
    sources/live/cursor.py

So the lint proves internal consistency of the archive_tiers/ inventory. It
cannot and does not prove the property the inventory implies -- that only the
declared modules write.

BLAST RADIUS: a new write path added outside archive_tiers/ acquires no tier
declaration, no durability/interruption contract, and no lint objection. The
durable/rebuildable/disposable distinction that the whole five-tier design rests
on is unpoliced outside one directory.

AC:
- Either mutation_roots is widened to polylogue/ (with the current out-of-root
  writers added to the inventory or explicitly exempted with reasons), or the
  layering.yaml header states the scope limit in the same place it claims the
  inventory is audited -- so a reader cannot mistake the guarantee's extent.
- The out-of-root DML sites listed above are triaged: declared, exempted, or
  routed through an archive_tiers/ entrypoint.

title: Nothing serializes a CLI write against a running daemon: 'the daemon owns all writes' is WAL contention, observed live
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ENFORCED for offline-rebuild exclusion; ASSERTED at the CLI-vs-daemon boundary;
DETECTED only as an unalerted log line.

CLAIM (CLAUDE.md, Runtime): "The daemon owns all writes (polylogued run)" and
"The main process is the sole SQLite writer".

WHAT THE THREE LOCKS ACTUALLY DO:
1. OwnedArchiveLocation -- exclusive flock on .archive-ownership.lock
   (storage/archive_identity.py:295-357, :416). Acquired by exactly two callers:
   devtools/campaign_archive_location.py:70 and maintenance/rebuild_index.py:459.
   Never by the daemon, never by ordinary CLI verbs. It keeps two offline
   rebuilds from racing, not live writers from each other.
2. ActiveWriterLease -- a SHARED (LOCK_SH) flock on .index-rebuild.lock
   (storage/index_generation.py:255-273), taken by every non-read-only
   ArchiveStore (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py:1274-1277). Because it
   is shared, a CLI process and polylogued hold it SIMULTANEOUSLY. It excludes
   the exclusive RebuildLease, i.e. offline rebuilds -- not each other.
3. daemon/cli.py:1685-1695 -- exclusive flock on the daemon pidfile. Prevents a
   second polylogued. Says nothing about CLI writes.

So nothing serializes an interactive CLI write against a running daemon. Traced
mark_verb / delete_verb (cli/query_verbs.py:1500, :1602) through
execute_delete_by_session_ids / add_tag to ordinary ArchiveStore/open_connection
writes on the live index.db, with no daemon-liveness check anywhere on that path.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS: plain SQLite WAL contention. WRITE_CONNECTION_PROFILE
(storage/sqlite/connection_profile.py:99-110) is journal_mode=WAL,
busy_timeout_ms=30000. A second writer's BEGIN IMMEDIATE blocks up to 30s, then
succeeds or raises "database is locked". No corruption -- WAL is crash-atomic --
but real failures.

MEASURED, live host journal (journalctl --user -u polylogued):
    lip 27 18:08:57  daemon: component task failed unexpectedly: database is locked
    lip 11 00:29:47  sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked
dozens of occurrences across 2026-07-11 / -18 / -27. This is happening in
production now.

DETECTION: a WARN log line and nothing else. is_transient_sqlite_lock
(sources/live/sqlite_locking.py:16-19) feeds best_effort_cursor_write, which
retries then warns. No writer-identity column, no audit trail, no metric
(grepped writer_identity|written_by|actor_id across polylogue/ excluding tests:
zero matches). A daemon convergence stage that loses the race fails silently
from the operator's point of view.

CONCRETE VIOLATION PATH (3 steps):
1. polylogued run is active and mid-write.
2. Operator runs `polylogue mark id:X --star` (or `delete --yes`).
3. Both hold write connections concurrently; the loser blocks up to 30s and may
   raise "database is locked" -- observed in the journal above.

BLAST RADIUS: no data corruption. Interactive command failures, and daemon
convergence stages dropping work with only a WARN to show for it. Ranked below
the identity/lineage findings for that reason.

AC:
- CLAUDE.md's "the daemon owns all writes" is either made true (CLI write verbs
  refuse or defer when a live daemon holds the archive) or corrected to describe
  what the locks actually guarantee (offline-rebuild exclusion + WAL contention).
- A lock-contention failure is observable as more than a log line: a counter, an
  ops-tier row, or a non-zero exit the operator can see.

title: literal_check has zero call sites: CLAUDE.md documents a Python-to-SQL lockstep mechanism that is never invoked
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
FALSE AS STATED. The named mechanism has zero call sites.

CLAIM (CLAUDE.md:72, "The data model"):
    "CHECK constraints are generated from Python types --
     literal_check(\"status\", *get_args(RunStatus)) embeds typing.Literal args
     into SQL, so Python type <-> SQL constraint stay in lockstep."

MEASURED, two independent greps against origin/master:
    rg -n "literal_check" .            -> CLAUDE.md:72 plus 4 lines inside
                                          storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/common.py
    git grep -n "literal_check" -- '*.py'
        common.py:18   def literal_check(...)          <- the definition
        common.py:27   its own ValueError string
        common.py:40   a docstring cross-reference from order_check
        common.py:107  the __all__ export
Zero call sites. The literal example CLAUDE.md gives does not exist: RunStatus
(insights/run_projection.py:19, Literal["completed","failed","unknown"]) is never
passed through literal_check and is not embedded in any CHECK constraint at all
-- it is an in-memory dataclass field with no SQL enforcement whatsoever.

WHAT IS REAL. check()/nullable_check() (common.py:13-15,32-34) take a
PolylogueStrEnum and call sql_check_in/nullable_sql_check_in (core/enums.py).
Those have ~20 call sites and genuinely do keep enum and DDL in lockstep, e.g.
    index.py:166  check("origin", Origin)
    index.py:245  check("role", Role)
    index.py:247  check("material_origin", MaterialOrigin)
Measured against the live archive, those three are exactly in sync with current
Python (11/5/9 values, zero drift) -- though the archive was rebuilt 2026-07-30,
so this shows freshness, not that the mechanism resisted drift.

THE UNGENERATED MAJORITY. ~50+ CHECK(col IN (...)) lists across
archive_tiers/{index,source,ops,user}.py are hand-written string literals with no
tie to any Python type. One is already a live divergence maintained by hand:
    ops.py:130   embedding_catchup_runs: status IN ('running','completed',
                                                    'failed','cancelled')
    storage/embeddings/progress.py:13  CatchupRunStatus = Literal["running",
                     "completed","stopped","failed","interrupted"]
    cli/commands/embed.py:878  translates "stopped" -> "cancelled" at the write
                               boundary to make the mismatch work
    progress.py:73  defines a SECOND, same-named embedding_catchup_runs table
                    whose own hand-written CHECK does match CatchupRunStatus
Two same-named tables, two independently hand-maintained vocabularies, one
deliberate translation -- correct today only because a human kept all three
consistent. Also: session_links.status CHECK permits only 2 of
TopologyEdgeStatus's 4 values (see the sibling bead on that over-claim).

BLAST RADIUS: no live incident. The cost is that CLAUDE.md tells every future
agent a lockstep mechanism protects the DDL, so nobody looks at the ~50
hand-written lists. A Literal that gains a member drifts silently until a write
hits the constraint.

Note what is NOT broken and should not be "fixed": the fresh-DB-vs-existing-DB
asymmetry is genuinely handled. DerivedDeltaClass.CONSTRAINT_ONLY
(storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py:21) exists for exactly this, was exercised for real
at INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION 36 (lifecycle.py:175-193, Origin gaining `beads-issue`),
and `devtools lab policy schema-versioning` is in the required per-PR lint job
(.github/workflows/ci.yml). Enum-add -> CHECK-text change -> version bump ->
fast-forward declaration is a real, CI-gated, historically-used path.

AC:
- CLAUDE.md no longer cites literal_check/RunStatus as the mechanism; it
  describes check()/nullable_check() over PolylogueStrEnum, which is what runs.
- literal_check is either given its first caller or deleted (surgical renewal --
  do not leave an exported, documented, uncalled helper).
- The hand-written CHECK lists that shadow a Python vocabulary are inventoried;
  each is either converted to check() or recorded as deliberately hand-held with
  the reason. The embedding_catchup_runs 'cancelled'/'stopped' pair is resolved
  or its translation at embed.py:878 is documented at both DDL sites.
close_reason: Landed on dedup-hunt PR branch. (1) CLAUDE.md data-model bullet now describes check()/nullable_check() over PolylogueStrEnum — the mechanism that actually runs — and warns that many CHECK lists are hand-written. (2) literal_check deleted (zero call sites; surgical renewal), order_check docstring cross-ref updated, unused sql_string_literal import dropped. (3) embedding_catchup_runs 'cancelled'/'stopped' pair resolved: the dead progress.py writer stack (zero production callers) is deleted; the ops-tier table is the sole writer target; the CLI 'stopped'/'complete' -> 'cancelled'/'completed' translation is documented at both the ops.py DDL site and the embed.py write site; the third drifted column-set copy (bootstrap's ensure helper, missing skipped_sessions) collapsed onto ops_write's, and skipped_sessions added to canonical DDL. title: layering.yaml has no rule object for cli/mcp/api/daemon: the surface-to-substrate boundary the spine advertises is unenforced (409 sites)
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ASSERTED. The advertised rule has no rule object; the lint that "enforces" it
enforces the opposite direction.

CLAIM: "Surfaces may not import substrate internals directly (enforced by
`devtools verify layering`)" -- docs/architecture-spine.md, "Four Rings / Rules";
repeated in CLAUDE.md ("Surfaces may not import substrate internals directly
(docs/plans/layering.yaml enforces this)").

WHAT layering.yaml ACTUALLY DECLARES. Its own header says so plainly
(docs/plans/layering.yaml:3-5):
    "The current enforced baseline is intentionally the no-backward-import
     contract: substrate rings must not reach into insight/lab/surface adapters.
     Aspirational surface slimming belongs in coverage manifests until call
     sites are moved."

In the rules block, every SUBSTRATE target carries a disallow list:
    target: polylogue/storage   disallow.from: [cli, mcp, daemon, ui, rendering]
    target: polylogue/pipeline  disallow.from: [cli, mcp, daemon, ui]
    target: polylogue/sources   disallow.from: [cli, mcp, daemon, ui]
    target: polylogue/insights  disallow.from: [daemon, mcp, ui]
    target: polylogue/declarations  disallow.from: [ ...12 packages... ]
while every SURFACE target carries a description and nothing else:
    target: polylogue/daemon    description only, NO disallow, NO allow
    target: polylogue/cli       description only
    target: polylogue/mcp       description only
    target: polylogue/api       description only
devtools/verify_layering.py emits a violation only when a rule dict actually
carries disallow/allow entries, so these four rules are structurally inert --
they cannot fail regardless of what cli/mcp/api/daemon import.

MEASURED. Surface packages importing substrate packages, counted from the repo
root against origin/master:
    git grep -n "from polylogue\.\(storage\|pipeline\|sources\)\." -- polylogue/cli     -> 120
    ... -- polylogue/mcp     ->  16
    ... -- polylogue/api     ->  64
    ... -- polylogue/daemon  -> 209
                                 -----
                                 409 import lines
and `uv run devtools verify layering` reports "No layering violations found."
Concrete examples:
    cli/click_app.py:276        from polylogue.storage.sqlite.archive_tiers.index import INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION
    cli/read_views/chronicle.py:24  from polylogue.storage.sqlite.async_sqlite import SQLiteBackend
    mcp/server_resources.py:24  archive_tiers.archive.ArchiveStore
    api/archive.py:60-71        six substrate imports incl. connection_profile.open_connection
    api/insights.py:55,194      archive_tiers.archive.ArchiveStore

NOT IN REQUIRED CI EITHER. .github/workflows/ci.yml's `lint` job runs
render all --check, verify public-claims, lab policy schema-versioning, ruff --
it does NOT run `devtools verify layering`. The lint reaches developers only via
the local pre-push `devtools verify`, not as a required check.

WHAT IS GENUINELY ENFORCED IN THE SAME FILE (do not break it): the reverse
direction (substrate must not import surfaces) is real and checked, and
_collect_writer_module_violations (devtools/verify_layering.py:448-644) is a
genuine AST-level DML-ownership check. The problem is only that the sentence the
architecture doc advertises is not the sentence the lint implements.

BLAST RADIUS: architectural, not runtime. The guardrail the spine names as the
defense against surface-to-substrate coupling does not exist, and 409 call sites
have already accumulated behind a green light. Whoever next reads
architecture-spine.md will believe a boundary is being held that is not.

AC (pick one and make the docs and the lint agree -- do not leave both):
- Either the doc is corrected to state the enforced direction (no-backward-
  import) and the aspirational direction is recorded as an explicit, tracked
  debt with its 409-site count, OR the surface rules gain real disallow blocks
  behind a baseline/allowlist so the count can only shrink.
- Whichever is chosen, `devtools verify layering` runs in the required per-PR
  lint job, so the claim and the gate are observed together.
close_reason: Satisfied: PR #3452 merged 2026-07-31 (gh pr view confirms state=MERGED). docs/plans/layering.yaml:152-215 has real disallow+baseline ratchet blocks for cli/mcp/api/daemon (baseline file, 311 entries). .github/workflows/ci.yml:41 runs 'uv run devtools verify layering' in the required lint CI job — real production gate, not a test-only check. Verified 2026-07-31 verify-first triage.

title: Verify append_ingest.py live path honors the classify_artifact session gate
description:
Follow-up to polylogue-9ykn. While tracing every code path that can turn a raw record into a
ParsedSession destined for write_parsed_session_to_archive (the sole INSERT INTO sessions
chokepoint), found THREE distinct upstream decision points instead of one:

1. pipeline/services/ingest_worker.py (live daemon ingest, default validation_mode=advisory) --
   already gated by archive.artifact_taxonomy.classify_artifact before calling parse_payload /
   parse_stream_payload.
2. sources/revision_backfill.py (`_parse_one` / `_parse_stream`, used by
   `polylogue ops reset --index` rebuild replay and historical backfill) -- previously gated ONLY
   by the narrower path-pattern-only artifact_rule_for_path (OriginSpec), NOT the richer content
   classifier; polylogue-9ykn's fix unified this with (1) by sampling the first ~64 records and
   running them through classify_artifact too, so a rebuild can no longer resurrect a phantom the
   live path now refuses.
3. sources/live/append_ingest.py (`_ingest_append_plans_archive`, live incremental append for a
   growing/watched file, source_index=-1) -- calls dispatch.parse_payload directly with NO
   classify_artifact / artifact_rule_for_path consultation at all.

(3) was NOT touched by polylogue-9ykn's fix, for lack of time to verify it safely. It is very
likely safe-by-construction: append plans should only ever be created for a path the watcher's
discovery phase (sources/live/batch.py) already classified as a session stream when it was first
registered for incremental-append tracking, so by the time _ingest_append_plans_archive runs, the
provider/path pair has already passed the gate once. But this was not empirically verified --
trace batch.py's registration path for _AppendPlan and confirm a record that classify_artifact
would refuse (or that fails artifact_rule_for_path's session policy) can never reach
_ingest_append_plans_archive's parse_payload call. If it CAN reach it (e.g. a directory that starts
producing a new artifact shape mid-watch, after the file was already registered), wire the same
classify_artifact(sample=...) gate used in revision_backfill.py's _is_declared_non_session_artifact
into this path too, so all three chokepoints agree.

Add a regression test proving append-only records that would fail classify_artifact never produce
a session through this path, whichever the finding turns out to be (already-safe -> pin it;
needs-a-gate -> add and pin it).
close_reason: Closed the third chokepoint: append_ingest.py now applies revision_backfill._is_declared_non_session_artifact (same classify_artifact/artifact_rule_for_path gate the other two chokepoints use) to the decoded record sample before calling parse_payload. Empirically verified before the fix: a declared non-session artifact (workflow_journal.jsonl) reaching append tracking did NOT leak a phantom session (parse_retained_raw_sessions' existing gate during replay accidentally protected it via a 'did not replay to exactly one session' RuntimeError), but wasted a raw write + parse + crash-shaped failure log on every observation forever since a failed append never advances its cursor. Now refuses cleanly up front. Regression test test_live_append_refuses_declared_non_session_artifact added (tests/unit/storage/test_raw_revision_authority.py), plus the two pre-existing live-append tests confirm real Codex session appends are unaffected. devtools test tests/unit/storage/test_raw_revision_authority.py -k test_live_append: 3 passed.

title: session_commit.py typed-evidence gaps: PR #0 coercion, cross-repo number collision, foreign-trailer false-disagreement
description:
Follow-up from CodeRabbit review on PR #3425 (fix/insights/session-commit-typed-evidence). Three P2 findings left unaddressed at merge time, filed here rather than blocking the merge of otherwise-complete, tested typed-evidence wiring:

1. polylogue/insights/session_commit.py (typed_refs_from_session_refs, around L785) - a session_refs row with a valid url/repo but no ref_number (observed for Codex Cloud's chatgpt_codex_sidecar._pull_request_ref(), which stores external_pull_request_id in url and leaves repo/number unset) coerces to PR #0 instead of being skipped or parsed from the URL. Since typed refs are authoritative over the regex fallback, this can suppress a correctly-parsed regex result with a bogus PR #0.
2. polylogue/insights/session_commit.py (disagreement detection, around L739) - PR/issue identity comparison uses only the bare number, not (owner, repo, number). acme/product#42 vs other/repo#42 compare equal, so a real disagreement across differently-named repos is not surfaced.
3. polylogue/insights/session_commit.py (foreign-trailer classification, around L500) - when the current session has no bridge_session_ids (own_trailer_tokens is empty), every commit carrying any Claude-Session trailer is labeled as naming a foreign session, producing a disagreement even though there is no typed identity to actually compare against.

Acceptance: (1) a session_refs row lacking ref_number is skipped or its number is parsed from url rather than defaulting to 0; (2) disagreement comparison uses full (owner,repo,number) identity, not bare number, when repo-qualified; (3) foreign-trailer disagreement classification is gated on having at least one own bridge/trailer token to compare against. Regression test per fix.
notes: Implemented in PR #3434 (feature/test/mock-scaffolding-extract). Fix 1: typed_refs_from_session_refs() now parses a real number from a genuine github.com PR/issue URL when the row's number is absent, else skips the row (no more PR #0 coercion). Fix 2: new _refs_match() compares full (owner, repo, number) identity when both refs are repo-qualified, falling back to number-only equality otherwise. Fix 3: foreign_trailer now additionally requires own_trailer_tokens non-empty (no disagreement fabricated when the session has no bridge identity of its own). Regression test added per finding in tests/unit/insights/test_session_commit.py. Verification: devtools test tests/unit/insights/test_session_commit.py -> 46 passed; also ran consumers tests/unit/cli/test_correlate_view.py tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tiers_write.py -> 80 passed; mypy --strict + devtools verify --quick clean.
close_reason: Merged in PR #3434: all three findings fixed with regression tests (PR#0 coercion, cross-repo identity comparison, foreign-trailer false disagreement).

title: Temporary-chat tabs never show accurate archive-state (always 'missing')
description: browser-extension: background.js's conversationIdForUrl returns TEMPORARY_CHAT_SENTINEL for a ChatGPT temporary-chat URL (fixed in PR #3411 to unblock automatic capture at all). Multiple call sites (refreshActiveTabArchiveState, captureTab's pageSessionId derivation) query /v1/archive-state and log ledger/UI state keyed by that sentinel rather than the conversation's real ephemeral provider_session_id (only known after a successful capture's envelope). Net effect: a temporary chat's popup/badge 'captured' indicator never turns accurate, and refreshActiveTabArchiveState's auto_capture_missing branch re-fires every ~30s (throttled) treating an already-captured temporary chat as missing. Not a data-loss bug (content-hash dedup makes the redundant re-captures cheap/idempotent), but real UI inaccuracy and wasted background work. Fix requires giving background.js a per-tab 'last known real captured id' to prefer over the sentinel at every archive-state query site, not just the ones fixed in #3411 (freshness-hint mismatch, captureTab's own pageSessionId). Found during PR #3411 Codex review (P1 finding), partially fixed there (freshness-hint rejection, which WAS a real data-loss bug, and captureTab's own log/state precedence); this bead tracks the remaining archive-state-query-site work.

title: embeddings.db has 4,186 message_embedding_refs pointing to messages no longer in index.db
description:
Adversarial dataset investigation (H10) cross-checked embeddings.db against the live index.db and found stale references left behind by index-tier changes (the tiers are independently rebuildable; embeddings.db is not automatically pruned when index.db loses rows).

Measured 2026-07-31 on live archive: 187,888 total message_embedding_refs. Of these, 4,186 (2.2%) reference a message_id absent from index.db messages, and 4,076 (2.2%) reference a session_id absent from index.db sessions. All sampled orphans are claude-code-session; the largest single orphaned session contributed 713 refs. Every embedding_input_hash in message_embedding_refs does have a matching message_embeddings_meta row (0/187,888 missing) -- the break is specifically refs-to-index, not refs-to-vectors.

Likely cause: a session/message set was deleted or replaced in index.db (targeted repair, de-inflation cleanup, or the 2026-07-30 08:36 index generation swap) without a corresponding embeddings.db cleanup pass. Related but not identical to polylogue-wmsc (embedding freshness/staleness invariant, about content-hash staleness not deletion) and polylogue-8jg9.6 (persistent lineage identity across tier generations, about archive-level identity not per-row cleanup).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Quantify whether this is a one-time backlog (e.g. from the 2026-07-30 index generation swap or a prior de-inflation pass) or an ongoing leak with no GC path -- check whether any current write path deletes index.db session/message rows without emitting a corresponding embeddings.db cleanup instruction. 2. Add a GC/reconciliation pass (startup check, convergence stage, or explicit devtools command) that removes message_embedding_refs (and any orphaned message_embeddings/message_embeddings_meta rows once refcounted) whose message_id/session_id no longer resolves in index.db. 3. Re-run the H10 measurement after the fix lands; both counts should be 0 on a quiescent archive.

title: Wire root: session filter end-to-end; default find to top-level sessions
description:
Split from polylogue-cijx.4 decision 4 ("default result unit is the
top-level session"). That bead's other three decisions (repo identity,
repo-relative paths, structural-label projection) landed; this one didn't,
because it turned out to be a separate-shaped, higher-blast-radius change.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY: `sessions.parent_session_id` and `Session.is_root`
(`parent_id is None`) are correct and already used by a plan-level `root:
bool | None` field (`archive/query/plan.py`) plus a fluent
`.is_root(True)` builder method (`archive/filter/builder.py`). But `root`
is completely unreachable from every actual query surface:

  - No `spec_attr` on its `QueryFieldDescriptor` in
    `archive/query/fields.py` (unlike `origin`/`repo`/`tag`/etc, which do
    have one) -- so `SessionQuerySpec.from_params`/`from_expression` can
    never set it.
  - No case in the Lark DSL transformer in `archive/query/expression.py`
    (`repo:`/`origin:`/`tag:`/... all have an explicit `fname == "..."`
    branch there; `root` has none). `continuation`/`sidechain`/
    `has_branches` are in the identical unreachable state -- this isn't
    unique to `root`.
  - No CLI flag anywhere (`rg` for `--root`/`--continuation`/`--sidechain`
    across `cli/*.py` returns nothing).

Live measurement (read-only, `/realm/db/polylogue/index.db`, 2026-07-31):
15,401 of 23,296 sessions (66.1%) are root/top-level; the other 33.9% are
subagent/branch children. A default `find` with no filters returns both,
unlabeled as to which is which.

SCOPE for whoever picks this up:
  1. Add `root: bool | None = None` to `SessionQuerySpec`
     (`archive/query/spec.py`) and wire it through `query_spec_to_plan`.
  2. Add a `root` case to the Lark DSL transformer
     (`archive/query/expression.py`) -- decide the value syntax (`root:true`
     /`root:false` to match other boolean-flavored fields, or a bare
     `root`/`-root` token; there's no existing precedent to copy since
     `continuation`/`sidechain` never got wired either -- worth deciding
     the pattern once for all three rather than one-off for `root`).
  3. Register field metadata/discovery docs
     (`archive/query/metadata.py`/`discovery.py`) and regenerate CLI/MCP/
     OpenAPI docs (`devtools render all`).
  4. DEFAULT-BEHAVIOR DECISION (the actual design call, not just plumbing):
     cijx.4's decision 4 wants the *default* list to be top-level-only,
     with children reachable only via an explicit `root:false` (or
     equivalent). That changes the result set of every unfiltered `find`/
     `list()`/MCP `query` call across CLI, Python API, MCP, and daemon HTTP
     -- audit existing callers/tests that assume today's "everything"
     default before flipping it, or scope the default change to the CLI
     `find` verb specifically (the interactive surface AC4's own proof
     text names: "re-running `polylogue find repo:polylogue` and showing
     named non-fanout rows") and leave the Python API/MCP defaults
     unfiltered for programmatic composability. Either choice needs to be
     made explicit and stated in the PR, not left implicit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (carried from polylogue-cijx.4 AC4, unchanged):
Default result unit is the top-level session, proven by re-running
`polylogue find repo:polylogue` and showing named non-fanout rows; children
remain reachable through an explicit filter, never silently filling the
default list.
notes:
REACHABILITY DONE 2026-07-31 (this pass, worktree agent-aaffe89902b670d4b, PR pending). `root` is now fully reachable and SQL-pushed end-to-end:

- SessionQuerySpec.root: bool | None (archive/query/spec.py), wired through build_query_spec_from_params (new optional_bool tri-state parser) and query_spec_to_plan.
- DSL: root:true / root:false field clause in the compact-query transformer (archive/query/expression.py); -root: negation is rejected with a message pointing at root:false (the value already carries polarity, unlike origin:/tag:'s inclusion-vs-exclusion split).
- CLI: --root/--no-root flag (cli/click_option_groups.py + cli/click_app.py's cli() signature, added last per this repo's "new Click params go last" convention).
- EXPRESSION_FIELD_REGISTRY["root"] + regenerated docs/cli-reference.md, docs/search.md (devtools render all).

DEEPER BUGS FOUND AND FIXED while making this reachable (both were silent no-ops before this pass, not merely "unreachable" -- worth recording since a future root:/continuation:/sidechain: wiring pass will hit the identical shape):

1. The CLI's actual browse/search path (cli/archive_query.py's _ArchiveFilterKwargs -> ArchiveStore.list_summaries/search_summaries/count_sessions/count_search_sessions/search_session_ids/semantic_summaries/stats/stats_by) is a SQL-level filter path entirely separate from the SessionQueryPlan/apply_common_filters post-filter machinery this field's descriptor (requires_post_filter=True) was designed against. None of those eight ArchiveStore methods accepted a root kwarg. Fixed by pushing root into _session_filter_clause as a direct SQL predicate (sessions.parent_session_id IS [NOT] NULL -- trivially SQL-pushable, unlike continuation/sidechain which derive from branch_type) and threading it through all eight methods + _ArchiveFilterKwargs.

2. Even the SessionQueryPlan post-filter path (Python API's list_summaries_archive/list_archive) was silently broken independent of reachability: ArchiveSessionSummary never carried parent_id (the SELECT never projected sessions.parent_session_id, _summary_from_row never read it), so is_root was True for every summary row regardless of actual parent -- a root:true filter would have silently returned everything even once reachable. Fixed by adding parent_id to ArchiveSessionSummary, projecting s.parent_session_id in both read_summary and list_summaries' SELECTs, and threading it through _summary_to_domain.

VERIFIED LIVE (read-only, /realm/db/polylogue/index.db): `find repo:polylogue --root` -> total 1906; `find repo:polylogue --no-root` -> total 3206; 1906+3206=5112, the unfiltered total -- the SQL pushdown partitions the real archive exactly.

NOT DONE -- the bead's own AC literally asks for the DEFAULT to change ("Default result unit is the top-level session ... re-running polylogue find repo:polylogue and showing named non-fanout rows"), not merely reachability. This pass deliberately did NOT flip any surface's default: find / Python API list() / MCP query / daemon HTTP all continue to return every session (root and child) unless root:/--root/.is_root() is given explicitly. Justification (per this pass's own operator instruction to propose-and-justify rather than silently flip): even the narrower option this bead's own scope note floated -- flipping only the CLI find verb's default -- still has real blast radius (every existing test/saved-query/demo-script assuming today's "everything" default needs re-auditing), and reachability is the load-bearing wedge that unblocks a cold-reader from getting the non-fanout view AT ALL via root:true; the default question is a separable, deliberately deferred design decision.

Also NOT wired (explicitly out of scope, unchanged from before this pass): query_unit_session_filters (the `with <units>` projection's separate session-filter adapter) does not read root; daemon HTTP's _build_query_spec_params named-param allowlist has no dedicated ?root= query param (the existing ?query=root:true DSL path already covers it via compile_expression_into). continuation/sidechain/has_branches remain exactly as unreachable as before -- this pass did not touch them, though the same two deeper-bug shapes above almost certainly apply to them too if/when someone wires them next.

Recommend: keep this bead open, narrowed to just the default-behavior decision (CLI find verb default, or a broader default across every surface) -- that is now the only remaining piece of the original scope, and it is a design decision + blast-radius audit, not more plumbing.

2026-08-03: fresh evidence from full-suite triage. tests/unit/core/test_filters_props.py::TestSessionFilterBranching::test_parent_filters_by_parent_id fails: SessionFilter(...).list() with NO filters returns only the root session even when non-root sessions exist and have real messages -- confirmed the root-only default applies at the SQL level (list_summaries), and .parent(x) is a Python-side POST-filter (archive/query/runtime_filters.py) applied AFTER that already-truncated fetch, so asking for children of a specific parent can never see them. This is the same gap this bead already describes; explicit repro confirms the exact failure mode (root default not relaxed when a child-relationship filter like .parent()/.since_session() is present).

title: Work-evidence adapter: Beads issues.jsonl as issue nodes + dependency edges (1vpm.6 adapter)
description:
Follow-on from the polylogue-qj5x decision (design doc: .agent/scratch/live/beads-handling-design-2026-07-31.html). The Origin route ingested only interactions.jsonl (100% field_change audit rows). The genuinely informative Beads artifact is issues.jsonl: measured in the polylogue workspace, 1,260 issues, 907 with notes, 1,857 dependency edges, plus descriptions/design/acceptance-criteria — none of it currently represented anywhere in the archive.

TARGET: a work-evidence adapter (sibling of BeadsIssueEffectAdapter in insights/work_effects.py) that reads a workspace's .beads/issues.jsonl and emits Beads-issue NODES for the 1vpm.6 work-evidence graph:
- node ref keyed by the bead id itself (e.g. beads:polylogue-x4s) — the workspace prefix already provides global uniqueness; do NOT reintroduce the removed parser's sha256(workspace-root) key, which splits worktrees exactly like the cijx.1 repo-identity defect.
- issue node carries title, status, priority, created/updated, and evidence_refs to the ledger lines; dependency edges become typed issue→issue edges (blocks/discovered-from/...), 1,857 measured in polylogue alone.
- interactions.jsonl rows remain ObservedRepositoryEffect facts (existing adapter) and attach to these nodes as observed_effect edges with occurred_at, old→new, and close reasons (which carry commit hashes — join material for claim reconciliation).
- CAVEAT measured 2026-07-31: interactions.jsonl actor is constant per repo ("Sinity" 2,249/2,249 in polylogue) — it is the git user, not real actor attribution. Session attribution must come from the session side (bd tool_use commands in action blocks), never from the ledger actor field.

This is an adapter of 1vpm.6's core graph per its 2026-07-15 invariant-collapse note ("Complete Beads baseline/history acquisition is a required adapter of the core work-evidence graph, not an independently valuable product surface"). It should also give 1vpm.6 the issue side of the session↔PR↔issue three-way join (session↔PR from pbuh's typed pr-link records; issue↔PR from exact-id tokens in PR bodies/close reasons).
