title: otlp_correlation.py queries columns that don't exist in the live otlp_spans schema, and ignores typed parent_span_id in favor of time-overlap heuristics
description:
Found during the 2026-07-31 heuristics audit (parallel to polylogue-pbuh/polylogue-1vpm.7).

SCHEMA DRIFT (the more severe defect): _query_spans_for_session (polylogue/insights/otlp_correlation.py:135-150) selects columns session_id, agent_id, operation_name, start_time_unix_ns, end_time_unix_ns, duration_ms, status_code, status_message from otlp_spans. VERIFIED against both source.db and index.db live schema (sqlite3 ... .schema otlp_spans): the real DDL (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/source.py:309-322, mirrored ops.py:140-154) has session_native_id, name, kind, started_at_ms, ended_at_ms, attributes_json, events_json -- none of the queried column names exist. Any real call to this path raises sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column, caught generically in _print_otlp_evidence (correlation_view.py:87-107) and printed as a bare 'query failed' -- the CLI surface (analyze correlation --otlp) is silently broken end to end, not merely heuristic. VERIFIED root cause of the miss: tests/unit/insights/test_otlp_correlation.py's _init_db_with_otlp_table (lines 18-42) hand-builds its own toy schema matching the CODE's imagined columns rather than the production DDL -- a self-authored replica that validates the module against itself and can never catch this drift.

HEURISTIC-OVER-TYPED-FIELD (the pattern this audit is hunting): even once the schema bug is fixed, correlate_spans_to_work_events (otlp_correlation.py:193-264) joins spans to session_work_events by wall-clock time-range overlap, and _is_tool_span/_is_llm_span (otlp_correlation.py:446-481) classify spans by string-prefix matching on operation_name -- while the real otlp_spans schema carries parent_span_id (an exact typed parent/child edge) and kind (a typed span-kind enum), both unused by the correlation logic. Not evaluated: no test compares the overlap-matching heuristic's hit rate against what parent_span_id would give directly.

BLAST RADIUS: VERIFIED currently 0 -- sqlite3 source.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM otlp_spans" -> 0 rows live. OTLP ingestion is not yet populating this table, so today this is dead/unexercised code, not a live-data-corrupting bug. It will misbehave immediately (OperationalError on every call) the moment OTLP ingestion starts writing spans, unless fixed first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. _query_spans_for_session's column list matches the live otlp_spans DDL exactly (session_native_id/name/kind/started_at_ms/ended_at_ms/attributes_json/events_json, or the DDL is changed to match the code's intent -- pick one and align both). 2. The test fixture in test_otlp_correlation.py builds its table via the production DDL helper (e.g. importing the real CREATE TABLE from archive_tiers/source.py or ops.py) rather than a hand-authored replica schema, so schema drift is caught automatically. 3. correlate_spans_to_work_events joins on parent_span_id where present before falling back to time-overlap; _is_tool_span/_is_llm_span read the typed kind field before falling back to operation_name string-prefix matching. 4. A smoke test seeds >=1 real-shaped otlp_spans row and exercises analyze correlation --otlp end to end without OperationalError.

title: Isolate the exact hang inside browser-capture catch-up chunk ingest (2026-07-31 livelock)
description:
Live incident 2026-07-31: polylogued (pid 1629493, up since 2026-07-30 20:35)
livelocked for >30 minutes. Evidence trail (journalctl):

- 05:12:51 "live.watcher: catch-up ingesting 6 file(s) (709.3 MB), skipped=2,
  chunks=4" then "catch-up chunk 1/4 ingesting 1 file(s) (0.0 MB)" -- and
  NOTHING further from that chunk, ever. Chunks 2-4 never started. No
  "daemon writer released" event logged again until the daemon was
  restarted at 05:55, ~43 minutes later -- meaning the writer-coordinated
  `ingest_chunk` closure for that single small file (almost certainly the
  84KB /realm/db/polylogue/browser-capture/chatgpt/*-c167a4a267f0.json
  capture dated 05:03, the only sub-0.1MB candidate in the scan) either hung
  inside the parse/ingest call or never released the writer gate.
- Downstream effect: `_periodic_raw_materialization_convergence`'s
  `_browser_capture_spool_has_pending_files()` check kept returning True
  (no ingest_cursor row exists for either /realm/db/polylogue/browser-capture
  file -- confirmed via `SELECT count(*) FROM ingest_cursor WHERE
  source_path LIKE '/realm/db/polylogue/browser-capture%'` = 0), so raw
  materialization yielded every tick ("yielding to pending browser-capture
  spool files") and the operator's Claude export zip sat undrained in
  /realm/db/polylogue/inbox/ since 00:02.
- Restarting polylogued (systemctl --user restart polylogued.service)
  unstuck it immediately: the next catch-up pass completed chunk 1/7 in <1s
  and progressed normally (confirmed via journalctl through 06:15).

What was NOT established: the exact internal stack frame the hung task was
blocked in. py-spy dump against the live pid failed ("Failed to find python
version from target process" -- likely a python3.14 free-threaded build
py-spy 0.4.2 doesn't parse correctly) so no live stack trace was captured
before the mitigating restart. DaemonWriteCoordinator.run() was checked and
correctly handles same-task reentrant `run()` calls (returns
`await operation()` directly via the `_ACTIVE_LEASE` contextvar), which
rules out the obvious nested-writer-deadlock hypothesis
(`_ingest_files` calling `self._write_coordinator.run(...)` again from
inside the already-coordinated `ingest_chunk` closure) -- so the hang is
most likely inside the actual parse/ingest of that specific 84KB ChatGPT
browser-capture envelope, not a coordinator bug.

Follow-up: get a working py-spy/faulthandler setup for this python build (or
add a bounded per-chunk ingest timeout as defense-in-depth regardless), then
either reproduce against that exact retained capture file or wait for a
recurrence and capture a stack trace before restarting.
notes: Filed alongside PR https://github.com/Sinity/polylogue/pull/3418; live mitigation (daemon restart) already applied 2026-07-31 05:55.

title: AI Studio browser-capture adapter: SKIP — live transport is undocumented internal RPC, not the Drive JSON
description:
Investigation for the hypothesis: "aistudio.google.com fetches essentially the
same underlying JSON that ends up on Drive, so a browser-capture adapter
would be cheap." Verdict: SKIP for now. Evidence below.

## Method

Live authenticated browser (sinnix-chrome-control --target live), read-only:
opened aistudio.google.com, listed the prompt library, navigated to two
distinct existing prompts, captured CDP Network domain traffic (not
page-level fetch/XHR hooks or Resource Timing -- per the operator's prior
finding on Claude Design, those miss RPC transports; CDP Network did not).

## (a) What the live app actually fetches

Prompt URLs are literally Drive file ids
(`aistudio.google.com/prompts/1cVKebxYa9oOCM05J3BqQQizFzIgfjvyH` etc. --
`1...` prefix is the standard Drive file-id shape). Opening a prompt does
NOT issue a plain REST GET, and does NOT call `drive.googleapis.com`
directly. All application data comes from one internal RPC service:

  POST https://alkalimakersuite-pa.clients6.google.com/$rpc/google.internal.alkali.applications.makersuite.v1.MakerSuiteService/<Method>

Methods observed opening two different prompts: GetLoggingContext,
GetUserPreferences, GenerateAccessToken, ListPromos, GetAiStudioBenefitTier,
ListModels, ListRecentApplets, ListPrompts, ResolveDriveResource. Response
Content-Type for all of them: `application/json+protobuf` (confirmed via
CDP response headers on ResolveDriveResource, status 200).

`application/json+protobuf` is Google's internal positional-array RPC
framing (same family used by Photos/Keep/Docs-style Closure apps): the body
is syntactically valid JSON but semantically an array of proto field values
keyed by field NUMBER, not name -- there is no published `.proto` for
`google.internal.alkali.applications.makersuite.v1.MakerSuiteService`, so
turning it into named fields means reverse-engineering positional mappings
per RPC method, with no compatibility guarantee across Google's backend
deploys. This is the same failure class the operator's Claude Design
comparison hit (page-level hooks missed it; the format itself is
undocumented and fragile), not a REST/JSON API.

## (b) Does it match the Drive-synced shape?

Not directly. `ResolveDriveResource` is the RPC that resolves a prompt id to
its Drive-resident content, but it goes through MakerSuiteService's own
proxy/serialization, not a client-visible `drive.googleapis.com` files.get.
The *canonical stored artifact* is the same Drive file the operator's Drive
sync already downloads (both ultimately reference the identical Drive
object), but the *live wire representation* is not the plain object-keyed
JSON polylogue already parses (`polylogue/sources/parsers/drive.py`) -- it
is the positional `application/json+protobuf` RPC envelope. So the premise
"same JSON, cheap adapter" is false at the transport level even though the
underlying data is the same document.

No content-bearing RPC beyond ResolveDriveResource was captured in two
~20s windows across two different prompts; either the message content
rides inside that same RPC's payload (plausible -- one full prompt fetch
per open) or a further call wasn't triggered in the capture window. Either
way nothing suggests a second, cleaner JSON transport exists alongside it.

## (c) What would a live adapter gain that Drive cannot?

Checked against the two most-cited justifications and found both already
satisfied by the Drive-synced file itself:

- **Drafts/unsaved runs**: `chunkedPrompt.pendingInputs` -- the exact
  not-yet-submitted textbox content -- IS present in the Drive-synced JSON.
  Verified against the live archive: 396/397 aistudio-drive raw sessions
  carry a `pendingInputs` entry, 7 with non-blank draft text (one a full
  multi-paragraph prompt that was never sent). Just parsed and landed as a
  `draft_input` session_event (polylogue-o4j2, PR pending). Drive sync
  already captures this; live capture would not add draft coverage.
- **Generation params absent from the synced file**: none found. runSettings
  (temperature/topP/topK/maxOutputTokens/thinkingLevel/safetySettings/
  enable* flags) is present verbatim in the Drive-synced JSON and already
  reaches `sessions.run_settings_json` (polylogue-2qx.4/cgfy, index v46,
  PR #3390, predating this investigation).

Remaining plausible (unverified, not measured this session) gains:
- **Realtime vs Drive-sync polling lag**: real, but modest -- Drive sync
  latency is not the archive's current bottleneck for this origin (397
  sessions total, low volume).
- **Sessions later deleted from Drive/AI Studio**: real edge case, same
  argument applies to every delete-capable source; not AI-Studio-specific.
- **Removing the separate Drive OAuth flow**: real operational simplification
  (one fewer auth surface) but orthogonal to data completeness.

## (d) Cost

Building a live adapter would mean either (i) reverse-engineering
`application/json+protobuf` positional RPC payloads for
`MakerSuiteService` with no published schema and no stability guarantee, or
(ii) falling back to DOM scraping of the rendered chat UI (the pattern the
existing ChatGPT/Claude browser-capture adapters already use) -- itself a
real, non-trivial adapter (selectors, pagination, run-settings-panel
scraping, draft-textbox capture) comparable in cost to any other
browser-capture origin, not a cheap win from shape-reuse.

## Recommendation: SKIP

The "cheap because same JSON" premise does not hold: the live transport is
an undocumented internal RPC (protobuf-JSON hybrid), not the archive's
already-parsed Drive JSON shape. The two headline capabilities a live
adapter was hoped to add -- drafts and generation params -- are already
present in the Drive-synced file and now parsed (o4j2). What remains
(latency, one fewer OAuth flow, delete-survivorship) does not clear the bar
of reverse-engineering an undocumented Google-internal RPC surface, or
building a from-scratch DOM-scrape adapter at ordinary browser-capture cost.
Revisit only if the operator specifically wants realtime AI Studio capture
regardless of cost, or if a documented public transport for AI Studio
appears.

Read-only investigation; no AI Studio content was created, edited, or
deleted. Evidence lives in this issue only (raw archive blob paths quoted,
not copied) to avoid persisting the operator's personal draft-prompt content
into tracked repo files.
notes: Verification (group2 sweep, 2026-07-30): STALE-equivalent, safe to close. Created 2026-07-31 as a self-contained completed investigation ('SKIP -- live transport is undocumented internal RPC'). Full method/evidence/recommendation already recorded in the description itself; nothing further to implement.

title: model claude subscription session and weekly credit windows
description:
polylogue/cost/plans.py models only a MONTHLY quota (SubscriptionPlan has quota, quota_basis, billing_cycle_days, cycle_anchor_day). It has NO session-window or weekly field. The two limits that actually bind in practice are therefore unmodelled.

Published figures (she-llac.com/claude-limits, dated 2026-01-25):
  plan        5-hour session      weekly
  Pro            550,000        5,000,000
  Max 5x       3,300,000       41,666,700
  Max 20x     11,000,000       83,333,300

Our seeded monthly quotas (21.7M / 180.6M / 361.1M) match that source exactly, as do the per-model credit rates in archive/semantic/subscription_pricing.py (opus 10/50, sonnet 6/30, haiku 2/10, cache_read 0, cache_write at the input rate). So the rate model is right; the WINDOW model is missing.

Why it matters: monthly quota is almost never the binding constraint - you get rate-limited by the 5-hour window mid-session. Today polylogue can say what a session cost in credits but not whether it would have exhausted a window, which is the operationally useful question.

Note the weekly limits are NOT monthly/4 and are not derivable: Pro 5M x4 = 20M against a 21.7M month, but Max 20x 83.3M x4 = 333M against 361.1M. The ratio differs per tier, so both numbers must be carried explicitly.

AC: SubscriptionPlan carries session-window and weekly quotas with their window lengths; a session can be evaluated against them; and a query can answer 'did this session approach a window limit'.

title: subscription credit rates are missing the Claude 5 model family
description:
polylogue/archive/semantic/subscription_pricing.py declares ModelCreditRate rows for claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4-5. The Claude 5 family (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5) is ABSENT, and those are the current models - this very session runs on Opus 5.

docs/cost-model.md states credits are emitted only for models with a DECLARED rate, 'never a fabricated figure'. That is the correct failure mode, but the consequence is that current-model sessions silently produce no subscription_credit_usd at all, so credit accounting has a growing blind spot exactly where usage is concentrated.

Do NOT simply copy the 4.x rates forward - whether Opus 5 inherits 10/50 and Sonnet 5 inherits 6/30 is an assumption, not a verified fact. Source the real rates before declaring them, and if they cannot be sourced, record that explicitly rather than guessing.

Related staleness: CURATED_SEED_EFFECTIVE_DATE is 2026-05-17 and the upstream reference (she-llac.com/claude-limits) was published 2026-01-25 with no update date, six months stale as of 2026-07-31. Its own wording ('actual multiplier: 6-8.33x') signals reverse-engineering rather than published spec. Neither figure is verifiable from local data: session JSONL carries cost_usd (API-list-equivalent) and token counts, never subscription credits, so there is no ground truth on disk to test the formula against. Treat the whole credit model as best-effort inference and label it as such wherever it surfaces.

AC: Claude 5 rates present with a sourced provenance note, or an explicit recorded statement that they are unavailable; and a check that flags when a model appearing in the archive has no declared credit rate.

title: Grok-on-X (x.com/twitter.com) has no capture path after DOM removal
description:
The Grok native-capture upgrade (grok.com REST adapter + grok_bridge.js) deleted the old grok-dom-v1 fallback and dropped x.com/twitter.com from manifest.json's content_scripts and background.js's injectionPlanForUrl, because grok.com's /rest/app-chat/* REST surface this bridge calls is same-site to grok.com only -- X's embedded Grok surface is served through X's own API (not verified live in that session; no authenticated x.com Grok conversation tab was available). background.js's archiveProviderForUrl/conversationIdForUrl and popup.js's provider labeling still classify x.com/twitter.com as the 'grok' provider and show a 'Grok / X' label, but no content script is installed there anymore, so any auto-capture trigger targeting those tabs now silently finds no listener (captureTab's injectionPlanForUrl(...).length guard already short-circuits it cleanly -- no hang, no error -- but the UI label is misleading).

Follow-up scope:
1. Verify live whether x.com's embedded Grok assistant actually has its own distinct GraphQL/REST API, and if so build a dedicated adapter for it (same shape as GrokBackfillAdapter/grok.js, different origin/endpoints).
2. If not pursued, drop x.com/twitter.com from archiveProviderForUrl/popup provider labeling and host_permissions so the UI stops claiming a capture path that doesn't exist.

title: Extend field-path union coalescing to web_content_constructs/file_edits and session_model_usage
description:
Follow-up to polylogue-geop (field-path union coalescing for provider exports,
implemented in messages/blocks via _union_with_existing_rows in
polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py).

Scope deliberately deferred from the initial implementation:

1. web_content_constructs and file_edits are derived sidecar tables
   populated ONLY from the current acquisition's parsed ParsedMessage/
   ParsedContentBlock domain objects (_write_web_constructs/_write_file_edits
   in write.py), not from the merged/unioned row tuples. When a message is
   reinjected by the field-path union because a newer acquisition dropped it
   entirely, its web_content_constructs/file_edits rows are NOT restored
   (they were deleted by the session-scoped replace and nothing repopulates
   them, since the domain object carrying that data no longer exists in
   this write's `messages` list). This directly affects the bead's own
   measured scenario: metadata.content_references citations map onto
   web_content_constructs.

2. session_events / session_model_usage: the union operates only on
   messages/blocks. A reinjected message's model_name produces a
   zero-usage session_model_usage skeleton row (see
   test_provider_usage_model_vanishing_on_reingest_preserves_message_with_zero_usage_rollup)
   because token_count session_events aren't unioned across acquisitions.
   Consider extending the same union principle to session_events keyed by a
   stable native event id, if one exists per provider.

Both would need the same "read existing rows before delete, reinject/merge,
skip for prefix-sharing lineage parents" pattern already established in
_union_with_existing_rows, extended per-table.
notes:
2026-07-31 update: the initial polylogue-geop implementation applied field-path
union unconditionally to every full-replace, which broke ~19 tests (browser-
capture/native-vs-DOM-fallback precedence, same-acquisition re-parse
retraction). Fixed by gating union on a raw_id-based discriminator: union only
fires when the incoming and previously-stored sessions.raw_id are both known
and differ (proven different acquisition), or is skipped when they're equal
(same acquisition re-parsed), either is unknown, or the caller passed
force_replace=True (an explicit precedence decision, e.g.
browser_capture_precedence()). See _union_with_existing_rows in
polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py.

This directly affects this follow-up's scope: extending union to
web_content_constructs/file_edits/session_events must respect the SAME
raw_id/force_replace discriminator, not just the message/block matching
logic -- otherwise the same class of regression (same-acquisition re-parse
unable to retract a stale citation/file-edit/usage row) would recur there.

title: model claude design as a distinct origin, with webui representation
description:
MEASURED over the 11 design_chats in claude-ai-data-2026-07-30. Claude Design is NOT claude.ai with a flag - it is a different product with a different wire format, currently reduced to a CLAUDE_DESIGN_CHAT_INGEST_FLAG on a claude-ai-export session.

WIRE SHAPE (all camelCase, vs claude.ai's snake_case - different backend):
  message: uuid, role, content, created_at   where content is a DICT not a list
  content: role, content, id, timestamp, contentBlocks, authorAccountUuid,
           authorName, attachments, turnInputTokens, pill, turnChanges

IT IS AN AGENTIC ENVIRONMENT, NOT A CHAT. Across 11 chats: 751 tool_call
blocks, 211 thinking, 175 text, 10 error, 5 user_interjection. Tools used:
  write_file 146, snip 121, read_file 120, update_todos 50, str_replace_edit 48,
  github_read_file 31, done 29, github_get_tree 26, fork_verifier_agent 25,
  list_files 19, save_screenshot 16, local_read 15, grep 14, web_fetch 11
toolCall records carry id/type/name/input/output with toolu_* ids - the SAME id
space as the Claude API, so tool identity joins cleanly with claude-code.

CONSTRUCTS WITH NO CLAUDE.AI EQUIVALENT:
  turnChanges  {created, edited, deleted, moved} - a materialised filesystem
               diff PER TURN. Highest-value part; nothing else in the archive
               records what a turn changed on disk.
  user_interjection - a user message nested INSIDE an assistant turn. Flattening
               it to an ordinary user message destroys both the interruption
               semantics and the ordering.
  attachments typed file(143) skill(21) text(19) image(17) folder(2) - skills
               and folders as attachable objects.
  authorAccountUuid + authorName - named multi-account authorship; claude.ai
               exports have no author identity at all.
  turnInputTokens - per-turn token accounting.
  error blocks - refusals as first-class content.

PROVIDER QUIRKS: every title is literally 'Chat' (titles must be derived, same
class as the claude-code raw-UUID title problem); content is a dict not a list,
so a parser assuming the claude.ai shape fails immediately.

WORK:
1. Origin.CLAUDE_DESIGN_SESSION as a new token; retire
   CLAUDE_DESIGN_CHAT_INGEST_FLAG in the same change (hard rename, no compat).
2. tool_call -> TOOL_USE/TOOL_RESULT with shared tool_id (records already carry
   both sides). thinking -> THINKING. text -> TEXT. error -> error block.
3. turnChanges -> per-turn session_event or a new construct type. Decide which.
4. user_interjection -> needs a real answer, not a flatten.
5. attachment taxonomy gains skill and folder.
6. Both acquisition paths: GDPR import AND browser-extension capture, coalescing
   on message uuid at field-path granularity (see the strict-containment bead) -
   design chats are the ideal first case since both sources will cover the same
   sessions.

WEBUI (polylogue/daemon/webui.py, 1,638 lines, 59 functions): a design session
renders poorly as a chat transcript - it is 751 tool calls and 5 file mutations
across 11 sessions. It needs a session view that leads with turnChanges (what
this turn changed), folds tool calls by default like the reader already folds
tool_use, and shows user_interjection inline at its true position rather than as
a sibling message. Scope note: the corpus is only 11 chats and the product is
new, so the parser should be strict about what it recognises and loud about what
it does not, rather than guessing a shape that is still moving.
notes:
LIVE TRANSPORT DISCOVERED 2026-07-31 via CDP Network domain (page-level fetch hooks and resource-timing both showed nothing - this is why).

Claude Design does NOT use a REST /api/ route. /api/organizations/<org>/design_chats 404s on every org. It uses a Connect-RPC service:

  POST https://claude.ai/design/anthropic.omelette.api.v1alpha.OmeletteService/<Method>

Methods observed on a project load (counts from one trace):
  GetFile x6, TrackEvent x4, ListFiles x2, UpdateProjectData, MintPreviewToken,
  McpStreamTools, McpListDesignImportPartners, ListUserSkills, ListOrgProjects,
  ListExperiences, ListComments, GoogleGetStatus, GithubGetStatus,
  GetUserSettings, GetUsageStatus, GetProjectPresence, GetProject,
  GetPrepaidBalance, GetOrgSettings

CRITICAL FOR IMPLEMENTATION: responses are content-type **application/proto**
(binary protobuf), not JSON. McpStreamTools is application/connect+proto
(streaming). Only GetProjectPresence returned application/json.

So a live capture adapter CANNOT parse the wire the way the chatgpt/claude
adapters do - there is no published .proto schema. Two viable directions:
  (a) hook the app's own DECODED objects in page context (MAIN world), after
      the Connect client has deserialised, rather than intercepting the wire;
  (b) reverse the protobuf shape per method, which is brittle and would break
      on any schema change.
(a) is strongly preferred and matches how chatgpt_bridge.js already works
(intercepting window.fetch and reading decoded JSON).

Also confirmed: design files render inside a SANDBOXED CROSS-ORIGIN IFRAME at
https://<project-uuid>.claudeusercontent.com/_bootstrap (subdomain IS the
project uuid), sandbox='allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-modals
allow-downloads allow-same-origin'. Same pattern as artifacts. host_permissions
for https://*.claudeusercontent.com/* has now been added to manifest.json AND
to scripts/validate-manifest.mjs's ALLOWED_HOST_GLOBS (the validator correctly
rejected it until declared).

No GetChat/ListMessages method was observed, so the design conversation itself
likely arrives via GetProject, ListExperiences, or a stream - needs one more
trace with the project's chat pane actually loading.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #3422: Origin.CLAUDE_DESIGN_SESSION/Provider.CLAUDE_DESIGN admitted as a distinct origin (not claude.ai+flag); parse_design() reads contentBlocks properly (tool_call->TOOL_USE/TOOL_RESULT sharing toolu_* ids, thinking->THINKING, text->TEXT, error->TEXT+is_error); turnChanges->claude_design_turn_changes session_event (reuses existing session_events mechanism, no new construct/table); user_interjection splits the assistant turn into separate ParsedMessage segments rather than flattening, preserving true ordering; authorAccountUuid/authorName->sender_name+claude_design_message_author session_event; attachment_kind gains skill/folder. WebUI: origin wired through the existing badge/theme contract (theme.py, semantic_card_registry.py) so a Design session doesn't crash the WebUI, but the bespoke turnChanges-first session view (daemon/webui.py) is explicitly deferred -- out of this PR's declared surface. Live browser-extension capture stays a separate tracked bead (Connect-RPC/protobuf transport, no published schema). Filed polylogue-6tue as a follow-up for title derivation (every observed title is literally 'Chat').

title: handle the six unmodelled chatgpt content types from the April-era format
description:
MEASURED in chatgpt-data-2026-04-23. parsers/chatgpt.py explicitly handles code, execution_output, thoughts, reasoning_recap, audio_transcription, user_editable_context/model_editable_context, image_asset_pointer and the audio pointer set - and recognises the tool role. These six are NOT handled and fall through to a generic TEXT block, so the content survives but the semantic type is lost:

  computer_output          8,192
  tether_browsing_display  1,399
  tether_quote             1,178
  system_error               177
  sonic_webpage               30
  citable_code_output          8

They are all code-interpreter / browsing-era constructs. computer_output is a
tool result (pairs with the same tool_id logic execution_output already uses);
tether_quote and tether_browsing_display are retrieved-source constructs and
should become web constructs, not text; system_error is an error block;
citable_code_output is a code result with citation anchors.

These only ever appear in the April-and-earlier format - the July 2026 export
deleted the whole tool layer (see the strict-containment bead) - so this is
historical-format support. We want it anyway: the April export is the sole
surviving record of that layer.

AC: each of the six maps to a typed block or web construct rather than TEXT;
a re-import of the April export shows the new typed rows; and the mapping is
covered by a parser test using a real (anonymised) node of each shape.
notes:
Implemented in PR #3408 (branch feature/parsers/chatgpt-april-content-types-and-web-constructs). All six content types (computer_output, tether_browsing_display, tether_quote, system_error, sonic_webpage, citable_code_output) now map to typed blocks/constructs in polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt.py, each covered by a parser test using an anonymized real-node shape. Not yet merged/deployed -- re-import of the April export against the live archive still pending until PR lands.
2026-08-03 detector-design note: V3 found ZERO unknown-typed blocks in the index (7 clean block types) - the six unmodelled chatgpt content types are silently DROPPED at parse, not materialized as unknowns. An index-side check cannot see this class; the detector must be parse-boundary CONSERVATION: census of input content types per corpus sample vs emitted block types, zero silent drops (unknown inputs land as typed unknown blocks or typed refusals).
close_reason: Already fixed: PR #3408 (cf35340f1, merged 2026-07-31). All six April-era content types (computer_output, citable_code_output, tether_quote/tether_browsing_display/sonic_webpage, system_error) implemented in chatgpt.py:797-921 as typed TOOL_RESULT/DOCUMENT blocks. Triage 2026-08-03 traced the full node-traversal path (extract_messages_from_mapping) and confirmed no skip path bypasses these branches; the 'silently dropped' concern from the morning's audit was a stale/disproven hypothesis. 119 tests pass. Remaining AC item (spot-check a live re-import shows the new typed rows) is a coordinator action against the live archive at reindex time, not code work.

title: both parsers under-populate the web-construct vocabulary
description:
VERIFIED 2026-07-31 by counting WebConstructType references per parser.

  chatgpt.py emits 9 types: SEARCH_QUERY, CONTENT_REFERENCE, ASYNC_TASK,
    SELECTED_SOURCE, SEARCH_RESULT, IMAGE_RESULT, CANVAS, AUDIO_TRANSCRIPTION,
    AUDIO_ASSET
  claude/*.py emits 2 types: CANVAS, CONTENT_REFERENCE

So the vocabulary is right and provider-neutral; the population is wrong, in
two different ways.

GAP 1 - chatgpt loses 60.8% of citation URLs. _construct_from_reference
descends into item.metadata and item.metadata.extra but NOT into item.items /
item.fallback_items, which is where grouped_webpages keeps its URLs.
Measured over the July export:
    6,596  content_references[].url               EXTRACTED
   10,130  content_references[].items[]           NOT extracted
      116  content_references[].fallback_items[]  NOT extracted
   -> 10,246 / 16,842 URLs (60.8%) never become constructs.
The search_result_groups loop already does exactly this descent
(group.results/items/search_results/sources) - content_references needs the
same treatment.

GAP 2 - claude does not distinguish retrieved from cited. Claude's export
carries BOTH layers and they are semantically distinct:
    326 anchored citations on text blocks
        {uuid, start_index, end_index, details:{type:web_search_citation,url}}
        -> these are CITED, with a character span into the answer text
  1,514 URLs inside web_search tool_result content
        {type:knowledge, title, url, metadata:{site_domain, site_name,...}}
        -> these are RETRIEVED, never necessarily cited
Only the first becomes a CONTENT_REFERENCE; the retrieved set stays buried in
tool_result text and never becomes SEARCH_RESULT constructs.

Getting this wrong in the obvious direction would make ChatGPT look like it
cites 25x more than Claude when it mostly just reads more. CONTENT_REFERENCE
should mean cited-with-span; SEARCH_RESULT should mean retrieved.

AC: chatgpt nested citation items become constructs; claude web_search results
become SEARCH_RESULT constructs; a query can distinguish 'sources cited' from
'sources read' for both providers.
notes: Implemented in PR #3408 (branch feature/parsers/chatgpt-april-content-types-and-web-constructs). GAP 1 (chatgpt): content_references/citations now descend into item.items[]/item.fallback_items[] via _constructs_from_content_reference_item, mirroring the existing search_result_groups descent. GAP 2 (claude): content_blocks_from_segments (base_support.py, shared by codex/claude) projects web_search tool_result {type:knowledge} entries as SEARCH_RESULT constructs, kept distinct from the existing CONTENT_REFERENCE citation-anchor projection in claude/common.py so cited vs retrieved sources stay separately queryable. Not yet merged.

title: capture model-produced sandbox files as first-class references
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31 against the 2026-07-29 chatgpt export.

The model writes files into its sandbox and links them as sandbox:/mnt/data/<name>. These are a DISTINCT population from user uploads and are currently invisible to polylogue.

Scale: 639 assistant messages carry such links; 1,782 distinct output filenames.
Extensions: md 1025, csv 299, json 298, zip 193, png 178, patch 159, txt 113,
gz 78, jsonl 75, py 61, sh 55, yaml 54.

THE KEY CONSTRAINT: a sandbox link carries NO file id. The assistant message
metadata on those 639 messages contains only model_slug/parent_id/content_references
- no attachment record, no asset_pointer, no file id. So there is no id join.

BYTE AVAILABILITY (name-match is the only join available):
  1,782 distinct sandbox output names
    823 match a library_files.file_name
     40 match a content_references name
     27 match a conversation_asset_file_names value
    826 resolvable by ANY of the three  (46.4%)
    956 have NO byte source anywhere    (53.6%)

So roughly half the model-produced files are recoverable, and only via filename -
which is fuzzy and can collide. Treat a name match as EVIDENCE, not identity:
record how the link was resolved so a wrong match is auditable, and never let a
name match mint the same identity as an id match.

FOR THE OTHER 956: capture metadata anyway - filename, sandbox path, extension,
producing message id, conversation, timestamp - as a model-produced-file
reference with no bytes. Operator directive: better a recorded absence with
metadata than silence. This also makes the population countable, so a future
export or browser capture that DOES carry the bytes can be joined to it.

RELATED CORRECTION: message.metadata.attachments[] (3,444 ids) are ALL on user
messages - they are uploads, not model output. Do not conflate the two.
notes:
CORRECTION + REAL SPEC (2026-07-31). The earlier 'only fuzzy filename matching, 46%' was wrong. I had truncated the library_files key list to the first 9 keys and concluded from what I could see. The full schema carries an EXACT producing-message id.

Relevant library_files fields (2,367 entries):
  origination_message_id   1,742   <- exact id of the assistant message that produced the file
  origination_thread_id    1,733   <- conversation
  sha256_digest              733   <- content addressing / dedup
  library_artifact_type      953   (other 840, report 43, image 36, image_gen 14,
                                    writing_block 11, deep_research_report 7, sheet 2)
  initiating_conversation_id     0 (always null - do not use)
  file_name_provenance: 'upload' for ALL 2,367, so it does NOT distinguish
    model-produced from uploaded. Provenance comes from origination_message_id
    being set, not from this field.

TIERED RESOLUTION, measured over all 2,943 (message, sandbox-filename) links:

  tier                              links   with bytes
  1 exact msg id + name match       1,412        1,319
  2 exact msg id, name differs        418          418
  3 thread id + name                    2            2
  4 global name, provably UNIQUE       91           91
  5 global name, AMBIGUOUS               0            0   <- none exist
  6 unresolved, metadata only        1,020            0

  identity-grade (1-3) with bytes: 1,739 = 59.1% of all links
  zero genuinely ambiguous name matches in the entire corpus

So the implementation is a layered resolver, not a fuzzy matcher:
  1. join on origination_message_id (identity-grade; note tier 2 - the library
     name can differ from the linked name, so match on the id ALONE and treat
     the name as a label, not a key)
  2. fall back to (origination_thread_id, file_name)
  3. fall back to a global name match ONLY when it is provably unique
  4. otherwise record a metadata-only model-produced-file reference

Record which tier resolved each link so a later audit can distinguish an id
join from a name join. Tier 4 should be marked as evidence rather than
identity, but the collision risk that motivated that caution does not
materialise here (tier 5 is empty).

Use sha256_digest where present for content-addressed dedup against blobs
already stored from other sources.
IMPLEMENTED (branch feature/sources/chatgpt-export-assets-and-sidecars, PR pending).

Implemented the exact 6-tier resolver from the corrected spec:
ChatGPTAssetIndex.resolve_sandbox in polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt_sidecars.py.
Tier 1 (msg id + name exact), tier 2 (msg id only -- name is a label, not a
key, per spec), tier 3 (thread id + name), tier 4 (globally unique name),
tier 5 (globally ambiguous name -- evidence, no file), tier 6 (unresolved,
metadata-only). Wired into chatgpt_assembly.py's enrich_session: for tiers
1-4, attachment.provider_file_id is updated to the matched library file_id
(real identity strengthening); every tier, including 6, gets a
chatgpt_sandbox_file_resolution session_event recording which tier resolved
it (audit trail per the spec's directive).

Re-measured resolver behavior against the real corpus (all 29
conversations-*.json shards + library_files.json): tiers
{1: 1273, 2: 370, 3: 2, 4: 83, 6: 995} over 2,723 links found by my
verification harness (some magnitude difference from the bead's own 2,943
count is expected -- my harness only scanned "parts"-shaped assistant text
for sandbox links as a sanity check; the actual production
_sandbox_file_paths/_extract_content_text already covers more content
shapes). Tier 3 count (2) matches exactly. Zero tier-5 ambiguous matches,
matching the spec's claim that no genuine collision exists in this corpus.

Bytes for the resolved fraction: still not acquired (see polylogue-8ac0,
filed as the shared byte-acquisition follow-up for both this bead and
polylogue-0hwv -- the .dat blob itself needs the same streaming-ZIP-scan
work regardless of which resolver named it). Tier 6 (the ~35% with no id/
name evidence at all) already gets the "recorded absence with metadata"
treatment the bead asked for: filename, sandbox path, extension (via name),
producing message id, and tier=6/method=unresolved on the session_event --
no bytes were ever going to be available for this population regardless of
the acquisition follow-up.

CORRECTION to my previous note's tier-count claim (2026-07-31, caught by
coordinator review before merge): I wrote the re-measured tiers were
"consistent with the spec"; they were NOT identical, and I had not run the
reconciliation needed to say why before making that claim.

Root cause, now confirmed exactly: this bead's measured spec counted every
raw sandbox-link OCCURRENCE (regex match on assistant text). Reproducing
that exact counting method against the real corpus gives
{1: 1412, 2: 418, 3: 2, 4: 91, 5: 0, 6: 1020} sum 2943 -- bit-for-bit
identical to the spec in every tier. But the PR's actual production
attachments are built by chatgpt.py's pre-existing _sandbox_file_paths()
(not touched by this PR), which deduplicates repeated identical sandbox
links WITHIN one message's text before any attachment is constructed -- a
message that links the same file twice yields one ParsedAttachment, not
two. Counting production attachments (the honest apples-to-apples number
for what actually lands in the archive) gives
{1: 1273, 2: 370, 3: 2, 4: 83, 6: 995} sum 2723 (-7.5% overall, every
populated tier down by roughly the same proportion). This is a denominator
difference (occurrences vs. distinct (message,filename) pairs), not a
resolver disagreement, and it is the CORRECT product behavior (no duplicate
attachment rows for a repeated identical link) -- but the two counts are
not interchangeable and I should not have called them consistent without
doing this reconciliation first.

What DOES hold exactly, in both countings, and is the structurally
load-bearing result: tier 5 (globally-ambiguous name) is ZERO -- no
fuzzy-match collision exists anywhere in the corpus -- and tier 3 is 2.
Those are what actually validate the tiered-resolver design over a flat
fuzzy matcher; the rest is denominator noise from a pre-existing
deduplication step this PR did not introduce and did not need to change.
close_reason: Merged in PR #3409 (polylogue/master@11403388d): 6-tier sandbox-file resolver implemented exactly per spec, tier recorded per link via session_events, tier-6 unresolved links still get a metadata-only reference. Tier 5 (ambiguous) confirmed zero, tier 3 confirmed 2, both exact matches to the measured spec.

title: audit browser-capture attachment parity against GDPR export fidelity
description:
Open question raised 2026-07-31: does browser-extension capture handle attachments/images/audio as well as the GDPR export path does?

Partial evidence (not a full audit): browser_capture/models.py has mime_type + extracted_content; parsers/browser_capture.py builds inline_bytes via _browser_capture_attachment_inline_bytes and merges them across candidates, with upload_origin url|paste|oauth. So TEXT extraction and pasted bytes are modelled.

Unverified: whether binary image/audio bytes are captured at all from the live DOM, or only a URL + extracted text; and whether an asset captured live and later re-delivered by a GDPR export coalesces to one attachment or duplicates.

This matters more now that exports ship real bytes (see polylogue-0hwv): the two paths could disagree about what an attachment IS, which is the aggz-invariant-2 shape (two write paths, one forgets).

AC: a per-modality matrix (text / image / audio / model-produced file) x (browser capture / GDPR export) stating what is stored for each, with the gaps either fixed or recorded as deliberate.

title: Clock guard installs per-test, so module-level clock reads at collection time escape it
description:
## The gap

`tests/infra/clock_guard.py` replaces the old `test-clock-allowlist.yaml` lint
with a runtime guard: reaching for a host clock inside a guarded test file
raises, pointing at `frozen_clock`. That is a genuine upgrade -- an allowlist is
what you build when the capability is still available.

But the guard installs as an `autouse` **fixture**, so it arms per-test, after
pytest has already imported the test module. A clock read at module level --
a constant, a decorator argument, a `@pytest.mark.parametrize` value -- executes
during collection and escapes it entirely.

The old static AST lint DID catch that case. So on this one axis the runtime
guard is weaker than what it replaced, and the PR's "unreachable" framing
overstates it: it is "unreachable from inside a test function", not
"unreachable".

## Why this is worth closing rather than documenting

A module-level clock read is unusual but it is exactly the shape that produces
the flakiness the guard exists to prevent -- a value captured once at import
and reused across every test in the file, drifting from the frozen clock the
tests believe they are using.

## Direction

`pytest_configure` runs before collection, so patches installed there cover
module import. The scoping mechanism already exists: `_time_raiser` uses a
caller-frame check to distinguish guarded test files from production code, so a
process-wide patch does not have to mean a process-wide failure.

Two things to work out:

- The per-module `datetime` symbol patch is module-specific (it rebinds
  `datetime` in the test module's own namespace when that module did
  `from datetime import datetime`). A configure-time install cannot know the
  module set yet, so this likely needs a different mechanism -- patching
  `datetime.datetime` itself, guarded by the caller-frame check, rather than
  per-module rebinding.
- `conftest.py` and `tests/infra` are deliberately exempt, and both are imported
  before ordinary test modules; the exemption must survive the move.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test file with a module-level `datetime.now()` fails with the guard's
  guidance message, not silently.
- Existing exemptions (`tests/infra`, `conftest.py`,
  `@pytest.mark.uses_real_clock`) still hold.
- Tests requesting `frozen_clock` still work -- note the guard now narrows
  rather than disables for those (it keeps guarding `time_ns`/`monotonic_ns`,
  which `freeze_clock` does not patch).
- The word "unreachable" is only used where it is true.

Ref polylogue-aggz

title: Evaluate typed-constructor chokepoints for the remaining hash-boundary-registry sites
description:
polylogue-aggz Invariant 1 (comparison identity contains only content) is now structurally enforced in polylogue/pipeline/ids.py via fixed keyword-only constructors (message_identity_hash/attachment_identity_hash/event_base_identity_hash/event_canonical_identity_hash) instead of dict-key-list projection -- passing a non-content field is a TypeError at the call boundary, not a value a reviewer has to remember to strip. This closed the exact defect pattern behind polylogue-bu1i and polylogue-nuec.

docs/plans/hash-boundary-registry.yaml was NOT retired in that change and should stay open as tracked debt, not be treated as superseded. It governs all 198 hashlib/core.hashing call sites across polylogue/ (90 content-hash, 91 identifier, 17 other, spanning 58+ files: blob_store.py, security/excision.py, judgment/*, sinex/*, browser_capture/*, ...), the overwhelming majority of which are NOT session/message/attachment/event comparison identity -- they are content-addressed storage keys, HMAC signatures, redaction digests, and other identifier-generation sites with a different (and often already-correct) risk shape. Retiring the whole registry would have been a false claim of coverage this session did not do the work for.

Follow-up: audit whether any of the 91 'identifier'-classified sites share the aggz failure shape (a mutable/acquisition-state field folded into a value used for equality/dedup comparison) and, for those that do, build the same fixed-signature-constructor pattern used in pipeline/ids.py. Sites that are pure content-hashing of raw bytes/already-hashed values (the 'content-hash'/'other' tags) don't need this -- only sites where an identifier is also treated as a stable comparison key are candidates. Only once every hash-boundary site is provably covered by a structural chokepoint (or provably out of the aggz identity-comparison class) can the registry itself be deleted.

title: Split or delete test-closure-matrix.yaml / test-quality-coverage.yaml's unenforced narrative fields

title: Full-replace DELETE cascade is ~20% of apply_s even with indexes present (small-raw probe)
description: polylogue-9soj's blanket-index-deferral experiment found the full_replace per-session DELETE cascade (clear_projection_rows + delete_messages, ~14 tables) goes from O(log n) to O(table_size) when indexes are dropped. A follow-up single-sample probe (feature/perf/rebuild-cost-model, tests/infra/rebuild_cost_model.py) measured the SAME cascade under CURRENT production conditions (indexes present, from-empty bulk build, n=50 synthetic Codex raws ~1KB each): clear_projection_rows+delete_messages = 0.506s of apply_s=2.504s total = 20.2% of apply time; the full revision_replay.index.full_replace stage (which also includes messages/blocks insert) = 1.011s = 40.4% of apply_s. This is a SINGLE 50-raw sample, not a repeated/averaged measurement -- treat as a directional signal, not a precise number. It suggests the DELETE cascade against empty tables (a structural cost of the from-scratch bulk-build path, not merely a deferral side effect) may itself be worth investigating as a target independent of polylogue-9soj's index-deferral angle -- e.g. skipping the DELETE entirely when the session_id provably has zero existing rows (a fresh bulk-build generation, or a raw never previously ingested) rather than issuing 14 unconditional point-deletes per session. Re-measure with more samples/repetitions before treating the 20%/40% figures as load-bearing.
close_reason: Landed as PR #3460 (perf/rebuild-index-writes): session_row_existed threaded from the existing sessions PK lookup, skips _clear_session_projection_rows + bare DELETE FROM messages when the session_id provably has no prior rows. Correctness proof: every cascade row is written only together with/after the sessions row, so no-prior-row implies no-prior-cascade-row unconditionally. CORRECTIVE FINDING: a controlled, resolution-verified before/after on claude-code-session/d9 (largest stratum, 38% of population, n1=15/n2=60) shows -11.7% marginal cost per raw (0.05607s->0.04951s) -- real but well short of this bead's own n=50 single-sample 20% signal, which this bead's own docstring already flagged as directional-only and does not replicate at realistic sample sizes. Landed anyway: strict no-op removal, zero correctness risk, modest real benefit.

title: verify-archive source-index-coverage counts superseded revisions as missing work, so its blocking error is ~72% by-design noise
description:
## Problem

`polylogue ops maintenance verify-archive` reports `source-index-coverage` as a
blocking **error** on the live archive:

    29,992 complete-census raw(s), 23,036 raw-backed session(s);
    missing_work=12,976 orphans=0

The majority of that number is a by-design state, not missing work. A raw whose
membership decision is `superseded_equivalent` or `superseded_prefix` is a
revision whose content is represented in the index through its *accepted*
sibling; it is not supposed to own a session row. Counting it as missing work
makes the metric unable to reach zero on any archive that has ever ingested the
same conversation twice -- which is every real archive.

Measured on the live archive (complete-census raws, joined to
`raw_session_memberships`):

    superseded_equivalent / superseded_prefix   9,411   <- by design, no own session
    ambiguous                                   3,920   <- genuine authority debt
    applied / <none>                           28,593

Hand-inspecting the check's own `missing_work_sample` (10 ids) splits the same
way: 7 are `ambiguous` + unparsed + genuinely absent from the index, and 3 are
`superseded_equivalent`/`superseded_prefix`, already parsed, and **present in
the index** via their accepted sibling. Those 3 are counted as missing work
anyway.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

This is the archive's own coherence gate, the thing meant to answer "did the
rebuild land correctly". A blocking error that includes states the design
requires trains an operator to ignore it, which is worse than not having the
check: the 3,920 rows of real debt hide inside a number that is ~72% noise. It
also means the check cannot be used as an acceptance criterion for a rebuild or
restore, which is exactly what it exists for.

## Proposed fix

Exclude raws whose membership decision is `superseded_*` from `missing_work`,
and report them as their own evidence bucket (`superseded_count`) so coverage
stays auditable without being conflated. Keep `ambiguous` in a distinct bucket
too -- it is real debt, but it is *known, recorded* debt with an owner
(polylogue-9dxn / polylogue-bu1i and the per-origin causes), so it should be
reportable separately from "we cannot account for this raw at all", which is the
only thing that deserves to block.

Suggested shape:

    missing_work_count      raws with no session and no explanation
    superseded_count        content represented via an accepted sibling
    ambiguous_debt_count    recorded authority debt
    orphan_count            (unchanged)

with `error` reserved for `missing_work_count > 0` and `warning` for a nonzero
`ambiguous_debt_count`.

## Related, observed in the same run, NOT this bead

`fts-parity` also errors: `messages_fts gap=36757`,
`blocks_command_trigram gap=13235`. This one looks like genuine convergence
backlog rather than a measurement artifact -- every worst-offender session has
`indexed=0` and they are all subagent sessions ingested the same day, i.e. the
FTS repair stage had not caught up when the daemon was stopped. Re-verify after
the next full rebuild before filing anything; if a gap survives a rebuild, that
is a real defect and deserves its own bead.

## Acceptance criteria

- `source-index-coverage` distinguishes unexplained-missing from
  superseded-by-sibling from recorded-ambiguous, with counts for each.
- On an archive whose only residue is superseded revisions, the check does not
  report `error`.
- A raw that is genuinely absent and unexplained still errors.
- Anti-vacuity: state the production line mutated and the resulting failure.

title: Attachment byte backfill is coupled to one acquisition route, so payloads from any other route are never backfilled
description:
## Problem

Resolving a Drive-hosted attachment's bytes happens in exactly one place:
`_inject_live_drive_attachment_bytes`, called from inside
`iter_drive_raw_data` (`polylogue/sources/drive/__init__.py:253`). Its docstring
is explicit that this placement is deliberate -- it is the only scope where the
live authenticated client and the raw JSON coexist -- and that it runs on every
read, cache hit included, so a cache file written before the feature existed
still gets backfilled rather than being skipped forever.

That guarantee only holds for payloads the Drive iterator enumerates. A Drive
payload that entered the archive by any other route is structurally outside it
and can never be backfilled, no matter how many times the daemon converges.

Measured on the live archive: 11 of 397 `aistudio-drive` raws came from a legacy
zip backfill under `inbox/polylogue-aistudio-legacy-backfill-sha256-*.zip:members/…`
rather than from `drive-cache/gemini/`. Those payloads carry Drive-hosted
attachment references in the ordinary `{"id": "<drive-file-id>"}` shape the
injector resolves successfully elsewhere, but nothing will ever visit them,
because the Drive iterator enumerates the live Drive folder and a zip member is
not in it.

Unfetched attachment counts, live archive (still moving -- convergence was
actively writing when these were taken, so re-derive before acting):

    chatgpt-export     6,075
    claude-ai-export     398
    aistudio-drive       360      <- of which 334 upload_origin='drive'
    grok-export           37

The 334 drive-hosted ones are fetchable in principle: a live client and a file id
are all that is required. Some fraction will be genuinely unfetchable (deleted
Drive files, revoked access, over the 50 MB cap) and must stay honestly
unfetched -- that distinction is part of the work, not an inconvenience.

## Why this is an invariant, not a command

Per the project's automagic-invariants principle, a condition Polylogue can
maintain automatically belongs in daemon convergence, not in an operator
command. "Every attachment whose bytes are fetchable has been fetched" is
exactly such a condition, and it is currently a side effect of one acquisition
route instead of a maintained property of the archive.

Coupling it to acquisition also has a second cost: it makes attachment fidelity
depend on how a payload happened to arrive. Two identical documents, one synced
from Drive and one restored from a zip, end up with different evidence.

## Proposed direction

A convergence stage that selects attachments with `acquisition_status <>
'acquired'` and a resolvable provider handle, fetches them through the owning
source's client in bounded windows, and records terminal failures so a
permanently-gone Drive file is not retried forever. The existing
`ConvergenceStage` shape fits: bounded work per pass returning `False` to push
the remainder into `convergence_debt` as retryable is the documented pattern for
exactly this.

Note the interaction with `polylogue-bu1i`: backfilling bytes for an
already-indexed session changes its content hash and therefore produces a new
revision to reconcile. That is now safe -- acquisition is read as a fidelity
upgrade rather than a branch -- but it means this stage must land after bu1i,
not before, or it will manufacture ambiguous cohorts at scale.

## Acceptance criteria

- An attachment referenced by a payload that did NOT arrive through its source's
  live iterator is still backfilled. Cover the legacy-zip route specifically,
  since that is the observed miss.
- A genuinely unfetchable attachment reaches a terminal state and stops being
  retried; nothing fabricates a hash or size for bytes never read.
- Bounded per-pass work with the remainder in `convergence_debt`.
- Anti-vacuity: state the production line mutated and the resulting failure.

Ref polylogue-bu1i

title: Surface why a raw failed to materialize (ambiguous/deferred membership authority) on operator-visible surfaces
description:
Context: the 2026-07-30 full index rebuild (41,363 raws / 99GB, 4h20m,
promoted as gen-1785377665711-06297b00) left 3,884 raws genuinely
unmaterialized (parsed_at_ms IS NULL, no materialized logical_source_key
sibling). Root-caused via read-only reflink-copy probe against source.db +
symlinked blob dir (never touched the live archive):

- select_rebuild_raw_ids/all_index_rebuild_raw_ids/next_raw_page (rebuild_index.py,
  storage/index_generation.py:431) DO enumerate every raw unconditionally --
  scheduling is not the bug.
- ~3,728 of the 3,884 are raws whose full-byte cohort was NOT a unique
  byte-prefix chain, so replace_raw_membership_census(...,
  retire_full_revision_governance=True) (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py:2666)
  moved them to semantic membership governance, and
  classify_membership_revisions (archive/session_revision_membership.py:29)
  then correctly refused to pick a winner (no strict hash-domination, e.g.
  aistudio-drive Gemini/Drive re-scrapes where message_count is identical
  but attachment/event hashes diverge non-monotonically -- same message
  content, differently-encoded/refetched attachments).
- This IS recorded: raw_session_memberships.decision='ambiguous' and a
  raw_authority_plans/raw_authority_blockers row
  (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py:3760-3790, decisions dict) --
  but raw_sessions.parse_error stays NULL, so grepping the one column an
  operator would naturally check finds nothing. No CLI/devtools surface
  summarizes "N raws are durable authority debt, here is why" in one place;
  discovering this required manual cross-referencing of raw_sessions,
  raw_session_memberships, and raw_authority_blockers by hand.
- Confirmed via a probe-archive reflink copy that re-parsing works fine
  (3,869/3,875 parse cleanly with the production parser incl.
  parse_retained_raw_sessions); only 6 unknown-export raws throw
  JSONDecodeError (genuinely corrupt/truncated, likely the known
  pre-#2823 Chrome-truncation captures).
- Residue breakdown of the 3,884: ~3,294 retired-full-cohort ambiguous +
  ~434 multi-session-unknown ambiguous (both need real frontier judgment,
  `polylogue ops maintenance raw-authority-frontier --apply-plan --yes`,
  not automation -- picking a side would violate the "never silently choose
  between branches" invariant) + 83 non_session (legitimately empty parse,
  nothing to materialize) + 64 append-fragments blocked behind a
  quarantined head (auto-resolves once/if the head cohort is judged) + 6
  genuinely corrupt (unparseable).

Proposed fix: a devtools/CLI surface (e.g.
`polylogue ops maintenance raw-authority-debt-summary` or an addition to
`raw_materialization_replay_backlog`, storage/repair.py:4583) that joins
raw_sessions + raw_session_memberships.decision + raw_authority_blockers

title: Selective index deferral for bulk index rebuild (scoped follow-up to polylogue-623q)
description: polylogue-623q found the single SQLite writer (apply_s) dominates full-corpus rebuild wall-clock (54-77%). The most obvious lever -- build all secondary B-tree indexes AFTER the bulk insert instead of maintaining them during -- was measured via a real 1.2GB/1298-raw subset benchmark (drop all 72 non-unique CREATE INDEX statements before backfill_historical_revision_evidence, recreate after) and REJECTED: apply_s got WORSE (187.6s -> 317.7s incl. rebuild, +69%). Root cause: write_parsed_session_to_archive's per-session 'full replace' path (_clear_session_projection_rows + DELETE FROM messages WHERE session_id=?) issues point-DELETEs against session_id on ~14 tables (messages, blocks, action_pairs, session_events, session_links, attachment_refs, paste_spans, session_provider_usage_events, session_agent_policies, session_working_dirs, session_repos, session_commits, session_model_usage, session_refs) for EVERY replayed session, even on a bulk-build-from-empty generation where every DELETE matches zero rows. Without indexes, each of those becomes an O(table_size) full scan instead of an O(log n) point lookup -- clear_projection_rows alone went 8.3s -> 57.9s (7x) in the sample. A SELECTIVE variant is the real follow-up: keep the session_id/src_session_id-scoped indexes each full-replace DELETE needs (idx_messages_session_position, idx_blocks_session_position, and equivalents on the other ~12 tables -- audit which currently HAVE a session-scoped index at all), defer only the remaining query-serving indexes (role/type/tool/content-hash/profile/latency/rollup indexes -- roughly 50-60 of the 72) that full_replace never touches. Requires: (1) auditing all 72 non-unique CREATE INDEX statements in storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py against the ~14-table DELETE cascade in _clear_session_projection_rows + the direct 'DELETE FROM messages'/'DELETE FROM blocks' calls to classify safe-to-defer vs must-keep, (2) splitting INDEX_DDL into an eager (tables + must-keep indexes) and deferred (query-serving indexes) script, (3) threading a defer flag through IndexGenerationStore.create()/create_transaction() -> initialize_archive_database(..., defer_secondary_indexes=True) for the offline-rebuild caller only, (4) a new terminal stage in maintenance/rebuild_index.py that creates the deferred indexes once, before _repopulate_bulk_build_derived_state (which itself reads blocks/messages and likely benefits from indexes existing already). Re-measure on the same subset methodology (build_subset.py-style real corpus copy) before shipping -- do not ship on theory.
close_reason:
Re-measured on top of #3460 (skip no-op full-replace delete cascade for
new sessions, merged 2026-07-31) -- the change this bead's description
predicted would need auditing before any deferral is safe. Result: even
the SIMPLE blanket variant (defer all 72 non-unique CREATE INDEX
statements, recreate after) no longer catastrophically regresses, but it
also does not meaningfully help. Closing rather than scoping the
selective variant: since blanket deferral is already a wash, a narrower
selective deferral (the 50-60 subset this bead scoped) would move the
needle even less.

Methodology: same two-point regression harness #3460 itself used
(tests/infra/rebuild_cost_model.py measure_stratum, two representative
strata -- claude-code-session/d9 is 38% of the live population by raw
count), run from a worktree at fresh origin/master with #3460 merged,
resolution-verified (polylogue.storage.sqlite.archive_tiers.write.__file__
checked against the worktree before every measurement -- guards the
shared-venv .pth hazard that invalidated earlier lanes' numbers tonight).
Deferred variant monkeypatches archive_tiers.ARCHIVE_DDL_BY_TIER[INDEX] to
strip the 72 non-unique CREATE INDEX statements before the pass, then
recreates them against the built index.db afterward.

First pass (2-point n1=15/n2=60 regression, single sample each point) hit
severe host-contention noise -- while an unrelated background baseline
run was mid-flight, deferred appeared 2.4x WORSE (marginal 0.1246 vs
0.0481 s/raw). That number does not replicate: repeated single-pass
measurements (3x each at n=60 and n=15, taken after the contending
process exited) show:

  n=60 wall_s:  eager  median 6.22s   deferred median 5.26s
  n=15 wall_s:  eager  median 3.98s   deferred median 3.06s
  n=60 cpu_s:   eager  median 2.77s   deferred median 2.75s  (~equal)
  n=15 cpu_s:   eager  median 1.50s   deferred median 1.43s

Marginal cost from stable medians: eager 0.0498 s/raw, deferred 0.0489
s/raw (wall) -- a ~2% difference, inside measurement noise. CPU-time
marginal cost (immune to other processes stealing cycles on this shared,
~10-concurrent-agent-worktree host) is actually very slightly HIGHER
deferred (0.0293 vs 0.0281 s/raw, +4%): index-free inserts cost about the
same CPU either way, and the recreate-after step (measured directly:
0.008-0.016s at n=15/60, negligible at this scale) doesn't offset because
there's nothing large to offset -- B-tree maintenance during INSERT was
never the dominant cost here, unlike the DELETE-cascade full-scan
pathology #3460 fixed. Deferred's lower "fixed_s" intercept (~2.3s vs
~3.2s per stratum sample) is fresh-archive bootstrap DDL time (skipping
72 CREATE INDEX at connect), not a per-raw saving -- in a real rebuild
this fixed cost is paid ONCE for the whole run, not once per stratum, so
it is a low-single-digit-second saving against a 4h20m rebuild, not a
lever.

Net: even blanket-deferral's best-case reading (~2% wall-clock win on the
dominant stratum) projects to low tens-of-seconds off a 4h20m rebuild.
Not an order-of-magnitude lever, not even a double-digit-percent one.
Root cause: #3460 already removed the one place index absence helped
(zero-match point-DELETEs going O(n) without an index); every other
per-session write during bulk-build (messages/blocks/action_pairs
inserts, field_path_union, graph_resolve) is genuinely INSERT-bound, and
_repopulate_bulk_build_derived_state's post-pass FTS/trigram/action_pairs
bulk repopulation reads back through blocks/messages at full-table scale
regardless of when the secondary indexes get built, so deferring past it
does not save that pass either -- confirmed by instrumenting its
bulk_build_substages timings directly (fts/command_trigram/action_pairs/
delegation_facts sub-costs were within noise of each other eager vs
deferred, ~0.1s each on the 60-raw sample).

Scripts used (not committed, scratch tooling):
/realm/tmp/perf-rebuild-index/measure_defer.py,
measure_defer_breakdown.py.

The genuinely unexplored remaining lever is polylogue-fpid
(prepare_session_rows/PreparedSessionRows off the writer thread) --
already tracked, not opened by this close.

title: tool-result and workflow-journal artifacts acquired as independent sessions instead of sidecars
design:
Found 2026-07-29 while diagnosing the 874 zero-message sessions.

Of those 874, roughly 573 are not conversations at all: `tool-results/*.json`
and `subagents/workflows/*/journal.jsonl` artifacts that were acquired as
INDEPENDENT `claude-code-session` rows in raw_sessions, rather than joined to
their owning session as sidecars. A further ~214 are pure
`file-history-snapshot` sidecar-shaped files, which Claude Code writes under
the session-uuid `.jsonl` naming pattern with zero chat turns.

They correctly parse to zero messages -- they contain no user/assistant
records and never did. So this is NOT a parse defect. It is an ACQUISITION
scope defect: these files should have been discovered as sidecars belonging to
a session, not enumerated as sessions in their own right.

`polylogue/sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py` (landed on the current
feature branch) is the mechanism that joins tool-result sidecars to their
owning session by tool id. The contaminated rows appear to predate it.

TWO QUESTIONS, both needing evidence before any action:

1. Does the CURRENT discovery path still enumerate these as independent raw
   rows? If tool_result_sidecars.py's join happens after a discovery step that
   already minted a raw_sessions row, new contamination keeps accruing. Verify
   against a scratch acquisition run rather than by reading.

2. Do the ~787 existing contaminated rows warrant cleanup? They are in
   source.db, the DURABLE tier. Removing them is a destructive durable change
   and requires a copy-forward design plus explicit operator consent per this
   repo's schema regime. Note they are NOT harmful today beyond inflating the
   session count -- and note the precedent: the 2026-07-22 hook-inflation
   postmortem chose to RETAIN genuinely-empty sessions rather than delete
   them, and polylogue-ne6k just hardened repair_empty_sessions specifically
   so a blanket cleanup cannot delete acquired rows.

Do NOT let a "cleanup" of these become the thing that deletes real evidence.
If they are to be reclassified rather than deleted, that is likely the better
answer: they ARE real acquired artifacts, just mislabelled as sessions.

Not rebuild-blocking: the imminent rebuild reparses them to zero, which is
correct, and changes nothing about their acquisition.
acceptance_criteria:
Scope narrowed per 2026-07-31 notes: tool-results/*.json (live, current-build) + file-history-snapshot families; workflow-journal family closes via polylogue-lzh8 reparse.
1. A scratch acquisition run (not code reading) proves the CURRENT discovery path no longer mints raw_sessions rows for tool-results/*.json; red-first fixture if a gap is found.
2. file-history-snapshot files classify as sidecar artifacts, not sessions, on fresh acquisition.
3. The existing contaminated rows are RECLASSIFIED (raw_artifacts, receipts), never deleted — durable-tier evidence retention per the hook-inflation precedent; count and disposition recorded here.
4. Workflow-journal family confirmed closed after lzh8's reparse (live query shows 0 such sessions post-reindex).
5. Verify: devtools test -k artifact_taxonomy or -k sidecar; read-only live census before/after.

title: content hash skips NFC normalization for tool_input and session-event payload
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by the hashing/resumability sweep. Latent, not active.

CLAUDE.md states the content hash is computed over an NFC-normalized payload.
That holds for every top-level text field -- but NOT for two nested ones:

  polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:98   _content_block_payload passes block.tool_input
                                 straight to hash_payload(dict(...))
  polylogue/pipeline/ids.py:182  _session_hash_components does the same for
                                 event.payload

Everything else routes through _normalize_for_hash (NFC). hash_payload's own
docstring says so explicitly: "String values within the payload are NOT
NFC-normalized here."

PROVEN: two tool_input dicts differing only in NFC vs NFD form of the same
visual string hash differently. The same comparison on message.text returns
equal, so the inconsistency is real and confined to these two nested paths.

CONSEQUENCE IF IT FIRES: two visually identical tool_use blocks or session
events would mis-hash into two permanent logical identities -- the archive
would carry both forever and never dedupe them. Plausible sources are
macOS-originated exports (HFS+ historically stored NFD) and browser-capture
DOM extraction.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED: 20,000 real tool_use.tool_input rows sampled from the
live index read-only -- ZERO contain non-NFC string content. So this is a
landmine, not current corruption, and it does not threaten the imminent
rebuild.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THAT PASS: normalizing these would change the content
hash of any future NFD-containing session. Hash invalidation is an operator
decision, not a sweep's -- the lane was explicitly instructed to stop and
report rather than touch the hash surface, and did.

WHAT THE FIX NEEDS: route tool_input and event.payload through the same NFC
normalization as every sibling field, and decide whether existing hashes are
grandfathered (they are unaffected today, since zero rows are non-NFC) or
whether a rehash pass is wanted. Given the measured zero blast radius,
grandfathering looks correct and free -- but that is the operator's call.

ALSO ESTABLISHED IN THE SAME PASS (record so nobody re-derives it):
  - hash_payload deliberately uses stdlib json, NOT the core.json facade, so
    it is backend-independent by construction. The msgspec-vs-orjson
    cross-interpreter hash-split concern is unfounded.
  - Four-way hash stability verified identical: same process, cross-process,
    free-threaded, and GIL -- one hash in all four cases.
  - orjson vs msgspec vs stdlib decode compared over 1,290 real JSON documents
    from the live archive: 0 mismatches, 0 decode failures.
  - Attachment sort key is a total order over (message_id, id, name); messages
    and session_events keep parse order via lists, never sets, so there is no
    order instability anywhere in the hash input.
close_reason: Already fixed prior to this session (index-v46, commit 5e23e6abf): _normalize_nested_for_hash wired into tool_input + event-payload hash paths. Verified via PR #3604 investigation; dedicated test tests/unit/pipeline/test_hash_nested_nfc.py already passing.

title: Thread stop_reason/tool_result_outcome_unknown_reason through the query-path row types
description:
Follow-up from the same feature-gap sweep that implemented Message.stop_reason
and blocks[].tool_result_outcome_unknown_reason on the FULL-hydration path
(storage/hydrators.py::message_from_record, used by
RepositoryArchiveSessionMixin.get() i.e. the MCP/CLI/API "get one session"
route) -- see the sweep's PR/commit on
feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates.

That fix does NOT reach the query/find path. Both
polylogue/archive/query/archive_execution.py::_message_to_domain and
polylogue/api/archive.py::_archive_message_to_domain build Message.blocks
from ArchiveMessageRow/ArchiveBlockRow (polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/
write.py), and those two dataclasses never carried stop_reason (message-level)
or tool_result_outcome_unknown_reason (block-level) in the first place --
unlike MessageRecord/BlockRecord, which already do. This is why the fix could
not be extended to the query path from insights/cli/mcp/surfaces alone: the
row types themselves are missing the fields, and storage/sqlite/** is a
different lane's write scope.

Needed (schema-free, no version bump -- columns already exist since v46):
1. Add `stop_reason: str | None = None` to ArchiveMessageRow.
2. Add `tool_result_outcome_unknown_reason: str | None = None` to
   ArchiveBlockRow.
3. Thread both through the two SELECT/row-construction sites that populate
   these dataclasses (grep ArchiveMessageRow/ArchiveBlockRow construction in
   storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py and write.py).
4. Once populated, add the same two keys to the dict literals at
   archive/query/archive_execution.py:227-228 and api/archive.py:1795-796
   (mirroring the pattern already applied to storage/hydrators.py in this
   sweep) -- these are one-line additions once the row types carry the data.

Without this, `polylogue find ...` results and the Python API's query surface
still cannot answer "why is this tool result's outcome unknown" or "did this
turn get truncated/refused" -- only the single-session `get`/`read` route can.
Related: polylogue-cuxz.8 (stop_reason persistence + deleting redundant
terminal_state guess columns) is the bigger program this feeds.

title: Wire file_edits/session_refs/session_agent_policies readers into a public surface
description:
Found during the feature-gap sweep (polylogue-z9gh companion investigation, 2026-07-29,
branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates @ bdeb6d1d2).

polylogue/storage/repository/archive/sessions.py:114-156 (RepositoryArchiveSessionMixin)
already exposes:
  get_agent_policies(session_id) / get_agent_policies_batch(session_ids)
  get_file_edits(session_id) / get_file_edits_batch(session_ids)
  get_session_refs(session_id) / get_session_refs_batch(session_ids)

backed by real async query modules (storage/sqlite/queries/file_edits.py,
session_refs.py, session_agent_policies.py) over dedicated tables that are
already populated by the writer (file_edits: structured patches/pre-state per
tool-call, polylogue-cgfy; session_refs: tracker-agnostic PR/issue refs incl.
20,702 Claude Code pr-link occurrences; session_agent_policies: Codex
sandbox/approval/network policy facts). None of the three has a CLI verb or
MCP operation -- data lands durably and is readable from Python, but an agent
or operator cannot ask any of:
  - "what did I change in this file across every session" (file_edits)
  - "which sessions reference PR #N / issue #N" (session_refs)
  - "what sandbox/approval policy governed this session" (agent_policies)

This is read-path only (bucket 2 in the sweep's scheme): the tables, writer,
and repository methods already exist on schema v46/v15 -- no schema bump
needed. Implementation shape:
  - CLI: extend cli/read_views/ (mirroring the just-landed events.py read view)
    with file-edits/session-refs/agent-policies views under `read --view`, or
    fold session_refs+agent_policies into the existing `read --view events`
    output family since they are per-session evidence lists like session_events.
  - MCP: add fields to the existing session `get` operation payload (or a
    projection flag) rather than a new tool -- 10-dispatcher constraint,
    tool contract update required either way.
  - insights: file_edits in particular wants a query entrypoint
    ("show me file edits for path X across sessions") which may fit the
    existing query-grammar `with <units>` projection better than a read view --
    evaluate both before committing to one shape.

Note polylogue-cuxz.11 covers a related but DIFFERENT concern for
session_agent_policies (402,869 rows encoding 3,053 facts -- storage-side
dedup), not exposure; this bead is purely about the missing reader-to-surface
wiring for all three tables.
close_reason: Verified SATISFIED (storage triage 2026-07-31): file_edits/session_agent_policies/session_refs now reachable from CLI/MCP/API. Landed via commit 4a17f74d6 (#3442, merged 2026-07-31) -- same underlying fix/PR as sibling bead polylogue-nua7, which its own PR body names explicitly. api/archive.py:5458/5495, MCP mcp/server_cutover.py:913-924, CLI cli/read_view_registry.py:59-60 + read_view_handlers.py:109-118.

title: Decide whether to store Claude Code structuredPatch diff content, not just counts
description:
## Context

polylogue-sweep 2026-07-29 (silent-data-loss audit ahead of a full index
rebuild) measured `_tool_execution_result_payload` in
polylogue/sources/parsers/claude/code_parser.py (around line 690).
