Claude Code's `toolUseResult.structuredPatch` carries the actual applied
diff hunks (old/new line content) for every Edit/Write/NotebookEdit tool
call. The parser currently discards the hunk content entirely and stores
only two derived counts in the `claude_tool_execution_result` session_events
payload:

    payload["structured_patch_hunk_count"] = len(hunks)
    payload["structured_patch_lines_changed"] = sum(...)

## Measurement (~/.claude/projects, ~4.17M JSONL records scanned, 2026-07-29)

- 95,931 records carry a non-empty `structuredPatch`.
- Total line-entries across all hunks: 2,971,589 (max 3,851 in one record).
- Total JSON-serialized bytes of the discarded patch content: ~146.6 MB.

This is a deliberate, documented decision from the same-day "parser-diff
triage" comment in code_parser.py (`_tool_execution_result_payload`
docstring), which frames the exclusion as being about *unbounded free-text
output* (stdout/stderr/output/fullOutput). structuredPatch is not that: it's
a bounded, structured diff -- the actual edit content -- not command output.
It is recoverable from raw JSONL bytes (source.db raw tier) on any future
reparse, so this is not unrecoverable loss, but it means the *materialized,
queryable* evidence (session_events / any downstream insight built on it)
never carries the actual diff, only its size.

## Decision needed

Should `claude_tool_execution_result` (or a new event type) store the
structuredPatch hunks themselves (or a bounded-but-generous slice of them),
analogous to how `extract_file_changes`/`FileChangeSummary` in
polylogue/pipeline/semantic_capture.py already models old/new content, but
unlike that module is actually wired into materialization?

If yes: this is additive-derived only (index.db session_events payload is
JSON, no CHECK constraint on shape) -- no INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bump needed,
just a parser change + a SEMANTIC_REPARSE-classified rebuild to backfill
existing sessions.

If no (operator judgement: diff content is redundant with the file on disk /
git history, and 146MB across the corpus is a real storage/perf cost): leave
as-is, but strike the "deliberately excluded" docstring language that groups
structuredPatch together with free-text stdout, since the size/recoverability
argument is different for each.

## Non-goal

Not proposing to touch INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION or SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION.
close_reason:
Already solved by the v46 file_edits table, which landed in parallel and the sweeping lane could not see.

The finding was accurate about the path it examined: _tool_execution_result_payload (code_parser.py:690-697) keeps only structured_patch_hunk_count and structured_patch_lines_changed in the claude_tool_execution_result session_event -- the diff content itself is not in that payload. Measured: 95,931 records, 2,971,589 line-entries, ~146.6 MB.

But that content now has a real destination. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION 46 added the file_edits table (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py), keyed on tool_use_block_id, carrying structured_patch_json (verbatim JSON, not decomposed), original_file, old_string, new_string, replace_all, user_modified. ParsedFileEdit (sources/parsers/base_models.py:62-71) is the writer contract, and _file_edit_from_tool_result (code_parser.py:701) reads structuredPatch/originalFile/oldString/newString off the wire and attaches it to the TOOL_RESULT block; the writer resolves the paired tool_use via tool_id.

So the two paths are complementary, not competing: the session_event keeps cheap queryable counts, file_edits holds the full patch. Measured coverage of the file_edit path is 7,335 of 44,125 tool_result blocks in the sampled corpus, and it is populated by the imminent rebuild.

No operator decision needed. What remains is a verification task, not a design one: after the rebuild, confirm file_edits row count and that structured_patch_json is non-null where the wire carried a patch. Recorded on the rebuild's post-checks rather than kept open here.

title: generate_schema_from_samples has no privacy_config plumbed through it
description: registry.promote_cluster's samples-based candidate generator (polylogue/schemas/generation/schema_builder.py:generate_schema_from_samples) never receives a PrivacyConfig, unlike the full 'generate' pipeline's _generate_cluster_schema which explicitly redacts via _build_redaction_report. This let a low-cardinality UUID-shaped field (claude-ai raw_provider_payload.current_leaf_message_uuid) get its literal per-record UUID values recorded verbatim under x-polylogue-values during a 2026-07-29 promotion; caught by devtools.schema_audit's privacy_guards check (which promotion_audit does not duplicate), fixed by manually stripping the one annotation. Any future promotion via promote_cluster (per-cluster or full-corpus-single) could reintroduce the same class of leak on a different field. Fix: thread privacy_config through generate_schema_from_samples (or route promote_cluster's samples path through _generate_cluster_schema instead), and/or add promotion_audit coverage for the same UUID/hex/high-entropy enum-value check schema_audit already runs, so promotion itself cannot regress this without a visible blocker.
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03; premise verified live — generate_schema_from_samples (schemas/generation/schema_builder.py:123) still takes no privacy/redaction parameter): two-layer fix, both cheap:
1. PLUMB: add privacy_config to generate_schema_from_samples and apply the same _build_redaction_report redaction the full pipeline's _generate_cluster_schema uses (or route promote_cluster's samples path through _generate_cluster_schema outright — prefer whichever avoids a second redaction implementation; one redactor, two callers).
2. GATE: add promotion_audit coverage for the UUID/hex/high-entropy enum-value check that devtools schema_audit already runs (the check that caught the 2026-07-29 current_leaf_message_uuid leak), so a promotion carrying verbatim values is a visible blocker regardless of which generator produced it.
Red-first: a fixture sample containing UUID-shaped low-cardinality values must produce a redacted candidate (test through promote_cluster's real path) and a promotion_audit failure when redaction is bypassed. Gates tnqqt (public-repo schema commit) — land before the inference run.
acceptance_criteria:
1. promote_cluster's samples path applies the same redaction as the full pipeline (one redactor implementation, both callers) — UUID-shaped low-cardinality fixture values never reach x-polylogue-values.
2. promotion_audit gains the schema_audit privacy_guards check; a promotion carrying verbatim values is a visible blocker.
3. Red-first tests for both layers through the real promote path.
4. Lands before tnqqt's inference run. Verify: devtools test -k promotion -k privacy or file-scoped selection.

title: collapse_dynamic_keys wipe-everything pattern may also affect _merge_observed_structure_pair
description:
polylogue-* fixed collapse_dynamic_keys (polylogue/schemas/generation/dynamic_keys.py:243)
so it only folds already-static properties into additionalProperties when the per-key
is_dynamic_key pass produced no dynamic entries at all -- previously it wiped every
static key whenever should_collapse_observed_keys(key_names) fired for the enclosing
object, even when individually-safe static keys coexisted with a content-bearing or
identifier-ish key that already triggered collapse on its own.

_merge_observed_structure_pair in the same file (around line 109-117) has the identical
wipe-everything shape:

    if properties and (already_high_cardinality or should_collapse_observed_keys(properties.keys())):
        additional = merge_observed_structure_schemas([additional, *map(json_document, properties.values())])
        properties = {}
        required = []

This path runs during observed-structure merging (schema promotion), not the
collapse_dynamic_keys path exercised by tests/unit/core/test_schema_laws.py, so it
wasn't caught by the same failing tests and wasn't touched in this fix (scope
discipline -- no test currently pins this path's behavior). Worth an explicit property
test analogous to test_collapse_dynamic_keys_preserves_static_fields_and_rehomes_
dynamic_maps, then the same "only wipe when nothing already collapsed" fix if it
reproduces the same defect.

title: Wire Codex thread-title/spawn-edge evidence into title resolution and topology
description:
polylogue-0jf4 built and wired acquisition for Codex state_5.sqlite: threads.title and
thread_spawn_edges now reach the archive as typed raw_hook_events evidence
(event_type codex_thread_title / codex_thread_spawn_edge), keyed to the EXISTING
codex-session row by thread_id via ArchiveStore.write_hook_event -- never a session
of their own (polylogue-31r1 precedent). Verified against the real live ~/.codex
install: 3,055 codex_thread_title rows + 1,030 codex_thread_spawn_edge rows acquired,
index.db sessions rows == 0 (no session minted by the state-db ingest).

Remaining, deliberately out of that lane's scope (sources/live/batch.py,
sources/parsers/codex_state.py):

1. Title resolution (polylogue-ih67's ladder, sources/assembly_codex.py): the
   acquired codex_thread_title hook events are NOT yet consulted by the title
   ladder. All Codex sessions remain UUID-titled in the visible session record
   until a consumer reads ArchiveStore.hook_event_summary_for_session (or a
   dedicated read helper) for the session's own thread_id and folds
   payload["title"] into the ladder's candidate list. codex_state.py's own
   docstring and origin_specs.py deliberately did not modify assembly_codex.py
   to avoid colliding with the still-in-flight ih67 ladder work.

2. Topology (thread_spawn_edges): sources/live/topology or the insights layer
   that currently derives spawn/subagent relationships from transcript
   inference (polylogue-1vpm, polylogue-4ts) should additionally read the
   acquired codex_thread_spawn_edge hook events and prefer them over inferred
   edges where both exist, reporting how many inferred edges get replaced by
   authoritative ones.

Both consumers can read the acquired evidence via the existing, already-wired
ArchiveStore.hook_event_summary_for_session read path (or a narrower
Codex-specific read helper) -- no further acquisition or schema work is needed,
this is purely a consumption-side wiring task.
design:
DESIGN (2026-08-03; AC already set — this is the wiring how; premise verified live: assembly_codex.py still has no hook-event consultation): two consumption-side wirings reading the already-acquired evidence (3,055 codex_thread_title + 1,030 codex_thread_spawn_edge raw_hook_events, keyed to sessions by thread_id):
1. TITLE LADDER (sources/assembly_codex.py): during assembly, read the session's thread_id's codex_thread_title hook events (ArchiveStore.hook_event_summary_for_session or a narrow read helper — prefer a dedicated read that returns just the newest title payload to avoid loading full summaries in the assembly hot path) and fold payload["title"] into the ladder's candidate list ABOVE the UUID fallback, below any operator-set title. COORDINATION: ih67 (title ladder rework) is in_progress — check its current ladder shape first and land as a candidate-source addition compatible with it, not a parallel ladder edit.
2. TOPOLOGY (where 1vpm/4ts inferred edges are read): additionally read codex_thread_spawn_edge events; where an authoritative edge and an inferred edge cover the same (parent, child), prefer authoritative and count the replacement (AC 2's report). New edges only found authoritatively are added with method marking them evidence-backed — which feeds 4ts.10's status/method population.
This is index-derived enrichment — assembly output changes for codex sessions: declare the delta (SEMANTIC_REPARSE or targeted-reprocess per lifecycle.py's vocabulary) so existing UUID-titled sessions actually refresh.
acceptance_criteria: 1. sources/assembly_codex.py's title resolution ladder consults the acquired codex_thread_title hook event for a session's thread_id and prefers a non-empty curated title over the UUID fallback. 2. The topology/spawn-edge consumer (wherever polylogue-1vpm/4ts's inferred edges are read) additionally reads codex_thread_spawn_edge hook events and reports how many previously-inferred edges are now backed by authoritative Codex evidence. 3. Report a real before/after UUID-title census for Origin.CODEX_SESSION sessions against a live archive.
close_reason: Title ladder and topology reconciliation against acquired codex_thread_title/codex_thread_spawn_edge hook events were already implemented (PR #3649). This session closed the residual AC#3 gap: a real before/after UUID-title coverage census (86.5% of unresolved sessions would resolve via the hook-event lane alone). PR #3654, merged.

title: three write-only tables (otlp_telemetry, query_runs, session_commits) and 7 unconsumed config properties
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by codebase audit (same detection that found the orphaned
`session_agent_policies` reader earlier this session -- that one is now fixed,
these three are not).

Tables written by production code with NO production reader anywhere -- no
SELECT/FROM/JOIN outside tests:

  otlp_telemetry     writer polylogue/daemon/otlp_receiver.py:140
                     prod reads 0 | test reads 2
                     Receives and durably stores OTLP spans/metrics/logs.
                     Nothing ever queries them back out.

  query_runs         writer polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/ops_write.py:503
                     prod reads 0 | test reads 4
                     Records every query execution. No surface reads it, so
                     the query-history it accumulates is unreachable -- note
                     `slow_query_notice_seconds` is also an unconsumed config
                     property (see below), suggesting a query-observability
                     feature that was half-built.

  session_commits    writer polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:3839
                     prod reads 0 | test reads 1
                     Git commit attribution per session. Adjacent tables
                     (repos, session_repos) ARE read; this one is not.

Each needs a disposition, not a default: wire a reader (the evidence is being
collected and is simply unreachable -- this was the right answer for
session_agent_policies), or delete the table and its writer (nothing needs the
evidence, and writing it costs rebuild time and disk on every ingest).

`otlp_telemetry` and `query_runs` are in the disposable ops tier, so deleting
them is cheap. `session_commits` is in the rebuildable index tier and its
sibling tables are live, so it most likely wants a reader.

ALSO: 7 config properties with zero production consumers
(polylogue/config.py) -- each is either an unwired feature or dead:
    active_index_db            prod=0 test=0
    hook_sidecar_dir           prod=0 test=0
    ingest_parse_workers       prod=0 test=0   <- notable: parse worker count,
                                 relevant to the imminent rebuild; verify the
                                 rebuild is not silently ignoring it
    log_level                  prod=0 test=0
    slow_query_notice_seconds  prod=0 test=0   <- pairs with query_runs above
    effective_path             prod=0 test=2
    layer_paths                prod=0 test=2

`ingest_parse_workers` is the one to check FIRST and before the rebuild: if the
parse-worker count is configurable but unread, the rebuild may not be honoring
it. (Detection is name-based; confirm each against source before acting --
a property could be reached via getattr or config-inventory reflection.)
close_reason: Merged via PR #3694: dropped write-only query_runs table (ops.db) + record_query_run writer + dead active_index_db config alias. Re-verified against present source before deleting: otlp_telemetry already removed by #3665, session_commits gained a real reader via cijx.3 (kept), 5 of the 7 named config properties were false positives on closer read (real consumers exist), 2 already removed by #3455. devtools test 87+332+28 passed across touched modules; devtools verify --quick exit 0. Found otlp_spans (source.db, durable tier) now fully dead (zero writer since #3665, zero reader) -- filed as follow-up polylogue-<id> since durable-tier table drops need the copy-forward/consent gate, not done here.

title: three parallel render-destination vocabularies; RenderFormat and alias map are inert
design:
Found 2026-07-29 by codebase audit. THREE parallel vocabularies describe the
same concept (where rendered output goes), and none is authoritative:

 1. polylogue/surfaces/projection_spec.py:58  RenderDestination enum
       TERMINAL, STDOUT, BROWSER, CLIPBOARD, FILE     (typed, validated)
 2. polylogue/cli/query_verbs.py:215          _READ_DESTINATIONS
       ("terminal","stdout","browser","clipboard","file")  (raw strings,
       duplicated literally; this is what click.Choice validates against)
 3. polylogue/cli/query_contracts.py:23       QueryDeliveryName
       Literal["stdout","browser","clipboard"]  (only 3 of the 5)

The typed enum exists but the actual dispatch sites compare raw strings
(read_views/base.py:158, read_views/standard.py:97) and the invocation field
is plain `destination: str` (read_views/base.py:99). So the enum validates
nothing on the path that matters. polylogue-bvnz (browser silently degrading
to terminal) is a direct consequence: vocabulary 2 accepts a value that
vocabulary 3 implements and the dispatch sites do not handle.

Same shape, same file, for timestamp policy:
    RenderTimestampPolicy enum (projection_spec.py:75)
    _READ_TIMESTAMP_POLICIES = ("renderer-default","include-available","omit")
        (query_verbs.py:218 -- the same three values re-spelled as strings)

INERT KNOBS in the same module:
  - RenderFormat (projection_spec.py:44) declares 8 members
    (MARKDOWN/JSON/NDJSON/HTML/OBSIDIAN/ORG/YAML/CSV). Nothing anywhere
    dispatches on RenderFormat -- zero `RenderFormat.` references outside the
    defining module. RenderSpec.format is a typed field nobody branches on.
  - RENDER_FORMAT_ALIASES (projection_spec.py:69) maps "text"/"plain" ->
    PLAINTEXT and has ZERO consumers in production or tests. The aliases it
    promises are not applied anywhere.
  - SelectionSpec (projection_spec.py:83) has zero references in production
    or tests outside its own module.

DO: pick ONE vocabulary -- the enum -- and make click.Choice derive from it
rather than re-spelling its members as a string tuple, so adding a member
cannot again produce an accepted-but-unhandled value. Type the invocation
field as the enum. Then either wire RenderFormat dispatch or delete the
members that no renderer implements; same for the alias map and SelectionSpec.
Per the standing directive: where one option dominates, delete the
alternatives rather than keeping them as inert configuration.

title: Schema promotion (c53ad94e0) dropped x-polylogue-semantic-role annotations for codex/claude-code
description:
Problem: the 2026-07-29 structural-merge promotion (c53ad94e0, "fix(schemas):
make structural merge monotonic and promote every provider") regenerated the
codex and claude-code baseline provider schemas
(polylogue/schemas/providers/{codex,claude-code}/versions/v1/elements/session_record_stream.schema.json.gz)
from scratch and did not carry forward the x-polylogue-semantic-role
annotation overlay (message_role/session_title/message_body/etc).

Evidence:
- Diffing the pre-promotion schema snapshot (master @ b64a074e5) against the
  current branch's schema for the same file shows the annotation set went
  from 6 entries (codex) / 7 entries (claude-code) including
  "/properties/payload/properties/role" (codex, message_role) and
  "/properties/type" (claude-code, message_role) down to zero.
- SyntheticCorpus.generate_batch_for_spec("codex"/"claude-code", seed=42) now
  fills the role-discriminator field with an opaque `synthetic-<n>`
  placeholder instead of a real user/assistant value, so every parsed
  message normalizes to Role.UNKNOWN.
- This is a synthetic-corpus generation defect, not a parser defect: real
  codex/claude-code exports always carry real role values, so production
  parsing is unaffected.
- Already caught independently by tests/unit/core/test_synthetic_semantic_wiring.py
  (TestBaselineSchemaAnnotations::test_schema_has_expected_semantic_roles[codex],
  [claude-code], and the idempotent-injection tests for
  claude-ai/codex/claude-code) and tests/unit/core/test_synthetic_semantics.py
  (test_generation_plants_independent_wire_facts_before_ingest) -- 6 failures,
  all pre-existing on this branch, unrelated to any parser change today.
- Also broke tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_props.py
  (test_provider_parser_contract[codex/claude-code],
  TestMessageOrderConsistency::test_messages_have_consistent_roles[codex/claude-code])
  -- worked around at the test-strategy layer in
  tests/infra/strategies/providers.py (repair_role_discriminators) and
  tests/conftest.py (synthetic_source fixture) since polylogue/schemas/** is
  out of scope for that fix.

Fix: run `devtools inject-semantic-annotations` (devtools/inject_semantic_annotations.py,
already exists as the sanctioned one-shot/re-annotation tool) against the
promoted codex/claude-code (and audit claude-ai too, since its idempotency
test also fails) schemas, verify test_synthetic_semantic_wiring.py goes
green, and consider removing the test-layer workaround in
tests/infra/strategies/providers.py / tests/conftest.py once the schema
carries real annotations again.
close_reason: Verified SATISFIED (storage triage 2026-07-31): the schema-annotation regression and its own two follow-up fixes were introduced and repaired within one unmerged branch before landing as squash-commit 5e23e6abf (PR #3390, index v46 wire-evidence batch, merged 2026-07-29) -- the regression never reached master in an unfixed state. Decoded live gzipped schemas: x-polylogue-semantic-role present (6 codex / 9 claude-code annotations).

title: Wire periodic (not just startup) blob-publication reservation reconciliation
description: Blob-store audit (bytes-per-object, orphan/dedup checks) found the blob-GC store itself correctly deduplicated and orphan-free except 2 stuck blob_publication_reservations rows (42.5MB, reserved 2026-07-12/13) that are blob_present=True, referenced=False -- the 'unresolved' classification that reconcile_blob_publication_reservations_under_exclusion() never auto-clears (by design; only abandon_blob_publication_receipts with --yes can remove it). The real gap: _reconcile_blob_publications() (polylogue/daemon/cli.py:1009) runs exactly ONCE at daemon startup, never periodically -- unlike blob-gc and embedding-orphan-reconcile, which both have periodic_*_check loops. A long-running daemon (weeks of uptime, the common case) means any reservation that becomes safely clearable (referenced or blob-missing) after startup sits until the next restart. Fix: add a periodic_blob_publication_reconcile_check loop (mirror polylogue/daemon/blob_gc_periodic.py's shape, ~900s interval) that calls reconcile_blob_publication_reservations_under_exclusion() on a schedule; it only ever clears rows already proven safe (referenced or blob missing), never touches 'unresolved' rows, so this is a low-risk periodic-maintenance addition, not a policy change.

title: Wire Claude Code tool-results sidecar join into dispatch.py acquisition path
description:
polylogue-rujy built the join+attach logic (polylogue/sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py:join_tool_result_sidecars, polylogue/sources/parsers/claude/code_parser.py:apply_tool_result_sidecars) and wired parse_code/parse_code_stream to accept an optional tool_result_sidecars kwarg -- passing nothing preserves current behavior exactly (tested).

Remaining wiring, out of that lane's write scope (polylogue/sources/dispatch.py is not under sources/live/** or sources/parsers/claude/**):

1. polylogue/sources/dispatch.py:1061 currently calls `claude.parse_code(payloads, spec.fallback_id)`. Needs to derive the session's tool-results directory from `spec.source_path` (the sibling `<session-stem>/tool-results/` directory -- for subagent JSONL under `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, the sidecar directory is still the SESSION-level `<session>/tool-results/`, not a per-subagent one; verified live), call `join_tool_result_sidecars(payloads, tool_results_dir)`, and pass the result through.
2. Decide whether this should be default-on immediately or gated behind a config/CLI flag until ingest wall-clock is measured against the polylogue-623q envelope (see AC5 on polylogue-rujy) -- this needs polylogue/config.py and/or CLI wiring, both explicitly out of the rujy lane's OWNS list.
3. Streaming path (parse_code_stream, used for multi-GiB Claude Code JSONL) needs the equivalent wiring at whatever call site constructs its Iterable[object] payload.

Measured live: acquiring genuinely-truncated sidecars is worth it (~60-65% of the 1.34GB total is genuinely new content per polylogue-rujy's sampling), so this is a real product win, not speculative -- the remaining work is glue, not design.
close_reason:
Wired on branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates (commit 2237e8a82, worktree-agent-a313d11dfce19c361).

1. dispatch.py wiring: the eager Provider.CLAUDE_CODE branch of _parse_lowered_spec (dispatch.py) now derives the tool-results dir from spec.source_path via a new resolve_tool_results_dir() (sources/live/tool_result_sidecars.py) and passes join_tool_result_sidecars(...) into claude.parse_code(..., tool_result_sidecars=...). source_path was previously dropped by _lower_grouped_payload/_claude_code_grouped_record_specs for CLAUDE_CODE -- threaded through both.
2. Default-on, no flag (measured, not assumed): ran join_tool_result_sidecars against the FULL population of Claude Code sessions with a tool-results/ dir under a real ~/.claude/projects corpus (read-only, scratch measurement script, not committed) -- 525 sessions matched resolve_tool_results_dir. Total added wall time for the join across all 525 dirs: 8.2s (704 MB matched + 708 MB debt bytes read, 9,421 files matched / 3,012 debt). That is ~23% on top of just those 525 sessions' own JSONL read time (35.0s), but those 525 sessions are ~3% of the corpus's ~17K distinct native_ids (polylogue-623q's latest corpus-shape note) -- so the join's share of a full-corpus rebuild is well under 1% of a <60min (3600s) budget. Default-on is correct; a flag nobody flips would be the dark-capability pattern this project avoids.
3. Streaming path: _claude_code_stream_sessions (dispatch.py) can't materialize the raw payload (that's the whole point of streaming). Added ToolResultIndexAccumulator + observe_tool_result_stream (tool_result_sidecars.py) so each session-group's records are teed through an index-builder as they stream past parse_code_stream; the join runs against the resulting index once the group iterator is exhausted, then apply_tool_result_sidecars (imported directly from code_parser, not edited) attaches it. Both parse_payload and parse_stream_payload now reach the same coverage -- confirmed by a dedicated streaming test and a subagent-source-path resolution test (subagent JSONL correctly resolves to the SESSION-level tool-results/ dir, not a per-subagent one).

New tests (tests/unit/sources/test_dispatch_payloads.py): 5 new tests covering batch wiring, streaming wiring, subagent-path resolution, and the source_path-absent no-op -- each verified by mutation (temporarily reverting the wiring) to fail without the change, then reverted.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_dispatch_payloads.py tests/unit/sources/test_dispatch_ordering.py tests/unit/sources/test_tool_result_sidecars.py -> 33 passed. mypy --strict clean on all 3 changed/added files. ruff check/format clean. devtools verify hash-boundary-census -> 0 unregistered/stale after updating the registry entry for the hash_text call site that moved into _join_from_index. devtools render all --check -> no "out of sync" lines (no new module added, so no topology regen needed).

No index schema bump: session_events stays bounded (id/filename/size/content_hash/status only), matching the design constraint.

title: Per-tick raw-materialization candidate rescan: cache attempt reverted, needs persistent backlog iterator (phase c)
description:
Two attempts at killing repair_raw_materialization's per-tick full O(backlog)
_raw_materialization_candidate_ids() rescan have both failed with the same
observable staleness shape, via two different mechanisms:

1. PRAGMA data_version memoization (prior lane): reverted because SQLite's
   file-header change counter does not advance under WAL until checkpoint,
   so writes were invisible to the cache. ~29 tests failed on staleness.

2. Explicit generation-counted cache with write-path invalidation hooks
   (this session, polylogue-m6tp fast-follow): reverted because the actual
   writers of raw_sessions/index-tier sessions/raw_membership_census/
   raw_session_memberships live in polylogue/sources/live/* (live ingest),
   polylogue/storage/repository/**, and
   polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py /
   storage/sqlite/queries/{raw_writes,raw_state}.py -- none reachable from
   the repair.py/raw_authority.py/revision_application.py/daemon/** write
   scope this task was granted. Two tests in tests/unit/storage/test_repair.py
   (test_raw_materialization_replays_governed_bundle_after_index_reset,
   test_raw_materialization_reports_uncensused_append_fragments_as_pending_debt)
   proved this concretely: both legitimately mutate raw_sessions/index.db
   directly between two repair_raw_materialization calls (an index reset,
   and an out-of-band census write), and the cache returned stale results
   in both cases. Full writeup: docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md
   item 5.

Conclusion: this item cannot be closed by caching a query over the current
per-tick-stateless design without either (a) invalidation hooks spanning
several other lanes' write scope, or (b) the persistent in-daemon backlog
iterator polylogue-m6tp's design sketch already names as the real fix
(phase c, bulk-routing). (b) is the only sound path -- it replaces "cache a
derived view" with "maintain the source of truth incrementally", which
sidesteps the invalidation-completeness problem entirely (the iterator is
updated by the same code that performs each write, not by a bystander
guessing which writes matter).

Do not re-attempt with a narrower/smaller cache; the failure is structural
(a correct source-of-truth cache needs write-scope this task doesn't have),
not a tuning problem.

title: Semantic-frontier heads make ~9,300 superseded raws structurally unreleasable
description:
Discovered while implementing the stale-supersession-receipt reissue pass for
polylogue-ktwa. Live-archive query (2026-07-29, /realm/db/polylogue):

Of the ~11,966 distinct (raw_id, session_id, logical_source_key) groups
carrying decision='superseded' receipts, only 2 are genuinely "stale"
(receipt mismatches the current head) after excluding the majority
population. The other ~9,320+ mismatches are all against a
raw_revision_heads row whose accepted_frontier_kind = 'semantic', not
'byte'.

active_raw_retention_authority's eligibility join
(polylogue/storage/raw_retention.py:148, _active_index_raw_authority)
unconditionally requires `head.accepted_frontier_kind = 'byte'` -- it never
admits a raw for release under a semantic head, by design (semantic
frontiers compare parsed-content hashes, not byte offsets, so there is no
byte-level proof of subsumption). This means the entire semantic-headed
population (predominantly antigravity multi-file sessions, e.g.
`antigravity:<id>:plan.md` / `task.md` / `report.md` etc.) is structurally
excluded from ever being released under the current retention design,
regardless of how many times it is reissued a fresh receipt.

The polylogue-ktwa reissue pass (raw_retention.py:
plan_stale_supersession_reissue / reissue_stale_supersession_receipts)
correctly fails closed on semantic heads (matches the retention join's own
requirement) and reports this population as ineligible with reason
"current head frontier_kind is not byte" -- it is not a bug in that pass,
just evidence that a much larger design question remains open: is a
semantic-frontier retention path (an analogous byte-safe proof for
content-hash-based supersession) worth building, or is this population
simply permanent evidence by design?

Needs a product decision before any code: (a) build a semantic-frontier
retention/reissue path with its own safety proof, or (b) explicitly accept
these raws as permanently retained and stop counting them as "debt" in
future audits. Either way, do not conflate this with the byte-frontier
reissue mechanism polylogue-ktwa ships -- they need separate proof
mechanisms if (a) is chosen.
notes:
VERDICT (2026-07-29, verified against live archive /realm/db/polylogue): frontier_kind='byte'
is a deliberate, correct, load-bearing safety boundary, not an unexamined narrowing. Semantic
frontiers cannot currently authorise release. Do not relax this predicate.

WHAT A SEMANTIC FRONTIER ACTUALLY PROVES. classify_membership_revisions /
_strictly_dominates (polylogue/archive/session_revision_membership.py:188) proves, at
membership-replay time, that an older raw's parsed message_hashes/event_hashes are an exact
ordered PREFIX of the newer accepted session's, and its attachment_hashes a subset -- a real
containment proof, but computed ONCE over transient PARSED projections. The receipt written
to raw_revision_heads/raw_revision_applications (storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py:3687)
persists only accepted_frontier = a SCALAR COUNT (len(message_hashes)+len(event_hashes)+
len(attachment_hashes)), never the hash sequences themselves. So the domination proof cannot
be re-verified later without re-parsing the raw and re-trusting the classifier code that
produced it -- a materially weaker guarantee than a byte frontier, whose claim
(_validate_byte_head / _validate_active_revision_chain, storage/raw_retention.py:307-345) is
re-derived independently from source-tier byte offsets/generations alone, every time, with
no dependency on parser semantics.

EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION THE GATE IS DOUBLY SAFE, NOT SINGLY. Even setting the domination-proof
question aside: of 10,607 raws superseded under a semantic head (live query), 10,606 carry
raw_sessions.revision_authority='quarantined' in the source tier -- never byte_proven -- and
1 is byte_proven for an unrelated reason. So removing the frontier_kind='byte' SQL predicate
in _active_index_raw_authority (storage/raw_retention.py:182) would change NOTHING
observable: every one of these raws would still be rejected downstream by
_validate_eligible_receipt's unconditional `revision_kind in {'full','append'}` +
`revision_authority == 'byte_proven'` requirement on the raw itself
(storage/raw_retention.py, ~line 326). Multi-session raws (the antigravity population) take
the deferred membership-census branch in sources/revision_backfill.py:453 and never acquire
byte-proven authority via bind_raw_revision -- that's a separate, upstream fact about the
authority model, not something this branch's scope (raw_retention.py/repair.py) can fix.

LIVE NUMBERS (2026-07-29, index.db generation gen-1784807190100-34534407):
  raw_revision_heads: 12,301 byte-frontier heads, 6,429 semantic-frontier heads
  superseded application rows joined to CURRENT head (any freshness): byte=1,184,
    semantic=10,862 (matches this bead's original ~9,320+ estimate within live-drift tolerance)
  distinct raw_ids superseded under a semantic head: 10,607, summing ~28.1 GB raw blob_size
    (upper bound on retained "already-semantically-superseded" evidence)
  revision_kind/authority of those 10,607 raws: unknown/quarantined=5,785, full/quarantined=4,821,
    full/byte_proven=1 -- i.e. 10,606/10,607 (99.99%) lack the authority state
    _validate_eligible_receipt requires regardless of frontier_kind

DECISION: (b) from this bead's original framing -- accept the semantic-headed population as
permanently retained evidence under the current authority model. This is NOT "debt" to keep
re-litigating: releasing it safely would require a genuinely new, schema-bearing proof
mechanism (a durable, source-tier-anchored fingerprint of the domination proof, e.g.
persisting the accepted message-hash-sequence identity rather than a scalar count, PLUS an
independent re-verification step mirroring _validate_byte_head for semantic heads, PLUS
promoting multi-session raws' raw_sessions.revision_authority off 'quarantined' through some
analogous byte_proven-equivalent check) touching raw_authority.py, revision_application.py,
and sources/revision_backfill.py, and very likely a derived-tier schema bump. All three are
explicitly out of this task's write scope (raw_retention.py/repair.py only) and out of
"no index schema bump" scope. If a future operator wants to fund building that mechanism, it
is a new, separate, ground-up design -- not a relaxation of this predicate.

NO CODE CHANGE TO ELIGIBILITY. Per this task's constraint ("a wrong answer here destroys
evidence permanently... do not manufacture a release path"), no release-eligibility logic
changed. Landed only documentation at the two decision points (
_active_index_raw_authority's SQL predicate and plan_stale_supersession_reissue's docstring,
storage/raw_retention.py) recording this verdict + evidence inline, so a future reader does
not reopen this as a quick relaxation without rereading this note first. Commit 89afb0850 on
branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates (worktree
worktree-agent-a796fb2b17960dafa). Verification: devtools test
tests/unit/storage/test_raw_retention.py -- 63 passed (docstring-only change, no logic
touched). devtools verify --quick -- exit 0.
close_reason: Not a bug: verified frontier_kind='byte' is a correct, doubly-enforced safety boundary. Decision (b) recorded — semantic-headed raws stay permanently retained under the current authority model. See notes for full evidence; a real semantic release path is separate, schema-bearing future work, not tracked as debt here.

title: Hermes JSON-snapshot parser (local_agent.py) drops tool-definitions/platform/base_url/message_count
description:
parser-diff triage (polylogue-2qx.3) for the hermes provider found 301 unread
wire keys. 280 of them belong to the real NeMo Relay ATIF trajectory format
(hermes_spans.py) and were fixed directly (see hermes_spans.py commits
aa9fc858c/0e46f702a/b9f14bbd2 on this task's branch). The remaining 21 keys
belong to a DIFFERENT, much higher-volume shape: the mainstream Hermes JSON
session-snapshot document (167 of 169 total sampled documents), parsed by
`polylogue/sources/parsers/local_agent.py::parse_hermes` /
`_parse_hermes_message` -- NOT any of the hermes_state/spans/lifecycle/
verification.py modules. This file is shared with gemini-cli
(`parse_gemini_cli`), so it was out of this task's assigned write scope
(hermes_state.py, hermes_spans.py, hermes_lifecycle.py, hermes_verification.py,
hermes_identity.py) and is filed here rather than edited.

Confirmed by reading local_agent.py directly (not just the parser-diff tool's
name-matching, which is approximate): `parse_hermes` reads `session_id`,
`system_prompt`, `model`, `messages`, `session_start`, `last_updated` --
`last_updated` itself is a FALSE POSITIVE in the parser-diff tool's output
(already read; the tool under-attributes hermes parsing to only the
hermes_state/spans/lifecycle/verification module list, missing local_agent.py
entirely -- a scoping gap in `devtools/schema_parser_diff.py`'s
`PROVIDER_PARSERS["hermes"]` worth fixing separately).

Genuinely unread, at 100% coverage over 167 real documents:
  - `tools`, `tools[].function`, `.description`, `.parameters`,
    `.parameters.properties`, `.parameters.required` (167 docs, 100%) --
    the full tool-definition schema offered to the model. Materially
    different signal from tool CALLS (already captured): which tools were
    AVAILABLE. The archive has no representation for this in the mainstream
    Hermes shape at all today.
  - `base_url`, `platform`, `message_count` (167 docs, 100%) -- session-level
    routing/deployment metadata and a producer-reported message count
    (useful as a parse-completeness cross-check against len(messages)).
  - `messages[].codex_message_items[].content[].text`/`.phase`,
    `messages[].codex_reasoning_items[].encrypted_content`/`.summary[].text`
    (97-98 docs, ~59%) -- reasoning/message-item blobs. hermes_state.py's
    SQLite path already handles the equivalent fields via
    `_reasoning_metadata` (stores the whole `codex_reasoning_items`/
    `codex_message_items` value verbatim as block metadata) -- the JSON
    snapshot path (`_parse_hermes_message`) has no equivalent and drops them
    entirely.
  - `messages[]._empty_recovery_synthetic` (3 docs), `messages[]._db_persisted`
    (1 doc), `messages[].tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature`
    (1 doc) -- low-volume, informational.

Suggested fix shape (mirrors what hermes_spans.py just did): a new
`ParsedSessionEvent` (e.g. `hermes_session_json_metadata` for base_url/
platform/message_count, `hermes_tool_availability` for the tools[] list,
verbatim -- not conversation content) plus verbatim capture of
`codex_reasoning_items`/`codex_message_items` on the THINKING block metadata,
matching hermes_state.py's existing pattern. No index-tier schema change
needed (session_events.event_type has no CHECK vocabulary).
close_reason:
Implemented on branch feature/chore/promote-schemas-and-wire-gates, commit 59c6ffb10.

Disposition of the 21 keys from this bead's triage:

READ (now captured verbatim as session_events, no index schema change):
- tools[], tools[].function.{name,description,parameters,parameters.properties,
  parameters.required,parameters.$schema,parameters.additionalProperties}
  -> new ParsedSessionEvent event_type="hermes_tool_availability"
  (payload={"tools": <verbatim>, "tool_count": n}). Distinct signal from tool
  CALLS already captured on TOOL_USE blocks: which tools were AVAILABLE.
- base_url, platform, message_count -> new event_type="hermes_session_metadata"
  (base_url/platform verbatim, message_count kept as reported_message_count
  alongside parsed_message_count as a completeness cross-check).
- messages[].codex_reasoning_items, messages[].codex_message_items (~59%),
  messages[]._empty_recovery_synthetic, messages[]._db_persisted (low-volume),
  messages[].tool_calls[].extra_content.google.thought_signature (1 doc)
  -> new event_type="hermes_message_wire_extras", one event per message,
  keyed via source_message_provider_id.

CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE (per this bead's own caveat about the tool's
name-based matching): `platform` only "resolves" via looks_like_hermes()'s
membership check (`"platform" in payload`), never actually read/stored --
genuinely unread until this change, same class as base_url/message_count.

ARCHITECTURE FINDING (not fixed here, needs follow-up):
ParsedContentBlock.metadata is parse-time-only and is NEVER persisted -- the
`blocks` table has no metadata column; every block read path
(attachment_blocks.py, mappers_archive.py callers) selects a literal
`NULL AS metadata`. This means hermes_state.py's existing `_reasoning_metadata`
pattern (attaching codex_reasoning_items/codex_message_items to a THINKING
block's metadata) and the shared `_tool_metadata()` helper (status/timestamp/
description/displayName/renderOutputAsMarkdown on tool blocks, used by both
gemini-cli and hermes) are ALL silently dropped at write time today -- a
pre-existing gap, not introduced by this change. I avoided reproducing it by
routing the new local_agent.py captures through session_events instead
(real, durable, already supports per-message attribution). Filing this
finding rather than fixing it: giving `blocks` a real metadata column is an
index-tier schema change, out of this task's no-schema-bump constraint and
out of local_agent.py's write scope (block persistence is storage/, not
sources/parsers/).

Also triaged gemini-cli (secondary, n=1 sampled document -- thin evidence but
same shape, cheap to add): userMessageCount/hasUserOrAssistantMessage ->
event_type="gemini_cli_session_metadata"; memoryScratchpad (subagent working-
memory summary: version/workflowSummary/toolSequence/touchedPaths/
validationStatus) -> event_type="gemini_cli_memory_scratchpad", captured
verbatim.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_local_agent.py
(26 passed, 2 new + 1 extended). devtools verify --quick (format/lint/mypy/
render-all-check/layering/closure-matrix/schema-roundtrip/hash-boundary-
census/schema-versioning/schema-promotion-audit), exit 0. Anti-vacuity:
mutated production code (dropped the hermes_tool_availability event append)
and confirmed the corresponding test fails with StopIteration before
reverting.

Follow-up recommended: file a new bead for the blocks.metadata dead-column
finding (affects hermes_state.py + shared _tool_metadata()/_reasoning_metadata
helpers across parsers, not just local_agent.py -- needs an index-tier schema
decision, out of this task's scope).

title: session_provider_usage_events.payload_json is 1.28 GiB of write-only data whose every field is a typed column beside it
design:
Measured on the live archive 2026-07-29 (index.db, 33.69 GiB by dbstat).

  session_provider_usage_events (table)   2443.9 MB   7.1% of the index tier
    of which payload_json                 1.28 GiB    (52% of the table)
    4,030,168 rows, avg 340 B, zero NULLs

WRITE-ONLY
`payload_json` is written by _PROVIDER_USAGE_EVENT_INSERT_SQL
(storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/write.py:3041-3047) and never read back. An AST-ish scan
for `SELECT ... FROM session_provider_usage_events` mentioning payload_json returns zero
hits; the only reads of this table anywhere select COUNT(*)
(archive_tiers/self_verify.py:28), `position` (ingest_precedence.py:146,196 and
write.py:2904), or `SELECT 1` (archive.py:4871).

(`insights/claude_workflow_materializer.py:458` does read a `payload_json`, but from
`session_events` -- a different table. Do not confuse the two.)

REDUNDANT BY CONSTRUCTION
Every field in the blob is already an extracted, typed column in the same row:
  {"last_token_usage":{"cache_write_tokens":451,"cached_input_tokens":54332,
    "input_tokens":7,"output_tokens":3},
   "model":"claude-opus-4-20250514","semantics":"per_message","type":"message_usage"}
maps to last_cache_write_tokens / last_cached_input_tokens / last_input_tokens /
last_output_tokens / model_name / provider_event_type. The table has 20 columns and the
blob adds no field they do not already carry.

It is also doubly redundant by tier: index.db is REBUILDABLE, and the authoritative raw
payload already lives in source.db's blob store. Keeping a copy of provider wire bytes in
the derived tier stores the same evidence a third time.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK WHILE HERE
`total_cache_write_tokens` is constant across a 400k-row sample (1 distinct value), and
`provider_event_type` / `model_context_window` have 2 each. A constant column over 4M rows
is its own small waste; confirm against the full table before acting, since the sample was
the first 400k rows and may not be representative.

DO
Drop payload_json from the table (index tier, so this is a derived-schema change: classify
per CLAUDE.md's "Schema regimes" and declare the delta class in
storage/sqlite/lifecycle.py -- an undeclared bump silently forces a full raw replay). If
some future consumer genuinely needs the provider's original wire shape, it should read it
from source.db's blob, not from a duplicate in a rebuildable tier.

Expected reclaim: ~1.28 GiB of index.db, plus a smaller write-path saving on every usage
event ingested. Batch this with any other index-tier change so it costs one rebuild, not
two -- a full rebuild currently replays 92 GiB.

title: master: 3 browser-capture coalescing tests fail on title precedence (GDPR export beats browser capture)
design:
Reproduced on pure origin/master (not introduced by any in-flight branch), verified by
checking out origin/master's polylogue/ and tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py into
a clean tree and running the selection:

    devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py -k coalesces   3 failed

    test_browser_capture_raw_payload_coalesces_with_claude_ai_export
      test_browser_capture.py:1008  assert 'Claude GDPR title' == 'Claude browser title'
    test_browser_capture_raw_payload_coalesces_with_chatgpt_export[browser-first]
    test_browser_capture_raw_payload_coalesces_with_chatgpt_export[export-first]
      test_browser_capture.py:922   assert 'GDPR title' == 'Browser title'

The tests assert a browser-capture title outranks a GDPR/export title when the two
coalesce into one session; the export title is winning instead. Both parametrizations
fail, so it is not acquisition-order dependent.

Either the precedence rule changed and these tests were not updated, or a real regression
in coalescing title selection landed without being caught -- per-PR CI skips the heavy
test suite (it runs post-merge on master), which is the mechanism that lets this sit
broken on master.

Determine which before editing: if the intended rule is now export-wins, the tests encode
a stale contract and should be rewritten to state the new one with its reason; if
browser-wins is still intended, this is a live bug in the coalescing path and the tests
are correct.

Found while merging two agent branches (pbuh sidecar evidence, ah21 browser-capture blocks);
neither touches title coalescing and both reproduce the failure identically, as does a
clean origin/master checkout.
close_reason:
Determined: precedence rule legitimately changed, tests were stale.

#3179 (commit b473d9256, Ref polylogue-z1c6, merged 2026-07-20) intentionally
added a mirror rule to browser_capture_precedence() in
polylogue/storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/ingest_precedence.py: a genuine
non-browser-capture arrival (direct/GDPR export) now always outranks
browser-capture-only content and vice versa is skipped, making the outcome
order-independent (fixing a real order-dependent flakiness bug where whichever
material a live daemon happened to process first would win). That PR added
and updated the sibling proof
test_archive_tiers_archive_facade_export_vs_native_precedence_is_order_independent
(tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tiers_archive.py:737, asserting
("Direct export", export_message_count) regardless of arrival order) but
missed updating the three browser_capture.py coalescing tests that predate
it (last touched by ddf4f3efc, well before #3179).

Fixed: rewrote the three stale title assertions in
tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py (now lines 930 and 1019) from
"Browser title"/"Claude browser title" to "GDPR title"/"Claude GDPR title",
with comments citing browser_capture_precedence(), #3179/polylogue-z1c6, and
the sibling order-independence test. No production code changed -- this was
never a live regression.

Live-archive impact (read-only check against /realm/db/polylogue, confirmed
POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT resolves there): 0 sessions in raw_sessions currently
have more than one distinct capture_mode for the same (origin, native_id), so
no live session's stored title is affected by this either way -- production
has been export-wins all along.

Gate recommendation: per-PR CI skipping the heavy test suite is the
documented mechanism (CLAUDE.md) that let a legitimate #3179 rule change
merge without updating every affected test; this is already a known,
accepted tradeoff (heavy suite runs post-merge). Not recommending a new
fossilized-diff-style check -- CLAUDE.md forbids gates that memorialize a
renamed spelling, and the actual missing net here is "did #3179 run the full
test_browser_capture.py file", which devtools test <changed files> would
have caught if run; no new lint needed.

Verification: devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_browser_capture.py -k coalesces
(3 passed), full file green, tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tiers_archive.py -k
precedence (13 passed), devtools verify --quick (exit_code 0). Committed as
1f0040353 on branch worktree-agent-acdc97dbfb9cf3928 (agent worktree; PR not
opened/merged per task scope -- report only).

title: Capture and export convergence on one session_id is untested and would silently downgrade fidelity
description:
Measured 2026-07-29 -- this is a LATENT hazard, not an active bug, which is why it needs recording before it fires.

  chatgpt conversations reachable by browser capture only:   43
  reachable by GDPR export only:                          2,423
  reachable by BOTH:                                          0
  sessions == distinct native_ids == 2,635 (no duplication today)

The two paths have never overlapped, so coalescing has never been exercised.
What would happen is determined by two facts already established:

  1. IDENTITY WOULD COLLIDE, NOT DUPLICATE. Both paths key the ChatGPT
     conversation id as native_id, and session_id is a generated column
     (origin || ':' || native_id). Same conversation, same session_id.
  2. THE PARSED WRITE PATH IS FULL-REPLACE. write.py deletes blocks and messages
     for the session id, then inserts. Whichever path ingests SECOND wins
     entirely.

And the two paths carry materially different fidelity: the export has the
mapping tree with tool nodes and status; the capture has flat text with no
blocks channel at all (see the BrowserCaptureTurn bead). So exporting a
conversation you had already captured is fine, and CAPTURING one you had
already exported silently replaces structured evidence with flattened text.

The raw tier already models this correctly -- raw_revision_heads, revision
authority, accepted frontiers. It is the parsed tier that resolves by
replacement instead of by fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Two observations of one conversation are retained as revisions, and the composed session reflects the higher-fidelity one regardless of arrival order. 2. A test ingests export-then-capture and capture-then-export for the same conversation and asserts the same, higher-fidelity result both ways. 3. Fidelity is declared per acquisition path in the OriginSpec so 'higher' is not a judgement call at write time. 4. Related: unknown-export currently holds 52 raws with NULL native_id -- conversations that failed origin detection and therefore cannot coalesce with anything.

title: aistudio-drive discards every model setting that produced its outputs
description:
The per-origin wire enumeration found the entire runSettings block unread for aistudio-drive:

  temperature, topP, topK, maxOutputTokens, thinkingLevel, safetySettings
  (with threshold), enableCodeExecution, enableSearchAsATool,
  enableBrowseAsATool, enableAutoFunctionResponse
  plus chunkedPrompt.pendingInputs

This is the model configuration for every AI Studio session in the archive.
Polylogue's stated purpose includes reconstructing what produced a result; for
this origin the generation parameters are present in the acquired bytes and
dropped at parse.

It is also the only origin where the operator can vary sampling settings freely,
which makes it the one place where 'same prompt, different settings, different
output' is answerable -- if the settings were kept.
acceptance_criteria: 1. runSettings is parsed into typed session-level evidence for aistudio-drive. 2. The settings are queryable, so 'sessions where temperature > X' is expressible. 3. Existing sessions acquire it by reprocess of retained bytes. 4. Other origins are checked for an equivalent settings block rather than assuming AI Studio is unique.
close_reason: runSettings storage was already shipped (PR #3390, polylogue-2qx.4/cgfy, index v46) before this bead was filed. The genuinely-remaining gap -- chunkedPrompt.pendingInputs (draft/unsent textbox content, 7/397 real sessions with non-blank drafts) -- is fixed on PR #3415 (draft_input session_event). AC2 (query-DSL numeric predicates over run_settings, e.g. temperature > X) is NOT satisfied: the boolean-query grammar only accepts integer literals and NumericQueryFieldInfo assumes a plain SQL column, not a JSON-extract expression -- needs a separate DSL float-literal + JSON-field-predicate feature, out of parser scope. AC4 checked: grepped sources/parsers + sources/providers for generationConfig/sampling_params/temperature/inference_config/model_settings, no other origin has an equivalent settings block.

title: Insights: the concept earns its place, five of eleven types do not
description:
DEEP REVIEW of polylogue/insights (23,103 lines, 11 registered types) 2026-07-29.

WHAT AN INSIGHT IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT JUST A NAMED QUERY. tool_usage pairs an
aggregate with per-origin COVERAGE: 'an origin with sessions but zero actions is
the explicit data-unavailable signal, not a quiet zero.' That distinction --
zero versus unavailable -- is real, is not expressible in the query DSL's
, and is the honest core of the concept. The insights package
should NOT be dissolved into the query algebra wholesale.

WHICH TYPES EARN THEIR EXISTENCE (materialized tables in parentheses):
  KEEP    threads (9,914)          a root session's lineage tree; single-session
                                   threads are correct, not degenerate -- 810
                                   multi-session threads correspond exactly to
                                   the 810 sessions with lineage children
  KEEP    tool_usage               computed; the coverage pairing is the value
                                   (but its CLI surface is currently BROKEN --
                                   see the analyze-tools bead)
  KEEP    session_costs, cost_rollups, usage_timeline, archive_coverage,
          archive_debt             computed rollups with coverage semantics
  DELETE  session_phases (29,432)  see the deletion bead: 82% single span, no
                                   label, index-synthesized timestamps
  DELETE  session_work_events (21,190)  82% single event, duplicates action_pairs
  REDUCE  session_profiles (18,871)     keep the profile, delete the five
                                   constant version/family columns and fix the
                                   100%-NULL cost columns (see f2qv.6)
  REDUCE  session_tag_rollups (3,593)   explicit_count constant 0

STRUCTURAL FINDING: 5 of 11 types are materialized tables, 6 are computed. There
is no stated rule for which. The materialized ones are precisely where the
freshness machinery lives (insight_materialization's seven proxy columns,
derived_refresh_guard, delegation_refresh_scope). Under content-addressed
derivation the distinction stops mattering -- a materialized insight becomes a
hash-keyed cache, and a stale row is a miss rather than a lie.

SURFACE FINDING: every type is MCP-reachable through
mcp/insight_tool_contracts.py and only some are CLI-reachable; see the
registry-surface bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Each of the 11 types carries a recorded verdict: keep / reduce / delete, with the discrimination evidence. 2. A stated rule governs materialized versus computed, or the distinction is removed by hash-keying. 3. The coverage-pairing property is documented as the reason the package exists, so a future refactor does not dissolve it into the query DSL by accident. 4. Deleting a type removes its table, materializer, registry entry, MCP contract and any FTS index together.

title: Registered insights are MCP-reachable and CLI-absent: decide the surface, do not let it drift
description:
Measured 2026-07-29. insights/registry.py registers insight types including session_phases (cli_command_name='phases'), session_work_events, threads, session_profiles, session_tag_rollups, session_costs, cost_rollups, usage_timeline, tool_usage, archive_coverage, archive_debt.

  $ polylogue analyze --help   ->  insights, latency, pace, tools, turns, usage

So 'polylogue analyze phases' does not exist despite the registry declaring that
name. MCP reaches all of them through mcp/insight_tool_contracts.py, which is
registry-driven. The registry is therefore authoritative for MCP and decorative
for the CLI -- a declare-once mechanism honoured by one surface and not the
other, which is the pattern polylogue-t46 exists to remove.

OPERATOR POSITION (2026-07-29): a registered insight should be CLI-reachable
unless there is a clear reason not to -- but the CLI itself must stay
disciplined rather than sprawling one subcommand per registry entry. Those pull
in opposite directions and the resolution is a decision, not a default.

Note this interacts with two deletions: session_phases and session_work_events
are condemned by a sibling bead, so their registry entries and MCP contracts go
with them rather than gaining CLI commands.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every registry entry is classified: CLI-reachable, MCP-only with a stated reason, or deleted. 2. No registry entry declares a cli_command_name that produces no command. 3. Whatever the decision, one mechanism generates both surfaces -- a registry honoured by MCP and ignored by the CLI does not survive. 4. The CLI does not gain a subcommand per entry by default; the disciplined shape is argued explicitly.

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: VERIFY-FIRST TRIAGE 2026-07-31: MISFRAMED. Bead claims the INSIGHT_REGISTRY is 'decorative for the CLI' — false on current master. cli/commands/insights.py:579-582 loops INSIGHT_REGISTRY and registers every entry with query_model+operations_method_name as a live 'polylogue analyze insights <name>' Click command, since commit 2b46af5f31 (2026-05-02, predates this bead). Confirmed via import: analyze_insights_command.commands includes phases/work-events/etc — all 12 registered names are CLI-reachable. The bead's cited repro (polylogue analyze --help) only shows top-level groups and never drilled into 'polylogue analyze insights --help', so 'CLI-absent' was an artifact of an incomplete repro. AC #1-3 are effectively already satisfied by the existing registry-driven loop. Recommend closing or narrowing this bead to just AC #4 (write the decision doc formalizing the shape that already exists in code).

comments.author: Sinity
comments.text: Re-verified 2026-08-03: this bead's premise ('MCP reaches all of them through mcp/insight_tool_contracts.py, which is registry-driven') does not hold against current source. grep -rn 'insight_tool_contracts' across polylogue/ and tests/ finds only the definition file itself (polylogue/mcp/insight_tool_contracts.py) -- InsightListToolSpec.from_insight_type has zero callers anywhere, including in mcp/server_cutover.py's actual tool registration. Last commit touching the file is cc0999bef (2026-07-13), before this bead's stated measurement, so this isn't a fresh regression -- the module appears built but never wired into MCP tool registration. Filed polylogue-nbls5 with corrected evidence and file:line citations; treat that as the accurate current-state description before acting on this bead's premise.

title: session_agent_policies: 402,869 rows encoding 3,053 facts
description:
Measured 2026-07-29, full scan.

  rows                                402,869
  distinct sessions                     3,031   (133 rows per session)
  sessions whose policy NEVER changes   3,010   (99.3%)
  rows remaining if deduped by value    3,053

The table records approval_policy / sandbox_policy / network_policy at every
message position, and the policy is invariant within a session 99.3% of the
time. It is a change-log of non-changes at 132x redundancy.

Already known degenerate on the same table: network_policy is constant 'false',
source_message_id is 100% NULL.

  sqlite3 -readonly index.db "with per as (select session_id,
    count(distinct coalesce(approval_policy,'')||'|'||coalesce(sandbox_policy,'')||'|'||coalesce(network_policy,'')) d,
    count(*) n from session_agent_policies group by session_id)
    select count(*), sum(n), sum(d=1), sum(d) from per;"
acceptance_criteria: 1. Policy is stored once per session (or per genuine change), not per message position. 2. If policy genuinely varies for some sessions, those keep interval rows; the 3,010 invariant sessions do not. 3. network_policy and source_message_id are dropped unless a producer is named. 4. Report row count before and after against the 402,869 baseline.

title: Evidence and method log for the 2026-07-29 audit: re-runnable commands and failed approaches
description:
Companion to the beads filed on 2026-07-29. Its purpose is to stop the next agent from repeating failed methods or trusting stale numbers.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE ACTING. Every quantitative claim in the 2026-07-29 beads carries its command inline. The polylogue-m3p9 precedent is the reason: that bead's headline was 12x stale (79%/65,946 -> 5.9%/1,117) because two unrelated changes moved the denominator and nobody re-derived it.

METHODS THAT WORKED
  1. Column degeneracy sweep -- per-column NULL%/distinct-count over the live
     archive. Found ~40 confirmed degenerate columns.
  2. Read/write matrix -- regex every SQL statement in polylogue/ against
     sqlite_master. Found session_commits (1 writer, 0 readers).
  3. Wire-vs-parser enumeration -- parse real transcripts, count every key,
     grep sources/ for each. Found 34 unread keys of the top 70.
  4. Fallback-bucket dominance -- find columns whose modal value is
     unknown/other/empty above ~30%. Found the whole terminal-state family.
  5. Artifact-name bead indexing -- index beads by tables/modules that ACTUALLY
     EXIST in schema or tree, then read clusters of 3+.

METHODS THAT FAILED -- do not repeat
  1. Keyword clustering of beads by root cause. 60-130 matches per cause, pure
     noise; bead prose is too interconnected and later notes contaminate it.
     polylogue-hjpx matched every category because its text mentions everything.
  2. Sampling the live archive with LIMIT without verification. LIMIT takes
     physically-adjacent rows: it falsely reported blocks.tool_result_exit_code
     as 100% NULL (144,616 are populated) and session_provider_usage_events
     totals as constant-zero (2,265,315 of 4,030,168 nonzero). ALWAYS confirm a
     sampled degeneracy with a full scan before filing.
  3. 'Unused command' detection over devtools by grepping docs -- contaminated
     by generated reference docs. After excluding them, 0 of 112 commands are
     unreferenced; the devtools cull argument is consolidation, not deletion.

CORRECTIONS MADE DURING THE AUDIT, recorded so they are not re-introduced
  - The 2026-07-10 incident was SPLIT-BRAIN (two writable indexes over shared
    durable tiers), NOT a session shrinking 8,076 -> 360. It was recovered and
    closed (polylogue-nkmy); the fix is structural (the second path is now a
    symlink). The full-replace concern stands on its own code evidence at
    write.py:4714-4715, not on this incident.
  - 'progress' records are NOT streaming noise. They carry parentToolUseID, the
    delegation join key -- 842,819 records.
  - usage.service_tier does NOT distinguish subscription from API billing:
    1,651,137 occurrences, every one 'standard'. A constant.
  - raw_revision_heads.append_end_offset is 100% NULL (18,730 rows), so the
    durable data to reconstruct an ingest cursor is NOT already present.
  - action_pairs' six copied columns show ZERO drift against blocks; the
    argument there is cost and coupling, not correctness.
  - sessions' 13 denormalized counts show ZERO drift; deprioritise them.

OPEN, NOT MEASURED
  - corpus-wide collision rate of the child-prompt/parent-Task content join
    (verified unique on ONE file: 1 match of 102 tool_use blocks)
  - collision rate of a structural/derived session label
  - contents of evidence_json / inference_json (non-empty on 100% of
    session_work_events rows; never inspected)
acceptance_criteria: 1. An agent acting on any 2026-07-29 bead re-runs its inline commands first and records the current value alongside the original. 2. No bead from that batch is closed citing a number nobody re-measured. 3. Failed methods above are not repeated; if one is retried, the reason is recorded.

title: Delete session_phases and session_work_events: 82% of sessions get one segment
description:
Measured 2026-07-29, full scan of 21,190 rows. This table is two different things under one name.

NOISE -- work_event_type='session', 5,797 rows (27%):
  file_paths_json  '[]' on 5,797 of 5,797   (100%)
  tools_used_json  '[]' on 5,797 of 5,797   (100%)
  duration_ms = 0  on 2,773                  (48%)
  confidence       constant 0.6
  summary          a first-prompt echo
It asserts that a session happened, which the sessions table already says.

REAL -- the other four types, 15,393 rows (73%):
  type            n      no_files  no_tools  no_duration
  implementation  8,289    2,152      0        1,162
  research        4,580       32      0            8
  review          1,837      303      0           33
  planning          687      212      0           41
tools_used_json is populated on 100% of all four; file paths on 74-99%.

BUT THE LABELS ARE SUSPECT. confidence is a per-type CONSTANT for four of five
types (session 0.6, research 0.7, review 0.6, planning 0.7 -- one distinct value
each); only implementation varies, across 3 discrete values in 0.4-0.75. And the
classification does not survive inspection:
  'Create my holiday video'                        -> implementation
  'HDD/storage, focusing on price per unit'        -> implementation
with file paths like '/Sora/implicit_link::connector_openai_santa/init' and
tools 'api_tool.call_tool' -- ChatGPT connector plumbing, not code work.

VERDICT: keep the structural columns (file_paths, tools_used, duration,
start/end index) -- they are derived from real evidence and are the inputs the
title design depends on. The semantic layer (work_event_type, its constant
confidence, and the echo summary) is a heuristic label wearing a number, the
same disease as this bead's parent documents for confidence columns generally.

INSPECTED 2026-07-29 -- and the row format already draws the right line, which
the columns then destroy:

  evidence_json  {"start_index":0,"end_index":62,"start_time":null,
                  "end_time":null,"canonical_session_date":null,
                  "timing_provenance":"untimestamped","date_provenance":...}
  inference_json {"heuristic_label":"session","summary":"It's still not
                  clear to me what is capitalism...","confidence":...}

So the JSON separates EVIDENCE from INFERENCE cleanly, and even names the label
'heuristic_label'. Then three top-level columns copy the inference side out and
strip the marking: work_event_type == inference_json.heuristic_label,
confidence == inference_json.confidence, summary == inference_json.summary.
A reader of the columns cannot tell they are looking at inference; a reader of
the JSON can. The columns are the defect, not the model.

'timing_provenance':'untimestamped' also explains the negative durations
measured on this table and on session_phases: start/end are synthesized from
indices, not observed, so ended < started is reachable.

DECISION 2026-07-29, REVISED after asking the right question. An earlier draft
said 'the concept survives, three columns do not'. That was too generous. The
question is not whether the table is wired -- it is -- but whether the CONCEPT
earns a table. It does not.

  work_events per session   avg 1.44;  12,072 of 14,669 sessions (82%) have
                                       exactly ONE work_event
  phases per session        avg 2.07;  12,363 sessions have exactly ONE phase

A segmentation that yields one segment for 82% of sessions is not a
segmentation. It is a label on the whole session stored in a span table. And the
spans it does produce are incoherent -- sampled from session_phases:
  start_index 0->110, 26,258 words, duration_ms 2
  start_index 0->4,    2,037 words, duration_ms 148,761
A single unlabelled span covering a whole session carries strictly less
information than the sessions row it points at.

  DELETE  session_phases entirely (29,432 rows). No label, index-synthesized
          timestamps (evidence_json timing_provenance='untimestamped'), 37.8%
          ending before they start, one span for most sessions. Registered at
          insights/registry.py with cli_command_name='phases' -- and
           does not exist; analyze exposes only
          insights/latency/pace/tools/turns/usage. MCP reaches it through
          insight_tool_contracts.py, so removal must drop the registry entry
          and the MCP contract together.
  DELETE  session_work_events entirely (21,190 rows) plus its FTS index. Its
          structural half duplicates action_pairs, which holds the same
          file/tool evidence at 1,870,733 rows of real per-call granularity;
          its inference half is already marked heuristic_label in
          inference_json and copied into columns that hide the marking. The
          1,011 sessions that have work_events but no action_pairs are ChatGPT
          connector sessions whose 'file paths' are URLs like
          '/Sora/implicit_link::connector_openai_santa/init' -- not files.

  DO NOT add the ended>=started CHECK to either table. Deleting them removes
  13,743 constraint violations and the max(0,...) clamping at once.

  BEFORE DELETING, confirm no consumer derives value rather than merely reading:
  the read sites are status.py, timeline_reads.py, storage.py, repair.py,
  fts_lifecycle, dangling_repair, otlp_correlation -- all maintenance plumbing
  on inspection, but verify rather than trust this list.
acceptance_criteria: 1. session_phases and session_work_events are deleted -- tables, materializers, FTS index, registry entries and MCP contracts together; a partial removal that leaves a registered-but-unbacked insight is not acceptable. 2. Each of the seven read sites is confirmed to be maintenance plumbing and removed with them, or a genuine consumer is named and its need met from action_pairs instead. 3. Any consumer that wanted per-session file/tool evidence reads action_pairs, which carries the same evidence at 1,870,733 rows of per-call granularity. 4. The 1,011 ChatGPT connector sessions that had work_events but no action_pairs are checked: if their connector URLs are worth keeping, they land as actions, not as a resurrected work-event table. 5. Report rows removed and the resulting drop in the ended<started violation count (13,743 across both tables).

title: Inventory every degenerate field by whether the data is available, derivable, or genuinely absent
description:
Operator framing 2026-07-29: 'just because there are some titles does not mean there are all titles -- this kind of thing might be worth figuring out how to cheaply produce the missing data. Worth inventorying schema for instances of such potentialities.'

The column-degeneracy sweep of 2026-07-29 found ~40 confirmed degenerate columns (100% NULL or constant, full-table scans). Degeneracy alone does not say what to do. Each needs a three-way classification:

  AVAILABLE   the value exists in acquired or acquirable bytes and is discarded
              or unread. Fix = parse it.
              e.g. Claude Code titles (ai-title records, discarded),
                   Codex titles (state_5.threads.title, unacquired),
                   session->PR links (pr-link records, discarded)
  DERIVABLE   the value is computable from what is already stored, cheaply and
              deterministically. Fix = derive it, ideally as a generated column.
              e.g. sessions.created_at_ms/updated_at_ms (1,117 NULL) from message
                   timestamps; totals in session_provider_usage_events from their
                   components; sort keys; repo identity from normalized remotes
  ABSENT      no provider evidence exists and no honest derivation does either.
              Fix = delete the column, or populate it only with a declared
              inference carrying its own provenance -- never a bare value.
              e.g. any field whose only possible source is a model's guess

The third category is where this bead earns its keep: today a degenerate column
is indistinguishable from a populated-but-constant one, and both are
indistinguishable from an inferred one, because confidence and method columns
are themselves constant (see this bead's parent note).

RESIDUAL AFTER THE AVAILABLE FIXES is the interesting number. Provider titles do
not cover the whole corpus -- older sessions predate the ai-title feature -- so
after un-skipping there is a genuine residual requiring synthesis. Quantify it
per field rather than assuming a single fix closes the column.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every degenerate column from the 2026-07-29 sweep carries a classification (available / derivable / absent) with the evidence for it. 2. For AVAILABLE, the source record or table is named. 3. For DERIVABLE, the derivation is stated and, where SQLite permits, implemented as a generated column so the field cannot regress to NULL. 4. For ABSENT, the column is deleted or its values carry declared provenance. 5. Post-fix residual is measured per field, not assumed to be zero.

title: The verification stack is not currently trustworthy
description:
Umbrella for independently-filed findings that together mean a green signal cannot be trusted, and a red one is routinely ignored. Filed 2026-07-29 to root beads discovered separately.

Members:
  ze5i  four of ten lab policies fail continuously behind --lab, which no gate runs
  p6rz  pre-existing test failures unrelated to the change under test
  lvz6  clean-master full-suite triage: 104 of 16,441 unreproduced
  07pt  flaky timing assertion in browser-extension build.test.js
  e6a0  index_v37_fast_forward fixture predates action_pairs: 9 failing tests
  n2f4  nix.yml CI failing on every recent run
  x7du  rebuild CI for speed on free public-repo runners

Why one concern: each individually looks like ordinary maintenance. Together
they mean the project cannot answer 'is master healthy' without a human
triaging known-bad signals from new ones -- and the schema-versioning incident
of 2026-07-28 (an index bump merged without its delta declaration, first
noticed when the live archive became unqueryable) is what that costs.

Related, already parented: 88jp (verification risk model) and d45p
(verification failure ledger) are the design side of the same problem.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every member is green, or is a named accepted exception with an expiry and an owner. 2. A policy that fails continuously is either gated so failure blocks, or deleted -- not left reporting into a void. 3. 'Is master healthy' is answerable from one signal without human triage. 4. Report the count of known-failing checks before and after; the target is zero, not a smaller number.

title: Storage economy: the archive stores bytes and rows it can reconstruct or does not read
description:
Umbrella for a cluster of independently-filed findings that are one concern: the archive persists data that is reconstructible, unread, or degenerate. Filed 2026-07-29 to root beads that were each discovered separately and never attached to anything.

Members and their measured claims (each keeps its own evidence as a child):
  vzn6  45 GB of byte-proven superseded prefix blobs are reconstructible
  bo9n  session_events mirrors the Codex wire stream row-per-record: 6.8M rows
  c3ip  session_provider_usage_events.payload_json: 700 MB with zero readers
