description:
Found incidentally during the polylogue-iiu6r break-glass/dead-surface audit, unrelated to that audit's main finding but real and quick to fix.

docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md line 288 contains a literal, unresolved merge-conflict marker: '||||||| b64a074e5' (the diff3 common-ancestor marker), sitting inside item 5's investigation history section. Confirmed present on the current tree (grep, not a rendering artifact) and landed via commit 5e23e6abf (#3390, 'index v46 wire-evidence batch, free-threaded-only runtime, parse-failure recovery') -- a 268-commit/329-file squash merge where this one conflict was apparently resolved by keeping both sides' text with the ancestor marker left in place, rather than fully resolving to one narrative.

The surrounding text (lines 280-358) is otherwise readable as three sequential investigation writeups (original finding, second attempt polylogue-iy3n, second attempt detail) so the marker is cosmetic corruption, not a semantic conflict -- but it is genuinely wrong markdown sitting in a tracked, non-generated doc and should be cleaned up (delete the ||||||| line and reconcile the immediately following duplicate 'What it is' block against the surrounding text, keeping the most detailed/most current version per this doc's own pattern elsewhere in item 5).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #3578: removed the ||||||| b64a074e5 diff3 marker at line 288 of docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md and the duplicate stale-ancestor 'What it is' paragraph it separated from the current text, keeping the more detailed/currently-line-numbered version per item 5's own existing pattern. Verified with devtools render all --check and devtools verify --quick (both exit 0).

title: docs: convergence-simplification-inventory.md items 1 & 3 no longer deletable as described
description:
Filed from polylogue-iiu6r audit (find-and-classify pass for 'automatic path already covers this, manual surface never deleted' gaps).

Re-investigated docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md items 1 and 3 against the current tree, since their stated preconditions ('once phase (b) 3.14t lands' / 'once daemon_parse_stage_split is no longer a flag') are both now true (dcz5 3.14t deploy closed; daemon_parse_stage_split confirmed deleted from polylogue/config.py). Both items are STILL-NEEDED despite that -- the doc is stale, not wrong about the precondition, wrong about the consequence.

Item 1 (process-pool machinery, polylogue/pipeline/services/process_pool.py): only the ONE call site item 1 actually describes -- _parse_unique_retained_raws in polylogue/sources/revision_backfill.py -- was retired (its own docstring now speaks of 'the retired process-pool alternative' in past tense). process_pool_executor()/process_pool_context()/terminate_process_pool() remain live, unconditional (NOT gated on parallel_threads_effective()) call sites in: polylogue/pipeline/services/ingest_batch/_core.py:1053, polylogue/pipeline/services/validation_flow.py:185 (measured Threads(24)=160MB/s vs Process(8)=605MB/s, 3.7x -- a real process-vs-thread win independent of GIL/free-threaded build), and polylogue/pipeline/services/archive_ingest.py:279. Deleting process_pool.py would break all three.

Item 3 (_RAW_MATERIALIZATION_DAEMON_BLOB_LIMIT_BYTES, polylogue/daemon/cli.py:107): doc says it 'becomes redundant with DaemonParseStage's budget alone' once the parse-stage-split flag is gone. But polylogue/storage/repair.py's raw_materialization_whale_pass_candidate (polylogue-t93b, added after the doc's item 3 was written) now threads this exact constant through as ordinary_max_payload_bytes -- the boundary distinguishing the daemon's ordinary trickle envelope from its escalation-tier whale pass. This is a capability unrelated to DaemonParseStage's in-flight-bytes budget; deleting the constant collapses the ordinary/whale distinction t93b's fairness tiering depends on.

Ask: update the two item sections in docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md to record 'reinvestigated <date>: still needed, see polylogue-iiu6r notes' (matching item 5's existing style of documenting failed-deletion investigations), so a future reader doesn't re-attempt the same now-stale deletion the doc still describes as pending.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #3578: updated items 1 and 3 in docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md with status notes recording current reality instead of stale 'deletable once X' framing. Item 1: re-verified process_pool.py's helpers -- only the one call site the row names (_parse_unique_retained_raws) was retired; three other unconditional call sites remain (ingest_batch/_core.py:1053, validation_flow.py:185 with a measured 3.7x thread-vs-process win independent of GIL, archive_ingest.py:279), so the module stays load-bearing despite the 3.14t free-threaded deploy landing. Item 3: re-verified _RAW_MATERIALIZATION_DAEMON_BLOB_LIMIT_BYTES -- daemon_parse_stage_split is confirmed gone, but storage/repair.py's raw_materialization_whale_pass_candidate (polylogue-t93b, added after this row was written) now threads the constant through as ordinary_max_payload_bytes, the ordinary/whale-pass boundary; deleting it would collapse that distinction. Original design-time text kept for history per item 5's own convention; new status notes mark it superseded. Verified with devtools render all --check and devtools verify --quick (both exit 0).

title: Excise ops maintenance rebuild-index: dead break-glass surface, daemon bulk routing is unconditional
notes:
INVESTIGATION FINDING (2026-08-02): did NOT delete the manual CLI command. Found a real, tracked gap -- the bead's own premise (daemon_bulk_rebuild_routing docstring in polylogue/daemon/cli.py claiming the routing is now "unconditional" and citing gd6v's "no break-glass residue" AC) is not the full story.

1. gd6v's actual acceptance criteria required TWO things before CLI deletion: (a) daemon routes bulk-scale backlogs with zero manual involvement -- shipped, PR #3189, but only proven at FIXTURE scale (6-raw corpus equivalence test); (b) "the ops maintenance rebuild-index CLI operator surface is DELETED in the same change-train once daemon routing is proven equivalent" -- gd6v's own close_reason states explicitly: "Archive-scale equivalence receipt + CLI deletion remain tracked by polylogue-4jsk." Deletion was never done in gd6v; it was deferred pending real-scale proof.

2. polylogue-4jsk (open, P3) inherited that item but is itself blocked behind polylogue-dcz5 (3.14t deploy, now closed) and its own 2026-07-31 note says the deletion inventory (docs/design/convergence-simplification-inventory.md) "exists but is still-to-execute, not executed."

3. polylogue-mkk0 (open, P2, created 2026-07-29, never touched since) is the bead that explicitly exists to carve the archive-scale equivalence receipt + flag-flip + CLI deletion out of 4jsk's dcz5 dependency so it isn't blocked on an unrelated runtime migration. Its own text: "The archive-scale equivalence receipt needs ONE archive-scale run with the flag on, comparing a daemon-built generation against the trickle/CLI-built index." That receipt is not recorded as landed anywhere in bd (grepped .beads/issues.jsonl and .beads/interactions.jsonl for "archive-scale equivalence" -- only mkk0's own filing text matches).

4. Someone did later make _maybe_route_daemon_bulk_rebuild in polylogue/daemon/cli.py unconditional and delete the daemon_bulk_rebuild_routing config flag (git log shows PR #3390, "index v46 wire-evidence batch... full index rebuild"), which reads as a real archive-scale rebuild having happened. But nothing closes or even updates mkk0 to record that event as satisfying its AC, and the docstring's self-declared justification ("A flag whose off-state is strictly worse is not a choice; it is a defect with a toggle") is a different argument (fixing an operationally-bad default) than the archive-scale equivalence proof mkk0 asks for. Treating an unattributed code comment as the formal verification receipt this repo's culture requires would be exactly the "claim the diff doesn't support" anti-pattern.

5. Independent of the receipt-gating question, the manual command is not functionally subsumed by the daemon's automatic routing even on its own terms: the daemon always drives ONE well-known fixed operation (DAEMON_BULK_REBUILD_OPERATION_ID) covering the WHOLE backlog once a bulk-scale threshold is crossed (polylogue/daemon/bulk_rebuild.py's own docstring: "keeps the daemon's own automagic operation distinct from any operator-run polylogue ops maintenance rebuild-index invocation ... untouched by this module"). The manual CLI additionally supports targeted --raw-id replay, --only-missing, --max-blob-mb bounded replay, --shard-count local parallel sharded execution, explicit --operation-id resume, and a --plan read-only preview -- none of which the fixed automatic routing provides. The design doc itself (convergence-simplification-inventory.md #6) says "Read-only diagnostic inspection surfaces may survive; nothing that mutates does" -- i.e. even under the strictest reading, --plan was never slated for deletion, so "delete the manual CLI command entirely" as framed would over-delete relative to the repo's own design intent.

Decision: left polylogue/cli/commands/maintenance/_rebuild_index.py, polylogue/maintenance/rebuild_index.py, the /api/maintenance/rebuild-index HTTP endpoint, and all related tests/docs in place, unmodified. No code changed in this session. Recommend: (a) do not close this bead as "done"; either fold it into mkk0 (which already owns exactly this receipt-then-delete sequence) or close rpuqn as superseded-by-mkk0 to avoid duplicate tracking; (b) whoever executes mkk0 should keep --plan (and any other genuinely read-only inspection subcommand) even after deleting the mutating rebuild-execution paths, per the inventory doc's own carve-out.

title: codex parser: extract real fields from thread_goal_updated/sub_agent_activity/task_started/task_complete/turn_aborted/thread_settings_applied/collab_*/item_completed/review_mode/web_search_end/thread_rolled_back/error
description:
Follow-up from polylogue-fuky's producer/consumer audit (2026-08-02) of sources/parsers/codex.py's generic response_item/event_msg session_event dispatch. That bead only decided a CLASSIFICATION (each type is now explicitly named in `_CODEX_KNOWN_RESPONSE_ITEM_TYPES`, codex.py) and resolved `agent_reasoning`'s fate (confirmed duplicate, filtered at write.py). It deliberately did NOT extract the real fields this audit found being silently dropped by `_compact_response_payload`'s generic allowlist (type/id/call_id/name/status/timestamp/output-or-argument-length/cwd/metadata.turn_id only).

Fields confirmed present on the raw wire (read directly, not inferred) but currently discarded:

- thread_goal_updated (45,814 live rows) -- goal.objective (free text session objective), goal.status/tokensUsed/timeUsedSeconds.
- sub_agent_activity (41,769) -- agent_thread_id, agent_path, kind (e.g. "interacted") -- subagent delegation evidence.
- task_started (20,432) -- turn_id, model_context_window, collaboration_mode_kind.
- task_complete (17,055) -- turn_id, last_agent_message.
- turn_aborted (3,394) -- turn_id, reason (e.g. "interrupted").
- thread_settings_applied (3,548) -- full per-turn settings snapshot (model, reasoning_effort, personality, collaboration_mode incl. developer_instructions text) -- check for overlap/redundancy with the existing turn_context capture (codex.py ~line 2232) before deciding what's incremental.
- collab_agent_spawn_end/collab_waiting_end/collab_close_end/collab_agent_interaction_end (~1,000 combined) -- subagent-delegation evidence: new_thread_id, new_agent_nickname, new_agent_role, prompt, receiver_thread_id, receiver_agent_nickname/role, status text.
- item_completed (199) -- item.text (e.g. full plan content).
- entered_review_mode/exited_review_mode (13 each) -- target.instructions/user_facing_hint and review_output.findings/overall_correctness/overall_explanation/overall_confidence_score.
- view_image_tool_call (62) -- path (referenced image file).
- web_search_end (1,357) -- query, action.queries -- distinct completion-marker wire shape from the already-handled web_search_call/web_search_output pair.
- thread_rolled_back (92) -- num_turns.
- error (42) -- message (user-facing text), codex_error_info (real error code, e.g. "usage_limit_exceeded").

Each needs its own bounded field-set decision (which fields are evidence vs noise, whether a dedicated typed table or session_events payload fields suffice) plus an INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION SEMANTIC_REPARSE bump (matching the v46 "unread-wire batch" precedent -- batch related fields onto one bump rather than one bump per type). sub_agent_activity and the collab_* cluster look like the highest-value target (delegation-graph evidence, complementary to session_links/delegation_facts); thread_settings_applied needs a redundancy check against turn_context first.

See sources/parsers/codex.py's _CODEX_KNOWN_RESPONSE_ITEM_TYPES comment (polylogue-fuky) for the full classification table this extends.

title: Reconciler has no graceful path when a live census plan's raw is already deleted
description:
recover_interrupted_raw_authority_frontier and the FOLD_DUPLICATE_ALIAS / other actuators in
polylogue/storage/raw_reconciler.py assume a 'planned', unresolved-outcome census plan's
input raws (named in raw_authority_plans.input_raw_ids_json) are still present in
raw_sessions when the reconciler re-attempts it after a crash or on the next convergence pass.
If a raw is deleted out from under an in-flight plan (e.g. by ordinary superseded-snapshot
retention racing an unusually long-lived 'planned' census, or by any future direct
raw_sessions delete that doesn't consult active_raw_retention_authority), the actuator's
postcondition checks fail with a generic RuntimeError (e.g. "duplicate strategy did not reach
its typed terminal postcondition") rather than a typed, diagnosable outcome -- the exact shape
of the 2026-07-22 live incident (cause: the now-deleted hook_deinflation.py one-time repair
deleting raws directly, bypassing retention authority).

Found while designing polylogue-i3zo's fix (PR #3530): that PR deliberately leaves a
census-referenced plan's raw_authority_plans row untouched even when every raw it names is
already gone, specifically to avoid corrupting the census's immutable plan_count ledger (see
raw_retention.py's _delete_orphaned_raw_authority_plans docstring). That is the correct
retention-side choice, but it means a plan in this state is left to the reconciler to handle,
and the reconciler currently has no typed "the raw evidence for this plan is gone" outcome --
it will raise the same generic RuntimeError shape as the original incident if it is ever
re-attempted.

Scope: teach the reconciler (or whichever actuator inspects duplicate/browser-capture/etc.
strategy state before applying) to detect "required raw is absent from raw_sessions" as a
distinct precondition-failure outcome (e.g. RawReplayPlanStatus.TERMINAL with a diagnosable
reason) instead of falling through to a generic postcondition RuntimeError. Separate,
schema/behavior-bearing design work; not a quick fix.

title: read_raw_authority_census pagination/plan_count go stale once plan-retention window prunes census_plans rows
description:
prune_raw_authority_census_history (polylogue/storage/raw_authority.py, ~line 880) deletes
raw_authority_census_plans / raw_authority_census_post_plans / raw_authority_blockers rows for
censuses older than RAW_AUTHORITY_CENSUS_PLAN_RETENTION (8) generations, once no unresolved
blocker remains, but never adjusts the surviving raw_authority_censuses.plan_count /
post_plan_count on that census's header row (which survives up to
RAW_AUTHORITY_CENSUS_HEADER_RETENTION=256 generations).

read_raw_authority_census (same file, ~line 426) reads plan_count/post_plan_count directly from
the header as the pagination total and to decide next_query_handle
(next_offset < max(total, post_total)). Once a census's plan-detail rows are pruned by the
mechanism above but its header survives, calling read_raw_authority_census against that census
returns a nonzero total with zero actual plan rows, and since next_offset advances only by
len(plans) (always 0 once rows are gone), next_query_handle is reissued forever -- the same
lying-total / non-terminating-pagination shape flagged by chatgpt-codex-connector's review on
PR #3530 (polylogue-i3zo), but via the pre-existing, already-shipped retention-window path
rather than anything introduced in that PR.

Found while designing the fix for polylogue-i3zo: that PR's revised design deliberately never
deletes raw_authority_plans until AFTER this exact mechanism has already cleared its
census/blocker references, specifically so the new code cannot trigger this bug any earlier
than it already exists today. This bead tracks fixing the pre-existing bug itself: either
recompute plan_count/post_plan_count from actual surviving rows on read (defensive, matches
"never trust a denormalized total" convention elsewhere) or decrement the header counts in the
same transaction as prune_raw_authority_census_history's deletes (keeps the header exact but
starts treating a "durable, immutable" ledger row as mutable -- needs the same
durable-tier-mutability discussion PR #3530 went through).

title: Consider refusing break-glass ops/maintenance apply subcommands on an env-derived archive root
description:
Follow-up to polylogue-l1qg. That bead's fix adds an always-on stderr banner (Archive root: <path> [source: ...]) printed by ops.maintenance.maintenance_group before any subcommand dispatches (polylogue/cli/commands/maintenance/__init__.py, _shared.py:print_archive_root_provenance). The bead's text also floated a stricter mitigation: refuse break-glass apply-style maintenance subcommands outright when the archive root resolved from POLYLOGUE_ARCHIVE_ROOT, requiring an explicit extra confirmation flag beyond the ones they already have.

Scoped out of polylogue-l1qg because the ~25 subcommands under ops maintenance do not share one uniform mutation-confirmation convention: raw-authority-frontier gates its apply path on --apply-plan + --preview-census + --yes; raw-authority-blocker-resolve uses --yes; blob-gc uses --yes; run uses --dry-run (mutates by default); rebuild-index has its own multi-flag confirmation shape (--daemon, --no-promote, etc). Auditing all of them to classify read-only vs mutating cleanly, then wiring a consistent additional env-root refusal without false-refusing a read-only command or a command whose apply path uses a differently-named flag, is real design work, not a follow-on line of code.

Next step: enumerate every _COMMANDS entry in polylogue/cli/commands/maintenance/__init__.py, classify mutating vs read-only from its actual implementation (not its docstring claim), and decide whether a shared confirmation-flag abstraction (e.g. a Click option decorator all mutating maintenance commands adopt) is worth the refactor before adding the env-root refusal on top of it.

title: Register devtools/benchmark_compare_nightly.py in the command catalog
description: From a devtools structural audit (2026-08-01): devtools/benchmark_compare_nightly.py is invoked directly by .github/workflows/nightly-scale.yml (`uv run python3 devtools/benchmark_compare_nightly.py ...`) but has no CommandSpec entry in devtools/command_catalog.py and is completely undocumented in docs/devtools.md, unlike its sibling benchmarking commands. Register it (category: benchmarking) so it is discoverable and documented like the rest of the benchmarking surface.

title: run_read_browser in read_views/standard.py is dead code: a second, unwired browser-delivery mechanism
description: Found while fixing polylogue-bvnz (PR #3504): run_read_browser implements browser-opening via a daemon URL (/s/{id}), distinct from and never wired into READ_VIEW_HANDLERS or READ_VIEW_HANDLER_METADATA in read_view_handlers.py (verified). The bug fix on bvnz uses the OTHER browser mechanism (query_output.open_in_browser, temp HTML file) since that's the one _READ_DESTINATIONS actually routes to. Reconcile: either delete run_read_browser as dead code, or determine it was meant to be the daemon-URL-based delivery for a live/running-daemon case and wire it in properly (distinct from the temp-file case for a daemonless CLI) — investigate which disposition is correct before acting, don't just delete without checking whether the daemon-URL approach was intentionally more capable (e.g. supports live updates).

title: master-red: clock guard's datetime replacement broke isinstance checks (fixed via PR #3500)
description: tests/infra/clock_guard.py installed a raising datetime subclass into guarded test modules' datetime symbol; isinstance(x, datetime) inside such a module became a false subclass check, failing 20+ tests (test_models timestamp parsing, timestamp guards, null-guard properties) for an unknown prior period before detection 2026-08-01. Fixed via PR #3500: GuardedDateTime gained a metaclass (_DelegatingInstanceCheck(type)) whose __instancecheck__ delegates to real datetime. Filed retroactively as a durable incident record; consider a regression test asserting isinstance(guarded_instance, datetime) stays true under the guard, to prevent recurrence if the guard mechanism changes again.
close_reason: Fixed same-day via merged PR #3500 (GuardedDateTime metaclass isinstance delegation). Retroactive record only.

Confirmed 2 of 4 findings stale, no code change: insight_materialization CHECK is fully live; price_catalogs metadata out of scope (table-level, tracked separately by resk). devtools test 18 affected files all pass (2 pre-existing flaky confirmed via baseline); devtools verify --quick exit 0.

description: Producer/consumer audit 2026-07-31. ops.db fts_drift_samples (28 rows) is written by storage/fts/drift_sampling.py:sample_fts_drift_to_ops_sync on each FTS freshness snapshot; its own docstring states the purpose ('operator can see drift magnitude trend'). title: Propose a lint for the disabled-capability-on-one-caller defect class
description:
Today's investigation (polylogue-czq2, the CLI/HTTP rebuild-index
prefetch_cache=None bug, plus polylogue-mznm's whale-pass sibling) is the
same defect shape as several already-fixed findings from the same session
(the three duplicated skip-stale-replace implementations; classify_tool's
Agent-tool bucketing; _mark_message_fts_ready_after_targeted_repair's
global-vs-session-scoped ready state; prepare_session_rows's zero-callers
gap; literal_check's zero call sites). The pattern: a capability/policy is
implemented ONCE, correctly, and adopted by ONE caller; every sibling caller
of the same underlying engine silently keeps the old/disabled path, usually
via a parameter defaulting to None/False.

Worth a real detectability proposal, not just another one-off fix. Candidate
shapes to check automatically:
  - A dataclass/function parameter that defaults to None/False AND has a
    docstring phrase like "every existing caller" / "every other caller" /
    "default None" describing itself as a backward-compatible additive knob
    -- grep for that phrasing, then enumerate every call site of the
    enclosing function/class and flag when 2+ callers exist and fewer than
    all of them pass a non-default value for that specific parameter.
  - A "policy" function (freshness/classification/identity/readiness/retry)
    that appears, by name or docstring similarity, in more than one module
    under storage/sqlite/archive_tiers or storage/ generally -- candidate
    duplicate-policy scan.
  - Structural diff between polylogue/daemon/*.py and its polylogue/cli/
    commands/*.py or polylogue/mcp/*.py counterpart that calls the SAME
    underlying engine function with a DIFFERENT set of keyword arguments
    supplied.

This is genuinely hard to get low-noise (the "every caller opts in
identically" case is the common, correct one), so scope this as a
`devtools lab policy` PROPOSAL/spike first -- work out a heuristic against
this session's known-instance corpus (should flag prefetch_cache,
should NOT flag e.g. bulk_fts/bulk_build which are deliberately
offline-rebuild-only and already documented as such) before deciding
whether to land it as a CI gate.

Ref: this bead's parent investigation is the rebuild-index prefetch_cache
fix (PR wiring polylogue.sources.census_parse_stage into
maintenance/rebuild_index.py) landed alongside it.

title: ChatGPT generation_lifecycle events anchor to a different message id across export vintages
description:
Measured while verifying polylogue-oycw's fix (#3401/#3405) against real
'ambiguous-only' cohorts. Reparsed 136 real chatgpt-export ambiguous cohorts
with the CURRENT set-based classifier (read-only simulation against
/realm/db/polylogue source.db + blob store, no writes): 125/136 (91.9%) now
resolve cleanly; 10/136 (7.4%) still hit a genuine `conflict` verdict.

Root cause traced for one example (logical_source_key containing
687f4424-1b1c-832f-8307-8cb83cc5908c, raws 14fa837e/a67d9010/024f7a39): all
46 messages are identical across all 3 revisions (message axis: equal,
attachment axis: equal). The conflict comes entirely from the EVENT axis:
each pair has exactly one `generation_lifecycle` event the other lacks --
same payload shape (`state: completed`, `evidence_source:
provider_native`, `fidelity: exact`, `elapsed_duration_ms` varies as
expected per polylogue-nuec) but anchored to a DIFFERENT
`source_message_provider_id` in each export vintage (e.g.
986a3a7e-6e2b-4fba-851f-ab308fe52fda vs
1175c3a7-66bc-424e-be9a-90a5767abb3c).

`event_base_identity_hash` is keyed on (event_type, anchoring message), so
when the anchor itself moves between exports, the event reads as two
disjoint identities instead of one revised one -- the same shape of bug
polylogue-nuec fixed for the event's payload content, but on the anchor
field instead.

Two other 'still-ambiguous' chatgpt cohorts (6898a012-..., 689b90d9-...)
show the same pairwise pattern (message+attachment axes equal, only the
event axis conflicts) -- worth confirming they share this exact cause
before designing a fix, but the shape strongly suggests it's the dominant
remaining chatgpt fork cause.

Fix sketch (needs verification against more samples first): either (a)
identity should not depend on anchor when only one `generation_lifecycle`
event exists per conversation-turn-window, keying instead on ordinal
position within the turn, or (b) treat two `generation_lifecycle` events as
comparable if their non-anchor content fields match and each side has
exactly one 'orphaned' event, folding them into one equal/growth relation
via a scoped exception mirroring `_provider_ordered_browser_snapshots`.

Not part of polylogue-oycw's scope (positional-prefix -> set containment is
already fixed by #3401/#3405) -- this is a different, event-anchor-specific
volatility axis discovered while verifying that fix's effect on real data.

Ref polylogue-oycw, polylogue-nuec, polylogue-aggz
design: DESIGN (2026-08-03): K-CLASS STAMP-POISONER (fsgdd sweep) — must land BEFORE xselt stamps; wire a blocks-edge to xselt. CONFIRM FIRST per the description: verify the other two still-ambiguous chatgpt cohorts (6898a012, 689b90d9) share the anchor-volatility cause via read-only reparse simulation before designing further. FIX DIRECTION: prefer sketch (b) — a scoped comparison exception: two generation_lifecycle events are comparable when their non-anchor content fields match AND each side has exactly one orphaned event in the turn-window, folding into one equal/growth relation (mirror _provider_ordered_browser_snapshots' precedent in revision_authority.py). Prefer (b) over (a) (ordinal-keyed identity) because (a) changes event_base_identity_hash for ALL chatgpt events — a much wider identity migration for a volatility that only manifests pairwise in membership comparison; (b) confines the change to the comparison layer where the instability lives. PITFALL: the exception must be tight (exactly-one-orphan-each-side, content-equal) or it will paper over genuine event divergence — red-twin fixture: two events with DIFFERENT content but moved anchors must still conflict. If (b) lands, event identity itself is untouched — no SEMANTIC_REPARSE needed for the fix, only re-classification of the affected cohorts (raw-authority path / reindex).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Anchor-volatility cause confirmed on cohorts 6898a012/689b90d9 (read-only simulation) before the fix.
2. The scoped comparison exception (exactly-one-orphan-each-side, non-anchor content equal) folds moved-anchor generation_lifecycle pairs into equal/growth; red-twin: content-differing events with moved anchors still conflict.
3. chatgpt-export ambiguous-cohort resolution rate re-measured (baseline 91.9%); affected cohorts re-classify via the raw-authority path or reindex.
4. Ordering: merged BEFORE xselt stamps (blocks-edge wired). Verify: devtools test -k revision_authority -k event or file-scoped.
notes:
Footprint: polylogue/sources/parsers/chatgpt.py, polylogue/archive/revision_authority.py (generation_lifecycle event anchoring across export vintages).
Executability pass (iteration 5; top-down): same shape as 0qfy — generation_lifecycle event ANCHORING is provider bookkeeping, not content; exclude lifecycle-anchor message-ids from comparison identity (or normalize anchors to content-position before compare) in the membership-comparison builder. RED FIRST: zoo 'lifecycle-anchor-drift' (ey4ro row 3); acceptance: the 10/136 live conflict cohorts resolve in the same read-only simulation.

2026-08-03 verification attempt (read-only, source.db mode=ro): tried to re-locate the 3 named repro cohorts (687f4424, 6898a012, 689b90d9) to confirm the anchor-drift pattern holds before designing a fix, per this bead's own prerequisite. None of the three logical_source_key/native_id fragments match any current raw_sessions row. Broader check: chatgpt-export's revision_authority distribution today is 212 byte_proven / 7498 quarantined / 0 in any other bucket -- note revision_authority itself only has 3 values (asserted/byte_proven/quarantined) at the raw_sessions level; "ambiguous" is a classify_membership_revisions runtime verdict computed over grouped quarantined candidates, not a stored column value, so it can't be queried directly and requires re-running the actual classifier to reproduce.

Conclusion: the live archive's raw-authority state has moved substantially since this bead's original diagnosis (concurrent lb39z/raw-authority work has been actively reclassifying this population throughout 2026-08-03), so the original repro cohorts are gone and a fresh read-only simulation would need to re-run the real classify_membership_revisions/session_revision_projection pipeline over the CURRENT quarantined population from scratch -- not a quick SQL check. This is real, nontrivial verification work (grouping by logical_source_key, loading each candidate's raw content, parsing, projecting, classifying) that deserves its own focused session with the right tooling, not a rushed pass. Leaving this bead exactly as scoped by its own author; did not attempt a fix without the verification it explicitly requires.

2026-08-03 real verification tool built + run (read-only, .agent/scratch/uqwd_verify.py -- gitignored scratch, not committed; script text preserved in this note's session transcript if it needs reconstruction). Groups quarantined chatgpt-export raw_sessions by native_id, decodes+parses each candidate's real blob content through the production pipeline (build_raw_payload_envelope -> parse_payload), builds real SessionRevisionProjections, and calls the REAL classify_membership_revisions -- the exact function the daemon uses, not a reimplementation.

Finding: of 2477 quarantined chatgpt-export rows, only 5 native_ids have >=2 candidate revisions (18 rows total) -- the other 2464 native_ids (99.5% of the population) are SINGLE, non-conflicting raws sitting in quarantined authority with nothing to compare against at all. Ran the real classifier against all 5 multi-candidate cohorts: 0/5 conflict. All 5 resolve cleanly (accepted chain + equivalents), zero ambiguous_raw_ids.

Interpretation: this bead's original vintage-anchor-drift hypothesis does not currently reproduce against the live archive's chatgpt-export population. Either (a) the original 10/136 conflict sample's specific cohorts were already resolved/reclassified by concurrent lb39z/raw-authority work since this bead was filed, or (b) the anchor-drift pattern was real but narrow and the surviving quarantine backlog is a different problem. The much larger finding is (c): 99.5% of quarantined chatgpt-export rows aren't vintage-conflict pairs at all -- they're singleton un-classified raws, which is squarely a Phase A / raw-admission-chokepoint (polylogue-1fijp) concern, not this bead's event-anchor hypothesis.

Recommendation: this bead's fix scope (excluding lifecycle-anchor message-ids from event-axis comparison identity) may still be correct in principle and worth landing defensively (matches 0qfy's already-merged pattern), but it is NOT currently blocking anything measurable in the live archive -- downgrading urgency. The real leverage for the 7498-row chatgpt-export quarantine backlog is 1fijp's admission chokepoint + the ordinary lb39z/w6hql drain, not a fix scoped to this bead's narrow hypothesis. Re-run this verification after 1fijp/lb39z land further if the vintage-conflict pattern needs re-checking on a cleaner population.

title: Leak audit L17: origin-token validation diverges between CLI, DSL and HTTP
description:
AUDIT 2026-07-31 (leak-surfaces). VERDICT: REACHABLE - coherence gap, not a leak.

Three places validate an origin token and they disagree:
 1. The CLI --origin flag validates in a Click parameter callback and raises before any query is built.
 2. The query DSL validates origin: independently inside the expression parser.
 3. The shared substrate does neither - the enum's string constructor is deliberately lenient and maps anything unrecognised to unknown-export, because its job is normalising untrusted wire tokens from provider exports, not gating user input.

The HTTP ?origin= parameter goes straight into the query spec with no validation call, lands on path 3, matches nothing, and returns HTTP 200 with total:0. A caller who mistypes an origin gets a false 'no results' instead of an error, inconsistent with the CLI and DSL on the same conceptual filter.

Fix: validate at the HTTP boundary so the three surfaces agree. No content exposure.

Report: /realm/inbox/polylogue-audits-2026-07-31/leak-surfaces.html

  patches: call real_resolve(...) then interleave, to prove snapshot isolation under concurrent
  writes. Sophisticated race tests.

title: benign-DDL allowlist regex admits CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ... AS SELECT, which transforms data on every archive open
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict: latent
gap in a regex-based allowlist. Currently unreachable; filed before it is used.

CLAIM (docs/internals.md, index-tier benign-DDL convergence, polylogue-jc1b): the
registry is restricted to "idempotent, data-non-transforming DDL statements
(CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS / DROP TABLE IF EXISTS
only)", and "devtools lab policy schema-versioning validates every registry entry
against the allowed idempotent-DDL shapes and rejects anything else".

WHAT THE VALIDATOR IS. _invalid_benign_ddl_entries
(devtools/verify_schema_upgrade_lane.py:144-171) is regex matching, not SQL
parsing:
    _ALLOWED_BENIGN_DDL_PATTERNS   (:120-135) e.g. ^\s*CREATE\s+TABLE\s+IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s
    _FORBIDDEN_BENIGN_DDL_PATTERNS (:120-135) ALTER TABLE / INSERT INTO / UPDATE / DELETE FROM
It does correctly block multi-statement smuggling: a ';' scan at :152-156 after
stripping one trailing semicolon.

THE GAP. `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS x AS SELECT ...` is idempotent-LOOKING and
genuinely data-transforming. It matches the allowed CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
prefix, contains none of the forbidden tokens, and carries no second statement --
so it passes. The allowlist has no rule against `... AS SELECT`, because a regex
on the statement prefix cannot see the statement's shape.

This matters more than a normal lint gap because of where these statements run:
apply_index_benign_ddl_convergence executes on EVERY same-version index.db open
(bootstrap.py:174-192), on fresh and existing archives alike, with no version
bump and no reparse. A data-transforming statement placed there would rewrite
derived content on every open, silently.

CURRENTLY UNREACHABLE: the live registry
(storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index_convergence.py:63-80) contains only DROP
TABLE IF EXISTS entries. Nothing is wrong today.

AC:
- The validator rejects `AS SELECT` (and any other data-producing tail) on a
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entry -- either an added forbidden pattern or a real
  statement parse.
- A test adds a `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t AS SELECT 1` registry entry and
  asserts the lint fails, so the guard is proven rather than assumed.

title: session_links over-claims: 4-value enum vs 2-value CHECK, unconstrained inheritance pairing, cycle-budget false positives
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Three small,
related over-claims on the session_links surface. All dormant on live data; filed
so they are tracked debt rather than anonymous debt.

--- 1. TopologyEdgeStatus advertises four values; the column permits two.
CLAUDE.md: "TopologyEdgeStatus = unresolved/resolved/repaired/quarantined
(cycle-break)". core/enums.py:323-329 does define four members. But the DDL,
storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/index.py:763:
    status TEXT CHECK(status IN ('repaired','quarantined') OR status IS NULL)
`resolved` and `unresolved` are never literal column values -- they are inferred
structurally from resolved_dst_session_id being NULL or not
(storage/sqlite/queries/session_links.py:26-29 only ever serializes QUARANTINED
and REPAIRED). MEASURED live: 9,333 session_links rows, 0 quarantined,
0 repaired, 1,426 unresolved-by-structure. Not a bug; a hand-maintained subset of
an enum with no check that the subset stays valid if the enum is renamed or
extended. Related to the literal_check bead (the generation mechanism CLAUDE.md
cites does not run).

--- 2. The inheritance <-> branch_point pairing is convention, not constraint.
The design requires inheritance='prefix-sharing' to carry a branch point and
'spawned-fresh' not to. MEASURED live -- it holds perfectly:
    inheritance NULL,            branch_point NULL      1,436
    inheritance 'prefix-sharing', branch_point NOT NULL    537
    inheritance 'spawned-fresh',  branch_point NULL      7,360
    contradictory rows                                       0
But nothing enforces it. index.py:762-763 constrains `inheritance` and `status`
independently; there is no cross-column CHECK. The consistency is a property of
one write path (write.py:5074-5096, where branch_point_message_id is computed
only alongside the 'prefix-sharing' assignment). A second writer, or a repair
that nulls one field without the other, produces a row the schema accepts and the
composition logic cannot interpret.

--- 3. Cycle-walk budget exhaustion is reported as a cycle.
_would_create_cycle (storage/sqlite/queries/session_links.py:93-128) walks
sessions.parent_session_id upward for at most _CYCLE_WALK_BUDGET = 1024 steps. On
exhaustion it appends "...budget-exceeded" to the path and returns it as a TRUTHY
cycle result (:109-111), so _quarantine_link (:131-173) records
evidence_json reason "cycle_rejected". A legitimate chain deeper than 1024 hops
is therefore quarantined as if it were a cycle -- a false positive that
permanently drops a real lineage edge and mislabels why.
True cycles are detected correctly (genuine parent-pointer traversal to a repeat).
The read-composition path has its own independent limit,
LINEAGE_ITERATIVE_DEPTH_LIMIT = 1024 (store_constants.py:16), which on exhaustion
sets LINEAGE_TRUNCATION_DEPTH_LIMIT instead of quarantining -- and that signal is
subject to the discard bug filed separately.
MEASURED: deepest live prefix-sharing chain is 60 hops. Dormant.

AC:
- The status CHECK either lists what the enum lists, or a comment at the DDL
  records that the column is deliberately a two-value subset and why.
- The inheritance/branch_point pairing is a CHECK constraint, or the invariant is
  stated at the DDL so a future writer sees it.
- Budget exhaustion is distinguishable from a detected cycle in the quarantine
  evidence, so an operator can tell a false positive from a real one.

title: Embedding catch-up planned and processed metrics are the same field: a shortfall can never be represented
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ASSERTED. Two Prometheus labels are populated from one field, so the differential
they exist to express is structurally always zero.

Same failure family as polylogue-roax (the FTS "100% indexed" that was never
measured, fixed tonight by PR #3429): a surface reports a property nothing
measured. This one is still live on origin/master.

daemon/metrics.py:838-839, the archive-mode (current, sole runtime) path:
    "latest_planned_sessions":   latest["scanned_sessions"] if latest is not None else 0,
    "latest_processed_sessions": latest["scanned_sessions"] if latest is not None else 0,
Both from the SAME field. Exported as two distinct series at
daemon/metrics.py:942-943:
    polylogue_embedding_catchup_sessions{state="planned"}
    polylogue_embedding_catchup_sessions{state="processed"}

There is no planned quantity to read. MEASURED on the live archive:
    sqlite3 "file:/realm/db/polylogue/ops.db?mode=ro" ".schema embedding_catchup_runs"
    -> columns: run_id, started_at_ms, finished_at_ms, status, origin,
       scanned_sessions, embedded_sessions, error_count, embedded_messages,
       estimated_cost_usd, error_message
No planned_sessions column exists in the ops tier at all.

CONTRADICTION PAIR: the legacy single-file path, daemon/metrics.py:761-762, reads
two genuinely distinct DB-backed values (latest_run["planned_sessions"],
latest_run["processed_sessions"]). So the same EmbeddingMetricState field pair
means "two independent measurements" on one path and "one measurement duplicated"
on the other, with no signal at the metric that they differ in kind.

BLAST RADIUS: a catch-up run that is interrupted, budget-capped, or otherwise
scans fewer sessions than intended can NEVER show a shortfall on this metric --
planned == processed by construction, so the dashboard always reads 0% shortfall.
Small blast radius (metrics consumers, not the default CLI) but the same
epistemics as roax: a reassuring number that no code computed.

AC:
- Either the archive path records a real planned count (an ops-tier column plus
  the write that populates it), or the planned series is removed rather than
  duplicated. Do not leave a metric whose two labels cannot disagree.
- If removed, note it wherever the dashboard/alerting consumes it.

title: Orphaned blob publication reservations pin blobs against GC forever: 2 rows, 42.5MB, 19 days, no TTL and no operator surface
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
MEASURED leak. A crashed publisher pins blobs against GC permanently, with no
TTL, no liveness test, and no operator surface.

MEASURED, live (sqlite3 "file:/realm/db/polylogue/source.db?mode=ro"):
    SELECT publication_id, size_bytes, publisher_id,
           datetime(reserved_at_ms/1000,'unixepoch') FROM blob_publication_reservations;
    f1c44ec2-...  16,021,146 bytes  publisher 36031cd4-...  2026-07-12 12:03:08
    0d21f742-...  26,470,839 bytes  publisher f498c976-...  2026-07-13 08:45:27
Two reservations, 19 and 18 days old, 42.5 MB pinned. Over the same window
gc_generations shows 92 completed GC passes (measured), i.e. GC has run ~92 times
and skipped these every time -- by design.

WHY THEY NEVER CLEAR. reconcile_blob_publication_reservations
(storage/blob_publication.py:312-370) classifies each reservation into exactly
three buckets:
    referenced        -> cleared (needs a live ArchiveWriterExclusion)
    blob missing      -> cleared (same)
    else              -> `unresolved += 1`   <-- never cleared, in any case
The third branch has no delete path at all. A reservation whose blob exists but
is not referenced -- precisely what a publisher that died between reserving and
committing leaves behind -- is retained forever. Age is not consulted:
MIN_AGE_S's own comment (storage/blob_gc.py:108-113) states the age floor "is not
used to infer that a live publisher has expired", so an abandoned publisher is
indistinguishable from a live one, permanently.

And GC honours it: _has_publication_reservation (blob_gc.py:225-232) is checked
at both the plan step (:415) and the unlink step (:452), incrementing
skipped_reserved.

The code knows the shape of this hazard. The docstring of
reconcile_blob_publication_reservations_under_exclusion (blob_publication.py:
382-390) already names a sibling case: "without one, may_clear is always false
and every classified row is merely retained forever, a durable reservation leak"
(polylogue-qs0a). That fix closed the missing-exclusion path. The `unresolved`
path was left open.

OPERATOR VISIBILITY: none found. `unresolved` is returned in
BlobPublicationReconciliation but grep of daemon/ and cli/ for it surfaces only
unrelated lineage/topology "unresolved" usages. blob_publication_reservations
appears in cli/commands/status.py:260 only as a row-count entry in the source-tier
table list -- an operator sees "2" with no indication that those 2 are permanent
GC exclusions.

BLAST RADIUS: unbounded, slow disk leak. 42.5 MB today; one entry per crashed
publisher forever, and each pinned blob is by definition unreferenced, so it is
dead bytes GC is structurally forbidden from reclaiming. Low severity, zero
recovery path without manual SQL.

AC:
- An abandoned reservation is distinguishable from a live one -- publisher
  liveness, an explicit TTL, or reconciliation against the owning publication --
  and the `unresolved` bucket has a terminal state.
- `unresolved > 0` is visible to an operator (status, check, or a debt row), not
  only as a return value nothing reads.
- The two live rows are cleanable by a documented command rather than hand SQL.

title: Blob GC safety invariants are described four mutually contradictory ways, incl. CLAUDE.md advertising a deleted lease mechanism
description:
AUDIT FINDING (claimed-vs-enforced invariants sweep, 2026-07-31). Verdict:
ASSERTED, and mutually contradictory across four statements about the same
property -- for the one operation in the system that irreversibly deletes files.

Four descriptions of what protects a blob from GC, all current:

1. CLAUDE.md:158 (the file every agent loads first):
     "Blob GC uses two independent safety invariants (leases + snapshot
      reference check) to bridge the acquire-blob -> commit-row window."
2. docs/architecture-spine.md:68-71:
     "GC combines a DB snapshot reference check with a generation-age floor
      (gc_generations, MIN_AGE_S) as its SOLE defense ... a lease-based second
      invariant was removed as unreachable dead code (polylogue-v7e0)."
3. storage/blob_gc.py module docstring (lines 7-26): FIVE numbered invariants,
   with #2 being a durable publication receipt and #4 the generation-age floor,
   and a closing paragraph confirming the lease mechanism
   (pending_blob_refs / acquire_blob_leases) was replaced in source schema v4.
4. storage/blob_gc.py:303-304, run_blob_gc's own docstring, renumbering to THREE
   invariants and calling the age floor
     "the sole protection against an in-flight ingest"
   -- while MIN_AGE_S's own comment 190 lines earlier (blob_gc.py:108-113) says
   the opposite:
     "Publication reservations provide the exact acquire-to-reference defense.
      This floor remains defense-in-depth ... it is not used to infer that a
      live publisher has expired."

So: CLAUDE.md advertises a mechanism that was DELETED; the spine says the age
floor is the sole defense; the module docstring says receipts are; and the two
docstrings inside the same file disagree with each other about which one is sole.
The numbering also drifts (the age gate is #4 in the module docstring, #2 in
run_blob_gc's, and _previous_generation_completed_at's docstring calls it "safety
invariant #2" too).

WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES (measured by reading it): reservations ARE consulted.
_has_publication_reservation (blob_gc.py:225-232) is called twice, at the plan
step (:415) and again at the unlink step (:452), and blob_publication.py:113
really does INSERT reservations. So the spine's "sole defense" wording is the
inaccurate one, and CLAUDE.md's is the stale one.

BLAST RADIUS: nobody reading any single source can tell what protects a blob.
This is the operation that unlinks content-addressed files permanently; GC has
reclaimed 171 blobs / 565.6 MB across 92 generations on the live archive
(measured, source.db gc_generations). A future change made against CLAUDE.md's
description would be reasoning about a lease system that no longer exists.

AC:
- One statement of the safety invariants, in the module docstring, with a
  consistent numbering; CLAUDE.md and architecture-spine.md either point at it or
  restate it verbatim.
- CLAUDE.md:158 no longer claims leases. Per the repo's surgical-renewal rule the
  stale description dies in the same change that replaces it.
- run_blob_gc's "sole protection" sentence and MIN_AGE_S's "defense-in-depth"
  sentence are reconciled -- they cannot both be true.

title: Embedding failure ledger and detached-writer failures: per-session forensic detail silently lost
description: Silent-degradation audit 2026-07-31. (a) storage/embeddings/materialization.py:1554-1583: in the embedding-failure handler, the SELECT origin lookup is wrapped in contextlib.suppress(sqlite3.Error); if it fails, record_embedding_failure() is skipped entirely — the durable per-session failure ledger (retry/backoff bookkeeping) loses the row while only the aggregate error count survives via embedding_catchup_runs. Fix: record with origin=None/unknown instead of skipping. (b) daemon/write_coordinator.py:357-361: detached background-writer task exceptions surface via log only, no counter across daemon lifetime. (c) write_coordinator.py:428-431: suppress(RuntimeError) in _run_in_daemon_thread worker — if the loop is already closed the awaiting future is never resolved (potential silent hang). (d) schemas/sampling_db.py:260-262: _iter_schema_units_from_db returns an empty generator when sibling source.db is missing — indistinguishable from zero matching rows; warn on missing tier file. Verdict: SHOULD-RECORD each.

description: Silent-degradation audit 2026-07-31. (b) storage/fts/drift_sampling.py:96-119 ops.db drift-sample write failure logged at DEBUG (feeds the drift-alerting pipeline itself) — bump to warning. title: bead-landing-check sweep abandoned: 6% precision even after live-consumer fix; note-staleness may be the better angle
notes:
CLOSED PR #3424 unmerged (2026-07-31) after measuring the tool against a
190-bead human-verified ground truth (5 independent review groups, complete
STALE/PARTIAL/LIVE verdict set recorded as bd notes on the reviewed beads
themselves -- durable, queryable via `bd sql "SELECT id, notes FROM issues
WHERE notes LIKE '%VERDICT%'"`).

WHAT WAS BUILT: `devtools workspace bead-landing-check` (code still exists on
branch feature/devtools/bead-landing-check, not merged) -- extracts cited
commit hashes/PR numbers from bead text, cherry-picks commits onto master in
a reused throwaway worktree to detect empty-diff landings (survives
squash-merge id rewriting, unlike git log --is-ancestor or issue-id grep),
checks PR merge state via gh, and after a first sweep's ~5% precision was
found (95% false-positive on 114 human-checked beads), added three
downgrade-only fixes: (1) require a live production consumer for a landed
commit via git grep outside tests, (2) suppress verdicts for beads with open
parent-child dependents, (3) suppress verdicts when the bead's own text
contains an explicit not-done phrase (deferred/xfail/not wired/etc).

RESULT AFTER THE FIXES: precision 6.1% overall (66 flagged beads), 20.0% at
strong confidence (10 beads), 3.6% at weak (56 beads). Recall 4/7 confirmed
STALE beads still flagged (57.1%; 44.4% against the reported 9 -- 2 STALE
beads' notes used phrasing my regex could not match). The three fixes
provably removed genuine STALE beads along with false positives:
polylogue-4fm3 (consumer check inconclusive on a non-Python change),
polylogue-6pii (consumer check found no grep-visible caller despite a
confirmed-safe closable chore), polylogue-7mtf (the suppression check's
"xfail" keyword, added to catch polylogue-hg97's genuine incompleteness
admission, fired on 7mtf's OWN unrelated use of the word describing a
regression-guard the fix itself added -- same word, opposite meaning).

WHY IT DOESN'T WORK: "is this work done" is a question about whether
acceptance criteria are semantically satisfied; a git/text query can only
check whether artifacts exist or specific phrases are present/absent.
polylogue-aggz is the clearest illustration: two directly-matching MERGED
PRs, and the PR bodies themselves state 2 of 3 declared invariants are
untouched -- no commit-graph query reaches that.

THE MORE PROMISING ANGLE, per the coordinator's read (which the data
supports): the suppression-phrase check reads the bead's OWN MOST RECENT
NOTE, not the commit graph -- that's the signal the human reviewers actually
used. A future tool aimed at NOTE STALENESS (has this bead's own
most-recent-note-implied status been contradicted by newer master state?)
rather than commit archaeology might do better, but the 7mtf false negative
shows a bare lexical keyword match isn't safe as-is -- it would need to
distinguish "this note admits incompleteness" from "this note happens to
mention a word like xfail/deferred/stale in an unrelated, completed
context." Likely needs something closer to reading the note's actual claim
sentence-by-sentence (an LLM-judge pass per candidate bead, not a sweep-scale
regex) rather than a cheap grep-shaped heuristic.

Do not resurrect the sweep-shaped tool as-is. If revisited, scope it as a
per-bead check invoked when a human already suspects ONE bead is stale
(narrower claim, human still reads the evidence), never a sweep that
produces a headline count -- per the coordinator's original framing of the
one outcome that would have kept a role for it, which this data did not
reach.

title: Verify grok.py export field coverage against a real xAI GDPR export (unverified, no sample corpus available)
description:
Surfaced during the 2026-07-31 heuristics/discard-site audit as a low-confidence, UNVERIFIED lead -- filed as a follow-up investigation, not a confirmed finding, per the audit's evidence discipline.

polylogue/sources/parsers/grok.py (178 lines) extracts only conversation.title, create_time, and per-response sender/message/create_time (grok.py:122-171). It documents itself as reverse-engineered from three third-party sources (a GitHub viewer, a blog post, a userscript) because 'no official xAI schema publication exists' (grok.py:1-38), and asserts the export has 'no native conversation id or attachment/image data.'

This audit could NOT verify that claim either way: no real Grok GDPR export exists under /realm/data/exports/chatlog, /realm/data/exports, or elsewhere searched (checked at audit time, 2026-07-31). The only grok-adjacent artifact found is a browser-capture DOM dump (/realm/inbox/polylogue-browser-spool-2026-07-10/grok/dom-e4e24461-4b1f7d02f3c4.json), which is a different capture path (live DOM scrape, not the GDPR export grok.py parses) and cannot substitute.

Every other provider audited this session (Claude Code via polylogue-pbuh/cgfy, ChatGPT, Codex, Hermes) turned out to have MORE typed fields in the real wire format than the parser initially read -- structuredPatch, patch_apply changes, reasoning traces, thread titles. Given that pattern, grok.py's self-reported 'no attachments, no conversation id' claim deserves the same corpus-diff treatment cgfy applied to Claude Code, but doing so requires acquiring one real xAI GDPR export first.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Acquire (or obtain from the operator) one real xAI/Grok GDPR export. 2. Run cgfy's key-enumeration method: list every top-level/response/message key present in the real export, diff against what grok.py currently reads. 3. Classify each unread key as read / deliberately-dropped-with-reason / to-acquire, same as cgfy's disposition table. 4. If grok.py's self-reported field coverage turns out accurate, close as verified-clean; if gaps are found, file follow-up beads per gap with corpus counts.

title: Query DSL: float-literal numeric predicates for JSON-extracted fields (run_settings temperature/topP)
description:
Follow-up from polylogue-o4j2 (AC2, deferred).

aistudio-drive's runSettings (temperature/topP/topK/maxOutputTokens/
thinkingLevel/safetySettings/enable* flags) is parsed and stored verbatim as
sessions.run_settings_json (polylogue-2qx.4/cgfy, index v46). It is not
exposed to the query DSL, so "sessions where temperature > 0.5" is not
expressible. Two independent gaps block it:

1. Grammar: the boolean-query numeric-comparison rule only accepts integer
   literals (`COUNT_FIELD COMP_OP INT` in archive/query/expression.py) --
   temperature/topP are floats (0.0-2.0 / 0.0-1.0 range).
2. SQL builder: NUMERIC_QUERY_FIELD_REGISTRY's NumericQueryFieldInfo.unit_columns
   values are treated as plain column names (`f"{table_alias}.{column}"` in
   storage/sqlite/archive_tiers/archive.py, two call sites) -- there is no
   path for a computed/JSON-extract expression like
   `json_extract(run_settings_json, '$.temperature')`.

Scope: extend the grammar to accept decimal literals for numeric predicates
(without breaking existing integer-only fields), and extend the SQL-builder
call sites (and NumericQueryFieldInfo, if needed) to support an expression
column alongside plain columns. Consider starting with the integer-typed
run_settings fields (topK, maxOutputTokens) which fit the existing INT-only
grammar and only need the SQL-builder JSON-extract half, then float support
(temperature, topP) as a second phase needing the grammar change too.

Not urgent: run_settings is durably stored and readable via `read --view`
already; this is about ergonomic filtering, not data loss.

title: 7 of 95 design-chat messages dropped by _parse_design_chat
